verses.kjv_text: And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here {am} I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where {is} the lamb for a burnt offering? {lamb: or, kid}
verses.nlt_text: Isaac turned to Abraham and said, "Father?" "Yes, my son?" Abraham replied."We have the fire and the wood," the boy said, "but where is the sheep for the burnt offering?"

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
verses.nlt_text: "God will provide a sheep for the burnt offering, my son," Abraham answered. And they both walked on together.

verses.kjv_text: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood.
verses.nlt_text: When they arrived at the place where God had told him to go, Abraham built an altar and arranged the wood on it. Then he tied his son, Isaac, and laid him on the altar on top of the wood.

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
verses.nlt_text: And Abraham picked up the knife to kill his son as a sacrifice.

verses.kjv_text: And the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here {am} I.
verses.nlt_text: At that moment the angel of the LORD called to him from heaven, "Abraham! Abraham!" "Yes," Abraham replied. "Here I am!"

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only {son} from me.
verses.nlt_text: "Don't lay a hand on the boy!" the angel said. "Do not hurt him in any way, for now I know that you truly fear God. You have not withheld from me even your son, your only son."

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind {him} a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
verses.nlt_text: Then Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in a thicket. So he took the ram and sacrificed it as a burnt offering in place of his son.

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovahjireh: as it is said {to} this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen. {Jehovahjireh: that is, The Lord will see, or, provide}
verses.nlt_text: Abraham named the place Yahweh-Yireh (which means "the LORD will provide"). To this day, people still use that name as a proverb: "On the mountain of the LORD it will be provided."

verses.kjv_text: And the angel of the LORD called unto Abraham out of heaven the second time,
verses.nlt_text: Then the angel of the LORD called again to Abraham from heaven.

verses.kjv_text: And said, By myself have I sworn, saith the LORD, for because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only {son}:
verses.nlt_text: "This is what the LORD says: Because you have obeyed me and have not withheld even your son, your only son, I swear by my own name that

verses.kjv_text: That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which {is} upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies; {shore: Heb. lip}
verses.nlt_text: I will certainly bless you. I will multiply your descendants beyond number, like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. Your descendants will conquer the cities of their enemies.

verses.kjv_text: And in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast obeyed my voice.
verses.nlt_text: And through your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed-- all because you have obeyed me."

verses.kjv_text: So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beersheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beersheba.
verses.nlt_text: Then they returned to the servants and traveled back to Beersheba, where Abraham continued to live.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after these things, that it was told Abraham, saying, Behold, Milcah, she hath also born children unto thy brother Nahor;
verses.nlt_text: Soon after this, Abraham heard that Milcah, his brother Nahor's wife, had borne Nahor eight sons.

verses.kjv_text: Huz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram,
verses.nlt_text: The oldest was named Uz, the next oldest was Buz, followed by Kemuel (the ancestor of the Arameans),

verses.kjv_text: And Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.
verses.nlt_text: Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.

verses.kjv_text: And Bethuel begat Rebekah: these eight Milcah did bear to Nahor, Abraham's brother. {Rebekah: Gr. Rebecca}
verses.nlt_text: (Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.) In addition to these eight sons from Milcah,

verses.kjv_text: And his concubine, whose name {was} Reumah, she bare also Tebah, and Gaham, and Thahash, and Maachah.
verses.nlt_text: Nahor had four other children from his concubine Reumah. Their names were Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

verses.kjv_text: And Sarah was an hundred and seven and twenty years old: {these were} the years of the life of Sarah.
verses.nlt_text: When Sarah was 127 years old,

verses.kjv_text: And Sarah died in Kirjatharba; the same {is} Hebron in the land of Canaan: and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah, and to weep for her.
verses.nlt_text: she died at Kiriath-arba (now called Hebron) in the land of Canaan. There Abraham mourned and wept for her.

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham stood up from before his dead, and spake unto the sons of Heth, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Then, leaving her body, he said to the Hittite elders,

verses.kjv_text: I {am} a stranger and a sojourner with you: give me a possession of a buryingplace with you, that I may bury my dead out of my sight.
verses.nlt_text: "Here I am, a stranger and a foreigner among you. Please sell me a piece of land so I can give my wife a proper burial."

verses.kjv_text: And the children of Heth answered Abraham, saying unto him,
verses.nlt_text: The Hittites replied to Abraham,

verses.kjv_text: Hear us, my lord: thou {art} a mighty prince among us: in the choice of our sepulchres bury thy dead; none of us shall withhold from thee his sepulchre, but that thou mayest bury thy dead. {a mighty...: Heb. a prince of God}
verses.nlt_text: "Listen, my lord, you are an honored prince among us. Choose the finest of our tombs and bury her there. No one here will refuse to help you in this way."

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham stood up, and bowed himself to the people of the land, {even} to the children of Heth.
verses.nlt_text: Then Abraham bowed low before the Hittites and said,

verses.kjv_text: And he communed with them, saying, If it be your mind that I should bury my dead out of my sight; hear me, and intreat for me to Ephron the son of Zohar,
verses.nlt_text: "Since you are willing to help me in this way, be so kind as to ask Ephron son of Zohar

verses.kjv_text: That he may give me the cave of Machpelah, which he hath, which {is} in the end of his field; for as much money as it is worth he shall give it me for a possession of a buryingplace amongst you. {as much...: Heb. full money}
verses.nlt_text: to let me buy his cave at Machpelah, down at the end of his field. I will pay the full price in the presence of witnesses, so I will have a permanent burial place for my family."

verses.kjv_text: And Ephron dwelt among the children of Heth: and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the audience of the children of Heth, {even} of all that went in at the gate of his city, saying, {audience: Heb. ears}
verses.nlt_text: Ephron was sitting there among the others, and he answered Abraham as the others listened, speaking publicly before all the Hittite elders of the town.

verses.kjv_text: Nay, my lord, hear me: the field give I thee, and the cave that {is} therein, I give it thee; in the presence of the sons of my people give I it thee: bury thy dead.
verses.nlt_text: "No, my lord," he said to Abraham, "please listen to me. I will give you the field and the cave. Here in the presence of my people, I give it to you. Go and bury your dead."

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham bowed down himself before the people of the land.
verses.nlt_text: Abraham again bowed low before the citizens of the land,

verses.kjv_text: And he spake unto Ephron in the audience of the people of the land, saying, But if thou {wilt give it}, I pray thee, hear me: I will give thee money for the field; take {it} of me, and I will bury my dead there.
verses.nlt_text: and he replied to Ephron as everyone listened. "No, listen to me. I will buy it from you. Let me pay the full price for the field so I can bury my dead there."

verses.kjv_text: And Ephron answered Abraham, saying unto him,
verses.nlt_text: Ephron answered Abraham,

verses.kjv_text: My lord, hearken unto me: the land {is worth} four hundred shekels of silver; what {is} that betwixt me and thee? bury therefore thy dead.
verses.nlt_text: "My lord, please listen to me. The land is worth 400 pieces of silver, but what is that between friends? Go ahead and bury your dead."

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham hearkened unto Ephron; and Abraham weighed to Ephron the silver, which he had named in the audience of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, current {money} with the merchant.
verses.nlt_text: So Abraham agreed to Ephron's price and paid the amount he had suggested-- 400 pieces of silver, weighed according to the market standard. The Hittite elders witnessed the transaction.

verses.kjv_text: And the field of Ephron, which {was} in Machpelah, which {was} before Mamre, the field, and the cave which {was} therein, and all the trees that {were} in the field, that {were} in all the borders round about, were made sure
verses.nlt_text: So Abraham bought the plot of land belonging to Ephron at Machpelah, near Mamre. This included the field itself, the cave that was in it, and all the surrounding trees.

verses.kjv_text: Unto Abraham for a possession in the presence of the children of Heth, before all that went in at the gate of his city.
verses.nlt_text: It was transferred to Abraham as his permanent possession in the presence of the Hittite elders at the city gate.

verses.kjv_text: And after this, Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre: the same {is} Hebron in the land of Canaan.
verses.nlt_text: Then Abraham buried his wife, Sarah, there in Canaan, in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre (also called Hebron).

verses.kjv_text: And the field, and the cave that {is} therein, were made sure unto Abraham for a possession of a buryingplace by the sons of Heth.
verses.nlt_text: So the field and the cave were transferred from the Hittites to Abraham for use as a permanent burial place.

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham was old, {and} well stricken in age: and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things. {well...: Heb. gone into days}
verses.nlt_text: Abraham was now a very old man, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
verses.nlt_text: One day Abraham said to his oldest servant, the man in charge of his household, "Take an oath by putting your hand under my thigh.

verses.kjv_text: And I will make thee swear by the LORD, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:
verses.nlt_text: Swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and earth, that you will not allow my son to marry one of these local Canaanite women.

verses.kjv_text: But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.
verses.nlt_text: Go instead to my homeland, to my relatives, and find a wife there for my son Isaac."

verses.kjv_text: And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the woman will not be willing to follow me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from whence thou camest?
verses.nlt_text: The servant asked, "But what if I can't find a young woman who is willing to travel so far from home? Should I then take Isaac there to live among your relatives in the land you came from?"

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham said unto him, Beware thou that thou bring not my son thither again.
verses.nlt_text: "No!" Abraham responded. "Be careful never to take my son there.

verses.kjv_text: The LORD God of heaven, which took me from my father's house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my son from thence.
verses.nlt_text: For the LORD, the God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and my native land, solemnly promised to give this land to my descendants. He will send his angel ahead of you, and he will see to it that you find a wife there for my son.

verses.kjv_text: And if the woman will not be willing to follow thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath: only bring not my son thither again.
verses.nlt_text: If she is unwilling to come back with you, then you are free from this oath of mine. But under no circumstances are you to take my son there."

verses.kjv_text: And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sware to him concerning that matter.
verses.nlt_text: So the servant took an oath by putting his hand under the thigh of his master, Abraham. He swore to follow Abraham's instructions.

verses.kjv_text: And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master {were} in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor. {for: or, and}
verses.nlt_text: Then he loaded ten of Abraham's camels with all kinds of expensive gifts from his master, and he traveled to distant Aram-naharaim. There he went to the town where Abraham's brother Nahor had settled.

verses.kjv_text: And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, {even} the time that women go out to draw {water}. {that...: Heb. that women who draw water go forth}
verses.nlt_text: He made the camels kneel beside a well just outside the town. It was evening, and the women were coming out to draw water.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.
verses.nlt_text: "O LORD, God of my master, Abraham," he prayed. "Please give me success today, and show unfailing love to my master, Abraham.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, I stand {here} by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:
verses.nlt_text: See, I am standing here beside this spring, and the young women of the town are coming out to draw water.

verses.kjv_text: And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: {let the same be} she {that} thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.
verses.nlt_text: This is my request. I will ask one of them, 'Please give me a drink from your jug.' If she says, 'Yes, have a drink, and I will water your camels, too!'-- let her be the one you have selected as Isaac's wife. This is how I will know that you have shown unfailing love to my master."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.
verses.nlt_text: Before he had finished praying, he saw a young woman named Rebekah coming out with her water jug on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel, who was the son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his wife, Milcah.

verses.kjv_text: And the damsel {was} very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up. {very...: Heb. good of countenance}
verses.nlt_text: Rebekah was very beautiful and old enough to be married, but she was still a virgin. She went down to the spring, filled her jug, and came up again.

verses.kjv_text: And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Let me, I pray thee, drink a little water of thy pitcher.
verses.nlt_text: Running over to her, the servant said, "Please give me a little drink of water from your jug."

verses.kjv_text: And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes, my lord," she answered, "have a drink." And she quickly lowered her jug from her shoulder and gave him a drink.

verses.kjv_text: And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw {water} for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.
verses.nlt_text: When she had given him a drink, she said, "I'll draw water for your camels, too, until they have had enough to drink."

verses.kjv_text: And she hasted, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again unto the well to draw {water}, and drew for all his camels.
verses.nlt_text: So she quickly emptied her jug into the watering trough and ran back to the well to draw water for all his camels.

verses.kjv_text: And the man wondering at her held his peace, to wit whether the LORD had made his journey prosperous or not.
verses.nlt_text: The servant watched her in silence, wondering whether or not the LORD had given him success in his mission.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden earring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten {shekels} weight of gold; {earring: or, jewel for the forehead}
verses.nlt_text: Then at last, when the camels had finished drinking, he took out a gold ring for her nose and two large gold bracelets for her wrists.

verses.kjv_text: And said, Whose daughter {art} thou? tell me, I pray thee: is there room {in} thy father's house for us to lodge in?
verses.nlt_text: "Whose daughter are you?" he asked. "And please tell me, would your father have any room to put us up for the night?"

verses.kjv_text: And she said unto him, I {am} the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bare unto Nahor.
verses.nlt_text: "I am the daughter of Bethuel," she replied. "My grandparents are Nahor and Milcah.

verses.kjv_text: She said moreover unto him, We have both straw and provender enough, and room to lodge in.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, we have plenty of straw and feed for the camels, and we have room for guests."

verses.kjv_text: And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: The man bowed low and worshiped the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Blessed {be} the LORD God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I {being} in the way, the LORD led me to the house of my master's brethren.
verses.nlt_text: "Praise the LORD, the God of my master, Abraham," he said. "The LORD has shown unfailing love and faithfulness to my master, for he has led me straight to my master's relatives."

verses.kjv_text: And the damsel ran, and told {them of} her mother's house these things.
verses.nlt_text: The young woman ran home to tell her family everything that had happened.

verses.kjv_text: And Rebekah had a brother, and his name {was} Laban: and Laban ran out unto the man, unto the well.
verses.nlt_text: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, who ran out to meet the man at the spring.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he saw the earring and bracelets upon his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister, saying, Thus spake the man unto me; that he came unto the man; and, behold, he stood by the camels at the well.
verses.nlt_text: He had seen the nose-ring and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and had heard Rebekah tell what the man had said. So he rushed out to the spring, where the man was still standing beside his camels. Laban said to him,

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Come in, thou blessed of the LORD; wherefore standest thou without? for I have prepared the house, and room for the camels.
verses.nlt_text: "Come and stay with us, you who are blessed by the LORD! Why are you standing here outside the town when I have a room all ready for you and a place prepared for the camels?"

verses.kjv_text: And the man came into the house: and he ungirded his camels, and gave straw and provender for the camels, and water to wash his feet, and the men's feet that {were} with him.
verses.nlt_text: So the man went home with Laban, and Laban unloaded the camels, gave him straw for their bedding, fed them, and provided water for the man and the camel drivers to wash their feet.

verses.kjv_text: And there was set {meat} before him to eat: but he said, I will not eat, until I have told mine errand. And he said, Speak on.
verses.nlt_text: Then food was served. But Abraham's servant said, "I don't want to eat until I have told you why I have come." "All right," Laban said, "tell us."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, I {am} Abraham's servant.
verses.nlt_text: "I am Abraham's servant," he explained.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD hath blessed my master greatly; and he is become great: and he hath given him flocks, and herds, and silver, and gold, and menservants, and maidservants, and camels, and asses.
verses.nlt_text: "And the LORD has greatly blessed my master; he has become a wealthy man. The LORD has given him flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, a fortune in silver and gold, and many male and female servants and camels and donkeys.

verses.kjv_text: And Sarah my master's wife bare a son to my master when she was old: and unto him hath he given all that he hath.
verses.nlt_text: "When Sarah, my master's wife, was very old, she gave birth to my master's son, and my master has given him everything he owns.

verses.kjv_text: And my master made me swear, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife to my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I dwell:
verses.nlt_text: And my master made me take an oath. He said, 'Do not allow my son to marry one of these local Canaanite women.

verses.kjv_text: But thou shalt go unto my father's house, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son.
verses.nlt_text: Go instead to my father's house, to my relatives, and find a wife there for my son.'

verses.kjv_text: And I said unto my master, Peradventure the woman will not follow me.
verses.nlt_text: "But I said to my master, 'What if I can't find a young woman who is willing to go back with me?'

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto me, The LORD, before whom I walk, will send his angel with thee, and prosper thy way; and thou shalt take a wife for my son of my kindred, and of my father's house:
verses.nlt_text: He responded, 'The LORD, in whose presence I have lived, will send his angel with you and will make your mission successful. Yes, you must find a wife for my son from among my relatives, from my father's family.

verses.kjv_text: Then shalt thou be clear from {this} my oath, when thou comest to my kindred; and if they give not thee {one}, thou shalt be clear from my oath.
verses.nlt_text: Then you will have fulfilled your obligation. But if you go to my relatives and they refuse to let her go with you, you will be free from my oath.'

verses.kjv_text: And I came this day unto the well, and said, O LORD God of my master Abraham, if now thou do prosper my way which I go:
verses.nlt_text: "So today when I came to the spring, I prayed this prayer: 'O LORD, God of my master, Abraham, please give me success on this mission.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, I stand by the well of water; and it shall come to pass, that when the virgin cometh forth to draw {water}, and I say to her, Give me, I pray thee, a little water of thy pitcher to drink;
verses.nlt_text: See, I am standing here beside this spring. This is my request. When a young woman comes to draw water, I will say to her, "Please give me a little drink of water from your jug."

verses.kjv_text: And she say to me, Both drink thou, and I will also draw for thy camels: {let} the same {be} the woman whom the LORD hath appointed out for my master's son.
verses.nlt_text: If she says, "Yes, have a drink, and I will draw water for your camels, too," let her be the one you have selected to be the wife of my master's son.'

verses.kjv_text: And before I had done speaking in mine heart, behold, Rebekah came forth with her pitcher on her shoulder; and she went down unto the well, and drew {water}: and I said unto her, Let me drink, I pray thee.
verses.nlt_text: "Before I had finished praying in my heart, I saw Rebekah coming out with her water jug on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and drew water. So I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'

verses.kjv_text: And she made haste, and let down her pitcher from her {shoulder}, and said, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: so I drank, and she made the camels drink also.
verses.nlt_text: She quickly lowered her jug from her shoulder and said, 'Yes, have a drink, and I will water your camels, too!' So I drank, and then she watered the camels.

verses.kjv_text: And I asked her, and said, Whose daughter {art} thou? And she said, The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bare unto him: and I put the earring upon her face, and the bracelets upon her hands.
verses.nlt_text: "Then I asked, 'Whose daughter are you?' She replied, 'I am the daughter of Bethuel, and my grandparents are Nahor and Milcah.' So I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her wrists.

verses.kjv_text: And I bowed down my head, and worshipped the LORD, and blessed the LORD God of my master Abraham, which had led me in the right way to take my master's brother's daughter unto his son.
verses.nlt_text: "Then I bowed low and worshiped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master, Abraham, because he had led me straight to my master's niece to be his son's wife.

verses.kjv_text: And now if ye will deal kindly and truly with my master, tell me: and if not, tell me; that I may turn to the right hand, or to the left.
verses.nlt_text: So tell me-- will you or won't you show unfailing love and faithfulness to my master? Please tell me yes or no, and then I'll know what to do next."

verses.kjv_text: Then Laban and Bethuel answered and said, The thing proceedeth from the LORD: we cannot speak unto thee bad or good.
verses.nlt_text: Then Laban and Bethuel replied, "The LORD has obviously brought you here, so there is nothing we can say.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, Rebekah {is} before thee, take {her}, and go, and let her be thy master's son's wife, as the LORD hath spoken.
verses.nlt_text: Here is Rebekah; take her and go. Yes, let her be the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has directed."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that, when Abraham's servant heard their words, he worshipped the LORD, {bowing himself} to the earth.
verses.nlt_text: When Abraham's servant heard their answer, he bowed down to the ground and worshiped the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And the servant brought forth jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment, and gave {them} to Rebekah: he gave also to her brother and to her mother precious things. {jewels: Heb. vessels}
verses.nlt_text: Then he brought out silver and gold jewelry and clothing and presented them to Rebekah. He also gave expensive presents to her brother and mother.

verses.kjv_text: And they did eat and drink, he and the men that {were} with him, and tarried all night; and they rose up in the morning, and he said, Send me away unto my master.
verses.nlt_text: Then they ate their meal, and the servant and the men with him stayed there overnight.But early the next morning, Abraham's servant said, "Send me back to my master."

verses.kjv_text: And her brother and her mother said, Let the damsel abide with us {a few} days, at the least ten; after that she shall go. {a few...: or, a full year, or ten months}
verses.nlt_text: "But we want Rebekah to stay with us at least ten days," her brother and mother said. "Then she can go."

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, Hinder me not, seeing the LORD hath prospered my way; send me away that I may go to my master.
verses.nlt_text: But he said, "Don't delay me. The LORD has made my mission successful; now send me back so I can return to my master."

verses.kjv_text: And they said, We will call the damsel, and enquire at her mouth.
verses.nlt_text: "Well," they said, "we'll call Rebekah and ask her what she thinks."

verses.kjv_text: And they called Rebekah, and said unto her, Wilt thou go with this man? And she said, I will go.
verses.nlt_text: So they called Rebekah. "Are you willing to go with this man?" they asked her.And she replied, "Yes, I will go."

verses.kjv_text: And they sent away Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant, and his men.
verses.nlt_text: So they said good-bye to Rebekah and sent her away with Abraham's servant and his men. The woman who had been Rebekah's childhood nurse went along with her.

verses.kjv_text: And they blessed Rebekah, and said unto her, Thou {art} our sister, be thou {the mother} of thousands of millions, and let thy seed possess the gate of those which hate them.
verses.nlt_text: They gave her this blessing as she parted: "Our sister, may you become the mother of many millions! May your descendants be strong and conquer the cities of their enemies."

verses.kjv_text: And Rebekah arose, and her damsels, and they rode upon the camels, and followed the man: and the servant took Rebekah, and went his way.
verses.nlt_text: Then Rebekah and her servant girls mounted the camels and followed the man. So Abraham's servant took Rebekah and went on his way.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac came from the way of the well Lahairoi; for he dwelt in the south country.
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Isaac, whose home was in the Negev, had returned from Beer-lahai-roi.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide: and he lifted up his eyes, and saw, and, behold, the camels {were} coming. {to meditate: or, to pray}
verses.nlt_text: One evening as he was walking and meditating in the fields, he looked up and saw the camels coming.

verses.kjv_text: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she lighted off the camel.
verses.nlt_text: When Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, she quickly dismounted from her camel.

verses.kjv_text: For she {had} said unto the servant, What man {is} this that walketh in the field to meet us? And the servant {had} said, It {is} my master: therefore she took a vail, and covered herself.
verses.nlt_text: "Who is that man walking through the fields to meet us?" she asked the servant.And he replied, "It is my master." So Rebekah covered her face with her veil.

verses.kjv_text: And the servant told Isaac all things that he had done.
verses.nlt_text: Then the servant told Isaac everything he had done.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her: and Isaac was comforted after his mother's {death}.
verses.nlt_text: And Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother Sarah's tent, and she became his wife. He loved her deeply, and she was a special comfort to him after the death of his mother.

verses.kjv_text: Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name {was} Keturah.
verses.nlt_text: Abraham married another wife, whose name was Keturah.

verses.kjv_text: And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
verses.nlt_text: She gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

verses.kjv_text: And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
verses.nlt_text: Jokshan was the father of Sheba and Dedan. Dedan's descendants were the Asshurites, Letushites, and Leummites.

verses.kjv_text: And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these {were} the children of Keturah.
verses.nlt_text: Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. These were all descendants of Abraham through Keturah.

verses.kjv_text: And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac.
verses.nlt_text: Abraham gave everything he owned to his son Isaac.

verses.kjv_text: But unto the sons of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.
verses.nlt_text: But before he died, he gave gifts to the sons of his concubines and sent them off to a land in the east, away from Isaac.

verses.kjv_text: And these {are} the days of the years of Abraham's life which he lived, an hundred threescore and fifteen years.
verses.nlt_text: Abraham lived for 175 years,

verses.kjv_text: Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full {of years}; and was gathered to his people.
verses.nlt_text: and he died at a ripe old age, having lived a long and satisfying life. He breathed his last and joined his ancestors in death.

verses.kjv_text: And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which {is} before Mamre;
verses.nlt_text: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.

verses.kjv_text: The field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.
verses.nlt_text: This was the field Abraham had purchased from the Hittites and where he had buried his wife Sarah.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac dwelt by the well Lahairoi.
verses.nlt_text: After Abraham's death, God blessed his son Isaac, who settled near Beer-lahai-roi in the Negev.

verses.kjv_text: Now these {are} the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's handmaid, bare unto Abraham:
verses.nlt_text: This is the account of the family of Ishmael, the son of Abraham through Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian servant.

verses.kjv_text: And these {are} the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
verses.nlt_text: Here is a list, by their names and clans, of Ishmael's descendants: The oldest was Nebaioth, followed by Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

verses.kjv_text: And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
verses.nlt_text: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

verses.kjv_text: Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah: {Hadar: or, Hadad}
verses.nlt_text: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

verses.kjv_text: These {are} the sons of Ishmael, and these {are} their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.
verses.nlt_text: These twelve sons of Ishmael became the founders of twelve tribes named after them, listed according to the places they settled and camped.

verses.kjv_text: And these {are} the years of the life of Ishmael, an hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died; and was gathered unto his people.
verses.nlt_text: Ishmael lived for 137 years. Then he breathed his last and joined his ancestors in death.

verses.kjv_text: And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that {is} before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria: {and} he died in the presence of all his brethren. {died: Heb. fell}
verses.nlt_text: Ishmael's descendants occupied the region from Havilah to Shur, which is east of Egypt in the direction of Asshur. There they lived in open hostility toward all their relatives.

verses.kjv_text: And these {are} the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham begat Isaac:
verses.nlt_text: This is the account of the family of Isaac, the son of Abraham.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padanaram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.
verses.nlt_text: When Isaac was forty years old, he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and the sister of Laban the Aramean.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac intreated the LORD for his wife, because she {was} barren: and the LORD was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
verses.nlt_text: Isaac pleaded with the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was unable to have children. The LORD answered Isaac's prayer, and Rebekah became pregnant with twins.

verses.kjv_text: And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If {it be} so, why {am} I thus? And she went to enquire of the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: But the two children struggled with each other in her womb. So she went to ask the LORD about it. "Why is this happening to me?" she asked.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto her, Two nations {are} in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and {the one} people shall be stronger than {the other} people; and the elder shall serve the younger.
verses.nlt_text: And the LORD told her, "The sons in your womb will become two nations. From the very beginning, the two nations will be rivals. One nation will be stronger than the other; and your older son will serve your younger son."

verses.kjv_text: And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, {there were} twins in her womb.
verses.nlt_text: And when the time came to give birth, Rebekah discovered that she did indeed have twins!

verses.kjv_text: And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.
verses.nlt_text: The first one was very red at birth and covered with thick hair like a fur coat. So they named him Esau.

verses.kjv_text: And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau's heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac {was} threescore years old when she bare them.
verses.nlt_text: Then the other twin was born with his hand grasping Esau's heel. So they named him Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when the twins were born.

verses.kjv_text: And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob {was} a plain man, dwelling in tents.
verses.nlt_text: As the boys grew up, Esau became a skillful hunter. He was an outdoorsman, but Jacob had a quiet temperament, preferring to stay at home.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of {his} venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob. {he...: Heb. venison was in his mouth}
verses.nlt_text: Isaac loved Esau because he enjoyed eating the wild game Esau brought home, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he {was} faint:
verses.nlt_text: One day when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau arrived home from the wilderness exhausted and hungry.

verses.kjv_text: And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red {pottage}; for I {am} faint: therefore was his name called Edom. {with...: Heb. with that red, with that red pottage} {Edom: that is Red}
verses.nlt_text: Esau said to Jacob, "I'm starved! Give me some of that red stew!" (This is how Esau got his other name, Edom, which means "red.")

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.
verses.nlt_text: "All right," Jacob replied, "but trade me your rights as the firstborn son."

verses.kjv_text: And Esau said, Behold, I {am} at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me? {at...: Heb. going to die}
verses.nlt_text: "Look, I'm dying of starvation!" said Esau. "What good is my birthright to me now?"

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
verses.nlt_text: But Jacob said, "First you must swear that your birthright is mine." So Esau swore an oath, thereby selling all his rights as the firstborn to his brother, Jacob.

verses.kjv_text: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised {his} birthright.
verses.nlt_text: Then Jacob gave Esau some bread and lentil stew. Esau ate the meal, then got up and left. He showed contempt for his rights as the firstborn.

verses.kjv_text: And there was a famine in the land, beside the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went unto Abimelech king of the Philistines unto Gerar.
verses.nlt_text: A severe famine now struck the land, as had happened before in Abraham's time. So Isaac moved to Gerar, where Abimelech, king of the Philistines, lived.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD appeared unto him, and said, Go not down into Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall tell thee of:
verses.nlt_text: The LORD appeared to Isaac and said, "Do not go down to Egypt, but do as I tell you.

verses.kjv_text: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;
verses.nlt_text: Live here as a foreigner in this land, and I will be with you and bless you. I hereby confirm that I will give all these lands to you and your descendants, just as I solemnly promised Abraham, your father.

verses.kjv_text: And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;
verses.nlt_text: I will cause your descendants to become as numerous as the stars of the sky, and I will give them all these lands. And through your descendants all the nations of the earth will be blessed.

verses.kjv_text: Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.
verses.nlt_text: I will do this because Abraham listened to me and obeyed all my requirements, commands, decrees, and instructions."

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac dwelt in Gerar:
verses.nlt_text: So Isaac stayed in Gerar.

verses.kjv_text: And the men of the place asked {him} of his wife; and he said, She {is} my sister: for he feared to say, {She is} my wife; lest, {said he}, the men of the place should kill me for Rebekah; because she {was} fair to look upon.
verses.nlt_text: When the men who lived there asked Isaac about his wife, Rebekah, he said, "She is my sister." He was afraid to say, "She is my wife." He thought, "They will kill me to get her, because she is so beautiful."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac {was} sporting with Rebekah his wife.
verses.nlt_text: But some time later, Abimelech, king of the Philistines, looked out his window and saw Isaac caressing Rebekah.

verses.kjv_text: And Abimelech called Isaac, and said, Behold, of a surety she {is} thy wife: and how saidst thou, She {is} my sister? And Isaac said unto him, Because I said, Lest I die for her.
verses.nlt_text: Immediately, Abimelech called for Isaac and exclaimed, "She is obviously your wife! Why did you say, 'She is my sister'?" "Because I was afraid someone would kill me to get her from me," Isaac replied.

verses.kjv_text: And Abimelech said, What {is} this thou hast done unto us? one of the people might lightly have lien with thy wife, and thou shouldest have brought guiltiness upon us.
verses.nlt_text: "How could you do this to us?" Abimelech exclaimed. "One of my people might easily have taken your wife and slept with her, and you would have made us guilty of great sin."

verses.kjv_text: And Abimelech charged all {his} people, saying, He that toucheth this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.
verses.nlt_text: Then Abimelech issued a public proclamation: "Anyone who touches this man or his wife will be put to death!"

verses.kjv_text: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year an hundredfold: and the LORD blessed him. {received: Heb. found}
verses.nlt_text: When Isaac planted his crops that year, he harvested a hundred times more grain than he planted, for the LORD blessed him.

verses.kjv_text: And the man waxed great, and went forward, and grew until he became very great: {went...: Heb. went going}
verses.nlt_text: He became a very rich man, and his wealth continued to grow.

verses.kjv_text: For he had possession of flocks, and possession of herds, and great store of servants: and the Philistines envied him. {servants: or, husbandry}
verses.nlt_text: He acquired so many flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and servants that the Philistines became jealous of him.

verses.kjv_text: For all the wells which his father's servants had digged in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped them, and filled them with earth.
verses.nlt_text: So the Philistines filled up all of Isaac's wells with dirt. These were the wells that had been dug by the servants of his father, Abraham.

verses.kjv_text: And Abimelech said unto Isaac, Go from us; for thou art much mightier than we.
verses.nlt_text: Finally, Abimelech ordered Isaac to leave the country. "Go somewhere else," he said, "for you have become too powerful for us."

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac departed thence, and pitched his tent in the valley of Gerar, and dwelt there.
verses.nlt_text: So Isaac moved away to the Gerar Valley, where he set up their tents and settled down.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac digged again the wells of water, which they had digged in the days of Abraham his father; for the Philistines had stopped them after the death of Abraham: and he called their names after the names by which his father had called them.
verses.nlt_text: He reopened the wells his father had dug, which the Philistines had filled in after Abraham's death. Isaac also restored the names Abraham had given them.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac's servants digged in the valley, and found there a well of springing water. {springing: Heb. living}
verses.nlt_text: Isaac's servants also dug in the Gerar Valley and discovered a well of fresh water.

verses.kjv_text: And the herdmen of Gerar did strive with Isaac's herdmen, saying, The water {is} ours: and he called the name of the well Esek; because they strove with him. {Esek: that is, Contention}
verses.nlt_text: But then the shepherds from Gerar came and claimed the spring. "This is our water," they said, and they argued over it with Isaac's herdsmen. So Isaac named the well Esek (which means "argument").

verses.kjv_text: And they digged another well, and strove for that also: and he called the name of it Sitnah. {Sitnah: that is, Hatred}
verses.nlt_text: Isaac's men then dug another well, but again there was a dispute over it. So Isaac named it Sitnah (which means "hostility").

verses.kjv_text: And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For now the LORD hath made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land. {Rehoboth: that is Room}
verses.nlt_text: Abandoning that one, Isaac moved on and dug another well. This time there was no dispute over it, so Isaac named the place Rehoboth (which means "open space"), for he said, "At last the LORD has created enough space for us to prosper in this land."

verses.kjv_text: And he went up from thence to Beersheba.
verses.nlt_text: From there Isaac moved to Beersheba,

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD appeared unto him the same night, and said, I {am} the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I {am} with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham's sake.
verses.nlt_text: where the LORD appeared to him on the night of his arrival. "I am the God of your father, Abraham," he said. "Do not be afraid, for I am with you and will bless you. I will multiply your descendants, and they will become a great nation. I will do this because of my promise to Abraham, my servant."

verses.kjv_text: And he builded an altar there, and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there: and there Isaac's servants digged a well.
verses.nlt_text: Then Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the LORD. He set up his camp at that place, and his servants dug another well.

verses.kjv_text: Then Abimelech went to him from Gerar, and Ahuzzath one of his friends, and Phichol the chief captain of his army.
verses.nlt_text: One day King Abimelech came from Gerar with his adviser, Ahuzzath, and also Phicol, his army commander.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac said unto them, Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me, and have sent me away from you?
verses.nlt_text: "Why have you come here?" Isaac asked. "You obviously hate me, since you kicked me off your land."

verses.kjv_text: And they said, We saw certainly that the LORD was with thee: and we said, Let there be now an oath betwixt us, {even} betwixt us and thee, and let us make a covenant with thee; {We saw...: Heb. Seeing we saw}
verses.nlt_text: They replied, "We can plainly see that the LORD is with you. So we want to enter into a sworn treaty with you. Let's make a covenant.

verses.kjv_text: That thou wilt do us no hurt, as we have not touched thee, and as we have done unto thee nothing but good, and have sent thee away in peace: thou {art} now the blessed of the LORD. {That...: Heb. If thou shalt}
verses.nlt_text: Swear that you will not harm us, just as we have never troubled you. We have always treated you well, and we sent you away from us in peace. And now look how the LORD has blessed you!"

verses.kjv_text: And he made them a feast, and they did eat and drink.
verses.nlt_text: So Isaac prepared a covenant feast to celebrate the treaty, and they ate and drank together.

verses.kjv_text: And they rose up betimes in the morning, and sware one to another: and Isaac sent them away, and they departed from him in peace.
verses.nlt_text: Early the next morning, they each took a solemn oath not to interfere with each other. Then Isaac sent them home again, and they left him in peace.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass the same day, that Isaac's servants came, and told him concerning the well which they had digged, and said unto him, We have found water.
verses.nlt_text: That very day Isaac's servants came and told him about a new well they had dug. "We've found water!" they exclaimed.

verses.kjv_text: And he called it Shebah: therefore the name of the city {is} Beersheba unto this day. {Shebah: That is, an oath} {Beersheba: that is, the well of the oath}
verses.nlt_text: So Isaac named the well Shibah (which means "oath"). And to this day the town that grew up there is called Beersheba (which means "well of the oath").

verses.kjv_text: And Esau was forty years old when he took to wife Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite:
verses.nlt_text: At the age of forty, Esau married two Hittite wives: Judith, the daughter of Beeri, and Basemath, the daughter of Elon.

verses.kjv_text: Which were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. {a grief...: Heb. bitterness of spirit}
verses.nlt_text: But Esau's wives made life miserable for Isaac and Rebekah.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his eldest son, and said unto him, My son: and he said unto him, Behold, {here am} I.
verses.nlt_text: One day when Isaac was old and turning blind, he called for Esau, his older son, and said, "My son." "Yes, Father?" Esau replied.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Behold now, I am old, I know not the day of my death:
verses.nlt_text: "I am an old man now," Isaac said, "and I don't know when I may die.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore take, I pray thee, thy weapons, thy quiver and thy bow, and go out to the field, and take me {some} venison; {take: Heb. hunt}
verses.nlt_text: Take your bow and a quiver full of arrows, and go out into the open country to hunt some wild game for me.

verses.kjv_text: And make me savoury meat, such as I love, and bring {it} to me, that I may eat; that my soul may bless thee before I die.
verses.nlt_text: Prepare my favorite dish, and bring it here for me to eat. Then I will pronounce the blessing that belongs to you, my firstborn son, before I die."

verses.kjv_text: And Rebekah heard when Isaac spake to Esau his son. And Esau went to the field to hunt {for} venison, {and} to bring {it}.
verses.nlt_text: But Rebekah overheard what Isaac had said to his son Esau. So when Esau left to hunt for the wild game,

verses.kjv_text: And Rebekah spake unto Jacob her son, saying, Behold, I heard thy father speak unto Esau thy brother, saying,
verses.nlt_text: she said to her son Jacob, "Listen. I overheard your father say to Esau,

verses.kjv_text: Bring me venison, and make me savoury meat, that I may eat, and bless thee before the LORD before my death.
verses.nlt_text: 'Bring me some wild game and prepare me a delicious meal. Then I will bless you in the LORD's presence before I die.'

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice according to that which I command thee.
verses.nlt_text: Now, my son, listen to me. Do exactly as I tell you.

verses.kjv_text: Go now to the flock, and fetch me from thence two good kids of the goats; and I will make them savoury meat for thy father, such as he loveth:
verses.nlt_text: Go out to the flocks, and bring me two fine young goats. I'll use them to prepare your father's favorite dish.

verses.kjv_text: And thou shalt bring {it} to thy father, that he may eat, and that he may bless thee before his death.
verses.nlt_text: Then take the food to your father so he can eat it and bless you before he dies."

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, Behold, Esau my brother {is} a hairy man, and I {am} a smooth man:
verses.nlt_text: "But look," Jacob replied to Rebekah, "my brother, Esau, is a hairy man, and my skin is smooth.

verses.kjv_text: My father peradventure will feel me, and I shall seem to him as a deceiver; and I shall bring a curse upon me, and not a blessing.
verses.nlt_text: What if my father touches me? He'll see that I'm trying to trick him, and then he'll curse me instead of blessing me."

verses.kjv_text: And his mother said unto him, Upon me {be} thy curse, my son: only obey my voice, and go fetch me {them}.
verses.nlt_text: But his mother replied, "Then let the curse fall on me, my son! Just do what I tell you. Go out and get the goats for me!"

verses.kjv_text: And he went, and fetched, and brought {them} to his mother: and his mother made savoury meat, such as his father loved.
verses.nlt_text: So Jacob went out and got the young goats for his mother. Rebekah took them and prepared a delicious meal, just the way Isaac liked it.

verses.kjv_text: And Rebekah took goodly raiment of her eldest son Esau, which {were} with her in the house, and put them upon Jacob her younger son: {goodly: Heb. desirable}
verses.nlt_text: Then she took Esau's favorite clothes, which were there in the house, and gave them to her younger son, Jacob.

verses.kjv_text: And she put the skins of the kids of the goats upon his hands, and upon the smooth of his neck:
verses.nlt_text: She covered his arms and the smooth part of his neck with the skin of the young goats.

verses.kjv_text: And she gave the savoury meat and the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Jacob.
verses.nlt_text: Then she gave Jacob the delicious meal, including freshly baked bread.

verses.kjv_text: And he came unto his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here {am} I; who {art} thou, my son?
verses.nlt_text: So Jacob took the food to his father. "My father?" he said."Yes, my son," Isaac answered. "Who are you-- Esau or Jacob?"

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob said unto his father, I {am} Esau thy firstborn; I have done according as thou badest me: arise, I pray thee, sit and eat of my venison, that thy soul may bless me.
verses.nlt_text: Jacob replied, "It's Esau, your firstborn son. I've done as you told me. Here is the wild game. Now sit up and eat it so you can give me your blessing."

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac said unto his son, How {is it} that thou hast found {it} so quickly, my son? And he said, Because the LORD thy God brought {it} to me. {to me: Heb. before me}
verses.nlt_text: Isaac asked, "How did you find it so quickly, my son?" "The LORD your God put it in my path!" Jacob replied.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac said unto Jacob, Come near, I pray thee, that I may feel thee, my son, whether thou {be} my very son Esau or not.
verses.nlt_text: Then Isaac said to Jacob, "Come closer so I can touch you and make sure that you really are Esau."

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob went near unto Isaac his father; and he felt him, and said, The voice {is} Jacob's voice, but the hands {are} the hands of Esau.
verses.nlt_text: So Jacob went closer to his father, and Isaac touched him. "The voice is Jacob's, but the hands are Esau's," Isaac said.

verses.kjv_text: And he discerned him not, because his hands were hairy, as his brother Esau's hands: so he blessed him.
verses.nlt_text: But he did not recognize Jacob, because Jacob's hands felt hairy just like Esau's. So Isaac prepared to bless Jacob.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, {Art} thou my very son Esau? And he said, I {am}.
verses.nlt_text: "But are you really my son Esau?" he asked."Yes, I am," Jacob replied.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Bring {it} near to me, and I will eat of my son's venison, that my soul may bless thee. And he brought {it} near to him, and he did eat: and he brought him wine, and he drank.
verses.nlt_text: Then Isaac said, "Now, my son, bring me the wild game. Let me eat it, and then I will give you my blessing." So Jacob took the food to his father, and Isaac ate it. He also drank the wine that Jacob served him. Then Isaac said to Jacob,

verses.kjv_text: And his father Isaac said unto him, Come near now, and kiss me, my son.
verses.nlt_text: "Please come a little closer and kiss me, my son."

verses.kjv_text: And he came near, and kissed him: and he smelled the smell of his raiment, and blessed him, and said, See, the smell of my son {is} as the smell of a field which the LORD hath blessed:
verses.nlt_text: So Jacob went over and kissed him. And when Isaac caught the smell of his clothes, he was finally convinced, and he blessed his son. He said, "Ah! The smell of my son is like the smell of the outdoors, which the LORD has blessed!

verses.kjv_text: Therefore God give thee of the dew of heaven, and the fatness of the earth, and plenty of corn and wine:
verses.nlt_text: "From the dew of heaven and the richness of the earth, may God always give you abundant harvests of grain and bountiful new wine.

verses.kjv_text: Let people serve thee, and nations bow down to thee: be lord over thy brethren, and let thy mother's sons bow down to thee: cursed {be} every one that curseth thee, and blessed {be} he that blesseth thee.
verses.nlt_text: May many nations become your servants, and may they bow down to you. May you be the master over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. All who curse you will be cursed, and all who bless you will be blessed."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as soon as Isaac had made an end of blessing Jacob, and Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac his father, that Esau his brother came in from his hunting.
verses.nlt_text: As soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and almost before Jacob had left his father, Esau returned from his hunt.

verses.kjv_text: And he also had made savoury meat, and brought it unto his father, and said unto his father, Let my father arise, and eat of his son's venison, that thy soul may bless me.
verses.nlt_text: Esau prepared a delicious meal and brought it to his father. Then he said, "Sit up, my father, and eat my wild game so you can give me your blessing."

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac his father said unto him, Who {art} thou? And he said, I {am} thy son, thy firstborn Esau.
verses.nlt_text: But Isaac asked him, "Who are you?" Esau replied, "It's your son, your firstborn son, Esau."

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac trembled very exceedingly, and said, Who? where {is} he that hath taken venison, and brought {it} me, and I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him? yea, {and} he shall be blessed. {trembled...: Heb. trembled with a great trembling greatly} {taken: Heb. hunted}
verses.nlt_text: Isaac began to tremble uncontrollably and said, "Then who just served me wild game? I have already eaten it, and I blessed him just before you came. And yes, that blessing must stand!"

verses.kjv_text: And when Esau heard the words of his father, he cried with a great and exceeding bitter cry, and said unto his father, Bless me, {even} me also, O my father.
verses.nlt_text: When Esau heard his father's words, he let out a loud and bitter cry. "Oh my father, what about me? Bless me, too!" he begged.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Thy brother came with subtilty, and hath taken away thy blessing.
verses.nlt_text: But Isaac said, "Your brother was here, and he tricked me. He has taken away your blessing."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me? {Jacob: that is, A supplanter}
verses.nlt_text: Esau exclaimed, "No wonder his name is Jacob, for now he has cheated me twice. First he took my rights as the firstborn, and now he has stolen my blessing. Oh, haven't you saved even one blessing for me?"

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac answered and said unto Esau, Behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants; and with corn and wine have I sustained him: and what shall I do now unto thee, my son? {sustained: or, supported}
verses.nlt_text: Isaac said to Esau, "I have made Jacob your master and have declared that all his brothers will be his servants. I have guaranteed him an abundance of grain and wine-- what is left for me to give you, my son?"

verses.kjv_text: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, {even} me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.
verses.nlt_text: Esau pleaded, "But do you have only one blessing? Oh my father, bless me, too!" Then Esau broke down and wept.

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; {the fatness: or, of the fatness}
verses.nlt_text: Finally, his father, Isaac, said to him, "You will live away from the richness of the earth, and away from the dew of the heaven above.

verses.kjv_text: And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother; and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck.
verses.nlt_text: You will live by your sword, and you will serve your brother. But when you decide to break free, you will shake his yoke from your neck."

verses.kjv_text: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
verses.nlt_text: From that time on, Esau hated Jacob because their father had given Jacob the blessing. And Esau began to scheme: "I will soon be mourning my father's death. Then I will kill my brother, Jacob."

verses.kjv_text: And these words of Esau her elder son were told to Rebekah: and she sent and called Jacob her younger son, and said unto him, Behold, thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, {purposing} to kill thee.
verses.nlt_text: But Rebekah heard about Esau's plans. So she sent for Jacob and told him, "Listen, Esau is consoling himself by plotting to kill you.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore, my son, obey my voice; and arise, flee thou to Laban my brother to Haran;
verses.nlt_text: So listen carefully, my son. Get ready and flee to my brother, Laban, in Haran.

verses.kjv_text: And tarry with him a few days, until thy brother's fury turn away;
verses.nlt_text: Stay there with him until your brother cools off.

verses.kjv_text: Until thy brother's anger turn away from thee, and he forget {that} which thou hast done to him: then I will send, and fetch thee from thence: why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?
verses.nlt_text: When he calms down and forgets what you have done to him, I will send for you to come back. Why should I lose both of you in one day?"

verses.kjv_text: And Rebekah said to Isaac, I am weary of my life because of the daughters of Heth: if Jacob take a wife of the daughters of Heth, such as these {which are} of the daughters of the land, what good shall my life do me?
verses.nlt_text: Then Rebekah said to Isaac, "I'm sick and tired of these local Hittite women! I would rather die than see Jacob marry one of them."

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.
verses.nlt_text: So Isaac called for Jacob, blessed him, and said, "You must not marry any of these Canaanite women.

verses.kjv_text: Arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father; and take thee a wife from thence of the daughters of Laban thy mother's brother.
verses.nlt_text: Instead, go at once to Paddan-aram, to the house of your grandfather Bethuel, and marry one of your uncle Laban's daughters.

verses.kjv_text: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a multitude of people; {a multitude...: Heb. an assembly of people}
verses.nlt_text: May God Almighty bless you and give you many children. And may your descendants multiply and become many nations!

verses.kjv_text: And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land wherein thou art a stranger, which God gave unto Abraham. {wherein...: Heb. of thy sojournings}
verses.nlt_text: May God pass on to you and your descendants the blessings he promised to Abraham. May you own this land where you are now living as a foreigner, for God gave this land to Abraham."

verses.kjv_text: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padanaram unto Laban, son of Bethuel the Syrian, the brother of Rebekah, Jacob's and Esau's mother.
verses.nlt_text: So Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-aram to stay with his uncle Laban, his mother's brother, the son of Bethuel the Aramean.

verses.kjv_text: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padanaram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan;
verses.nlt_text: Esau knew that his father, Isaac, had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to find a wife, and that he had warned Jacob, "You must not marry a Canaanite woman."

verses.kjv_text: And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padanaram;
verses.nlt_text: He also knew that Jacob had obeyed his parents and gone to Paddan-aram.

verses.kjv_text: And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father; {pleased...: Heb. were evil in the eyes, etc}
verses.nlt_text: It was now very clear to Esau that his father did not like the local Canaanite women.

verses.kjv_text: Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife. {Mahalath: or, Bashemath}
verses.nlt_text: So Esau visited his uncle Ishmael's family and married one of Ishmael's daughters, in addition to the wives he already had. His new wife's name was Mahalath. She was the sister of Nebaioth and the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran. {Haran: Gr. Charran}
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Jacob left Beersheba and traveled toward Haran.

verses.kjv_text: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put {them for} his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.
verses.nlt_text: At sundown he arrived at a good place to set up camp and stopped there for the night. Jacob found a stone to rest his head against and lay down to sleep.

verses.kjv_text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth, and the top of it reached to heaven: and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
verses.nlt_text: As he slept, he dreamed of a stairway that reached from the earth up to heaven. And he saw the angels of God going up and down the stairway.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said, I {am} the LORD God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;
verses.nlt_text: At the top of the stairway stood the LORD, and he said, "I am the LORD, the God of your grandfather Abraham, and the God of your father, Isaac. The ground you are lying on belongs to you. I am giving it to you and your descendants.

verses.kjv_text: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south: and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed. {spread...: Heb. break forth}
verses.nlt_text: Your descendants will be as numerous as the dust of the earth! They will spread out in all directions-- to the west and the east, to the north and the south. And all the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your descendants.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, I {am} with thee, and will keep thee in all {places} whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done {that} which I have spoken to thee of.
verses.nlt_text: What's more, I am with you, and I will protect you wherever you go. One day I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have finished giving you everything I have promised you."

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew {it} not.
verses.nlt_text: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, "Surely the LORD is in this place, and I wasn't even aware of it!"

verses.kjv_text: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful {is} this place! this {is} none other but the house of God, and this {is} the gate of heaven.
verses.nlt_text: But he was also afraid and said, "What an awesome place this is! It is none other than the house of God, the very gateway to heaven!"

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put {for} his pillows, and set it up {for} a pillar, and poured oil upon the top of it.
verses.nlt_text: The next morning Jacob got up very early. He took the stone he had rested his head against, and he set it upright as a memorial pillar. Then he poured olive oil over it.

verses.kjv_text: And he called the name of that place Bethel: but the name of that city {was called} Luz at the first. {Bethel: that is, The house of God}
verses.nlt_text: He named that place Bethel (which means "house of God"), although the name of the nearby village was Luz.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on,
verses.nlt_text: Then Jacob made this vow: "If God will indeed be with me and protect me on this journey, and if he will provide me with food and clothing,

verses.kjv_text: So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:
verses.nlt_text: and if I return safely to my father's home, then the LORD will certainly be my God.

verses.kjv_text: And this stone, which I have set {for} a pillar, shall be God's house: and of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: And this memorial pillar I have set up will become a place for worshiping God, and I will present to God a tenth of everything he gives me."

verses.kjv_text: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east. {went...: Heb. lift up his feet} {people: Heb. children}
verses.nlt_text: Then Jacob hurried on, finally arriving in the land of the east.

verses.kjv_text: And he looked, and behold a well in the field, and, lo, there {were} three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks: and a great stone {was} upon the well's mouth.
verses.nlt_text: He saw a well in the distance. Three flocks of sheep and goats lay in an open field beside it, waiting to be watered. But a heavy stone covered the mouth of the well.

verses.kjv_text: And thither were all the flocks gathered: and they rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again upon the well's mouth in his place.
verses.nlt_text: It was the custom there to wait for all the flocks to arrive before removing the stone and watering the animals. Afterward the stone would be placed back over the mouth of the well.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, whence {be} ye? And they said, Of Haran {are} we.
verses.nlt_text: Jacob went over to the shepherds and asked, "Where are you from, my friends?" "We are from Haran," they answered.

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor? And they said, We know {him}.
verses.nlt_text: "Do you know a man there named Laban, the grandson of Nahor?" he asked."Yes, we do," they replied.

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, {Is} he well? And they said, {He is} well: and, behold, Rachel his daughter cometh with the sheep. {Is he...: Heb. Is there peace to him?}
verses.nlt_text: "Is he doing well?" Jacob asked."Yes, he's well," they answered. "Look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the flock now."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Lo, {it is} yet high day, neither {is it} time that the cattle should be gathered together: water ye the sheep, and go {and} feed {them}. {it is...: Heb. yet the day is great}
verses.nlt_text: Jacob said, "Look, it's still broad daylight-- too early to round up the animals. Why don't you water the sheep and goats so they can get back out to pasture?"

verses.kjv_text: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together, and {till} they roll the stone from the well's mouth; then we water the sheep.
verses.nlt_text: "We can't water the animals until all the flocks have arrived," they replied. "Then the shepherds move the stone from the mouth of the well, and we water all the sheep and goats."

verses.kjv_text: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep: for she kept them.
verses.nlt_text: Jacob was still talking with them when Rachel arrived with her father's flock, for she was a shepherd.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, that Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well's mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
verses.nlt_text: And because Rachel was his cousin-- the daughter of Laban, his mother's brother-- and because the sheep and goats belonged to his uncle Laban, Jacob went over to the well and moved the stone from its mouth and watered his uncle's flock.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
verses.nlt_text: Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and he wept aloud.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob told Rachel that he {was} her father's brother, and that he {was} Rebekah's son: and she ran and told her father.
verses.nlt_text: He explained to Rachel that he was her cousin on her father's side-- the son of her aunt Rebekah. So Rachel quickly ran and told her father, Laban.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob his sister's son, that he ran to meet him, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things. {tidings: Heb. hearing}
verses.nlt_text: As soon as Laban heard that his nephew Jacob had arrived, he ran out to meet him. He embraced and kissed him and brought him home. When Jacob had told him his story,

verses.kjv_text: And Laban said to him, Surely thou {art} my bone and my flesh. And he abode with him the space of a month. {the space...: Heb. a month of days}
verses.nlt_text: Laban exclaimed, "You really are my own flesh and blood!" After Jacob had stayed with Laban for about a month,

verses.kjv_text: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou {art} my brother, shouldest thou therefore serve me for nought? tell me, what {shall} thy wages {be}?
verses.nlt_text: Laban said to him, "You shouldn't work for me without pay just because we are relatives. Tell me how much your wages should be."

verses.kjv_text: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder {was} Leah, and the name of the younger {was} Rachel.
verses.nlt_text: Now Laban had two daughters. The older daughter was named Leah, and the younger one was Rachel.

verses.kjv_text: Leah {was} tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.
verses.nlt_text: There was no sparkle in Leah's eyes, but Rachel had a beautiful figure and a lovely face.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.
verses.nlt_text: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he told her father, "I'll work for you for seven years if you'll give me Rachel, your younger daughter, as my wife."

verses.kjv_text: And Laban said, {It is} better that I give her to thee, than that I should give her to another man: abide with me.
verses.nlt_text: "Agreed!" Laban replied. "I'd rather give her to you than to anyone else. Stay and work with me."

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him {but} a few days, for the love he had to her.
verses.nlt_text: So Jacob worked seven years to pay for Rachel. But his love for her was so strong that it seemed to him but a few days.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give {me} my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.
verses.nlt_text: Finally, the time came for him to marry her. "I have fulfilled my agreement," Jacob said to Laban. "Now give me my wife so I can marry her."

verses.kjv_text: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
verses.nlt_text: So Laban invited everyone in the neighborhood and prepared a wedding feast.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.
verses.nlt_text: But that night, when it was dark, Laban took Leah to Jacob, and he slept with her.

verses.kjv_text: And Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid {for} an handmaid.
verses.nlt_text: (Laban had given Leah a servant, Zilpah, to be her maid.)

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it {was} Leah: and he said to Laban, What {is} this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?
