verses.kjv_text: And Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told {it} his brethren: and they hated him yet the more.
verses.nlt_text: One night Joseph had a dream, and when he told his brothers about it, they hated him more than ever.

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, Hear, I pray you, this dream which I have dreamed:
verses.nlt_text: "Listen to this dream," he said.

verses.kjv_text: For, behold, we {were} binding sheaves in the field, and, lo, my sheaf arose, and also stood upright; and, behold, your sheaves stood round about, and made obeisance to my sheaf.
verses.nlt_text: "We were out in the field, tying up bundles of grain. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles all gathered around and bowed low before mine!"

verses.kjv_text: And his brethren said to him, Shalt thou indeed reign over us? or shalt thou indeed have dominion over us? And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.
verses.nlt_text: His brothers responded, "So you think you will be our king, do you? Do you actually think you will reign over us?" And they hated him all the more because of his dreams and the way he talked about them.

verses.kjv_text: And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.
verses.nlt_text: Soon Joseph had another dream, and again he told his brothers about it. "Listen, I have had another dream," he said. "The sun, moon, and eleven stars bowed low before me!"

verses.kjv_text: And he told {it} to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What {is} this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth?
verses.nlt_text: This time he told the dream to his father as well as to his brothers, but his father scolded him. "What kind of dream is that?" he asked. "Will your mother and I and your brothers actually come and bow to the ground before you?"

verses.kjv_text: And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.
verses.nlt_text: But while his brothers were jealous of Joseph, his father wondered what the dreams meant.

verses.kjv_text: And his brethren went to feed their father's flock in Shechem.
verses.nlt_text: Soon after this, Joseph's brothers went to pasture their father's flocks at Shechem.

verses.kjv_text: And Israel said unto Joseph, Do not thy brethren feed {the flock} in Shechem? come, and I will send thee unto them. And he said to him, Here {am I}.
verses.nlt_text: When they had been gone for some time, Jacob said to Joseph, "Your brothers are pasturing the sheep at Shechem. Get ready, and I will send you to them." "I'm ready to go," Joseph replied.

verses.kjv_text: And he said to him, Go, I pray thee, see whether it be well with thy brethren, and well with the flocks; and bring me word again. So he sent him out of the vale of Hebron, and he came to Shechem. {see...: Heb. see the peace of thy brethren, etc.}
verses.nlt_text: "Go and see how your brothers and the flocks are getting along," Jacob said. "Then come back and bring me a report." So Jacob sent him on his way, and Joseph traveled to Shechem from their home in the valley of Hebron.

verses.kjv_text: And a certain man found him, and, behold, {he was} wandering in the field: and the man asked him, saying, What seekest thou?
verses.nlt_text: When he arrived there, a man from the area noticed him wandering around the countryside. "What are you looking for?" he asked.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, I seek my brethren: tell me, I pray thee, where they feed {their flocks}.
verses.nlt_text: "I'm looking for my brothers," Joseph replied. "Do you know where they are pasturing their sheep?"

verses.kjv_text: And the man said, They are departed hence; for I heard them say, Let us go to Dothan. And Joseph went after his brethren, and found them in Dothan.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes," the man told him. "They have moved on from here, but I heard them say, 'Let's go on to Dothan.' " So Joseph followed his brothers to Dothan and found them there.

verses.kjv_text: And when they saw him afar off, even before he came near unto them, they conspired against him to slay him.
verses.nlt_text: When Joseph's brothers saw him coming, they recognized him in the distance. As he approached, they made plans to kill him.

verses.kjv_text: And they said one to another, Behold, this dreamer cometh. {dreamer: Heb. master of dreams}
verses.nlt_text: "Here comes the dreamer!" they said.

verses.kjv_text: Come now therefore, and let us slay him, and cast him into some pit, and we will say, Some evil beast hath devoured him: and we shall see what will become of his dreams.
verses.nlt_text: "Come on, let's kill him and throw him into one of these cisterns. We can tell our father, 'A wild animal has eaten him.' Then we'll see what becomes of his dreams!"

verses.kjv_text: And Reuben heard {it}, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him.
verses.nlt_text: But when Reuben heard of their scheme, he came to Joseph's rescue. "Let's not kill him," he said.

verses.kjv_text: And Reuben said unto them, Shed no blood, {but} cast him into this pit that {is} in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might rid him out of their hands, to deliver him to his father again.
verses.nlt_text: "Why should we shed any blood? Let's just throw him into this empty cistern here in the wilderness. Then he'll die without our laying a hand on him." Reuben was secretly planning to rescue Joseph and return him to his father.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph out of his coat, {his} coat of {many} colours that {was} on him; {colours: or, pieces}
verses.nlt_text: So when Joseph arrived, his brothers ripped off the beautiful robe he was wearing.

verses.kjv_text: And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit {was} empty, {there was} no water in it.
verses.nlt_text: Then they grabbed him and threw him into the cistern. Now the cistern was empty; there was no water in it.

verses.kjv_text: And they sat down to eat bread: and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and, behold, a company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead with their camels bearing spicery and balm and myrrh, going to carry {it} down to Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: Then, just as they were sitting down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of camels in the distance coming toward them. It was a group of Ishmaelite traders taking a load of gum, balm, and aromatic resin from Gilead down to Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And Judah said unto his brethren, What profit {is it} if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?
verses.nlt_text: Judah said to his brothers, "What will we gain by killing our brother? His blood would just give us a guilty conscience.

verses.kjv_text: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he {is} our brother {and} our flesh. And his brethren were content. {were...: Heb. hearkened}
verses.nlt_text: Instead of hurting him, let's sell him to those Ishmaelite traders. After all, he is our brother-- our own flesh and blood!" And his brothers agreed.

verses.kjv_text: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty {pieces} of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: So when the Ishmaelites, who were Midianite traders, came by, Joseph's brothers pulled him out of the cistern and sold him to them for twenty pieces of silver. And the traders took him to Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And Reuben returned unto the pit; and, behold, Joseph {was} not in the pit; and he rent his clothes.
verses.nlt_text: Some time later, Reuben returned to get Joseph out of the cistern. When he discovered that Joseph was missing, he tore his clothes in grief.

verses.kjv_text: And he returned unto his brethren, and said, The child {is} not; and I, whither shall I go?
verses.nlt_text: Then he went back to his brothers and lamented, "The boy is gone! What will I do now?"

verses.kjv_text: And they took Joseph's coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood;
verses.nlt_text: Then the brothers killed a young goat and dipped Joseph's robe in its blood.

verses.kjv_text: And they sent the coat of {many} colours, and they brought {it} to their father; and said, This have we found: know now whether it {be} thy son's coat or no.
verses.nlt_text: They sent the beautiful robe to their father with this message: "Look at what we found. Doesn't this robe belong to your son?"

verses.kjv_text: And he knew it, and said, {It is} my son's coat; an evil beast hath devoured him; Joseph is without doubt rent in pieces.
verses.nlt_text: Their father recognized it immediately. "Yes," he said, "it is my son's robe. A wild animal must have eaten him. Joseph has clearly been torn to pieces!"

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
verses.nlt_text: Then Jacob tore his clothes and dressed himself in burlap. He mourned deeply for his son for a long time.

verses.kjv_text: And all his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him; but he refused to be comforted; and he said, For I will go down into the grave unto my son mourning. Thus his father wept for him.
verses.nlt_text: His family all tried to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. "I will go to my grave mourning for my son," he would say, and then he would weep.

verses.kjv_text: And the Midianites sold him into Egypt unto Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh's, {and} captain of the guard. {officer: Heb. eunuch: but the word doth signify not only eunuchs, but also chamberlains, courtiers, and officers} {captain...: or, chief marshal: Heb. chief of the slaughter men, or executioners}
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, the Midianite traders arrived in Egypt, where they sold Joseph to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Potiphar was captain of the palace guard.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass at that time, that Judah went down from his brethren, and turned in to a certain Adullamite, whose name {was} Hirah.
verses.nlt_text: About this time, Judah left home and moved to Adullam, where he stayed with a man named Hirah.

verses.kjv_text: And Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite, whose name {was} Shuah; and he took her, and went in unto her.
verses.nlt_text: There he saw a Canaanite woman, the daughter of Shua, and he married her. When he slept with her,

verses.kjv_text: And she conceived, and bare a son; and he called his name Er.
verses.nlt_text: she became pregnant and gave birth to a son, and he named the boy Er.

verses.kjv_text: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and she called his name Onan.
verses.nlt_text: Then she became pregnant again and gave birth to another son, and she named him Onan.

verses.kjv_text: And she yet again conceived, and bare a son; and called his name Shelah: and he was at Chezib, when she bare him.
verses.nlt_text: And when she gave birth to a third son, she named him Shelah. At the time of Shelah's birth, they were living at Kezib.

verses.kjv_text: And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, whose name {was} Tamar.
verses.nlt_text: In the course of time, Judah arranged for his firstborn son, Er, to marry a young woman named Tamar.

verses.kjv_text: And Er, Judah's firstborn, was wicked in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD slew him.
verses.nlt_text: But Er was a wicked man in the LORD's sight, so the LORD took his life.

verses.kjv_text: And Judah said unto Onan, Go in unto thy brother's wife, and marry her, and raise up seed to thy brother.
verses.nlt_text: Then Judah said to Er's brother Onan, "Go and marry Tamar, as our law requires of the brother of a man who has died. You must produce an heir for your brother."

verses.kjv_text: And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled {it} on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.
verses.nlt_text: But Onan was not willing to have a child who would not be his own heir. So whenever he had intercourse with his brother's wife, he spilled the semen on the ground. This prevented her from having a child who would belong to his brother.

verses.kjv_text: And the thing which he did displeased the LORD: wherefore he slew him also. {displeased...: Heb. was evil in the eyes of the Lord}
verses.nlt_text: But the LORD considered it evil for Onan to deny a child to his dead brother. So the LORD took Onan's life, too.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Judah to Tamar his daughter in law, Remain a widow at thy father's house, till Shelah my son be grown: for he said, Lest peradventure he die also, as his brethren {did}. And Tamar went and dwelt in her father's house.
verses.nlt_text: Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, "Go back to your parents' home and remain a widow until my son Shelah is old enough to marry you." (But Judah didn't really intend to do this because he was afraid Shelah would also die, like his two brothers.) So Tamar went back to live in her father's home.

verses.kjv_text: And in process of time the daughter of Shuah Judah's wife died; and Judah was comforted, and went up unto his sheepshearers to Timnath, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite. {in process...: Heb. the days were multiplied}
verses.nlt_text: Some years later Judah's wife died. After the time of mourning was over, Judah and his friend Hirah the Adullamite went up to Timnah to supervise the shearing of his sheep.

verses.kjv_text: And it was told Tamar, saying, Behold thy father in law goeth up to Timnath to shear his sheep.
verses.nlt_text: Someone told Tamar, "Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep."

verses.kjv_text: And she put her widow's garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which {is} by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife. {an open...: Heb. the door of eyes, or, of Enajim}
verses.nlt_text: Tamar was aware that Shelah had grown up, but no arrangements had been made for her to come and marry him. So she changed out of her widow's clothing and covered herself with a veil to disguise herself. Then she sat beside the road at the entrance to the village of Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah.

verses.kjv_text: When Judah saw her, he thought her {to be} an harlot; because she had covered her face.
verses.nlt_text: Judah noticed her and thought she was a prostitute, since she had covered her face.

verses.kjv_text: And he turned unto her by the way, and said, Go to, I pray thee, let me come in unto thee; (for he knew not that she {was} his daughter in law.) And she said, What wilt thou give me, that thou mayest come in unto me?
verses.nlt_text: So he stopped and propositioned her. "Let me have sex with you," he said, not realizing that she was his own daughter-in-law."How much will you pay to have sex with me?" Tamar asked.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, I will send {thee} a kid from the flock. And she said, Wilt thou give {me} a pledge, till thou send {it}? {a kid: Heb. a kid of the goats}
verses.nlt_text: "I'll send you a young goat from my flock," Judah promised."But what will you give me to guarantee that you will send the goat?" she asked.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that {is} in thine hand. And he gave {it} her, and came in unto her, and she conceived by him.
verses.nlt_text: "What kind of guarantee do you want?" he replied.She answered, "Leave me your identification seal and its cord and the walking stick you are carrying." So Judah gave them to her. Then he had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant.

verses.kjv_text: And she arose, and went away, and laid by her vail from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.
verses.nlt_text: Afterward she went back home, took off her veil, and put on her widow's clothing as usual.

verses.kjv_text: And Judah sent the kid by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to receive {his} pledge from the woman's hand: but he found her not.
verses.nlt_text: Later Judah asked his friend Hirah the Adullamite to take the young goat to the woman and to pick up the things he had given her as his guarantee. But Hirah couldn't find her.

verses.kjv_text: Then he asked the men of that place, saying, Where {is} the harlot, that {was} openly by the way side? And they said, There was no harlot in this {place}. {openly: or, in Enajim}
verses.nlt_text: So he asked the men who lived there, "Where can I find the shrine prostitute who was sitting beside the road at the entrance to Enaim?" "We've never had a shrine prostitute here," they replied.

verses.kjv_text: And he returned to Judah, and said, I cannot find her; and also the men of the place said, {that} there was no harlot in this {place}.
verses.nlt_text: So Hirah returned to Judah and told him, "I couldn't find her anywhere, and the men of the village claim they've never had a shrine prostitute there."

verses.kjv_text: And Judah said, Let her take {it} to her, lest we be shamed: behold, I sent this kid, and thou hast not found her. {be shamed: Heb. become a contempt}
verses.nlt_text: "Then let her keep the things I gave her," Judah said. "I sent the young goat as we agreed, but you couldn't find her. We'd be the laughingstock of the village if we went back again to look for her."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass about three months after, that it was told Judah, saying, Tamar thy daughter in law hath played the harlot; and also, behold, she {is} with child by whoredom. And Judah said, Bring her forth, and let her be burnt.
verses.nlt_text: About three months later, Judah was told, "Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has acted like a prostitute. And now, because of this, she's pregnant." "Bring her out, and let her be burned!" Judah demanded.

verses.kjv_text: When she {was} brought forth, she sent to her father in law, saying, By the man, whose these {are, am} I with child: and she said, Discern, I pray thee, whose {are} these, the signet, and bracelets, and staff.
verses.nlt_text: But as they were taking her out to kill her, she sent this message to her father-in-law: "The man who owns these things made me pregnant. Look closely. Whose seal and cord and walking stick are these?"

verses.kjv_text: And Judah acknowledged {them}, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.
verses.nlt_text: Judah recognized them immediately and said, "She is more righteous than I am, because I didn't arrange for her to marry my son Shelah." And Judah never slept with Tamar again.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, twins {were} in her womb.
verses.nlt_text: When the time came for Tamar to give birth, it was discovered that she was carrying twins.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when she travailed, that {the one} put out {his} hand: and the midwife took and bound upon his hand a scarlet thread, saying, This came out first.
verses.nlt_text: While she was in labor, one of the babies reached out his hand. The midwife grabbed it and tied a scarlet string around the child's wrist, announcing, "This one came out first."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as he drew back his hand, that, behold, his brother came out: and she said, How hast thou broken forth? {this} breach {be} upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez. {How hast...: or, Wherefore hast thou made this breach against thee?} {Pharez: that is A breach}
verses.nlt_text: But then he pulled back his hand, and out came his brother! "What!" the midwife exclaimed. "How did you break out first?" So he was named Perez.

verses.kjv_text: And afterward came out his brother, that had the scarlet thread upon his hand: and his name was called Zarah.
verses.nlt_text: Then the baby with the scarlet string on his wrist was born, and he was named Zerah.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph was brought down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him of the hands of the Ishmeelites, which had brought him down thither.
verses.nlt_text: When Joseph was taken to Egypt by the Ishmaelite traders, he was purchased by Potiphar, an Egyptian officer. Potiphar was captain of the guard for Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD was with Joseph, so he succeeded in everything he did as he served in the home of his Egyptian master.

verses.kjv_text: And his master saw that the LORD {was} with him, and that the LORD made all that he did to prosper in his hand.
verses.nlt_text: Potiphar noticed this and realized that the LORD was with Joseph, giving him success in everything he did.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph found grace in his sight, and he served him: and he made him overseer over his house, and all {that} he had he put into his hand.
verses.nlt_text: This pleased Potiphar, so he soon made Joseph his personal attendant. He put him in charge of his entire household and everything he owned.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass from the time {that} he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; and the blessing of the LORD was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.
verses.nlt_text: From the day Joseph was put in charge of his master's household and property, the LORD began to bless Potiphar's household for Joseph's sake. All his household affairs ran smoothly, and his crops and livestock flourished.

verses.kjv_text: And he left all that he had in Joseph's hand; and he knew not ought he had, save the bread which he did eat. And Joseph was {a} goodly {person}, and well favoured.
verses.nlt_text: So Potiphar gave Joseph complete administrative responsibility over everything he owned. With Joseph there, he didn't worry about a thing-- except what kind of food to eat!Joseph was a very handsome and well-built young man,

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.
verses.nlt_text: and Potiphar's wife soon began to look at him lustfully. "Come and sleep with me," she demanded.

verses.kjv_text: But he refused, and said unto his master's wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what {is} with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand;
verses.nlt_text: But Joseph refused. "Look," he told her, "my master trusts me with everything in his entire household.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou {art} his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
verses.nlt_text: No one here has more authority than I do. He has held back nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How could I do such a wicked thing? It would be a great sin against God."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, {or} to be with her.
verses.nlt_text: She kept putting pressure on Joseph day after day, but he refused to sleep with her, and he kept out of her way as much as possible.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass about this time, that {Joseph} went into the house to do his business; and {there was} none of the men of the house there within.
verses.nlt_text: One day, however, no one else was around when he went in to do his work.

verses.kjv_text: And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.
verses.nlt_text: She came and grabbed him by his cloak, demanding, "Come on, sleep with me!" Joseph tore himself away, but he left his cloak in her hand as he ran from the house.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and was fled forth,
verses.nlt_text: When she saw that she was holding his cloak and he had fled,

verses.kjv_text: That she called unto the men of her house, and spake unto them, saying, See, he hath brought in an Hebrew unto us to mock us; he came in unto me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice: {loud: Heb. great}
verses.nlt_text: she called out to her servants. Soon all the men came running. "Look!" she said. "My husband has brought this Hebrew slave here to make fools of us! He came into my room to rape me, but I screamed.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled, and got him out.
verses.nlt_text: When he heard me scream, he ran outside and got away, but he left his cloak behind with me."

verses.kjv_text: And she laid up his garment by her, until his lord came home.
verses.nlt_text: She kept the cloak with her until her husband came home.

verses.kjv_text: And she spake unto him according to these words, saying, The Hebrew servant, which thou hast brought unto us, came in unto me to mock me:
verses.nlt_text: Then she told him her story. "That Hebrew slave you've brought into our house tried to come in and fool around with me," she said.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as I lifted up my voice and cried, that he left his garment with me, and fled out.
verses.nlt_text: "But when I screamed, he ran outside, leaving his cloak with me!"

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spake unto him, saying, After this manner did thy servant to me; that his wrath was kindled.
verses.nlt_text: Potiphar was furious when he heard his wife's story about how Joseph had treated her.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners {were} bound: and he was there in the prison.
verses.nlt_text: So he took Joseph and threw him into the prison where the king's prisoners were held, and there he remained.

verses.kjv_text: But the LORD was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison. {shewed...: Heb. extended kindness unto him}
verses.nlt_text: But the LORD was with Joseph in the prison and showed him his faithful love. And the LORD made Joseph a favorite with the prison warden.

verses.kjv_text: And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph's hand all the prisoners that {were} in the prison; and whatsoever they did there, he was the doer {of it}.
verses.nlt_text: Before long, the warden put Joseph in charge of all the other prisoners and over everything that happened in the prison.

verses.kjv_text: The keeper of the prison looked not to any thing {that was} under his hand; because the LORD was with him, and {that} which he did, the LORD made {it} to prosper.
verses.nlt_text: The warden had no more worries, because Joseph took care of everything. The LORD was with him and caused everything he did to succeed.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after these things, {that} the butler of the king of Egypt and {his} baker had offended their lord the king of Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: Some time later, Pharaoh's chief cup-bearer and chief baker offended their royal master.

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh was wroth against two {of} his officers, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers.
verses.nlt_text: Pharaoh became angry with these two officials,

verses.kjv_text: And he put them in ward in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph {was} bound.
verses.nlt_text: and he put them in the prison where Joseph was, in the palace of the captain of the guard.

verses.kjv_text: And the captain of the guard charged Joseph with them, and he served them: and they continued a season in ward.
verses.nlt_text: They remained in prison for quite some time, and the captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, who looked after them.

verses.kjv_text: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which {were} bound in the prison.
verses.nlt_text: While they were in prison, Pharaoh's cup-bearer and baker each had a dream one night, and each dream had its own meaning.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph came in unto them in the morning, and looked upon them, and, behold, they {were} sad.
verses.nlt_text: When Joseph saw them the next morning, he noticed that they both looked upset.

verses.kjv_text: And he asked Pharaoh's officers that {were} with him in the ward of his lord's house, saying, Wherefore look ye {so} sadly to day? {look...: Heb. are your faces evil?}
verses.nlt_text: "Why do you look so worried today?" he asked them.

verses.kjv_text: And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and {there is} no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, {Do} not interpretations {belong} to God? tell me {them}, I pray you.
verses.nlt_text: And they replied, "We both had dreams last night, but no one can tell us what they mean." "Interpreting dreams is God's business," Joseph replied. "Go ahead and tell me your dreams."

verses.kjv_text: And the chief butler told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine {was} before me;
verses.nlt_text: So the chief cup-bearer told Joseph his dream first. "In my dream," he said, "I saw a grapevine in front of me.

verses.kjv_text: And in the vine {were} three branches: and it {was} as though it budded, {and} her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:
verses.nlt_text: The vine had three branches that began to bud and blossom, and soon it produced clusters of ripe grapes.

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh's cup {was} in my hand: and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.
verses.nlt_text: I was holding Pharaoh's wine cup in my hand, so I took a cluster of grapes and squeezed the juice into the cup. Then I placed the cup in Pharaoh's hand."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph said unto him, This {is} the interpretation of it: The three branches {are} three days:
verses.nlt_text: "This is what the dream means," Joseph said. "The three branches represent three days.

verses.kjv_text: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler. {lift...: or, reckon}
verses.nlt_text: Within three days Pharaoh will lift you up and restore you to your position as his chief cup-bearer.

verses.kjv_text: But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and shew kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house: {think...: Heb. remember me with thee}
verses.nlt_text: And please remember me and do me a favor when things go well for you. Mention me to Pharaoh, so he might let me out of this place.

verses.kjv_text: For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.
verses.nlt_text: For I was kidnapped from my homeland, the land of the Hebrews, and now I'm here in prison, but I did nothing to deserve it."

verses.kjv_text: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also {was} in my dream, and, behold, {I had} three white baskets on my head: {white: or, full of holes}
verses.nlt_text: When the chief baker saw that Joseph had given the first dream such a positive interpretation, he said to Joseph, "I had a dream, too. In my dream there were three baskets of white pastries stacked on my head.

verses.kjv_text: And in the uppermost basket {there was} of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head. {bakemeats...: Heb. meat of Pharaoh, the work of a baker, or, cook}
verses.nlt_text: The top basket contained all kinds of pastries for Pharaoh, but the birds came and ate them from the basket on my head."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph answered and said, This {is} the interpretation thereof: The three baskets {are} three days:
verses.nlt_text: "This is what the dream means," Joseph told him. "The three baskets also represent three days.

verses.kjv_text: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee. {lift...: or, reckon thee, and take thy office from thee}
verses.nlt_text: Three days from now Pharaoh will lift you up and impale your body on a pole. Then birds will come and peck away at your flesh."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass the third day, {which was} Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and of the chief baker among his servants. {lifted...: or, reckoned}
verses.nlt_text: Pharaoh's birthday came three days later, and he prepared a banquet for all his officials and staff. He summoned his chief cup-bearer and chief baker to join the other officials.

verses.kjv_text: And he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand:
verses.nlt_text: He then restored the chief cup-bearer to his former position, so he could again hand Pharaoh his cup.

verses.kjv_text: But he hanged the chief baker: as Joseph had interpreted to them.
verses.nlt_text: But Pharaoh impaled the chief baker, just as Joseph had predicted when he interpreted his dream.

verses.kjv_text: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.
verses.nlt_text: Pharaoh's chief cup-bearer, however, forgot all about Joseph, never giving him another thought.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.
verses.nlt_text: Two full years later, Pharaoh dreamed that he was standing on the bank of the Nile River.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven well favoured kine and fatfleshed; and they fed in a meadow.
verses.nlt_text: In his dream he saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river and begin grazing in the marsh grass.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, seven other kine came up after them out of the river, ill favoured and leanfleshed; and stood by the {other} kine upon the brink of the river.
verses.nlt_text: Then he saw seven more cows come up behind them from the Nile, but these were scrawny and thin. These cows stood beside the fat cows on the riverbank.

verses.kjv_text: And the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.
verses.nlt_text: Then the scrawny, thin cows ate the seven healthy, fat cows! At this point in the dream, Pharaoh woke up.

verses.kjv_text: And he slept and dreamed the second time: and, behold, seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good. {rank: Heb. fat}
verses.nlt_text: But he fell asleep again and had a second dream. This time he saw seven heads of grain, plump and beautiful, growing on a single stalk.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them.
verses.nlt_text: Then seven more heads of grain appeared, but these were shriveled and withered by the east wind.

verses.kjv_text: And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and, behold, {it was} a dream.
verses.nlt_text: And these thin heads swallowed up the seven plump, well-formed heads! Then Pharaoh woke up again and realized it was a dream.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but {there was} none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.
verses.nlt_text: The next morning Pharaoh was very disturbed by the dreams. So he called for all the magicians and wise men of Egypt. When Pharaoh told them his dreams, not one of them could tell him what they meant.

verses.kjv_text: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:
verses.nlt_text: Finally, the king's chief cup-bearer spoke up. "Today I have been reminded of my failure," he told Pharaoh.

verses.kjv_text: Pharaoh was wroth with his servants, and put me in ward in the captain of the guard's house, {both} me and the chief baker:
verses.nlt_text: "Some time ago, you were angry with the chief baker and me, and you imprisoned us in the palace of the captain of the guard.

verses.kjv_text: And we dreamed a dream in one night, I and he; we dreamed each man according to the interpretation of his dream.
verses.nlt_text: One night the chief baker and I each had a dream, and each dream had its own meaning.

verses.kjv_text: And {there was} there with us a young man, an Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard; and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams; to each man according to his dream he did interpret.
verses.nlt_text: There was a young Hebrew man with us in the prison who was a slave of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he told us what each of our dreams meant.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; me he restored unto mine office, and him he hanged.
verses.nlt_text: And everything happened just as he had predicted. I was restored to my position as cup-bearer, and the chief baker was executed and impaled on a pole."

verses.kjv_text: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved {himself}, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh. {brought...: Heb. made him run}
verses.nlt_text: Pharaoh sent for Joseph at once, and he was quickly brought from the prison. After he shaved and changed his clothes, he went in and stood before Pharaoh.

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I have dreamed a dream, and {there is} none that can interpret it: and I have heard say of thee, {that} thou canst understand a dream to interpret it. {thou...: or, when thou hearest a dream thou canst interpret it}
verses.nlt_text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I had a dream last night, and no one here can tell me what it means. But I have heard that when you hear about a dream you can interpret it."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, {It is} not in me: God shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.
verses.nlt_text: "It is beyond my power to do this," Joseph replied. "But God can tell you what it means and set you at ease."

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, In my dream, behold, I stood upon the bank of the river:
verses.nlt_text: So Pharaoh told Joseph his dream. "In my dream," he said, "I was standing on the bank of the Nile River,

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, there came up out of the river seven kine, fatfleshed and well favoured; and they fed in a meadow:
verses.nlt_text: and I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river and begin grazing in the marsh grass.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, seven other kine came up after them, poor and very ill favoured and leanfleshed, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for badness:
verses.nlt_text: But then I saw seven sick-looking cows, scrawny and thin, come up after them. I've never seen such sorry-looking animals in all the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And the lean and the ill favoured kine did eat up the first seven fat kine:
verses.nlt_text: These thin, scrawny cows ate the seven fat cows.

verses.kjv_text: And when they had eaten them up, it could not be known that they had eaten them; but they {were} still ill favoured, as at the beginning. So I awoke. {eaten...: Heb. come to the inward parts of them}
verses.nlt_text: But afterward you wouldn't have known it, for they were still as thin and scrawny as before! Then I woke up.

verses.kjv_text: And I saw in my dream, and, behold, seven ears came up in one stalk, full and good:
verses.nlt_text: "Then I fell asleep again, and I had another dream. This time I saw seven heads of grain, full and beautiful, growing on a single stalk.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, seven ears, withered, thin, {and} blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them: {withered: or, small}
verses.nlt_text: Then seven more heads of grain appeared, but these were blighted, shriveled, and withered by the east wind.

verses.kjv_text: And the thin ears devoured the seven good ears: and I told {this} unto the magicians; but {there was} none that could declare {it} to me.
verses.nlt_text: And the shriveled heads swallowed the seven healthy heads. I told these dreams to the magicians, but no one could tell me what they mean."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph said unto Pharaoh, The dream of Pharaoh {is} one: God hath shewed Pharaoh what he {is} about to do.
verses.nlt_text: Joseph responded, "Both of Pharaoh's dreams mean the same thing. God is telling Pharaoh in advance what he is about to do.

verses.kjv_text: The seven good kine {are} seven years; and the seven good ears {are} seven years: the dream {is} one.
verses.nlt_text: The seven healthy cows and the seven healthy heads of grain both represent seven years of prosperity.

verses.kjv_text: And the seven thin and ill favoured kine that came up after them {are} seven years; and the seven empty ears blasted with the east wind shall be seven years of famine.
verses.nlt_text: The seven thin, scrawny cows that came up later and the seven thin heads of grain, withered by the east wind, represent seven years of famine.

verses.kjv_text: This {is} the thing which I have spoken unto Pharaoh: What God {is} about to do he sheweth unto Pharaoh.
verses.nlt_text: "This will happen just as I have described it, for God has revealed to Pharaoh in advance what he is about to do.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:
verses.nlt_text: The next seven years will be a period of great prosperity throughout the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land;
verses.nlt_text: But afterward there will be seven years of famine so great that all the prosperity will be forgotten in Egypt. Famine will destroy the land.

verses.kjv_text: And the plenty shall not be known in the land by reason of that famine following; for it {shall be} very grievous. {grievous: Heb. heavy}
verses.nlt_text: This famine will be so severe that even the memory of the good years will be erased.

verses.kjv_text: And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; {it is} because the thing {is} established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass. {established...: or, prepared of God}
verses.nlt_text: As for having two similar dreams, it means that these events have been decreed by God, and he will soon make them happen.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: "Therefore, Pharaoh should find an intelligent and wise man and put him in charge of the entire land of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: Let Pharaoh do {this}, and let him appoint officers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt in the seven plenteous years. {officers: or, overseers}
verses.nlt_text: Then Pharaoh should appoint supervisors over the land and let them collect one-fifth of all the crops during the seven good years.

verses.kjv_text: And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.
verses.nlt_text: Have them gather all the food produced in the good years that are just ahead and bring it to Pharaoh's storehouses. Store it away, and guard it so there will be food in the cities.

verses.kjv_text: And that food shall be for store to the land against the seven years of famine, which shall be in the land of Egypt; that the land perish not through the famine. {perish...: Heb. be not cut off}
verses.nlt_text: That way there will be enough to eat when the seven years of famine come to the land of Egypt. Otherwise this famine will destroy the land."

verses.kjv_text: And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.
verses.nlt_text: Joseph's suggestions were well received by Pharaoh and his officials.

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find {such a one} as this {is}, a man in whom the Spirit of God {is}?
verses.nlt_text: So Pharaoh asked his officials, "Can we find anyone else like this man so obviously filled with the spirit of God?"

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, {there is} none so discreet and wise as thou {art}:
verses.nlt_text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, "Since God has revealed the meaning of the dreams to you, clearly no one else is as intelligent or wise as you are.

verses.kjv_text: Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou. {be ruled: Heb. be armed, or, kiss}
verses.nlt_text: You will be in charge of my court, and all my people will take orders from you. Only I, sitting on my throne, will have a rank higher than yours."

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, See, I have set thee over all the land of Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, "I hereby put you in charge of the entire land of Egypt."

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph's hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck; {fine...: or, silk}
verses.nlt_text: Then Pharaoh removed his signet ring from his hand and placed it on Joseph's finger. He dressed him in fine linen clothing and hung a gold chain around his neck.

verses.kjv_text: And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him {ruler} over all the land of Egypt. {Bow...: or, Tender father: Heb. Abrech}
verses.nlt_text: Then he had Joseph ride in the chariot reserved for his second-in-command. And wherever Joseph went, the command was shouted, "Kneel down!" So Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of all Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, I {am} Pharaoh, and without thee shall no man lift up his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: And Pharaoh said to him, "I am Pharaoh, but no one will lift a hand or foot in the entire land of Egypt without your approval."

verses.kjv_text: And Pharaoh called Joseph's name Zaphnathpaaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over {all} the land of Egypt. {Zaphnathpaaneah: which in the Coptic signifies, A revealer of secrets, or, The man to whom secrets are revealed} {priest: or, prince}
verses.nlt_text: Then Pharaoh gave Joseph a new Egyptian name, Zaphenath-paneah. He also gave him a wife, whose name was Asenath. She was the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On. So Joseph took charge of the entire land of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph {was} thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: He was thirty years old when he began serving in the court of Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. And when Joseph left Pharaoh's presence, he inspected the entire land of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And in the seven plenteous years the earth brought forth by handfuls.
verses.nlt_text: As predicted, for seven years the land produced bumper crops.

verses.kjv_text: And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which {was} round about every city, laid he up in the same.
verses.nlt_text: During those years, Joseph gathered all the crops grown in Egypt and stored the grain from the surrounding fields in the cities.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for {it was} without number.
verses.nlt_text: He piled up huge amounts of grain like sand on the seashore. Finally, he stopped keeping records because there was too much to measure.

verses.kjv_text: And unto Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, which Asenath the daughter of Potipherah priest of On bare unto him. {priest: or, prince}
verses.nlt_text: During this time, before the first of the famine years, two sons were born to Joseph and his wife, Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, the priest of On.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: For God, {said he}, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father's house. {Manasseh: that is, Forgetting}
verses.nlt_text: Joseph named his older son Manasseh, for he said, "God has made me forget all my troubles and everyone in my father's family."

verses.kjv_text: And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For God hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction. {Ephraim: that is, Fruitful}
verses.nlt_text: Joseph named his second son Ephraim, for he said, "God has made me fruitful in this land of my grief."

verses.kjv_text: And the seven years of plenteousness, that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.
verses.nlt_text: At last the seven years of bumper crops throughout the land of Egypt came to an end.

verses.kjv_text: And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.
verses.nlt_text: Then the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had predicted. The famine also struck all the surrounding countries, but throughout Egypt there was plenty of food.

verses.kjv_text: And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; what he saith to you, do.
verses.nlt_text: Eventually, however, the famine spread throughout the land of Egypt as well. And when the people cried out to Pharaoh for food, he told them, "Go to Joseph, and do whatever he tells you."

verses.kjv_text: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: And Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt. {all the storehouses: Heb. all wherein was}
verses.nlt_text: So with severe famine everywhere, Joseph opened up the storehouses and distributed grain to the Egyptians, for the famine was severe throughout the land of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy {corn}; because that the famine was {so} sore in all lands.
verses.nlt_text: And people from all around came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph because the famine was severe throughout the world.

verses.kjv_text: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?
verses.nlt_text: When Jacob heard that grain was available in Egypt, he said to his sons, "Why are you standing around looking at one another?

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Behold, I have heard that there is corn in Egypt: get you down thither, and buy for us from thence; that we may live, and not die.
verses.nlt_text: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy enough grain to keep us alive. Otherwise we'll die."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph's ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: So Joseph's ten older brothers went down to Egypt to buy grain.

verses.kjv_text: But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest peradventure mischief befall him.
verses.nlt_text: But Jacob wouldn't let Joseph's younger brother, Benjamin, go with them, for fear some harm might come to him.

verses.kjv_text: And the sons of Israel came to buy {corn} among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
verses.nlt_text: So Jacob's sons arrived in Egypt along with others to buy food, for the famine was in Canaan as well.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph {was} the governor over the land, {and} he {it was} that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph's brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him {with} their faces to the earth.
verses.nlt_text: Since Joseph was governor of all Egypt and in charge of selling grain to all the people, it was to him that his brothers came. When they arrived, they bowed before him with their faces to the ground.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but made himself strange unto them, and spake roughly unto them; and he said unto them, Whence come ye? And they said, From the land of Canaan to buy food. {roughly...: Heb. hard things with them}
verses.nlt_text: Joseph recognized his brothers instantly, but he pretended to be a stranger and spoke harshly to them. "Where are you from?" he demanded."From the land of Canaan," they replied. "We have come to buy food."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.
verses.nlt_text: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they didn't recognize him.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said unto them, Ye {are} spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.
verses.nlt_text: And he remembered the dreams he'd had about them many years before. He said to them, "You are spies! You have come to see how vulnerable our land has become."

verses.kjv_text: And they said unto him, Nay, my lord, but to buy food are thy servants come.
verses.nlt_text: "No, my lord!" they exclaimed. "Your servants have simply come to buy food.

verses.kjv_text: We {are} all one man's sons; we {are} true {men}, thy servants are no spies.
verses.nlt_text: We are all brothers-- members of the same family. We are honest men, sir! We are not spies!"

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, Nay, but to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes, you are!" Joseph insisted. "You have come to see how vulnerable our land has become."

verses.kjv_text: And they said, Thy servants {are} twelve brethren, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and, behold, the youngest {is} this day with our father, and one {is} not.
verses.nlt_text: "Sir," they said, "there are actually twelve of us. We, your servants, are all brothers, sons of a man living in the land of Canaan. Our youngest brother is back there with our father right now, and one of our brothers is no longer with us."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph said unto them, That {is it} that I spake unto you, saying, Ye {are} spies:
verses.nlt_text: But Joseph insisted, "As I said, you are spies!

verses.kjv_text: Hereby ye shall be proved: By the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither.
verses.nlt_text: This is how I will test your story. I swear by the life of Pharaoh that you will never leave Egypt unless your youngest brother comes here!

verses.kjv_text: Send one of you, and let him fetch your brother, and ye shall be kept in prison, that your words may be proved, whether {there be any} truth in you: or else by the life of Pharaoh surely ye {are} spies. {kept...: Heb. bound}
verses.nlt_text: One of you must go and get your brother. I'll keep the rest of you here in prison. Then we'll find out whether or not your story is true. By the life of Pharaoh, if it turns out that you don't have a younger brother, then I'll know you are spies."

verses.kjv_text: And he put them all together into ward three days. {put: Heb. gathered}
verses.nlt_text: So Joseph put them all in prison for three days.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph said unto them the third day, This do, and live; {for} I fear God:
verses.nlt_text: On the third day Joseph said to them, "I am a God-fearing man. If you do as I say, you will live.

verses.kjv_text: If ye {be} true {men}, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your prison: go ye, carry corn for the famine of your houses:
verses.nlt_text: If you really are honest men, choose one of your brothers to remain in prison. The rest of you may go home with grain for your starving families.

verses.kjv_text: But bring your youngest brother unto me; so shall your words be verified, and ye shall not die. And they did so.
verses.nlt_text: But you must bring your youngest brother back to me. This will prove that you are telling the truth, and you will not die." To this they agreed.

verses.kjv_text: And they said one to another, We {are} verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.
verses.nlt_text: Speaking among themselves, they said, "Clearly we are being punished because of what we did to Joseph long ago. We saw his anguish when he pleaded for his life, but we wouldn't listen. That's why we're in this trouble."

verses.kjv_text: And Reuben answered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear? therefore, behold, also his blood is required.
verses.nlt_text: "Didn't I tell you not to sin against the boy?" Reuben asked. "But you wouldn't listen. And now we have to answer for his blood!"

verses.kjv_text: And they knew not that Joseph understood {them}; for he spake unto them by an interpreter. {he spake...: Heb. an interpreter was between them}
verses.nlt_text: Of course, they didn't know that Joseph understood them, for he had been speaking to them through an interpreter.

verses.kjv_text: And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and returned to them again, and communed with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.
verses.nlt_text: Now he turned away from them and began to weep. When he regained his composure, he spoke to them again. Then he chose Simeon from among them and had him tied up right before their eyes.

verses.kjv_text: Then Joseph commanded to fill their sacks with corn, and to restore every man's money into his sack, and to give them provision for the way: and thus did he unto them.
verses.nlt_text: Joseph then ordered his servants to fill the men's sacks with grain, but he also gave secret instructions to return each brother's payment at the top of his sack. He also gave them supplies for their journey home.

verses.kjv_text: And they laded their asses with the corn, and departed thence.
verses.nlt_text: So the brothers loaded their donkeys with the grain and headed for home.

verses.kjv_text: And as one of them opened his sack to give his ass provender in the inn, he espied his money; for, behold, it {was} in his sack's mouth.
verses.nlt_text: But when they stopped for the night and one of them opened his sack to get grain for his donkey, he found his money in the top of his sack.

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto his brethren, My money is restored; and, lo, {it is} even in my sack: and their heart failed {them}, and they were afraid, saying one to another, What {is} this {that} God hath done unto us? {failed...: Heb. went forth}
verses.nlt_text: "Look!" he exclaimed to his brothers. "My money has been returned; it's here in my sack!" Then their hearts sank. Trembling, they said to each other, "What has God done to us?"

verses.kjv_text: And they came unto Jacob their father unto the land of Canaan, and told him all that befell unto them; saying,
verses.nlt_text: When the brothers came to their father, Jacob, in the land of Canaan, they told him everything that had happened to them.

verses.kjv_text: The man, {who is} the lord of the land, spake roughly to us, and took us for spies of the country. {roughly...: Heb. with us hard things}
verses.nlt_text: "The man who is governor of the land spoke very harshly to us," they told him. "He accused us of being spies scouting the land.

verses.kjv_text: And we said unto him, We {are} true {men}; we are no spies:
verses.nlt_text: But we said, 'We are honest men, not spies.

verses.kjv_text: We {be} twelve brethren, sons of our father; one {is} not, and the youngest {is} this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
verses.nlt_text: We are twelve brothers, sons of one father. One brother is no longer with us, and the youngest is at home with our father in the land of Canaan.'

verses.kjv_text: And the man, the lord of the country, said unto us, Hereby shall I know that ye {are} true {men}; leave one of your brethren {here} with me, and take {food for} the famine of your households, and be gone:
verses.nlt_text: "Then the man who is governor of the land told us, 'This is how I will find out if you are honest men. Leave one of your brothers here with me, and take grain for your starving families and go on home.

verses.kjv_text: And bring your youngest brother unto me: then shall I know that ye {are} no spies, but {that} ye {are} true {men: so} will I deliver you your brother, and ye shall traffick in the land.
verses.nlt_text: But you must bring your youngest brother back to me. Then I will know you are honest men and not spies. Then I will give you back your brother, and you may trade freely in the land.'"

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that, behold, every man's bundle of money {was} in his sack: and when {both} they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.
verses.nlt_text: As they emptied out their sacks, there in each man's sack was the bag of money he had paid for the grain! The brothers and their father were terrified when they saw the bags of money.

verses.kjv_text: And Jacob their father said unto them, Me have ye bereaved {of my children}: Joseph {is} not, and Simeon {is} not, and ye will take Benjamin {away}: all these things are against me.
verses.nlt_text: Jacob exclaimed, "You are robbing me of my children! Joseph is gone! Simeon is gone! And now you want to take Benjamin, too. Everything is going against me!"

verses.kjv_text: And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.
verses.nlt_text: Then Reuben said to his father, "You may kill my two sons if I don't bring Benjamin back to you. I'll be responsible for him, and I promise to bring him back."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which ye go, then shall ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.
verses.nlt_text: But Jacob replied, "My son will not go down with you. His brother Joseph is dead, and he is all I have left. If anything should happen to him on your journey, you would send this grieving, white-haired man to his grave. "

verses.kjv_text: And the famine {was} sore in the land.
verses.nlt_text: But the famine continued to ravage the land of Canaan.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when they had eaten up the corn which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said unto them, Go again, buy us a little food.
verses.nlt_text: When the grain they had brought from Egypt was almost gone, Jacob said to his sons, "Go back and buy us a little more food."

verses.kjv_text: And Judah spake unto him, saying, The man did solemnly protest unto us, saying, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother {be} with you. {did...: Heb. protesting protested}
verses.nlt_text: But Judah said, "The man was serious when he warned us, 'You won't see my face again unless your brother is with you.'

verses.kjv_text: If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food:
verses.nlt_text: If you send Benjamin with us, we will go down and buy more food.

verses.kjv_text: But if thou wilt not send {him}, we will not go down: for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother {be} with you.
verses.nlt_text: But if you don't let Benjamin go, we won't go either. Remember, the man said, 'You won't see my face again unless your brother is with you.'"

verses.kjv_text: And Israel said, Wherefore dealt ye {so} ill with me, {as} to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?
verses.nlt_text: "Why were you so cruel to me?" Jacob moaned. "Why did you tell him you had another brother?"

verses.kjv_text: And they said, The man asked us straitly of our state, and of our kindred, saying, {Is} your father yet alive? have ye {another} brother? and we told him according to the tenor of these words: could we certainly know that he would say, Bring your brother down? {asked...: Heb. asking asked us} {tenor: Heb. mouth} {could...: Heb. knowing could we know}
verses.nlt_text: "The man kept asking us questions about our family," they replied. "He asked, 'Is your father still alive? Do you have another brother?' So we answered his questions. How could we know he would say, 'Bring your brother down here'?"

verses.kjv_text: And Judah said unto Israel his father, Send the lad with me, and we will arise and go; that we may live, and not die, both we, and thou, {and} also our little ones.
verses.nlt_text: Judah said to his father, "Send the boy with me, and we will be on our way. Otherwise we will all die of starvation-- and not only we, but you and our little ones.

verses.kjv_text: I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:
verses.nlt_text: I personally guarantee his safety. You may hold me responsible if I don't bring him back to you. Then let me bear the blame forever.

verses.kjv_text: For except we had lingered, surely now we had returned this second time. {this: or, twice by this}
verses.nlt_text: If we hadn't wasted all this time, we could have gone and returned twice by now."

verses.kjv_text: And their father Israel said unto them, If {it must be} so now, do this; take of the best fruits in the land in your vessels, and carry down the man a present, a little balm, and a little honey, spices, and myrrh, nuts, and almonds:
verses.nlt_text: So their father, Jacob, finally said to them, "If it can't be avoided, then at least do this. Pack your bags with the best products of this land. Take them down to the man as gifts-- balm, honey, gum, aromatic resin, pistachio nuts, and almonds.

verses.kjv_text: And take double money in your hand; and the money that was brought again in the mouth of your sacks, carry {it} again in your hand; peradventure it {was} an oversight:
verses.nlt_text: Also take double the money that was put back in your sacks, as it was probably someone's mistake.

verses.kjv_text: Take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man:
verses.nlt_text: Then take your brother, and go back to the man.

verses.kjv_text: And God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may send away your other brother, and Benjamin. If I be bereaved {of my children}, I am bereaved. {If...: or, And I, as I have been, etc.}
verses.nlt_text: May God Almighty give you mercy as you go before the man, so that he will release Simeon and let Benjamin return. But if I must lose my children, so be it."

verses.kjv_text: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.
verses.nlt_text: So the men packed Jacob's gifts and double the money and headed off with Benjamin. They finally arrived in Egypt and presented themselves to Joseph.

verses.kjv_text: And when Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the ruler of his house, Bring {these} men home, and slay, and make ready; for {these} men shall dine with me at noon. {slay: Heb. kill a killing} {dine: Heb. eat}
verses.nlt_text: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the manager of his household, "These men will eat with me this noon. Take them inside the palace. Then go slaughter an animal, and prepare a big feast."

verses.kjv_text: And the man did as Joseph bade; and the man brought the men into Joseph's house.
verses.nlt_text: So the man did as Joseph told him and took them into Joseph's palace.

verses.kjv_text: And the men were afraid, because they were brought into Joseph's house; and they said, Because of the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time are we brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, and fall upon us, and take us for bondmen, and our asses. {seek...: Heb. roll himself upon us}
verses.nlt_text: The brothers were terrified when they saw that they were being taken into Joseph's house. "It's because of the money someone put in our sacks last time we were here," they said. "He plans to pretend that we stole it. Then he will seize us, make us slaves, and take our donkeys."

verses.kjv_text: And they came near to the steward of Joseph's house, and they communed with him at the door of the house,
verses.nlt_text: The brothers approached the manager of Joseph's household and spoke to him at the entrance to the palace.

verses.kjv_text: And said, O sir, we came indeed down at the first time to buy food: {we...: Heb. coming down we came down}
verses.nlt_text: "Sir," they said, "we came to Egypt once before to buy food.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when we came to the inn, that we opened our sacks, and, behold, {every} man's money {was} in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight: and we have brought it again in our hand.
verses.nlt_text: But as we were returning home, we stopped for the night and opened our sacks. Then we discovered that each man's money-- the exact amount paid-- was in the top of his sack! Here it is; we have brought it back with us.

verses.kjv_text: And other money have we brought down in our hands to buy food: we cannot tell who put our money in our sacks.
verses.nlt_text: We also have additional money to buy more food. We have no idea who put our money in our sacks."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Peace {be} to you, fear not: your God, and the God of your father, hath given you treasure in your sacks: I had your money. And he brought Simeon out unto them. {I had...: Heb. your money came to me}
verses.nlt_text: "Relax. Don't be afraid," the household manager told them. "Your God, the God of your father, must have put this treasure into your sacks. I know I received your payment." Then he released Simeon and brought him out to them.

verses.kjv_text: And the man brought the men into Joseph's house, and gave {them} water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their asses provender.
verses.nlt_text: The manager then led the men into Joseph's palace. He gave them water to wash their feet and provided food for their donkeys.

verses.kjv_text: And they made ready the present against Joseph came at noon: for they heard that they should eat bread there.
verses.nlt_text: They were told they would be eating there, so they prepared their gifts for Joseph's arrival at noon.

verses.kjv_text: And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which {was} in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.
verses.nlt_text: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought him, then bowed low to the ground before him.

verses.kjv_text: And he asked them of {their} welfare, and said, {Is} your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? {Is} he yet alive? {welfare: Heb. peace} {Is your...: Heb. Is there peace to your father?}
verses.nlt_text: After greeting them, he asked, "How is your father, the old man you spoke about? Is he still alive?"

verses.kjv_text: And they answered, Thy servant our father {is} in good health, he {is} yet alive. And they bowed down their heads, and made obeisance.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes," they replied. "Our father, your servant, is alive and well." And they bowed low again.

verses.kjv_text: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother's son, and said, {Is} this your younger brother, of whom ye spake unto me? And he said, God be gracious unto thee, my son.
verses.nlt_text: Then Joseph looked at his brother Benjamin, the son of his own mother. "Is this your youngest brother, the one you told me about?" Joseph asked. "May God be gracious to you, my son."

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought {where} to weep; and he entered into {his} chamber, and wept there.
verses.nlt_text: Then Joseph hurried from the room because he was overcome with emotion for his brother. He went into his private room, where he broke down and wept.

verses.kjv_text: And he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.
verses.nlt_text: After washing his face, he came back out, keeping himself under control. Then he ordered, "Bring out the food!"

verses.kjv_text: And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that {is} an abomination unto the Egyptians.
verses.nlt_text: The waiters served Joseph at his own table, and his brothers were served at a separate table. The Egyptians who ate with Joseph sat at their own table, because Egyptians despise Hebrews and refuse to eat with them.

verses.kjv_text: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one at another.
verses.nlt_text: Joseph told each of his brothers where to sit, and to their amazement, he seated them according to age, from oldest to youngest.

verses.kjv_text: And he took {and sent} messes unto them from before him: but Benjamin's mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him. {were...: Heb. drank largely}
verses.nlt_text: And Joseph filled their plates with food from his own table, giving Benjamin five times as much as he gave the others. So they feasted and drank freely with him.

verses.kjv_text: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men's sacks {with} food, as much as they can carry, and put every man's money in his sack's mouth. {the steward...: Heb. him that was over his house}
verses.nlt_text: When his brothers were ready to leave, Joseph gave these instructions to his palace manager: "Fill each of their sacks with as much grain as they can carry, and put each man's money back into his sack.

verses.kjv_text: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack's mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.
verses.nlt_text: Then put my personal silver cup at the top of the youngest brother's sack, along with the money for his grain." So the manager did as Joseph instructed him.

verses.kjv_text: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their asses.
verses.nlt_text: The brothers were up at dawn and were sent on their journey with their loaded donkeys.

verses.kjv_text: {And} when they were gone out of the city, {and} not {yet} far off, Joseph said unto his steward, Up, follow after the men; and when thou dost overtake them, say unto them, Wherefore have ye rewarded evil for good?
verses.nlt_text: But when they had gone only a short distance and were barely out of the city, Joseph said to his palace manager, "Chase after them and stop them. When you catch up with them, ask them, 'Why have you repaid my kindness with such evil?

verses.kjv_text: {Is} not this {it} in which my lord drinketh, and whereby indeed he divineth? ye have done evil in so doing. {divineth: or, maketh trial?}
verses.nlt_text: Why have you stolen my master's silver cup, which he uses to predict the future? What a wicked thing you have done!' "

verses.kjv_text: And he overtook them, and he spake unto them these same words.
verses.nlt_text: When the palace manager caught up with the men, he spoke to them as he had been instructed.

verses.kjv_text: And they said unto him, Wherefore saith my lord these words? God forbid that thy servants should do according to this thing:
verses.nlt_text: "What are you talking about?" the brothers responded. "We are your servants and would never do such a thing!

verses.kjv_text: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks' mouths, we brought again unto thee out of the land of Canaan: how then should we steal out of thy lord's house silver or gold?
verses.nlt_text: Didn't we return the money we found in our sacks? We brought it back all the way from the land of Canaan. Why would we steal silver or gold from your master's house?

verses.kjv_text: With whomsoever of thy servants it be found, both let him die, and we also will be my lord's bondmen.
verses.nlt_text: If you find his cup with any one of us, let that man die. And all the rest of us, my lord, will be your slaves."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Now also {let} it {be} according unto your words: he with whom it is found shall be my servant; and ye shall be blameless.
verses.nlt_text: "That's fair," the man replied. "But only the one who stole the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may go free."

verses.kjv_text: Then they speedily took down every man his sack to the ground, and opened every man his sack.
verses.nlt_text: They all quickly took their sacks from the backs of their donkeys and opened them.

verses.kjv_text: And he searched, {and} began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin's sack.
verses.nlt_text: The palace manager searched the brothers' sacks, from the oldest to the youngest. And the cup was found in Benjamin's sack!

verses.kjv_text: Then they rent their clothes, and laded every man his ass, and returned to the city.
verses.nlt_text: When the brothers saw this, they tore their clothing in despair. Then they loaded their donkeys again and returned to the city.

verses.kjv_text: And Judah and his brethren came to Joseph's house; for he {was} yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.
verses.nlt_text: Joseph was still in his palace when Judah and his brothers arrived, and they fell to the ground before him.

verses.kjv_text: And Joseph said unto them, What deed {is} this that ye have done? wot ye not that such a man as I can certainly divine? {divine: or, make trial?}
verses.nlt_text: "What have you done?" Joseph demanded. "Don't you know that a man like me can predict the future?"

verses.kjv_text: And Judah said, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we {are} my lord's servants, both we, and {he} also with whom the cup is found.
verses.nlt_text: Judah answered, "Oh, my lord, what can we say to you? How can we explain this? How can we prove our innocence? God is punishing us for our sins. My lord, we have all returned to be your slaves-- all of us, not just our brother who had your cup in his sack."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, God forbid that I should do so: {but} the man in whose hand the cup is found, he shall be my servant; and as for you, get you up in peace unto your father.
verses.nlt_text: "No," Joseph said. "I would never do such a thing! Only the man who stole the cup will be my slave. The rest of you may go back to your father in peace."
