verses.nlt_text: Whenever Aaron and his sons bless the people of Israel in my name, I myself will bless them."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass on the day that Moses had fully set up the tabernacle, and had anointed it, and sanctified it, and all the instruments thereof, both the altar and all the vessels thereof, and had anointed them, and sanctified them;
verses.nlt_text: On the day Moses set up the Tabernacle, he anointed it and set it apart as holy. He also anointed and set apart all its furnishings and the altar with its utensils.

verses.kjv_text: That the princes of Israel, heads of the house of their fathers, who {were} the princes of the tribes, and were over them that were numbered, offered: {and were: Heb. who stood}
verses.nlt_text: Then the leaders of Israel-- the tribal leaders who had registered the troops-- came and brought their offerings.

verses.kjv_text: And they brought their offering before the LORD, six covered wagons, and twelve oxen; a wagon for two of the princes, and for each one an ox: and they brought them before the tabernacle.
verses.nlt_text: Together they brought six large wagons and twelve oxen. There was a wagon for every two leaders and an ox for each leader. They presented these to the LORD in front of the Tabernacle.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said to Moses,

verses.kjv_text: Take {it} of them, that they may be to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation; and thou shalt give them unto the Levites, to every man according to his service.
verses.nlt_text: "Receive their gifts, and use these oxen and wagons for transporting the Tabernacle. Distribute them among the Levites according to the work they have to do."

verses.kjv_text: And Moses took the wagons and the oxen, and gave them unto the Levites.
verses.nlt_text: So Moses took the wagons and oxen and presented them to the Levites.

verses.kjv_text: Two wagons and four oxen he gave unto the sons of Gershon, according to their service:
verses.nlt_text: He gave two wagons and four oxen to the Gershonite division for their work,

verses.kjv_text: And four wagons and eight oxen he gave unto the sons of Merari, according unto their service, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.
verses.nlt_text: and he gave four wagons and eight oxen to the Merarite division for their work. All their work was done under the leadership of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.

verses.kjv_text: But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none: because the service of the sanctuary belonging unto them {was that} they should bear upon their shoulders.
verses.nlt_text: But he gave none of the wagons or oxen to the Kohathite division, since they were required to carry the sacred objects of the Tabernacle on their shoulders.

verses.kjv_text: And the princes offered for dedicating of the altar in the day that it was anointed, even the princes offered their offering before the altar.
verses.nlt_text: The leaders also presented dedication gifts for the altar at the time it was anointed. They each placed their gifts before the altar.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, They shall offer their offering, each prince on his day, for the dedicating of the altar.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD said to Moses, "Let one leader bring his gift each day for the dedication of the altar."

verses.kjv_text: And he that offered his offering the first day was Nahshon the son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah:
verses.nlt_text: On the first day Nahshon son of Amminadab, leader of the tribe of Judah, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And his offering {was} one silver charger, the weight thereof {was} an hundred and thirty {shekels}, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them {were} full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering:
verses.nlt_text: His offering consisted of a silver platter weighing 3-1/4 pounds and a silver basin weighing 1-3/4 pounds (as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel). These were both filled with grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil.

verses.kjv_text: One spoon of ten {shekels} of gold, full of incense:
verses.nlt_text: He also brought a gold container weighing four ounces, which was filled with incense.

verses.kjv_text: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the first year, for a burnt offering:
verses.nlt_text: He brought a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old male lamb for a burnt offering,

verses.kjv_text: One kid of the goats for a sin offering:
verses.nlt_text: and a male goat for a sin offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Nahshon son of Amminadab.

verses.kjv_text: On the second day Nethaneel the son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, did offer:
verses.nlt_text: On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, leader of the tribe of Issachar, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: He offered {for} his offering one silver charger, the weight whereof {was} an hundred and thirty {shekels}, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering:
verses.nlt_text: His offering consisted of a silver platter weighing 3-1/4 pounds and a silver basin weighing 1-3/4 pounds (as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel). These were both filled with grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil.

verses.kjv_text: One spoon of gold of ten {shekels}, full of incense:
verses.nlt_text: He also brought a gold container weighing four ounces, which was filled with incense.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Nethaneel the son of Zuar.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Nethanel son of Zuar.

verses.kjv_text: On the third day Eliab the son of Helon, prince of the children of Zebulun, {did offer}:
verses.nlt_text: On the third day Eliab son of Helon, leader of the tribe of Zebulun, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: His offering {was} one silver charger, the weight whereof {was} an hundred and thirty {shekels}, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering:
verses.nlt_text: His offering consisted of a silver platter weighing 3-1/4 pounds and a silver basin weighing 1-3/4 pounds (as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel). These were both filled with grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil.

verses.kjv_text: One golden spoon of ten {shekels}, full of incense:
verses.nlt_text: He also brought a gold container weighing four ounces, which was filled with incense.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Eliab the son of Helon.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Eliab son of Helon.

verses.kjv_text: On the fourth day Elizur the son of Shedeur, prince of the children of Reuben, {did offer}:
verses.nlt_text: On the fourth day Elizur son of Shedeur, leader of the tribe of Reuben, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: His offering {was} one silver charger of the weight of an hundred and thirty {shekels}, one silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering:
verses.nlt_text: His offering consisted of a silver platter weighing 3-1/4 pounds and a silver basin weighing 1-3/4 pounds (as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel). These were both filled with grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Elizur the son of Shedeur.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Elizur son of Shedeur.

verses.kjv_text: On the fifth day Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai, prince of the children of Simeon, {did offer}:
verses.nlt_text: On the fifth day Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, leader of the tribe of Simeon, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

verses.kjv_text: On the sixth day Eliasaph the son of Deuel, prince of the children of Gad, {offered}:
verses.nlt_text: On the sixth day Eliasaph son of Deuel, leader of the tribe of Gad, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: His offering {was} one silver charger of the weight of an hundred and thirty {shekels}, a silver bowl of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meat offering:
verses.nlt_text: His offering consisted of a silver platter weighing 3-1/4 pounds and a silver basin weighing 1-3/4 pounds (as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel). These were both filled with grain offerings of choice flour moistened with olive oil.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Eliasaph son of Deuel.

verses.kjv_text: On the seventh day Elishama the son of Ammihud, prince of the children of Ephraim, {offered}:
verses.nlt_text: On the seventh day Elishama son of Ammihud, leader of the tribe of Ephraim, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Elishama the son of Ammihud.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Elishama son of Ammihud.

verses.kjv_text: On the eighth day {offered} Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur, prince of the children of Manasseh:
verses.nlt_text: On the eighth day Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, leader of the tribe of Manasseh, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

verses.kjv_text: On the ninth day Abidan the son of Gideoni, prince of the children of Benjamin, {offered}:
verses.nlt_text: On the ninth day Abidan son of Gideoni, leader of the tribe of Benjamin, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Abidan the son of Gideoni.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Abidan son of Gideoni.

verses.kjv_text: On the tenth day Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai, prince of the children of Dan, {offered}:
verses.nlt_text: On the tenth day Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, leader of the tribe of Dan, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

verses.kjv_text: On the eleventh day Pagiel the son of Ocran, prince of the children of Asher, {offered}:
verses.nlt_text: On the eleventh day Pagiel son of Ocran, leader of the tribe of Asher, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Pagiel the son of Ocran.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Pagiel son of Ocran.

verses.kjv_text: On the twelfth day Ahira the son of Enan, prince of the children of Naphtali, {offered}:
verses.nlt_text: On the twelfth day Ahira son of Enan, leader of the tribe of Naphtali, presented his offering.

verses.kjv_text: And for a sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he goats, five lambs of the first year: this {was} the offering of Ahira the son of Enan.
verses.nlt_text: For a peace offering he brought two bulls, five rams, five male goats, and five one-year-old male lambs. This was the offering brought by Ahira son of Enan.

verses.kjv_text: This {was} the dedication of the altar, in the day when it was anointed, by the princes of Israel: twelve chargers of silver, twelve silver bowls, twelve spoons of gold:
verses.nlt_text: So this was the dedication offering brought by the leaders of Israel at the time the altar was anointed: twelve silver platters, twelve silver basins, and twelve gold incense containers.

verses.kjv_text: Each charger of silver {weighing} an hundred and thirty {shekels}, each bowl seventy: all the silver vessels {weighed} two thousand and four hundred {shekels}, after the shekel of the sanctuary:
verses.nlt_text: Each silver platter weighed 3-1/4 pounds, and each silver basin weighed 1-1/4 pounds. The total weight of the silver was 60 pounds (as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel).

verses.kjv_text: The golden spoons {were} twelve, full of incense, {weighing} ten {shekels} apiece, after the shekel of the sanctuary: all the gold of the spoons {was} an hundred and twenty {shekels}.
verses.nlt_text: Each of the twelve gold containers that was filled with incense weighed four ounces (as measured by the weight of the sanctuary shekel). The total weight of the gold was three pounds.

verses.kjv_text: All the oxen for the burnt offering {were} twelve bullocks, the rams twelve, the lambs of the first year twelve, with their meat offering: and the kids of the goats for sin offering twelve.
verses.nlt_text: Twelve young bulls, twelve rams, and twelve one-year-old male lambs were donated for the burnt offerings, along with their prescribed grain offerings. Twelve male goats were brought for the sin offerings.

verses.kjv_text: And all the oxen for the sacrifice of the peace offerings {were} twenty and four bullocks, the rams sixty, the he goats sixty, the lambs of the first year sixty. This {was} the dedication of the altar, after that it was anointed.
verses.nlt_text: Twenty-four bulls, sixty rams, sixty male goats, and sixty one-year-old male lambs were donated for the peace offerings. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

verses.kjv_text: And when Moses was gone into the tabernacle of the congregation to speak with him, then he heard the voice of one speaking unto him from off the mercy seat that {was} upon the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubims: and he spake unto him. {with him: that is, with God}
verses.nlt_text: Whenever Moses went into the Tabernacle to speak with the LORD, he heard the voice speaking to him from between the two cherubim above the Ark's cover-- the place of atonement-- that rests on the Ark of the Covenant. The LORD spoke to him from there.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.nlt_text: The LORD said to Moses,

verses.kjv_text: Speak unto Aaron, and say unto him, When thou lightest the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light over against the candlestick.
verses.nlt_text: "Give Aaron the following instructions: When you set up the seven lamps in the lampstand, place them so their light shines forward in front of the lampstand."

verses.kjv_text: And Aaron did so; he lighted the lamps thereof over against the candlestick, as the LORD commanded Moses.
verses.nlt_text: So Aaron did this. He set up the seven lamps so they reflected their light forward, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

verses.kjv_text: And this work of the candlestick {was of} beaten gold, unto the shaft thereof, unto the flowers thereof, {was} beaten work: according unto the pattern which the LORD had shewed Moses, so he made the candlestick.
verses.nlt_text: The entire lampstand, from its base to its decorative blossoms, was made of beaten gold. It was built according to the exact design the LORD had shown Moses.

verses.kjv_text: Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them.
verses.nlt_text: "Now set the Levites apart from the rest of the people of Israel and make them ceremonially clean.

verses.kjv_text: And thus shalt thou do unto them, to cleanse them: Sprinkle water of purifying upon them, and let them shave all their flesh, and let them wash their clothes, and {so} make themselves clean. {let them shave...: Heb. let them cause a razor to pass over, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Do this by sprinkling them with the water of purification, and have them shave their entire body and wash their clothing. Then they will be ceremonially clean.

verses.kjv_text: Then let them take a young bullock with his meat offering, {even} fine flour mingled with oil, and another young bullock shalt thou take for a sin offering.
verses.nlt_text: Have them bring a young bull and a grain offering of choice flour moistened with olive oil, along with a second young bull for a sin offering.

verses.kjv_text: And thou shalt bring the Levites before the tabernacle of the congregation: and thou shalt gather the whole assembly of the children of Israel together:
verses.nlt_text: Then assemble the whole community of Israel, and present the Levites at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

verses.kjv_text: And thou shalt bring the Levites before the LORD: and the children of Israel shall put their hands upon the Levites:
verses.nlt_text: When you present the Levites before the LORD, the people of Israel must lay their hands on them.

verses.kjv_text: And Aaron shall offer the Levites before the LORD {for} an offering of the children of Israel, that they may execute the service of the LORD. {offer: Heb. wave} {offering: Heb. wave offering} {they...: Heb. they may be to execute, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Raising his hands, Aaron must then present the Levites to the LORD as a special offering from the people of Israel, thus dedicating them to the LORD's service.

verses.kjv_text: And the Levites shall lay their hands upon the heads of the bullocks: and thou shalt offer the one {for} a sin offering, and the other {for} a burnt offering, unto the LORD, to make an atonement for the Levites.
verses.nlt_text: "Next the Levites will lay their hands on the heads of the young bulls. Present one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to purify the Levites and make them right with the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And thou shalt set the Levites before Aaron, and before his sons, and offer them {for} an offering unto the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: Then have the Levites stand in front of Aaron and his sons, and raise your hands and present them as a special offering to the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: Thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the children of Israel: and the Levites shall be mine.
verses.nlt_text: In this way, you will set the Levites apart from the rest of the people of Israel, and the Levites will belong to me.

verses.kjv_text: And after that shall the Levites go in to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation: and thou shalt cleanse them, and offer them {for} an offering.
verses.nlt_text: After this, they may go into the Tabernacle to do their work, because you have purified them and presented them as a special offering.

verses.kjv_text: For they {are} wholly given unto me from among the children of Israel; instead of such as open every womb, {even instead of} the firstborn of all the children of Israel, have I taken them unto me.
verses.nlt_text: "Of all the people of Israel, the Levites are reserved for me. I have claimed them for myself in place of all the firstborn sons of the Israelites; I have taken the Levites as their substitutes.

verses.kjv_text: For all the firstborn of the children of Israel {are} mine, {both} man and beast: on the day that I smote every firstborn in the land of Egypt I sanctified them for myself.
verses.nlt_text: For all the firstborn males among the people of Israel are mine, both of people and of animals. I set them apart for myself on the day I struck down all the firstborn sons of the Egyptians.

verses.kjv_text: And I have taken the Levites for all the firstborn of the children of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, I have claimed the Levites in place of all the firstborn sons of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And I have given the Levites {as} a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the tabernacle of the congregation, and to make an atonement for the children of Israel: that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come nigh unto the sanctuary. {a gift: Heb. given}
verses.nlt_text: And of all the Israelites, I have assigned the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They will serve in the Tabernacle on behalf of the Israelites and make sacrifices to purify the people so no plague will strike them when they approach the sanctuary."

verses.kjv_text: And Moses, and Aaron, and all the congregation of the children of Israel, did to the Levites according unto all that the LORD commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so did the children of Israel unto them.
verses.nlt_text: So Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel dedicated the Levites, carefully following all the LORD's instructions to Moses.

verses.kjv_text: And the Levites were purified, and they washed their clothes; and Aaron offered them {as} an offering before the LORD; and Aaron made an atonement for them to cleanse them.
verses.nlt_text: The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes, and Aaron lifted them up and presented them to the LORD as a special offering. He then offered a sacrifice to purify them and make them right with the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And after that went the Levites in to do their service in the tabernacle of the congregation before Aaron, and before his sons: as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so did they unto them.
verses.nlt_text: After that the Levites went into the Tabernacle to perform their duties, assisting Aaron and his sons. So they carried out all the commands that the LORD gave Moses concerning the Levites.

verses.kjv_text: This {is it} that {belongeth} unto the Levites: from twenty and five years old and upward they shall go in to wait upon the service of the tabernacle of the congregation: {to...: Heb. to war the warfare of, etc}
verses.nlt_text: "This is the rule the Levites must follow: They must begin serving in the Tabernacle at the age of twenty-five,

verses.kjv_text: And from the age of fifty years they shall cease waiting upon the service {thereof}, and shall serve no more: {cease...: Heb. return from the warfare of the service}
verses.nlt_text: and they must retire at the age of fifty.

verses.kjv_text: But shall minister with their brethren in the tabernacle of the congregation, to keep the charge, and shall do no service. Thus shalt thou do unto the Levites touching their charge.
verses.nlt_text: After retirement they may assist their fellow Levites by serving as guards at the Tabernacle, but they may not officiate in the service. This is how you must assign duties to the Levites."

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they were come out of the land of Egypt, saying,
verses.nlt_text: A year after Israel's departure from Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai. In the first month of that year he said,

verses.kjv_text: Let the children of Israel also keep the passover at his appointed season.
verses.nlt_text: "Tell the Israelites to celebrate the Passover at the prescribed time,

verses.kjv_text: In the fourteenth day of this month, at even, ye shall keep it in his appointed season: according to all the rites of it, and according to all the ceremonies thereof, shall ye keep it. {at even: Heb. between the two evenings}
verses.nlt_text: at twilight on the fourteenth day of the first month. Be sure to follow all my decrees and regulations concerning this celebration."

verses.kjv_text: And Moses spake unto the children of Israel, that they should keep the passover.
verses.nlt_text: So Moses told the people to celebrate the Passover

verses.kjv_text: And they kept the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month at even in the wilderness of Sinai: according to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so did the children of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: in the wilderness of Sinai as twilight fell on the fourteenth day of the month. And they celebrated the festival there, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

verses.kjv_text: And there were certain men, who were defiled by the dead body of a man, that they could not keep the passover on that day: and they came before Moses and before Aaron on that day:
verses.nlt_text: But some of the men had been ceremonially defiled by touching a dead body, so they could not celebrate the Passover that day. They came to Moses and Aaron that day

verses.kjv_text: And those men said unto him, We {are} defiled by the dead body of a man: wherefore are we kept back, that we may not offer an offering of the LORD in his appointed season among the children of Israel?
verses.nlt_text: and said, "We have become ceremonially unclean by touching a dead body. But why should we be prevented from presenting the LORD's offering at the proper time with the rest of the Israelites?"

verses.kjv_text: And Moses said unto them, Stand still, and I will hear what the LORD will command concerning you.
verses.nlt_text: Moses answered, "Wait here until I have received instructions for you from the LORD."

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.nlt_text: This was the LORD's reply to Moses.

verses.kjv_text: Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If any man of you or of your posterity shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or {be} in a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: "Give the following instructions to the people of Israel: If any of the people now or in future generations are ceremonially unclean at Passover time because of touching a dead body, or if they are on a journey and cannot be present at the ceremony, they may still celebrate the LORD's Passover.

verses.kjv_text: The fourteenth day of the second month at even they shall keep it, {and} eat it with unleavened bread and bitter {herbs}.
verses.nlt_text: They must offer the Passover sacrifice one month later, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the second month. They must eat the Passover lamb at that time with bitter salad greens and bread made without yeast.

verses.kjv_text: They shall leave none of it unto the morning, nor break any bone of it: according to all the ordinances of the passover they shall keep it.
verses.nlt_text: They must not leave any of the lamb until the next morning, and they must not break any of its bones. They must follow all the normal regulations concerning the Passover.

verses.kjv_text: But the man that {is} clean, and is not in a journey, and forbeareth to keep the passover, even the same soul shall be cut off from among his people: because he brought not the offering of the LORD in his appointed season, that man shall bear his sin.
verses.nlt_text: "But those who neglect to celebrate the Passover at the regular time, even though they are ceremonially clean and not away on a trip, will be cut off from the community of Israel. If they fail to present the LORD's offering at the proper time, they will suffer the consequences of their guilt.

verses.kjv_text: And if a stranger shall sojourn among you, and will keep the passover unto the LORD; according to the ordinance of the passover, and according to the manner thereof, so shall he do: ye shall have one ordinance, both for the stranger, and for him that was born in the land.
verses.nlt_text: And if foreigners living among you want to celebrate the Passover to the LORD, they must follow these same decrees and regulations. The same laws apply both to native-born Israelites and to the foreigners living among you."

verses.kjv_text: And on the day that the tabernacle was reared up the cloud covered the tabernacle, {namely}, the tent of the testimony: and at even there was upon the tabernacle as it were the appearance of fire, until the morning.
verses.nlt_text: On the day the Tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered it. But from evening until morning the cloud over the Tabernacle looked like a pillar of fire.

verses.kjv_text: So it was alway: the cloud covered it {by day}, and the appearance of fire by night.
verses.nlt_text: This was the regular pattern-- at night the cloud that covered the Tabernacle had the appearance of fire.

verses.kjv_text: And when the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, then after that the children of Israel journeyed: and in the place where the cloud abode, there the children of Israel pitched their tents.
verses.nlt_text: Whenever the cloud lifted from over the sacred tent, the people of Israel would break camp and follow it. And wherever the cloud settled, the people of Israel would set up camp.

verses.kjv_text: At the commandment of the LORD the children of Israel journeyed, and at the commandment of the LORD they pitched: as long as the cloud abode upon the tabernacle they rested in their tents.
verses.nlt_text: In this way, they traveled and camped at the LORD's command wherever he told them to go. Then they remained in their camp as long as the cloud stayed over the Tabernacle.

verses.kjv_text: And when the cloud tarried long upon the tabernacle many days, then the children of Israel kept the charge of the LORD, and journeyed not. {tarried...: Heb. prolonged}
verses.nlt_text: If the cloud remained over the Tabernacle for a long time, the Israelites stayed and performed their duty to the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And {so} it was, when the cloud was a few days upon the tabernacle; according to the commandment of the LORD they abode in their tents, and according to the commandment of the LORD they journeyed.
verses.nlt_text: Sometimes the cloud would stay over the Tabernacle for only a few days, so the people would stay for only a few days, as the LORD commanded. Then at the LORD's command they would break camp and move on.

verses.kjv_text: And {so} it was, when the cloud abode from even unto the morning, and {that} the cloud was taken up in the morning, then they journeyed: whether {it was} by day or by night that the cloud was taken up, they journeyed. {abode: Heb. was}
verses.nlt_text: Sometimes the cloud stayed only overnight and lifted the next morning. But day or night, when the cloud lifted, the people broke camp and moved on.

verses.kjv_text: Or {whether it were} two days, or a month, or a year, that the cloud tarried upon the tabernacle, remaining thereon, the children of Israel abode in their tents, and journeyed not: but when it was taken up, they journeyed.
verses.nlt_text: Whether the cloud stayed above the Tabernacle for two days, a month, or a year, the people of Israel stayed in camp and did not move on. But as soon as it lifted, they broke camp and moved on.

verses.kjv_text: At the commandment of the LORD they rested in the tents, and at the commandment of the LORD they journeyed: they kept the charge of the LORD, at the commandment of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
verses.nlt_text: So they camped or traveled at the LORD's command, and they did whatever the LORD told them through Moses.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Now the LORD said to Moses,

verses.kjv_text: Make thee two trumpets of silver; of a whole piece shalt thou make them: that thou mayest use them for the calling of the assembly, and for the journeying of the camps.
verses.nlt_text: "Make two trumpets of hammered silver for calling the community to assemble and for signaling the breaking of camp.

verses.kjv_text: And when they shall blow with them, all the assembly shall assemble themselves to thee at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
verses.nlt_text: When both trumpets are blown, everyone must gather before you at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

verses.kjv_text: And if they blow {but} with one {trumpet}, then the princes, {which are} heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather themselves unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: But if only one trumpet is blown, then only the leaders-- the heads of the clans of Israel-- must present themselves to you.

verses.kjv_text: When ye blow an alarm, then the camps that lie on the east parts shall go forward.
verses.nlt_text: "When you sound the signal to move on, the tribes camped on the east side of the Tabernacle must break camp and move forward.

verses.kjv_text: When ye blow an alarm the second time, then the camps that lie on the south side shall take their journey: they shall blow an alarm for their journeys.
verses.nlt_text: When you sound the signal a second time, the tribes camped on the south will follow. You must sound short blasts as the signal for moving on.

verses.kjv_text: But when the congregation is to be gathered together, ye shall blow, but ye shall not sound an alarm.
verses.nlt_text: But when you call the people to an assembly, blow the trumpets with a different signal.

verses.kjv_text: And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow with the trumpets; and they shall be to you for an ordinance for ever throughout your generations.
verses.nlt_text: Only the priests, Aaron's descendants, are allowed to blow the trumpets. This is a permanent law for you, to be observed from generation to generation.

verses.kjv_text: And if ye go to war in your land against the enemy that oppresseth you, then ye shall blow an alarm with the trumpets; and ye shall be remembered before the LORD your God, and ye shall be saved from your enemies.
verses.nlt_text: "When you arrive in your own land and go to war against your enemies who attack you, sound the alarm with the trumpets. Then the LORD your God will remember you and rescue you from your enemies.

verses.kjv_text: Also in the day of your gladness, and in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; that they may be to you for a memorial before your God: I {am} the LORD your God.
verses.nlt_text: Blow the trumpets in times of gladness, too, sounding them at your annual festivals and at the beginning of each month. And blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and peace offerings. The trumpets will remind the LORD your God of his covenant with you. I am the LORD your God."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass on the twentieth {day} of the second month, in the second year, that the cloud was taken up from off the tabernacle of the testimony.
verses.nlt_text: In the second year after Israel's departure from Egypt-- on the twentieth day of the second month-- the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Covenant.

verses.kjv_text: And the children of Israel took their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Paran.
verses.nlt_text: So the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai and traveled on from place to place until the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.

verses.kjv_text: And they first took their journey according to the commandment of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
verses.nlt_text: When the people set out for the first time, following the instructions the LORD had given through Moses,

verses.kjv_text: In the first {place} went the standard of the camp of the children of Judah according to their armies: and over his host {was} Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
verses.nlt_text: Judah's troops led the way. They marched behind their banner, and their leader was Nahshon son of Amminadab.

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Issachar {was} Nethaneel the son of Zuar.
verses.nlt_text: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Issachar, led by Nethanel son of Zuar,

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Zebulun {was} Eliab the son of Helon.
verses.nlt_text: and the troops of the tribe of Zebulun, led by Eliab son of Helon.

verses.kjv_text: And the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari set forward, bearing the tabernacle.
verses.nlt_text: Then the Tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonite and Merarite divisions of the Levites were next in the line of march, carrying the Tabernacle with them.

verses.kjv_text: And the standard of the camp of Reuben set forward according to their armies: and over his host {was} Elizur the son of Shedeur.
verses.nlt_text: Reuben's troops went next, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elizur son of Shedeur.

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Simeon {was} Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.
verses.nlt_text: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Simeon, led by Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai,

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Gad {was} Eliasaph the son of Deuel.
verses.nlt_text: and the troops of the tribe of Gad, led by Eliasaph son of Deuel.

verses.kjv_text: And the Kohathites set forward, bearing the sanctuary: and {the other} did set up the tabernacle against they came. {the other: that is, the Gershonites and the Merarites}
verses.nlt_text: Next came the Kohathite division of the Levites, carrying the sacred objects from the Tabernacle. Before they arrived at the next camp, the Tabernacle would already be set up at its new location.

verses.kjv_text: And the standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim set forward according to their armies: and over his host {was} Elishama the son of Ammihud.
verses.nlt_text: Ephraim's troops went next, marching behind their banner. Their leader was Elishama son of Ammihud.

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Manasseh {was} Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.
verses.nlt_text: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Manasseh, led by Gamaliel son of Pedahzur,

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Benjamin {was} Abidan the son of Gideoni.
verses.nlt_text: and the troops of the tribe of Benjamin, led by Abidan son of Gideoni.

verses.kjv_text: And the standard of the camp of the children of Dan set forward, {which was} the rereward of all the camps throughout their hosts: and over his host {was} Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
verses.nlt_text: Dan's troops went last, marching behind their banner and serving as the rear guard for all the tribal camps. Their leader was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Asher {was} Pagiel the son of Ocran.
verses.nlt_text: They were joined by the troops of the tribe of Asher, led by Pagiel son of Ocran,

verses.kjv_text: And over the host of the tribe of the children of Naphtali {was} Ahira the son of Enan.
verses.nlt_text: and the troops of the tribe of Naphtali, led by Ahira son of Enan.

verses.kjv_text: Thus {were} the journeyings of the children of Israel according to their armies, when they set forward. {Thus: Heb. These}
verses.nlt_text: This was the order in which the Israelites marched, division by division.

verses.kjv_text: And Moses said unto Hobab, the son of Raguel the Midianite, Moses' father in law, We are journeying unto the place of which the LORD said, I will give it you: come thou with us, and we will do thee good: for the LORD hath spoken good concerning Israel.
verses.nlt_text: One day Moses said to his brother-in-law, Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, "We are on our way to the place the LORD promised us, for he said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised wonderful blessings for Israel!"

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto him, I will not go; but I will depart to mine own land, and to my kindred.
verses.nlt_text: But Hobab replied, "No, I will not go. I must return to my own land and family."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Leave us not, I pray thee; forasmuch as thou knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness, and thou mayest be to us instead of eyes.
verses.nlt_text: "Please don't leave us," Moses pleaded. "You know the places in the wilderness where we should camp. Come, be our guide.

verses.kjv_text: And it shall be, if thou go with us, yea, it shall be, that what goodness the LORD shall do unto us, the same will we do unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: If you do, we'll share with you all the blessings the LORD gives us."

verses.kjv_text: And they departed from the mount of the LORD three days' journey: and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them in the three days' journey, to search out a resting place for them.
verses.nlt_text: They marched for three days after leaving the mountain of the LORD, with the Ark of the LORD's Covenant moving ahead of them to show them where to stop and rest.

verses.kjv_text: And the cloud of the LORD {was} upon them by day, when they went out of the camp.
verses.nlt_text: As they moved on each day, the cloud of the LORD hovered over them.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said, Rise up, LORD, and let thine enemies be scattered; and let them that hate thee flee before thee.
verses.nlt_text: And whenever the Ark set out, Moses would shout, "Arise, O LORD, and let your enemies be scattered! Let them flee before you!"

verses.kjv_text: And when it rested, he said, Return, O LORD, unto the many thousands of Israel. {many thousands: Heb. ten thousand thousands}
verses.nlt_text: And when the Ark was set down, he would say, "Return, O LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel!"

verses.kjv_text: And {when} the people complained, it displeased the LORD: and the LORD heard {it}; and his anger was kindled; and the fire of the LORD burnt among them, and consumed {them that were} in the uttermost parts of the camp. {complained: or, were as it were complainers} {it displeased: Heb. it was evil in the ears of}
verses.nlt_text: Soon the people began to complain about their hardship, and the LORD heard everything they said. Then the LORD's anger blazed against them, and he sent a fire to rage among them, and he destroyed some of the people in the outskirts of the camp.

verses.kjv_text: And the people cried unto Moses; and when Moses prayed unto the LORD, the fire was quenched. {was...: Heb. sunk}
verses.nlt_text: Then the people screamed to Moses for help, and when he prayed to the LORD, the fire stopped.

verses.kjv_text: And he called the name of the place Taberah: because the fire of the LORD burnt among them. {Taberah: that is, A burning}
verses.nlt_text: After that, the area was known as Taberah (which means "the place of burning"), because fire from the LORD had burned among them there.

verses.kjv_text: And the mixt multitude that {was} among them fell a lusting: and the children of Israel also wept again, and said, Who shall give us flesh to eat? {fell...: Heb. lusted a lust} {wept...: Heb. returned and wept}
verses.nlt_text: Then the foreign rabble who were traveling with the Israelites began to crave the good things of Egypt. And the people of Israel also began to complain. "Oh, for some meat!" they exclaimed.

verses.kjv_text: We remember the fish, which we did eat in Egypt freely; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlick:
verses.nlt_text: "We remember the fish we used to eat for free in Egypt. And we had all the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic we wanted.

verses.kjv_text: But now our soul {is} dried away: {there is} nothing at all, beside this manna, {before} our eyes.
verses.nlt_text: But now our appetites are gone. All we ever see is this manna!"

verses.kjv_text: And the manna {was} as coriander seed, and the colour thereof as the colour of bdellium. {colour thereof...: Heb. eye of it as the eye of}
verses.nlt_text: The manna looked like small coriander seeds, and it was pale yellow like gum resin.

verses.kjv_text: {And} the people went about, and gathered {it}, and ground {it} in mills, or beat {it} in a mortar, and baked {it} in pans, and made cakes of it: and the taste of it was as the taste of fresh oil.
verses.nlt_text: The people would go out and gather it from the ground. They made flour by grinding it with hand mills or pounding it in mortars. Then they boiled it in a pot and made it into flat cakes. These cakes tasted like pastries baked with olive oil.

verses.kjv_text: And when the dew fell upon the camp in the night, the manna fell upon it.
verses.nlt_text: The manna came down on the camp with the dew during the night.

verses.kjv_text: Then Moses heard the people weep throughout their families, every man in the door of his tent: and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly; Moses also was displeased.
verses.nlt_text: Moses heard all the families standing in the doorways of their tents whining, and the LORD became extremely angry. Moses was also very aggravated.

verses.kjv_text: And Moses said unto the LORD, Wherefore hast thou afflicted thy servant? and wherefore have I not found favour in thy sight, that thou layest the burden of all this people upon me?
verses.nlt_text: And Moses said to the LORD, "Why are you treating me, your servant, so harshly? Have mercy on me! What did I do to deserve the burden of all these people?

verses.kjv_text: Have I conceived all this people? have I begotten them, that thou shouldest say unto me, Carry them in thy bosom, as a nursing father beareth the sucking child, unto the land which thou swarest unto their fathers?
verses.nlt_text: Did I give birth to them? Did I bring them into the world? Why did you tell me to carry them in my arms like a mother carries a nursing baby? How can I carry them to the land you swore to give their ancestors?

verses.kjv_text: Whence should I have flesh to give unto all this people? for they weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.
verses.nlt_text: Where am I supposed to get meat for all these people? They keep whining to me, saying, 'Give us meat to eat!'

verses.kjv_text: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because {it is} too heavy for me.
verses.nlt_text: I can't carry all these people by myself! The load is far too heavy!

verses.kjv_text: And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness.
verses.nlt_text: If this is how you intend to treat me, just go ahead and kill me. Do me a favor and spare me this misery!"

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Gather unto me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them unto the tabernacle of the congregation, that they may stand there with thee.
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Gather before me seventy men who are recognized as elders and leaders of Israel. Bring them to the Tabernacle to stand there with you.

verses.kjv_text: And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which {is} upon thee, and will put {it} upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear {it} not thyself alone.
verses.nlt_text: I will come down and talk to you there. I will take some of the Spirit that is upon you, and I will put the Spirit upon them also. They will bear the burden of the people along with you, so you will not have to carry it alone.

verses.kjv_text: And say thou unto the people, Sanctify yourselves against to morrow, and ye shall eat flesh: for ye have wept in the ears of the LORD, saying, Who shall give us flesh to eat? for {it was} well with us in Egypt: therefore the LORD will give you flesh, and ye shall eat.
verses.nlt_text: "And say to the people, 'Purify yourselves, for tomorrow you will have meat to eat. You were whining, and the LORD heard you when you cried, "Oh, for some meat! We were better off in Egypt!" Now the LORD will give you meat, and you will have to eat it.

verses.kjv_text: Ye shall not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days;
verses.nlt_text: And it won't be for just a day or two, or for five or ten or even twenty.

verses.kjv_text: {But} even a whole month, until it come out at your nostrils, and it be loathsome unto you: because that ye have despised the LORD which {is} among you, and have wept before him, saying, Why came we forth out of Egypt? {whole...: Heb. month of days}
verses.nlt_text: You will eat it for a whole month until you gag and are sick of it. For you have rejected the LORD, who is here among you, and you have whined to him, saying, "Why did we ever leave Egypt?" '"

verses.kjv_text: And Moses said, The people, among whom I {am}, {are} six hundred thousand footmen; and thou hast said, I will give them flesh, that they may eat a whole month.
verses.nlt_text: But Moses responded to the LORD, "There are 600,000 foot soldiers here with me, and yet you say, 'I will give them meat for a whole month!'

verses.kjv_text: Shall the flocks and the herds be slain for them, to suffice them? or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to suffice them?
verses.nlt_text: Even if we butchered all our flocks and herds, would that satisfy them? Even if we caught all the fish in the sea, would that be enough?"

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Is the LORD'S hand waxed short? thou shalt see now whether my word shall come to pass unto thee or not.
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said to Moses, "Has my arm lost its power? Now you will see whether or not my word comes true!"

verses.kjv_text: And Moses went out, and told the people the words of the LORD, and gathered the seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle.
verses.nlt_text: So Moses went out and reported the LORD's words to the people. He gathered the seventy elders and stationed them around the Tabernacle.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD came down in a cloud, and spake unto him, and took of the spirit that {was} upon him, and gave {it} unto the seventy elders: and it came to pass, {that}, when the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, and did not cease.
verses.nlt_text: And the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. Then he gave the seventy elders the same Spirit that was upon Moses. And when the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied. But this never happened again.

verses.kjv_text: But there remained two {of the} men in the camp, the name of the one {was} Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the spirit rested upon them; and they {were} of them that were written, but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.
verses.nlt_text: Two men, Eldad and Medad, had stayed behind in the camp. They were listed among the elders, but they had not gone out to the Tabernacle. Yet the Spirit rested upon them as well, so they prophesied there in the camp.

verses.kjv_text: And there ran a young man, and told Moses, and said, Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.
verses.nlt_text: A young man ran and reported to Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"

verses.kjv_text: And Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, {one} of his young men, answered and said, My lord Moses, forbid them.
verses.nlt_text: Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' assistant since his youth, protested, "Moses, my master, make them stop!"

verses.kjv_text: And Moses said unto him, Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD'S people were prophets, {and} that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!
verses.nlt_text: But Moses replied, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets and that the LORD would put his Spirit upon them all!"

verses.kjv_text: And Moses gat him into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: Then Moses returned to the camp with the elders of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And there went forth a wind from the LORD, and brought quails from the sea, and let {them} fall by the camp, as it were a day's journey on this side, and as it were a day's journey on the other side, round about the camp, and as it were two cubits {high} upon the face of the earth. {as it were a day's...: Heb. as it were the way of a day}
verses.nlt_text: Now the LORD sent a wind that brought quail from the sea and let them fall all around the camp. For miles in every direction there were quail flying about three feet above the ground.

verses.kjv_text: And the people stood up all that day, and all {that} night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quails: he that gathered least gathered ten homers: and they spread {them} all abroad for themselves round about the camp.
verses.nlt_text: So the people went out and caught quail all that day and throughout the night and all the next day, too. No one gathered less than fifty bushels! They spread the quail all around the camp to dry.

verses.kjv_text: And while the flesh {was} yet between their teeth, ere it was chewed, the wrath of the LORD was kindled against the people, and the LORD smote the people with a very great plague.
verses.nlt_text: But while they were gorging themselves on the meat-- while it was still in their mouths-- the anger of the LORD blazed against the people, and he struck them with a severe plague.

verses.kjv_text: And he called the name of that place Kibrothhattaavah: because there they buried the people that lusted. {Kibrothhattaavah: that is, The graves of lust}
verses.nlt_text: So that place was called Kibroth-hattaavah (which means "graves of gluttony") because there they buried the people who had craved meat from Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: {And} the people journeyed from Kibrothhattaavah unto Hazeroth; and abode at Hazeroth. {abode at: Heb. they were in}
verses.nlt_text: From Kibroth-hattaavah the Israelites traveled to Hazeroth, where they stayed for some time.

verses.kjv_text: And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman. {Ethiopian: or, Cushite} {married: Heb. taken}
verses.nlt_text: While they were at Hazeroth, Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because he had married a Cushite woman.

verses.kjv_text: And they said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard {it}.
verses.nlt_text: They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Hasn't he spoken through us, too?" But the LORD heard them.

verses.kjv_text: (Now the man Moses {was} very meek, above all the men which {were} upon the face of the earth.)
verses.nlt_text: (Now Moses was very humble-- more humble than any other person on earth.)

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake suddenly unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, Come out ye three unto the tabernacle of the congregation. And they three came out.
verses.nlt_text: So immediately the LORD called to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam and said, "Go out to the Tabernacle, all three of you!" So the three of them went to the Tabernacle.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood {in} the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam: and they both came forth.
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD descended in the pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tabernacle. "Aaron and Miriam!" he called, and they stepped forward.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, {I} the LORD will make myself known unto him in a vision, {and} will speak unto him in a dream.
verses.nlt_text: And the LORD said to them, "Now listen to what I say: "If there were prophets among you, I, the LORD, would reveal myself in visions. I would speak to them in dreams.

verses.kjv_text: My servant Moses {is} not so, who {is} faithful in all mine house.
verses.nlt_text: But not with my servant Moses. Of all my house, he is the one I trust.

verses.kjv_text: With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the LORD shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
verses.nlt_text: I speak to him face to face, clearly, and not in riddles! He sees the LORD as he is. So why were you not afraid to criticize my servant Moses?"

verses.kjv_text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against them; and he departed.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD was very angry with them, and he departed.

verses.kjv_text: And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam {became} leprous, {white} as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, {she was} leprous.
verses.nlt_text: As the cloud moved from above the Tabernacle, there stood Miriam, her skin as white as snow from leprosy. When Aaron saw what had happened to her,

verses.kjv_text: And Aaron said unto Moses, Alas, my lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sin upon us, wherein we have done foolishly, and wherein we have sinned.
verses.nlt_text: he cried out to Moses, "Oh, my master! Please don't punish us for this sin we have so foolishly committed.

verses.kjv_text: Let her not be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he cometh out of his mother's womb.
verses.nlt_text: Don't let her be like a stillborn baby, already decayed at birth."

verses.kjv_text: And Moses cried unto the LORD, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.
verses.nlt_text: So Moses cried out to the LORD, "O God, I beg you, please heal her!"

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in {again}.
verses.nlt_text: But the LORD said to Moses, "If her father had done nothing more than spit in her face, wouldn't she be defiled for seven days? So keep her outside the camp for seven days, and after that she may be accepted back."

verses.kjv_text: And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in {again}.
verses.nlt_text: So Miriam was kept outside the camp for seven days, and the people waited until she was brought back before they traveled again.

verses.kjv_text: And afterward the people removed from Hazeroth, and pitched in the wilderness of Paran.
verses.nlt_text: Then they left Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,
verses.nlt_text: The LORD now said to Moses,

verses.kjv_text: Send thou men, that they may search the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel: of every tribe of their fathers shall ye send a man, every one a ruler among them.
verses.nlt_text: "Send out men to explore the land of Canaan, the land I am giving to the Israelites. Send one leader from each of the twelve ancestral tribes."

verses.kjv_text: And Moses by the commandment of the LORD sent them from the wilderness of Paran: all those men {were} heads of the children of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: So Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He sent out twelve men, all tribal leaders of Israel, from their camp in the wilderness of Paran.

verses.kjv_text: And these {were} their names: of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.
verses.nlt_text: These were the tribes and the names of their leaders: Tribe Leader Reuben Shammua son of Zaccur

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.
verses.nlt_text: Simeon Shaphat son of Hori

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
verses.nlt_text: Judah Caleb son of Jephunneh

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.
verses.nlt_text: Issachar Igal son of Joseph

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun. {Oshea: also called, Joshua}
verses.nlt_text: Ephraim Hoshea son of Nun

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.
verses.nlt_text: Benjamin Palti son of Raphu

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.
verses.nlt_text: Zebulun Gaddiel son of Sodi

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Joseph, {namely}, of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.
verses.nlt_text: Manasseh son of Joseph Gaddi son of Susi

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
verses.nlt_text: Dan Ammiel son of Gemalli

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.
verses.nlt_text: Asher Sethur son of Michael

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.
verses.nlt_text: Naphtali Nahbi son of Vophsi

verses.kjv_text: Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.
verses.nlt_text: Gad Geuel son of Maki

verses.kjv_text: These {are} the names of the men which Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua. {Oshea: also called Joshua} {Jehoshua: or, Joshua}
verses.nlt_text: These are the names of the men Moses sent out to explore the land. (Moses called Hoshea son of Nun by the name Joshua.)

verses.kjv_text: And Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, and said unto them, Get you up this {way} southward, and go up into the mountain:
verses.nlt_text: Moses gave the men these instructions as he sent them out to explore the land: "Go north through the Negev into the hill country.

verses.kjv_text: And see the land, what it {is}; and the people that dwelleth therein, whether they {be} strong or weak, few or many;
verses.nlt_text: See what the land is like, and find out whether the people living there are strong or weak, few or many.

verses.kjv_text: And what the land {is} that they dwell in, whether it {be} good or bad; and what cities {they be} that they dwell in, whether in tents, or in strong holds;
verses.nlt_text: See what kind of land they live in. Is it good or bad? Do their towns have walls, or are they unprotected like open camps?

verses.kjv_text: And what the land {is}, whether it {be} fat or lean, whether there be wood therein, or not. And be ye of good courage, and bring of the fruit of the land. Now the time {was} the time of the firstripe grapes.
verses.nlt_text: Is the soil fertile or poor? Are there many trees? Do your best to bring back samples of the crops you see." (It happened to be the season for harvesting the first ripe grapes.)

verses.kjv_text: So they went up, and searched the land from the wilderness of Zin unto Rehob, as men come to Hamath.
verses.nlt_text: So they went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, near Lebo-hamath.

verses.kjv_text: And they ascended by the south, and came unto Hebron; where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, {were}. (Now Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.)
verses.nlt_text: Going north, they passed through the Negev and arrived at Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai-- all descendants of Anak-- lived. (The ancient town of Hebron was founded seven years before the Egyptian city of Zoan.)

verses.kjv_text: And they came unto the brook of Eshcol, and cut down from thence a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bare it between two upon a staff; and {they brought} of the pomegranates, and of the figs. {brook: or, valley}
verses.nlt_text: When they came to the valley of Eshcol, they cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes so large that it took two of them to carry it on a pole between them! They also brought back samples of the pomegranates and figs.

verses.kjv_text: The place was called the brook Eshcol, because of the cluster of grapes which the children of Israel cut down from thence. {brook: or, valley} {Eshcol: that is, A cluster of grapes}
verses.nlt_text: That place was called the valley of Eshcol (which means "cluster"), because of the cluster of grapes the Israelite men cut there.

verses.kjv_text: And they returned from searching of the land after forty days.
verses.nlt_text: After exploring the land for forty days, the men returned

verses.kjv_text: And they went and came to Moses, and to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, unto the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and brought back word unto them, and unto all the congregation, and shewed them the fruit of the land.
verses.nlt_text: to Moses, Aaron, and the whole community of Israel at Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran. They reported to the whole community what they had seen and showed them the fruit they had taken from the land.

verses.kjv_text: And they told him, and said, We came unto the land whither thou sentest us, and surely it floweth with milk and honey; and this {is} the fruit of it.
verses.nlt_text: This was their report to Moses: "We entered the land you sent us to explore, and it is indeed a bountiful country-- a land flowing with milk and honey. Here is the kind of fruit it produces.

verses.kjv_text: Nevertheless the people {be} strong that dwell in the land, and the cities {are} walled, {and} very great: and moreover we saw the children of Anak there.
verses.nlt_text: But the people living there are powerful, and their towns are large and fortified. We even saw giants there, the descendants of Anak!

verses.kjv_text: The Amalekites dwell in the land of the south: and the Hittites, and the Jebusites, and the Amorites, dwell in the mountains: and the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast of Jordan.
verses.nlt_text: The Amalekites live in the Negev, and the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country. The Canaanites live along the coast of the Mediterranean Sea and along the Jordan Valley."

verses.kjv_text: And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
verses.nlt_text: But Caleb tried to quiet the people as they stood before Moses. "Let's go at once to take the land," he said. "We can certainly conquer it!"

verses.kjv_text: But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they {are} stronger than we.
verses.nlt_text: But the other men who had explored the land with him disagreed. "We can't go up against them! They are stronger than we are!"

verses.kjv_text: And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched unto the children of Israel, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, {is} a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it {are} men of a great stature. {men...: Heb. men of statures}
verses.nlt_text: So they spread this bad report about the land among the Israelites: "The land we traveled through and explored will devour anyone who goes to live there. All the people we saw were huge.

verses.kjv_text: And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, {which come} of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.
verses.nlt_text: We even saw giants there, the descendants of Anak. Next to them we felt like grasshoppers, and that's what they thought, too!"

verses.kjv_text: And all the congregation lifted up their voice, and cried; and the people wept that night.
verses.nlt_text: Then the whole community began weeping aloud, and they cried all night.

verses.kjv_text: And all the children of Israel murmured against Moses and against Aaron: and the whole congregation said unto them, Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! or would God we had died in this wilderness!
verses.nlt_text: Their voices rose in a great chorus of protest against Moses and Aaron. "If only we had died in Egypt, or even here in the wilderness!" they complained.

verses.kjv_text: And wherefore hath the LORD brought us unto this land, to fall by the sword, that our wives and our children should be a prey? were it not better for us to return into Egypt?
verses.nlt_text: "Why is the LORD taking us to this country only to have us die in battle? Our wives and our little ones will be carried off as plunder! Wouldn't it be better for us to return to Egypt?"

verses.kjv_text: And they said one to another, Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: Then they plotted among themselves, "Let's choose a new leader and go back to Egypt!"

verses.kjv_text: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: Then Moses and Aaron fell face down on the ground before the whole community of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, {which were} of them that searched the land, rent their clothes:
verses.nlt_text: Two of the men who had explored the land, Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, tore their clothing.

verses.kjv_text: And they spake unto all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, {is} an exceeding good land.
verses.nlt_text: They said to all the people of Israel, "The land we traveled through and explored is a wonderful land!

verses.kjv_text: If the LORD delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which floweth with milk and honey.
verses.nlt_text: And if the LORD is pleased with us, he will bring us safely into that land and give it to us. It is a rich land flowing with milk and honey.

verses.kjv_text: Only rebel not ye against the LORD, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they {are} bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the LORD {is} with us: fear them not. {defence: Heb. shadow}
verses.nlt_text: Do not rebel against the LORD, and don't be afraid of the people of the land. They are only helpless prey to us! They have no protection, but the LORD is with us! Don't be afraid of them!"

verses.kjv_text: But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of the LORD appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: But the whole community began to talk about stoning Joshua and Caleb. Then the glorious presence of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites at the Tabernacle.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Moses, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them?
verses.nlt_text: And the LORD said to Moses, "How long will these people treat me with contempt? Will they never believe me, even after all the miraculous signs I have done among them?

verses.kjv_text: I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a greater nation and mightier than they.
verses.nlt_text: I will disown them and destroy them with a plague. Then I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are!"

verses.kjv_text: And Moses said unto the LORD, Then the Egyptians shall hear {it}, (for thou broughtest up this people in thy might from among them;)
verses.nlt_text: But Moses objected. "What will the Egyptians think when they hear about it?" he asked the LORD. "They know full well the power you displayed in rescuing your people from Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And they will tell {it} to the inhabitants of this land: {for} they have heard that thou LORD {art} among this people, that thou LORD art seen face to face, and {that} thy cloud standeth over them, and {that} thou goest before them, by day time in a pillar of a cloud, and in a pillar of fire by night.
verses.nlt_text: Now if you destroy them, the Egyptians will send a report to the inhabitants of this land, who have already heard that you live among your people. They know, LORD, that you have appeared to your people face to face and that your pillar of cloud hovers over them. They know that you go before them in the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night.

verses.kjv_text: Now {if} thou shalt kill {all} this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of thee will speak, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Now if you slaughter all these people with a single blow, the nations that have heard of your fame will say,

verses.kjv_text: Because the LORD was not able to bring this people into the land which he sware unto them, therefore he hath slain them in the wilderness.
verses.nlt_text: 'The LORD was not able to bring them into the land he swore to give them, so he killed them in the wilderness.'

verses.kjv_text: And now, I beseech thee, let the power of my Lord be great, according as thou hast spoken, saying,
verses.nlt_text: "Please, Lord, prove that your power is as great as you have claimed. For you said,

verses.kjv_text: The LORD {is} longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression, and by no means clearing {the guilty}, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth {generation}.
verses.nlt_text: 'The LORD is slow to anger and filled with unfailing love, forgiving every kind of sin and rebellion. But he does not excuse the guilty. He lays the sins of the parents upon their children; the entire family is affected-- even children in the third and fourth generations.'

verses.kjv_text: Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according unto the greatness of thy mercy, and as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now. {until...: or, hitherto}
verses.nlt_text: In keeping with your magnificent, unfailing love, please pardon the sins of this people, just as you have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt."

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said, I have pardoned according to thy word:
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said, "I will pardon them as you have requested.

verses.kjv_text: But {as} truly {as} I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: But as surely as I live, and as surely as the earth is filled with the LORD's glory,

verses.kjv_text: Because all those men which have seen my glory, and my miracles, which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice;
verses.nlt_text: not one of these people will ever enter that land. They have all seen my glorious presence and the miraculous signs I performed both in Egypt and in the wilderness, but again and again they have tested me by refusing to listen to my voice.

verses.kjv_text: Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it: {Surely...: Heb. If they see the land}
verses.nlt_text: They will never even see the land I swore to give their ancestors. None of those who have treated me with contempt will ever see it.

verses.kjv_text: But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.
verses.nlt_text: But my servant Caleb has a different attitude than the others have. He has remained loyal to me, so I will bring him into the land he explored. His descendants will possess their full share of that land.

verses.kjv_text: (Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites dwelt in the valley.) To morrow turn you, and get you into the wilderness by the way of the Red sea.
verses.nlt_text: Now turn around, and don't go on toward the land where the Amalekites and Canaanites live. Tomorrow you must set out for the wilderness in the direction of the Red Sea. "

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and unto Aaron, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

verses.kjv_text: How long {shall I bear with} this evil congregation, which murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me.
verses.nlt_text: "How long must I put up with this wicked community and its complaints about me? Yes, I have heard the complaints the Israelites are making against me.

verses.kjv_text: Say unto them, {As truly as} I live, saith the LORD, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you:
verses.nlt_text: Now tell them this: 'As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you the very things I heard you say.

verses.kjv_text: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me,
verses.nlt_text: You will all drop dead in this wilderness! Because you complained against me, every one of you who is twenty years old or older and was included in the registration will die.

verses.kjv_text: Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, {concerning} which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. {sware: Heb. lifted up my hand}
verses.nlt_text: You will not enter and occupy the land I swore to give you. The only exceptions will be Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

verses.kjv_text: But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.
verses.nlt_text: " 'You said your children would be carried off as plunder. Well, I will bring them safely into the land, and they will enjoy what you have despised.

verses.kjv_text: But {as for} you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness.
verses.nlt_text: But as for you, you will drop dead in this wilderness.

verses.kjv_text: And your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your whoredoms, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness. {wander: or, feed}
verses.nlt_text: And your children will be like shepherds, wandering in the wilderness for forty years. In this way, they will pay for your faithlessness, until the last of you lies dead in the wilderness.

verses.kjv_text: After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, {even} forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, {even} forty years, and ye shall know my breach of promise. {breach...: or, altering of my purpose}
verses.nlt_text: " 'Because your men explored the land for forty days, you must wander in the wilderness for forty years-- a year for each day, suffering the consequences of your sins. Then you will discover what it is like to have me for an enemy.'
