verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said, What hast thou done? And Saul said, Because I saw that the people were scattered from me, and {that} thou camest not within the days appointed, and {that} the Philistines gathered themselves together at Michmash;
verses.nlt_text: but Samuel said, "What is this you have done?" Saul replied, "I saw my men scattering from me, and you didn't arrive when you said you would, and the Philistines are at Micmash ready for battle.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore said I, The Philistines will come down now upon me to Gilgal, and I have not made supplication unto the LORD: I forced myself therefore, and offered a burnt offering. {made...: Heb. intreated the face}
verses.nlt_text: So I said, 'The Philistines are ready to march against us at Gilgal, and I haven't even asked for the LORD's help!' So I felt compelled to offer the burnt offering myself before you came."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said to Saul, Thou hast done foolishly: thou hast not kept the commandment of the LORD thy God, which he commanded thee: for now would the LORD have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever.
verses.nlt_text: "How foolish!" Samuel exclaimed. "You have not kept the command the LORD your God gave you. Had you kept it, the LORD would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.

verses.kjv_text: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the LORD hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the LORD hath commanded him {to be} captain over his people, because thou hast not kept {that} which the LORD commanded thee.
verses.nlt_text: But now your kingdom must end, for the LORD has sought out a man after his own heart. The LORD has already appointed him to be the leader of his people, because you have not kept the LORD's command."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel arose, and gat him up from Gilgal unto Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul numbered the people {that were} present with him, about six hundred men. {present: Heb. found}
verses.nlt_text: Samuel then left Gilgal and went on his way, but the rest of the troops went with Saul to meet the army. They went up from Gilgal to Gibeah in the land of Benjamin. When Saul counted the men who were still with him, he found only 600 were left!

verses.kjv_text: And Saul, and Jonathan his son, and the people {that were} present with them, abode in Gibeah of Benjamin: but the Philistines encamped in Michmash. {present: Heb. found} {Gibeah: Heb. Geba}
verses.nlt_text: Saul and Jonathan and the troops with them were staying at Geba in the land of Benjamin. The Philistines set up their camp at Micmash.

verses.kjv_text: And the spoilers came out of the camp of the Philistines in three companies: one company turned unto the way {that leadeth to} Ophrah, unto the land of Shual:
verses.nlt_text: Three raiding parties soon left the camp of the Philistines. One went north toward Ophrah in the land of Shual,

verses.kjv_text: And another company turned the way {to} Bethhoron: and another company turned {to} the way of the border that looketh to the valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness.
verses.nlt_text: another went west to Beth-horon, and the third moved toward the border above the valley of Zeboim near the wilderness.

verses.kjv_text: Now there was no smith found throughout all the land of Israel: for the Philistines said, Lest the Hebrews make {them} swords or spears:
verses.nlt_text: There were no blacksmiths in the land of Israel in those days. The Philistines wouldn't allow them for fear they would make swords and spears for the Hebrews.

verses.kjv_text: But all the Israelites went down to the Philistines, to sharpen every man his share, and his coulter, and his axe, and his mattock.
verses.nlt_text: So whenever the Israelites needed to sharpen their plowshares, picks, axes, or sickles, they had to take them to a Philistine blacksmith.

verses.kjv_text: Yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the coulters, and for the forks, and for the axes, and to sharpen the goads. {a file: Heb. a file with mouths, or Heb. a pim, a third of a shekel} {sharpen: Heb. set}
verses.nlt_text: (The charges were as follows: a quarter of an ounce of silver for sharpening a plowshare or a pick, and an eighth of an ounce for sharpening an ax, a sickle, or an ox goad.)

verses.kjv_text: So it came to pass in the day of battle, that there was neither sword nor spear found in the hand of any of the people that {were} with Saul and Jonathan: but with Saul and with Jonathan his son was there found.
verses.nlt_text: So on the day of the battle none of the people of Israel had a sword or spear, except for Saul and Jonathan.

verses.kjv_text: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the passage of Michmash. {garrison: or, standing camp}
verses.nlt_text: The pass at Micmash had meanwhile been secured by a contingent of the Philistine army.

verses.kjv_text: Now it came to pass upon a day, that Jonathan the son of Saul said unto the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over to the Philistines' garrison, that {is} on the other side. But he told not his father. {it came...: or, there was a day}
verses.nlt_text: One day Jonathan said to his armor bearer, "Come on, let's go over to where the Philistines have their outpost." But Jonathan did not tell his father what he was doing.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul tarried in the uttermost part of Gibeah under a pomegranate tree which {is} in Migron: and the people that {were} with him {were} about six hundred men;
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Saul and his 600 men were camped on the outskirts of Gibeah, around the pomegranate tree at Migron.

verses.kjv_text: And Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the LORD'S priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod. And the people knew not that Jonathan was gone. {Ahiah: called Ahimelech}
verses.nlt_text: Among Saul's men was Ahijah the priest, who was wearing the ephod, the priestly vest. Ahijah was the son of Ichabod's brother Ahitub, son of Phinehas, son of Eli, the priest of the LORD who had served at Shiloh.No one realized that Jonathan had left the Israelite camp.

verses.kjv_text: And between the passages, by which Jonathan sought to go over unto the Philistines' garrison, {there was} a sharp rock on the one side, and a sharp rock on the other side: and the name of the one {was} Bozez, and the name of the other Seneh.
verses.nlt_text: To reach the Philistine outpost, Jonathan had to go down between two rocky cliffs that were called Bozez and Seneh.

verses.kjv_text: The forefront of the one {was} situate northward over against Michmash, and the other southward over against Gibeah. {forefront: Heb. tooth}
verses.nlt_text: The cliff on the north was in front of Micmash, and the one on the south was in front of Geba.

verses.kjv_text: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that the LORD will work for us: for {there is} no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few.
verses.nlt_text: "Let's go across to the outpost of those pagans," Jonathan said to his armor bearer. "Perhaps the LORD will help us, for nothing can hinder the LORD. He can win a battle whether he has many warriors or only a few!"

verses.kjv_text: And his armourbearer said unto him, Do all that {is} in thine heart: turn thee; behold, I {am} with thee according to thy heart.
verses.nlt_text: "Do what you think is best," the armor bearer replied. "I'm with you completely, whatever you decide."

verses.kjv_text: Then said Jonathan, Behold, we will pass over unto {these} men, and we will discover ourselves unto them.
verses.nlt_text: "All right then," Jonathan told him. "We will cross over and let them see us.

verses.kjv_text: If they say thus unto us, Tarry until we come to you; then we will stand still in our place, and will not go up unto them. {Tarry: Heb. Be still}
verses.nlt_text: If they say to us, 'Stay where you are or we'll kill you,' then we will stop and not go up to them.

verses.kjv_text: But if they say thus, Come up unto us; then we will go up: for the LORD hath delivered them into our hand: and this {shall be} a sign unto us.
verses.nlt_text: But if they say, 'Come on up and fight,' then we will go up. That will be the LORD's sign that he will help us defeat them."

verses.kjv_text: And both of them discovered themselves unto the garrison of the Philistines: and the Philistines said, Behold, the Hebrews come forth out of the holes where they had hid themselves.
verses.nlt_text: When the Philistines saw them coming, they shouted, "Look! The Hebrews are crawling out of their holes!"

verses.kjv_text: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for the LORD hath delivered them into the hand of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: Then the men from the outpost shouted to Jonathan, "Come on up here, and we'll teach you a lesson!" "Come on, climb right behind me," Jonathan said to his armor bearer, "for the LORD will help us defeat them!"

verses.kjv_text: And Jonathan climbed up upon his hands and upon his feet, and his armourbearer after him: and they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.
verses.nlt_text: So they climbed up using both hands and feet, and the Philistines fell before Jonathan, and his armor bearer killed those who came behind them.

verses.kjv_text: And that first slaughter, which Jonathan and his armourbearer made, was about twenty men, within as it were an half acre of land, {which} a yoke {of oxen might plow}. {an...: or, half a furrow of an acre of land}
verses.nlt_text: They killed some twenty men in all, and their bodies were scattered over about half an acre.

verses.kjv_text: And there was trembling in the host, in the field, and among all the people: the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled, and the earth quaked: so it was a very great trembling. {a very...: Heb. a trembling of God}
verses.nlt_text: Suddenly, panic broke out in the Philistine army, both in the camp and in the field, including even the outposts and raiding parties. And just then an earthquake struck, and everyone was terrified.

verses.kjv_text: And the watchmen of Saul in Gibeah of Benjamin looked; and, behold, the multitude melted away, and they went on beating down {one another}.
verses.nlt_text: Saul's lookouts in Gibeah of Benjamin saw a strange sight-- the vast army of Philistines began to melt away in every direction.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Saul unto the people that {were} with him, Number now, and see who is gone from us. And when they had numbered, behold, Jonathan and his armourbearer {were} not {there}.
verses.nlt_text: "Call the roll and find out who's missing," Saul ordered. And when they checked, they found that Jonathan and his armor bearer were gone.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said unto Ahiah, Bring hither the ark of God. For the ark of God was at that time with the children of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul shouted to Ahijah, "Bring the ephod here!" For at that time Ahijah was wearing the ephod in front of the Israelites.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, while Saul talked unto the priest, that the noise that {was} in the host of the Philistines went on and increased: and Saul said unto the priest, Withdraw thine hand. {noise: or, tumult}
verses.nlt_text: But while Saul was talking to the priest, the confusion in the Philistine camp grew louder and louder. So Saul said to the priest, "Never mind; let's get going!"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul and all the people that {were} with him assembled themselves, and they came to the battle: and, behold, every man's sword was against his fellow, {and there was} a very great discomfiture. {assembled...: Heb. were cried together}
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul and all his men rushed out to the battle and found the Philistines killing each other. There was terrible confusion everywhere.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover the Hebrews {that} were with the Philistines before that time, which went up with them into the camp {from the country} round about, even they also {turned} to be with the Israelites that {were} with Saul and Jonathan.
verses.nlt_text: Even the Hebrews who had previously gone over to the Philistine army revolted and joined in with Saul, Jonathan, and the rest of the Israelites.

verses.kjv_text: Likewise all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim, {when} they heard that the Philistines fled, even they also followed hard after them in the battle.
verses.nlt_text: Likewise, the men of Israel who were hiding in the hill country of Ephraim joined the chase when they saw the Philistines running away.

verses.kjv_text: So the LORD saved Israel that day: and the battle passed over unto Bethaven.
verses.nlt_text: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle continued to rage even beyond Beth-aven.

verses.kjv_text: And the men of Israel were distressed that day: for Saul had adjured the people, saying, Cursed {be} the man that eateth {any} food until evening, that I may be avenged on mine enemies. So none of the people tasted {any} food.
verses.nlt_text: Now the men of Israel were pressed to exhaustion that day, because Saul had placed them under an oath, saying, "Let a curse fall on anyone who eats before evening-- before I have full revenge on my enemies." So no one ate anything all day,

verses.kjv_text: And all {they of} the land came to a wood; and there was honey upon the ground.
verses.nlt_text: even though they had all found honeycomb on the ground in the forest.

verses.kjv_text: And when the people were come into the wood, behold, the honey dropped; but no man put his hand to his mouth: for the people feared the oath.
verses.nlt_text: They didn't dare touch the honey because they all feared the oath they had taken.

verses.kjv_text: But Jonathan heard not when his father charged the people with the oath: wherefore he put forth the end of the rod that {was} in his hand, and dipped it in an honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth; and his eyes were enlightened.
verses.nlt_text: But Jonathan had not heard his father's command, and he dipped the end of his stick into a piece of honeycomb and ate the honey. After he had eaten it, he felt refreshed.

verses.kjv_text: Then answered one of the people, and said, Thy father straitly charged the people with an oath, saying, Cursed {be} the man that eateth {any} food this day. And the people were faint. {faint: or, weary}
verses.nlt_text: But one of the men saw him and said, "Your father made the army take a strict oath that anyone who eats food today will be cursed. That is why everyone is weary and faint."

verses.kjv_text: Then said Jonathan, My father hath troubled the land: see, I pray you, how mine eyes have been enlightened, because I tasted a little of this honey.
verses.nlt_text: "My father has made trouble for us all!" Jonathan exclaimed. "A command like that only hurts us. See how refreshed I am now that I have eaten this little bit of honey.

verses.kjv_text: How much more, if haply the people had eaten freely to day of the spoil of their enemies which they found? for had there not been now a much greater slaughter among the Philistines?
verses.nlt_text: If the men had been allowed to eat freely from the food they found among our enemies, think how many more Philistines we could have killed!"

verses.kjv_text: And they smote the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon: and the people were very faint.
verses.nlt_text: They chased and killed the Philistines all day from Micmash to Aijalon, growing more and more faint.

verses.kjv_text: And the people flew upon the spoil, and took sheep, and oxen, and calves, and slew {them} on the ground: and the people did eat {them} with the blood.
verses.nlt_text: That evening they rushed for the battle plunder and butchered the sheep, goats, cattle, and calves, but they ate them without draining the blood.

verses.kjv_text: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against the LORD, in that they eat with the blood. And he said, Ye have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day. {transgressed: or, dealt treacherously}
verses.nlt_text: Someone reported to Saul, "Look, the men are sinning against the LORD by eating meat that still has blood in it." "That is very wrong," Saul said. "Find a large stone and roll it over here.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said, Disperse yourselves among the people, and say unto them, Bring me hither every man his ox, and every man his sheep, and slay {them} here, and eat; and sin not against the LORD in eating with the blood. And all the people brought every man his ox with him that night, and slew {them} there. {with him: Heb. in his hand}
verses.nlt_text: Then go out among the troops and tell them, 'Bring the cattle, sheep, and goats here to me. Kill them here, and drain the blood before you eat them. Do not sin against the LORD by eating meat with the blood still in it.' " So that night all the troops brought their animals and slaughtered them there.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul built an altar unto the LORD: the same was the first altar that he built unto the LORD. {the same...: Heb. that altar he began to build unto the LORD}
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first of the altars he built to the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said, Let us go down after the Philistines by night, and spoil them until the morning light, and let us not leave a man of them. And they said, Do whatsoever seemeth good unto thee. Then said the priest, Let us draw near hither unto God.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul said, "Let's chase the Philistines all night and plunder them until sunrise. Let's destroy every last one of them." His men replied, "We'll do whatever you think is best." But the priest said, "Let's ask God first."

verses.kjv_text: And Saul asked counsel of God, Shall I go down after the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into the hand of Israel? But he answered him not that day.
verses.nlt_text: So Saul asked God, "Should we go after the Philistines? Will you help us defeat them?" But God made no reply that day.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said, Draw ye near hither, all the chief of the people: and know and see wherein this sin hath been this day. {chief: Heb. corners}
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul said to the leaders, "Something's wrong! I want all my army commanders to come here. We must find out what sin was committed today.

verses.kjv_text: For, {as} the LORD liveth, which saveth Israel, though it be in Jonathan my son, he shall surely die. But {there was} not a man among all the people {that} answered him.
verses.nlt_text: I vow by the name of the LORD who rescued Israel that the sinner will surely die, even if it is my own son Jonathan!" But no one would tell him what the trouble was.

verses.kjv_text: Then said he unto all Israel, Be ye on one side, and I and Jonathan my son will be on the other side. And the people said unto Saul, Do what seemeth good unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul said, "Jonathan and I will stand over here, and all of you stand over there." And the people responded to Saul, "Whatever you think is best."

verses.kjv_text: Therefore Saul said unto the LORD God of Israel, Give a perfect {lot}. And Saul and Jonathan were taken: but the people escaped. {Give...: or, Shew the innocent} {escaped: Heb. went forth}
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul prayed, "O LORD, God of Israel, please show us who is guilty and who is innocent. " Then they cast sacred lots, and Jonathan and Saul were chosen as the guilty ones, and the people were declared innocent.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said, Cast {lots} between me and Jonathan my son. And Jonathan was taken.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul said, "Now cast lots again and choose between me and Jonathan." And Jonathan was shown to be the guilty one.

verses.kjv_text: Then Saul said to Jonathan, Tell me what thou hast done. And Jonathan told him, and said, I did but taste a little honey with the end of the rod that {was} in mine hand, {and}, lo, I must die.
verses.nlt_text: "Tell me what you have done," Saul demanded of Jonathan."I tasted a little honey," Jonathan admitted. "It was only a little bit on the end of my stick. Does that deserve death?"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul answered, God do so and more also: for thou shalt surely die, Jonathan.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes, Jonathan," Saul said, "you must die! May God strike me and even kill me if you do not die for this."

verses.kjv_text: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Israel? God forbid: {as} the LORD liveth, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he hath wrought with God this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.
verses.nlt_text: But the people broke in and said to Saul, "Jonathan has won this great victory for Israel. Should he die? Far from it! As surely as the LORD lives, not one hair on his head will be touched, for God helped him do a great deed today." So the people rescued Jonathan, and he was not put to death.

verses.kjv_text: Then Saul went up from following the Philistines: and the Philistines went to their own place.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul called back the army from chasing the Philistines, and the Philistines returned home.

verses.kjv_text: So Saul took the kingdom over Israel, and fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom, and against the kings of Zobah, and against the Philistines: and whithersoever he turned himself, he vexed {them}.
verses.nlt_text: Now when Saul had secured his grasp on Israel's throne, he fought against his enemies in every direction-- against Moab, Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines. And wherever he turned, he was victorious.

verses.kjv_text: And he gathered an host, and smote the Amalekites, and delivered Israel out of the hands of them that spoiled them. {gathered...: or, wrought mightily}
verses.nlt_text: He performed great deeds and conquered the Amalekites, saving Israel from all those who had plundered them.

verses.kjv_text: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchishua: and the names of his two daughters {were these}; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:
verses.nlt_text: Saul's sons included Jonathan, Ishbosheth, and Malkishua. He also had two daughters: Merab, who was older, and Michal.

verses.kjv_text: And the name of Saul's wife {was} Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host {was} Abner, the son of Ner, Saul's uncle. {Abner: Heb. Abiner}
verses.nlt_text: Saul's wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz. The commander of Saul's army was Abner, the son of Saul's uncle Ner.

verses.kjv_text: And Kish {was} the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner {was} the son of Abiel.
verses.nlt_text: Saul's father, Kish, and Abner's father, Ner, were both sons of Abiel.

verses.kjv_text: And there was sore war against the Philistines all the days of Saul: and when Saul saw any strong man, or any valiant man, he took him unto him.
verses.nlt_text: The Israelites fought constantly with the Philistines throughout Saul's lifetime. So whenever Saul observed a young man who was brave and strong, he drafted him into his army.

verses.kjv_text: Samuel also said unto Saul, The LORD sent me to anoint thee {to be} king over his people, over Israel: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: One day Samuel said to Saul, "It was the LORD who told me to anoint you as king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the LORD!

verses.kjv_text: Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I remember {that} which Amalek did to Israel, how he laid {wait} for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: This is what the LORD of Heaven's Armies has declared: I have decided to settle accounts with the nation of Amalek for opposing Israel when they came from Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.
verses.nlt_text: Now go and completely destroy the entire Amalekite nation-- men, women, children, babies, cattle, sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys."

verses.kjv_text: And Saul gathered the people together, and numbered them in Telaim, two hundred thousand footmen, and ten thousand men of Judah.
verses.nlt_text: So Saul mobilized his army at Telaim. There were 200,000 soldiers from Israel and 10,000 men from Judah.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul came to a city of Amalek, and laid wait in the valley. {laid...: or, fought}
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul and his army went to a town of the Amalekites and lay in wait in the valley.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said unto the Kenites, Go, depart, get you down from among the Amalekites, lest I destroy you with them: for ye shewed kindness to all the children of Israel, when they came up out of Egypt. So the Kenites departed from among the Amalekites.
verses.nlt_text: Saul sent this warning to the Kenites: "Move away from where the Amalekites live, or you will die with them. For you showed kindness to all the people of Israel when they came up from Egypt." So the Kenites packed up and left.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul smote the Amalekites from Havilah {until} thou comest to Shur, that {is} over against Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul slaughtered the Amalekites from Havilah all the way to Shur, east of Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: And he took Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and utterly destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.
verses.nlt_text: He captured Agag, the Amalekite king, but completely destroyed everyone else.

verses.kjv_text: But Saul and the people spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the oxen, and of the fatlings, and the lambs, and all {that was} good, and would not utterly destroy them: but every thing {that was} vile and refuse, that they destroyed utterly. {fatlings: or, second sort}
verses.nlt_text: Saul and his men spared Agag's life and kept the best of the sheep and goats, the cattle, the fat calves, and the lambs-- everything, in fact, that appealed to them. They destroyed only what was worthless or of poor quality.

verses.kjv_text: Then came the word of the LORD unto Samuel, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said to Samuel,

verses.kjv_text: It repenteth me that I have set up Saul {to be} king: for he is turned back from following me, and hath not performed my commandments. And it grieved Samuel; and he cried unto the LORD all night.
verses.nlt_text: "I am sorry that I ever made Saul king, for he has not been loyal to me and has refused to obey my command." Samuel was so deeply moved when he heard this that he cried out to the LORD all night.

verses.kjv_text: And when Samuel rose early to meet Saul in the morning, it was told Samuel, saying, Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he set him up a place, and is gone about, and passed on, and gone down to Gilgal.
verses.nlt_text: Early the next morning Samuel went to find Saul. Someone told him, "Saul went to the town of Carmel to set up a monument to himself; then he went on to Gilgal."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel came to Saul: and Saul said unto him, Blessed {be} thou of the LORD: I have performed the commandment of the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: When Samuel finally found him, Saul greeted him cheerfully. "May the LORD bless you," he said. "I have carried out the LORD's command!"

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said, What {meaneth} then this bleating of the sheep in mine ears, and the lowing of the oxen which I hear?
verses.nlt_text: "Then what is all the bleating of sheep and goats and the lowing of cattle I hear?" Samuel demanded.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said, They have brought them from the Amalekites: for the people spared the best of the sheep and of the oxen, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God; and the rest we have utterly destroyed.
verses.nlt_text: "It's true that the army spared the best of the sheep, goats, and cattle," Saul admitted. "But they are going to sacrifice them to the LORD your God. We have destroyed everything else."

verses.kjv_text: Then Samuel said unto Saul, Stay, and I will tell thee what the LORD hath said to me this night. And he said unto him, Say on.
verses.nlt_text: Then Samuel said to Saul, "Stop! Listen to what the LORD told me last night!" "What did he tell you?" Saul asked.

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said, When thou {wast} little in thine own sight, {wast} thou not {made} the head of the tribes of Israel, and the LORD anointed thee king over Israel?
verses.nlt_text: And Samuel told him, "Although you may think little of yourself, are you not the leader of the tribes of Israel? The LORD has anointed you king of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD sent thee on a journey, and said, Go and utterly destroy the sinners the Amalekites, and fight against them until they be consumed. {they...: Heb. they consume them}
verses.nlt_text: And the LORD sent you on a mission and told you, 'Go and completely destroy the sinners, the Amalekites, until they are all dead.'

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore then didst thou not obey the voice of the LORD, but didst fly upon the spoil, and didst evil in the sight of the LORD?
verses.nlt_text: Why haven't you obeyed the LORD? Why did you rush for the plunder and do what was evil in the LORD's sight?"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said unto Samuel, Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the LORD, and have gone the way which the LORD sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.
verses.nlt_text: "But I did obey the LORD," Saul insisted. "I carried out the mission he gave me. I brought back King Agag, but I destroyed everyone else.

verses.kjv_text: But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the LORD thy God in Gilgal.
verses.nlt_text: Then my troops brought in the best of the sheep, goats, cattle, and plunder to sacrifice to the LORD your God in Gilgal."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said, Hath the LORD {as great} delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey {is} better than sacrifice, {and} to hearken than the fat of rams.
verses.nlt_text: But Samuel replied, "What is more pleasing to the LORD: your burnt offerings and sacrifices or your obedience to his voice? Listen! Obedience is better than sacrifice, and submission is better than offering the fat of rams.

verses.kjv_text: For rebellion {is as} the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness {is as} iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, he hath also rejected thee from {being} king. {witchcraft: Heb. divination}
verses.nlt_text: Rebellion is as sinful as witchcraft, and stubbornness as bad as worshiping idols. So because you have rejected the command of the LORD, he has rejected you as king."

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the LORD, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul admitted to Samuel, "Yes, I have sinned. I have disobeyed your instructions and the LORD's command, for I was afraid of the people and did what they demanded.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: But now, please forgive my sin and come back with me so that I may worship the LORD."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.
verses.nlt_text: But Samuel replied, "I will not go back with you! Since you have rejected the LORD's command, he has rejected you as king of Israel."

verses.kjv_text: And as Samuel turned about to go away, he laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent.
verses.nlt_text: As Samuel turned to go, Saul tried to hold him back and tore the hem of his robe.

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said unto him, The LORD hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, {that is} better than thou.
verses.nlt_text: And Samuel said to him, "The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to someone else-- one who is better than you.

verses.kjv_text: And also the Strength of Israel will not lie nor repent: for he {is} not a man, that he should repent. {Strength: or, Eternity, or, Victory}
verses.nlt_text: And he who is the Glory of Israel will not lie, nor will he change his mind, for he is not human that he should change his mind!"

verses.kjv_text: Then he said, I have sinned: {yet} honour me now, I pray thee, before the elders of my people, and before Israel, and turn again with me, that I may worship the LORD thy God.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul pleaded again, "I know I have sinned. But please, at least honor me before the elders of my people and before Israel by coming back with me so that I may worship the LORD your God."

verses.kjv_text: So Samuel turned again after Saul; and Saul worshipped the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: So Samuel finally agreed and went back with him, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately. And Agag said, Surely the bitterness of death is past.
verses.nlt_text: Then Samuel said, "Bring King Agag to me." Agag arrived full of hope, for he thought, "Surely the worst is over, and I have been spared!"

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said, As thy sword hath made women childless, so shall thy mother be childless among women. And Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
verses.nlt_text: But Samuel said, "As your sword has killed the sons of many mothers, now your mother will be childless." And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.

verses.kjv_text: Then Samuel went to Ramah; and Saul went up to his house to Gibeah of Saul.
verses.nlt_text: Then Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his house at Gibeah of Saul.

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel came no more to see Saul until the day of his death: nevertheless Samuel mourned for Saul: and the LORD repented that he had made Saul king over Israel.
verses.nlt_text: Samuel never went to meet with Saul again, but he mourned constantly for him. And the LORD was sorry he had ever made Saul king of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Samuel, How long wilt thou mourn for Saul, seeing I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? fill thine horn with oil, and go, I will send thee to Jesse the Bethlehemite: for I have provided me a king among his sons.
verses.nlt_text: Now the LORD said to Samuel, "You have mourned long enough for Saul. I have rejected him as king of Israel, so fill your flask with olive oil and go to Bethlehem. Find a man named Jesse who lives there, for I have selected one of his sons to be my king."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said, How can I go? if Saul hear {it}, he will kill me. And the LORD said, Take an heifer with thee, and say, I am come to sacrifice to the LORD. {with thee: Heb. in thine hand}
verses.nlt_text: But Samuel asked, "How can I do that? If Saul hears about it, he will kill me." "Take a heifer with you," the LORD replied, "and say that you have come to make a sacrifice to the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And call Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will shew thee what thou shalt do: and thou shalt anoint unto me {him} whom I name unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you which of his sons to anoint for me."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel did that which the LORD spake, and came to Bethlehem. And the elders of the town trembled at his coming, and said, Comest thou peaceably? {coming: Heb. meeting}
verses.nlt_text: So Samuel did as the LORD instructed. When he arrived at Bethlehem, the elders of the town came trembling to meet him. "What's wrong?" they asked. "Do you come in peace?"

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Peaceably: I am come to sacrifice unto the LORD: sanctify yourselves, and come with me to the sacrifice. And he sanctified Jesse and his sons, and called them to the sacrifice.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes," Samuel replied. "I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Purify yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice." Then Samuel performed the purification rite for Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice, too.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when they were come, that he looked on Eliab, and said, Surely the LORD'S anointed {is} before him. {Eliab: called Elihu}
verses.nlt_text: When they arrived, Samuel took one look at Eliab and thought, "Surely this is the LORD's anointed!"

verses.kjv_text: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for {the LORD seeth} not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart. {outward...: Heb. eyes}
verses.nlt_text: But the LORD said to Samuel, "Don't judge by his appearance or height, for I have rejected him. The LORD doesn't see things the way you see them. People judge by outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart."

verses.kjv_text: Then Jesse called Abinadab, and made him pass before Samuel. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this.
verses.nlt_text: Then Jesse told his son Abinadab to step forward and walk in front of Samuel. But Samuel said, "This is not the one the LORD has chosen."

verses.kjv_text: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by. And he said, Neither hath the LORD chosen this. {Shammah: Shimeah, also called, Shimma}
verses.nlt_text: Next Jesse summoned Shimea, but Samuel said, "Neither is this the one the LORD has chosen."

verses.kjv_text: Again, Jesse made seven of his sons to pass before Samuel. And Samuel said unto Jesse, The LORD hath not chosen these.
verses.nlt_text: In the same way all seven of Jesse's sons were presented to Samuel. But Samuel said to Jesse, "The LORD has not chosen any of these."

verses.kjv_text: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all {thy} children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither. {down: Heb. round}
verses.nlt_text: Then Samuel asked, "Are these all the sons you have?" "There is still the youngest," Jesse replied. "But he's out in the fields watching the sheep and goats." "Send for him at once," Samuel said. "We will not sit down to eat until he arrives."

verses.kjv_text: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he {was} ruddy, {and} withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And the LORD said, Arise, anoint him: for this {is} he. {of a...: Heb. fair of eyes}
verses.nlt_text: So Jesse sent for him. He was dark and handsome, with beautiful eyes.And the LORD said, "This is the one; anoint him."

verses.kjv_text: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
verses.nlt_text: So as David stood there among his brothers, Samuel took the flask of olive oil he had brought and anointed David with the oil. And the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon David from that day on. Then Samuel returned to Ramah.

verses.kjv_text: But the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD troubled him. {troubled: or, terrified}
verses.nlt_text: Now the Spirit of the LORD had left Saul, and the LORD sent a tormenting spirit that filled him with depression and fear.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul's servants said unto him, Behold now, an evil spirit from God troubleth thee.
verses.nlt_text: Some of Saul's servants said to him, "A tormenting spirit from God is troubling you.

verses.kjv_text: Let our lord now command thy servants, {which are} before thee, to seek out a man, {who is} a cunning player on an harp: and it shall come to pass, when the evil spirit from God is upon thee, that he shall play with his hand, and thou shalt be well.
verses.nlt_text: Let us find a good musician to play the harp whenever the tormenting spirit troubles you. He will play soothing music, and you will soon be well again."

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said unto his servants, Provide me now a man that can play well, and bring {him} to me.
verses.nlt_text: "All right," Saul said. "Find me someone who plays well, and bring him here."

verses.kjv_text: Then answered one of the servants, and said, Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite, {that is} cunning in playing, and a mighty valiant man, and a man of war, and prudent in matters, and a comely person, and the LORD {is} with him. {matters: or, speech}
verses.nlt_text: One of the servants said to Saul, "One of Jesse's sons from Bethlehem is a talented harp player. Not only that-- he is a brave warrior, a man of war, and has good judgment. He is also a fine-looking young man, and the LORD is with him."

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore Saul sent messengers unto Jesse, and said, Send me David thy son, which {is} with the sheep.
verses.nlt_text: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse to say, "Send me your son David, the shepherd."

verses.kjv_text: And Jesse took an ass {laden} with bread, and a bottle of wine, and a kid, and sent {them} by David his son unto Saul.
verses.nlt_text: Jesse responded by sending David to Saul, along with a young goat, a donkey loaded with bread, and a wineskin full of wine.

verses.kjv_text: And David came to Saul, and stood before him: and he loved him greatly; and he became his armourbearer.
verses.nlt_text: So David went to Saul and began serving him. Saul loved David very much, and David became his armor bearer.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul sent to Jesse, saying, Let David, I pray thee, stand before me; for he hath found favour in my sight.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul sent word to Jesse asking, "Please let David remain in my service, for I am very pleased with him."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when the {evil} spirit from God was upon Saul, that David took an harp, and played with his hand: so Saul was refreshed, and was well, and the evil spirit departed from him.
verses.nlt_text: And whenever the tormenting spirit from God troubled Saul, David would play the harp. Then Saul would feel better, and the tormenting spirit would go away.

verses.kjv_text: Now the Philistines gathered together their armies to battle, and were gathered together at Shochoh, which {belongeth} to Judah, and pitched between Shochoh and Azekah, in Ephesdammim. {Ephesdammim: or, the coast of Dammim, called Pasdammim}
verses.nlt_text: The Philistines now mustered their army for battle and camped between Socoh in Judah and Azekah at Ephes-dammim.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered together, and pitched by the valley of Elah, and set the battle in array against the Philistines. {set...: Heb. ranged the battle}
verses.nlt_text: Saul countered by gathering his Israelite troops near the valley of Elah.

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistines stood on a mountain on the one side, and Israel stood on a mountain on the other side: and {there was} a valley between them.
verses.nlt_text: So the Philistines and Israelites faced each other on opposite hills, with the valley between them.

verses.kjv_text: And there went out a champion out of the camp of the Philistines, named Goliath, of Gath, whose height {was} six cubits and a span.
verses.nlt_text: Then Goliath, a Philistine champion from Gath, came out of the Philistine ranks to face the forces of Israel. He was over nine feet tall!

verses.kjv_text: And {he had} an helmet of brass upon his head, and he {was} armed with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat {was} five thousand shekels of brass. {armed: Heb. clothed}
verses.nlt_text: He wore a bronze helmet, and his bronze coat of mail weighed 125 pounds.

verses.kjv_text: And {he had} greaves of brass upon his legs, and a target of brass between his shoulders. {target: or, gorget}
verses.nlt_text: He also wore bronze leg armor, and he carried a bronze javelin on his shoulder.

verses.kjv_text: And the staff of his spear {was} like a weaver's beam; and his spear's head {weighed} six hundred shekels of iron: and one bearing a shield went before him.
verses.nlt_text: The shaft of his spear was as heavy and thick as a weaver's beam, tipped with an iron spearhead that weighed 15 pounds. His armor bearer walked ahead of him carrying a shield.

verses.kjv_text: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Israel, and said unto them, Why are ye come out to set {your} battle in array? {am} not I a Philistine, and ye servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.
verses.nlt_text: Goliath stood and shouted a taunt across to the Israelites. "Why are you all coming out to fight?" he called. "I am the Philistine champion, but you are only the servants of Saul. Choose one man to come down here and fight me!

verses.kjv_text: If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall ye be our servants, and serve us.
verses.nlt_text: If he kills me, then we will be your slaves. But if I kill him, you will be our slaves!

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together.
verses.nlt_text: I defy the armies of Israel today! Send me a man who will fight me!"

verses.kjv_text: When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.
verses.nlt_text: When Saul and the Israelites heard this, they were terrified and deeply shaken.

verses.kjv_text: Now David {was} the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehemjudah, whose name {was} Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man went among men {for} an old man in the days of Saul.
verses.nlt_text: Now David was the son of a man named Jesse, an Ephrathite from Bethlehem in the land of Judah. Jesse was an old man at that time, and he had eight sons.

verses.kjv_text: And the three eldest sons of Jesse went {and} followed Saul to the battle: and the names of his three sons that went to the battle {were} Eliab the firstborn, and next unto him Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
verses.nlt_text: Jesse's three oldest sons-- Eliab, Abinadab, and Shimea-- had already joined Saul's army to fight the Philistines.

verses.kjv_text: And David {was} the youngest: and the three eldest followed Saul.
verses.nlt_text: David was the youngest son. David's three oldest brothers stayed with Saul's army,

verses.kjv_text: But David went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem.
verses.nlt_text: but David went back and forth so he could help his father with the sheep in Bethlehem.

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days.
verses.nlt_text: For forty days, every morning and evening, the Philistine champion strutted in front of the Israelite army.

verses.kjv_text: And Jesse said unto David his son, Take now for thy brethren an ephah of this parched {corn}, and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to thy brethren;
verses.nlt_text: One day Jesse said to David, "Take this basket of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread, and carry them quickly to your brothers.

verses.kjv_text: And carry these ten cheeses unto the captain of {their} thousand, and look how thy brethren fare, and take their pledge. {cheeses: Heb. cheeses of milk} {of...: Heb. of a thousand}
verses.nlt_text: And give these ten cuts of cheese to their captain. See how your brothers are getting along, and bring back a report on how they are doing. "

verses.kjv_text: Now Saul, and they, and all the men of Israel, {were} in the valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.
verses.nlt_text: David's brothers were with Saul and the Israelite army at the valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.

verses.kjv_text: And David rose up early in the morning, and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the trench, as the host was going forth to the fight, and shouted for the battle. {trench: or, place of the carriage} {fight: or, battle array, or, place of fight}
verses.nlt_text: So David left the sheep with another shepherd and set out early the next morning with the gifts, as Jesse had directed him. He arrived at the camp just as the Israelite army was leaving for the battlefield with shouts and battle cries.

verses.kjv_text: For Israel and the Philistines had put the battle in array, army against army.
verses.nlt_text: Soon the Israelite and Philistine forces stood facing each other, army against army.

verses.kjv_text: And David left his carriage in the hand of the keeper of the carriage, and ran into the army, and came and saluted his brethren. {his carriage: Heb. the vessels from upon him} {saluted...: Heb. asked his brethren of peace}
verses.nlt_text: David left his things with the keeper of supplies and hurried out to the ranks to greet his brothers.

verses.kjv_text: And as he talked with them, behold, there came up the champion, the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name, out of the armies of the Philistines, and spake according to the same words: and David heard {them}.
verses.nlt_text: As he was talking with them, Goliath, the Philistine champion from Gath, came out from the Philistine ranks. Then David heard him shout his usual taunt to the army of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him, and were sore afraid. {from...: Heb. from his face}
verses.nlt_text: As soon as the Israelite army saw him, they began to run away in fright.

verses.kjv_text: And the men of Israel said, Have ye seen this man that is come up? surely to defy Israel is he come up: and it shall be, {that} the man who killeth him, the king will enrich him with great riches, and will give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel.
verses.nlt_text: "Have you seen the giant?" the men asked. "He comes out each day to defy Israel. The king has offered a huge reward to anyone who kills him. He will give that man one of his daughters for a wife, and the man's entire family will be exempted from paying taxes!"

verses.kjv_text: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who {is} this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
verses.nlt_text: David asked the soldiers standing nearby, "What will a man get for killing this Philistine and ending his defiance of Israel? Who is this pagan Philistine anyway, that he is allowed to defy the armies of the living God?"

verses.kjv_text: And the people answered him after this manner, saying, So shall it be done to the man that killeth him.
verses.nlt_text: And these men gave David the same reply. They said, "Yes, that is the reward for killing him."

verses.kjv_text: And Eliab his eldest brother heard when he spake unto the men; and Eliab's anger was kindled against David, and he said, Why camest thou down hither? and with whom hast thou left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart; for thou art come down that thou mightest see the battle.
verses.nlt_text: But when David's oldest brother, Eliab, heard David talking to the men, he was angry. "What are you doing around here anyway?" he demanded. "What about those few sheep you're supposed to be taking care of? I know about your pride and deceit. You just want to see the battle!"

verses.kjv_text: And David said, What have I now done? {Is there} not a cause?
verses.nlt_text: "What have I done now?" David replied. "I was only asking a question!"

verses.kjv_text: And he turned from him toward another, and spake after the same manner: and the people answered him again after the former manner. {manner: Heb. word}
verses.nlt_text: He walked over to some others and asked them the same thing and received the same answer.

verses.kjv_text: And when the words were heard which David spake, they rehearsed {them} before Saul: and he sent for him. {sent...: Heb. took him}
verses.nlt_text: Then David's question was reported to King Saul, and the king sent for him.

verses.kjv_text: And David said to Saul, Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.
verses.nlt_text: "Don't worry about this Philistine," David told Saul. "I'll go fight him!"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said to David, Thou art not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him: for thou {art but} a youth, and he a man of war from his youth.
verses.nlt_text: "Don't be ridiculous!" Saul replied. "There's no way you can fight this Philistine and possibly win! You're only a boy, and he's been a man of war since his youth."

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock: {lamb: or, kid}
verses.nlt_text: But David persisted. "I have been taking care of my father's sheep and goats," he said. "When a lion or a bear comes to steal a lamb from the flock,

verses.kjv_text: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered {it} out of his mouth: and when he arose against me, I caught {him} by his beard, and smote him, and slew him.
verses.nlt_text: I go after it with a club and rescue the lamb from its mouth. If the animal turns on me, I catch it by the jaw and club it to death.

verses.kjv_text: Thy servant slew both the lion and the bear: and this uncircumcised Philistine shall be as one of them, seeing he hath defied the armies of the living God.
verses.nlt_text: I have done this to both lions and bears, and I'll do it to this pagan Philistine, too, for he has defied the armies of the living God!

verses.kjv_text: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD who rescued me from the claws of the lion and the bear will rescue me from this Philistine!" Saul finally consented. "All right, go ahead," he said. "And may the LORD be with you!"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail. {armed David...: Heb. clothed David with his clothes}
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul gave David his own armor-- a bronze helmet and a coat of mail.

verses.kjv_text: And David girded his sword upon his armour, and he assayed to go; for he had not proved {it}. And David said unto Saul, I cannot go with these; for I have not proved {them}. And David put them off him.
verses.nlt_text: David put it on, strapped the sword over it, and took a step or two to see what it was like, for he had never worn such things before."I can't go in these," he protested to Saul. "I'm not used to them." So David took them off again.

verses.kjv_text: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling {was} in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine. {brook: or, valley} {bag: Heb. vessel}
verses.nlt_text: He picked up five smooth stones from a stream and put them into his shepherd's bag. Then, armed only with his shepherd's staff and sling, he started across the valley to fight the Philistine.

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistine came on and drew near unto David; and the man that bare the shield {went} before him.
verses.nlt_text: Goliath walked out toward David with his shield bearer ahead of him,

verses.kjv_text: And when the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him: for he was {but} a youth, and ruddy, and of a fair countenance.
verses.nlt_text: sneering in contempt at this ruddy-faced boy.

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistine said unto David, {Am} I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves? And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.
verses.nlt_text: "Am I a dog," he roared at David, "that you come at me with a stick?" And he cursed David by the names of his gods.

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistine said to David, Come to me, and I will give thy flesh unto the fowls of the air, and to the beasts of the field.
verses.nlt_text: "Come over here, and I'll give your flesh to the birds and wild animals!" Goliath yelled.

verses.kjv_text: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.
verses.nlt_text: David replied to the Philistine, "You come to me with sword, spear, and javelin, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Heaven's Armies-- the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.

verses.kjv_text: This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand; and I will smite thee, and take thine head from thee; and I will give the carcases of the host of the Philistines this day unto the fowls of the air, and to the wild beasts of the earth; that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel. {deliver...: Heb. shut thee up}
verses.nlt_text: Today the LORD will conquer you, and I will kill you and cut off your head. And then I will give the dead bodies of your men to the birds and wild animals, and the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel!

verses.kjv_text: And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle {is} the LORD'S, and he will give you into our hands.
verses.nlt_text: And everyone assembled here will know that the LORD rescues his people, but not with sword and spear. This is the LORD's battle, and he will give you to us!"

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when the Philistine arose, and came and drew nigh to meet David, that David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.
verses.nlt_text: As Goliath moved closer to attack, David quickly ran out to meet him.

verses.kjv_text: And David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang {it}, and smote the Philistine in his forehead, that the stone sunk into his forehead; and he fell upon his face to the earth.
verses.nlt_text: Reaching into his shepherd's bag and taking out a stone, he hurled it with his sling and hit the Philistine in the forehead. The stone sank in, and Goliath stumbled and fell face down on the ground.

verses.kjv_text: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone, and smote the Philistine, and slew him; but {there was} no sword in the hand of David.
verses.nlt_text: So David triumphed over the Philistine with only a sling and a stone, for he had no sword.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.
verses.nlt_text: Then David ran over and pulled Goliath's sword from its sheath. David used it to kill him and cut off his head. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they turned and ran.

verses.kjv_text: And the men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until thou come to the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.
verses.nlt_text: Then the men of Israel and Judah gave a great shout of triumph and rushed after the Philistines, chasing them as far as Gath and the gates of Ekron. The bodies of the dead and wounded Philistines were strewn all along the road from Shaaraim, as far as Gath and Ekron.

verses.kjv_text: And the children of Israel returned from chasing after the Philistines, and they spoiled their tents.
verses.nlt_text: Then the Israelite army returned and plundered the deserted Philistine camp.

verses.kjv_text: And David took the head of the Philistine, and brought it to Jerusalem; but he put his armour in his tent.
verses.nlt_text: (David took the Philistine's head to Jerusalem, but he stored the man's armor in his own tent.)

verses.kjv_text: And when Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine, he said unto Abner, the captain of the host, Abner, whose son {is} this youth? And Abner said, {As} thy soul liveth, O king, I cannot tell.
verses.nlt_text: As Saul watched David go out to fight the Philistine, he asked Abner, the commander of his army, "Abner, whose son is this young man?" "I really don't know," Abner declared.

verses.kjv_text: And the king said, Enquire thou whose son the stripling {is}.
verses.nlt_text: "Well, find out who he is!" the king told him.

verses.kjv_text: And as David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, Abner took him, and brought him before Saul with the head of the Philistine in his hand.
verses.nlt_text: As soon as David returned from killing Goliath, Abner brought him to Saul with the Philistine's head still in his hand.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said to him, Whose son {art} thou, {thou} young man? And David answered, I {am} the son of thy servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.
verses.nlt_text: "Tell me about your father, young man," Saul said.And David replied, "His name is Jesse, and we live in Bethlehem."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
verses.nlt_text: After David had finished talking with Saul, he met Jonathan, the king's son. There was an immediate bond of love between them, and they became the best of friends.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father's house.
verses.nlt_text: From that day on Saul kept David with him and wouldn't let him return home.

verses.kjv_text: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
verses.nlt_text: And Jonathan made a solemn pact with David, because he loved him as he loved himself.

verses.kjv_text: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that {was} upon him, and gave it to David, and his garments, even to his sword, and to his bow, and to his girdle.
verses.nlt_text: Jonathan sealed the pact by taking off his robe and giving it to David, together with his tunic, sword, bow, and belt.

verses.kjv_text: And David went out whithersoever Saul sent him, {and} behaved himself wisely: and Saul set him over the men of war, and he was accepted in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul's servants. {behaved...: or, prospered}
verses.nlt_text: Whatever Saul asked David to do, David did it successfully. So Saul made him a commander over the men of war, an appointment that was welcomed by the people and Saul's officers alike.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick. {Philistine: or, Philistines} {instruments...: Heb. three stringed instruments}
verses.nlt_text: When the victorious Israelite army was returning home after David had killed the Philistine, women from all the towns of Israel came out to meet King Saul. They sang and danced for joy with tambourines and cymbals.

verses.kjv_text: And the women answered {one another} as they played, and said, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
verses.nlt_text: This was their song: "Saul has killed his thousands, and David his ten thousands!"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul was very wroth, and the saying displeased him; and he said, They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed {but} thousands: and {what} can he have more but the kingdom? {displeased him: Heb. was evil in his eyes}
verses.nlt_text: This made Saul very angry. "What's this?" he said. "They credit David with ten thousands and me with only thousands. Next they'll be making him their king!"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.
verses.nlt_text: So from that time on Saul kept a jealous eye on David.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that the evil spirit from God came upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of the house: and David played with his hand, as at other times: and {there was} a javelin in Saul's hand.
verses.nlt_text: The very next day a tormenting spirit from God overwhelmed Saul, and he began to rave in his house like a madman. David was playing the harp, as he did each day. But Saul had a spear in his hand,

verses.kjv_text: And Saul cast the javelin; for he said, I will smite David even to the wall {with it}. And David avoided out of his presence twice.
verses.nlt_text: and he suddenly hurled it at David, intending to pin him to the wall. But David escaped him twice.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him, and was departed from Saul.
verses.nlt_text: Saul was then afraid of David, for the LORD was with David and had turned away from Saul.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore Saul removed him from him, and made him his captain over a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people.
verses.nlt_text: Finally, Saul sent him away and appointed him commander over 1,000 men, and David faithfully led his troops into battle.

verses.kjv_text: And David behaved himself wisely in all his ways; and the LORD {was} with him. {behaved...: or, prospered}
verses.nlt_text: David continued to succeed in everything he did, for the LORD was with him.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore when Saul saw that he behaved himself very wisely, he was afraid of him.
verses.nlt_text: When Saul recognized this, he became even more afraid of him.

verses.kjv_text: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he went out and came in before them.
verses.nlt_text: But all Israel and Judah loved David because he was so successful at leading his troops into battle.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said to David, Behold my elder daughter Merab, her will I give thee to wife: only be thou valiant for me, and fight the LORD'S battles. For Saul said, Let not mine hand be upon him, but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him. {valiant: Heb. a son of valour}
verses.nlt_text: One day Saul said to David, "I am ready to give you my older daughter, Merab, as your wife. But first you must prove yourself to be a real warrior by fighting the LORD's battles." For Saul thought, "I'll send him out against the Philistines and let them kill him rather than doing it myself."

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto Saul, Who {am} I? and what {is} my life, {or} my father's family in Israel, that I should be son in law to the king?
verses.nlt_text: "Who am I, and what is my family in Israel that I should be the king's son-in-law?" David exclaimed. "My father's family is nothing!"

verses.kjv_text: But it came to pass at the time when Merab Saul's daughter should have been given to David, that she was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife.
verses.nlt_text: So when the time came for Saul to give his daughter Merab in marriage to David, he gave her instead to Adriel, a man from Meholah.

verses.kjv_text: And Michal Saul's daughter loved David: and they told Saul, and the thing pleased him. {pleased him: Heb. was right in his eyes}
verses.nlt_text: In the meantime, Saul's daughter Michal had fallen in love with David, and Saul was delighted when he heard about it.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said, I will give him her, that she may be a snare to him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him. Wherefore Saul said to David, Thou shalt this day be my son in law in {the one of} the twain.
verses.nlt_text: "Here's another chance to see him killed by the Philistines!" Saul said to himself. But to David he said, "Today you have a second chance to become my son-in-law!"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul commanded his servants, {saying}, Commune with David secretly, and say, Behold, the king hath delight in thee, and all his servants love thee: now therefore be the king's son in law.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul told his men to say to David, "The king really likes you, and so do we. Why don't you accept the king's offer and become his son-in-law?"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul's servants spake those words in the ears of David. And David said, Seemeth it to you {a} light {thing} to be a king's son in law, seeing that I {am} a poor man, and lightly esteemed?
verses.nlt_text: When Saul's men said these things to David, he replied, "How can a poor man from a humble family afford the bride price for the daughter of a king?"

verses.kjv_text: And the servants of Saul told him, saying, On this manner spake David. {On...: Heb. According to these words}
verses.nlt_text: When Saul's men reported this back to the king,

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said, Thus shall ye say to David, The king desireth not any dowry, but an hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king's enemies. But Saul thought to make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.
verses.nlt_text: he told them, "Tell David that all I want for the bride price is 100 Philistine foreskins! Vengeance on my enemies is all I really want." But what Saul had in mind was that David would be killed in the fight.

verses.kjv_text: And when his servants told David these words, it pleased David well to be the king's son in law: and the days were not expired. {expired: Heb. fulfilled}
verses.nlt_text: David was delighted to accept the offer. Before the time limit expired,

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full tale to the king, that he might be the king's son in law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.
verses.nlt_text: he and his men went out and killed 200 Philistines. Then David fulfilled the king's requirement by presenting all their foreskins to him. So Saul gave his daughter Michal to David to be his wife.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul saw and knew that the LORD {was} with David, and {that} Michal Saul's daughter loved him.
verses.nlt_text: When Saul realized that the LORD was with David and how much his daughter Michal loved him,

verses.kjv_text: And Saul was yet the more afraid of David; and Saul became David's enemy continually.
verses.nlt_text: Saul became even more afraid of him, and he remained David's enemy for the rest of his life.

verses.kjv_text: Then the princes of the Philistines went forth: and it came to pass, after they went forth, {that} David behaved himself more wisely than all the servants of Saul; so that his name was much set by. {set by: Heb. precious}
verses.nlt_text: Every time the commanders of the Philistines attacked, David was more successful against them than all the rest of Saul's officers. So David's name became very famous.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul spake to Jonathan his son, and to all his servants, that they should kill David.
verses.nlt_text: Saul now urged his servants and his son Jonathan to assassinate David. But Jonathan, because of his close friendship with David,

verses.kjv_text: But Jonathan Saul's son delighted much in David: and Jonathan told David, saying, Saul my father seeketh to kill thee: now therefore, I pray thee, take heed to thyself until the morning, and abide in a secret {place}, and hide thyself:
verses.nlt_text: told him what his father was planning. "Tomorrow morning," he warned him, "you must find a hiding place out in the fields.

verses.kjv_text: And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where thou {art}, and I will commune with my father of thee; and what I see, that I will tell thee.
verses.nlt_text: I'll ask my father to go out there with me, and I'll talk to him about you. Then I'll tell you everything I can find out."

verses.kjv_text: And Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul his father, and said unto him, Let not the king sin against his servant, against David; because he hath not sinned against thee, and because his works {have been} to thee-ward very good:
verses.nlt_text: The next morning Jonathan spoke with his father about David, saying many good things about him. "The king must not sin against his servant David," Jonathan said. "He's never done anything to harm you. He has always helped you in any way he could.

verses.kjv_text: For he did put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine, and the LORD wrought a great salvation for all Israel: thou sawest {it}, and didst rejoice: wherefore then wilt thou sin against innocent blood, to slay David without a cause?
verses.nlt_text: Have you forgotten about the time he risked his life to kill the Philistine giant and how the LORD brought a great victory to all Israel as a result? You were certainly happy about it then. Why should you murder an innocent man like David? There is no reason for it at all!"

verses.kjv_text: And Saul hearkened unto the voice of Jonathan: and Saul sware, {As} the LORD liveth, he shall not be slain.
verses.nlt_text: So Saul listened to Jonathan and vowed, "As surely as the LORD lives, David will not be killed."

verses.kjv_text: And Jonathan called David, and Jonathan shewed him all those things. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence, as in times past. {in times...: Heb. yesterday, third day}
verses.nlt_text: Afterward Jonathan called David and told him what had happened. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in the court as before.

verses.kjv_text: And there was war again: and David went out, and fought with the Philistines, and slew them with a great slaughter; and they fled from him. {him: Heb. his face}
verses.nlt_text: War broke out again after that, and David led his troops against the Philistines. He attacked them with such fury that they all ran away.

verses.kjv_text: And the evil spirit from the LORD was upon Saul, as he sat in his house with his javelin in his hand: and David played with {his} hand.
verses.nlt_text: But one day when Saul was sitting at home, with spear in hand, the tormenting spirit from the LORD suddenly came upon him again. As David played his harp,

verses.kjv_text: And Saul sought to smite David even to the wall with the javelin; but he slipped away out of Saul's presence, and he smote the javelin into the wall: and David fled, and escaped that night.
verses.nlt_text: Saul hurled his spear at David. But David dodged out of the way, and leaving the spear stuck in the wall, he fled and escaped into the night.

verses.kjv_text: Saul also sent messengers unto David's house, to watch him, and to slay him in the morning: and Michal David's wife told him, saying, If thou save not thy life to night, to morrow thou shalt be slain.
verses.nlt_text: Then Saul sent troops to watch David's house. They were told to kill David when he came out the next morning. But Michal, David's wife, warned him, "If you don't escape tonight, you will be dead by morning."

verses.kjv_text: So Michal let David down through a window: and he went, and fled, and escaped.
verses.nlt_text: So she helped him climb out through a window, and he fled and escaped.

verses.kjv_text: And Michal took an image, and laid {it} in the bed, and put a pillow of goats' {hair} for his bolster, and covered {it} with a cloth. {image: Heb. teraphim}
verses.nlt_text: Then she took an idol and put it in his bed, covered it with blankets, and put a cushion of goat's hair at its head.

verses.kjv_text: And when Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, He {is} sick.
verses.nlt_text: When the troops came to arrest David, she told them he was sick and couldn't get out of bed.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul sent the messengers {again} to see David, saying, Bring him up to me in the bed, that I may slay him.
verses.nlt_text: But Saul sent the troops back to get David. He ordered, "Bring him to me in his bed so I can kill him!"

verses.kjv_text: And when the messengers were come in, behold, {there was} an image in the bed, with a pillow of goats' {hair} for his bolster.
verses.nlt_text: But when they came to carry David out, they discovered that it was only an idol in the bed with a cushion of goat's hair at its head.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul said unto Michal, Why hast thou deceived me so, and sent away mine enemy, that he is escaped? And Michal answered Saul, He said unto me, Let me go; why should I kill thee?
verses.nlt_text: "Why have you betrayed me like this and let my enemy escape?" Saul demanded of Michal."I had to," Michal replied. "He threatened to kill me if I didn't help him."

verses.kjv_text: So David fled, and escaped, and came to Samuel to Ramah, and told him all that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and dwelt in Naioth.
verses.nlt_text: So David escaped and went to Ramah to see Samuel, and he told him all that Saul had done to him. Then Samuel took David with him to live at Naioth.

verses.kjv_text: And it was told Saul, saying, Behold, David {is} at Naioth in Ramah.
verses.nlt_text: When the report reached Saul that David was at Naioth in Ramah,

verses.kjv_text: And Saul sent messengers to take David: and when they saw the company of the prophets prophesying, and Samuel standing {as} appointed over them, the Spirit of God was upon the messengers of Saul, and they also prophesied.
verses.nlt_text: he sent troops to capture him. But when they arrived and saw Samuel leading a group of prophets who were prophesying, the Spirit of God came upon Saul's men, and they also began to prophesy.

verses.kjv_text: And when it was told Saul, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied likewise. And Saul sent messengers again the third time, and they prophesied also.
verses.nlt_text: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent other troops, but they, too, prophesied! The same thing happened a third time.

verses.kjv_text: Then went he also to Ramah, and came to a great well that {is} in Sechu: and he asked and said, Where {are} Samuel and David? And {one} said, Behold, {they be} at Naioth in Ramah.
verses.nlt_text: Finally, Saul himself went to Ramah and arrived at the great well in Secu. "Where are Samuel and David?" he demanded."They are at Naioth in Ramah," someone told him.

verses.kjv_text: And he went thither to Naioth in Ramah: and the Spirit of God was upon him also, and he went on, and prophesied, until he came to Naioth in Ramah.
verses.nlt_text: But on the way to Naioth in Ramah the Spirit of God came even upon Saul, and he, too, began to prophesy all the way to Naioth!

verses.kjv_text: And he stripped off his clothes also, and prophesied before Samuel in like manner, and lay down naked all that day and all that night. Wherefore they say, {Is} Saul also among the prophets? {lay: Heb. fell}
verses.nlt_text: He tore off his clothes and lay naked on the ground all day and all night, prophesying in the presence of Samuel. The people who were watching exclaimed, "What? Is even Saul a prophet?"

verses.kjv_text: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and came and said before Jonathan, What have I done? what {is} mine iniquity? and what {is} my sin before thy father, that he seeketh my life?
