verses.kjv_text: Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the LORD is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?
verses.nlt_text: But Samuel replied, "Why ask me, since the LORD has left you and has become your enemy?

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the LORD hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, {even} to David: {to him: or, for himself} {me: Heb. mine hand}
verses.nlt_text: The LORD has done just as he said he would. He has torn the kingdom from you and given it to your rival, David.

verses.kjv_text: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the LORD, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the LORD done this thing unto thee this day.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD has done this to you today because you refused to carry out his fierce anger against the Amalekites.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover the LORD will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow {shalt} thou and thy sons {be} with me: the LORD also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.
verses.nlt_text: What's more, the LORD will hand you and the army of Israel over to the Philistines tomorrow, and you and your sons will be here with me. The LORD will bring down the entire army of Israel in defeat."

verses.kjv_text: Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night. {fell...: Heb. made haste, and fell with the fulness of his stature}
verses.nlt_text: Saul fell full length on the ground, paralyzed with fright because of Samuel's words. He was also faint with hunger, for he had eaten nothing all day and all night.

verses.kjv_text: And the woman came unto Saul, and saw that he was sore troubled, and said unto him, Behold, thine handmaid hath obeyed thy voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened unto thy words which thou spakest unto me.
verses.nlt_text: When the woman saw how distraught he was, she said, "Sir, I obeyed your command at the risk of my life.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also unto the voice of thine handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayest have strength, when thou goest on thy way.
verses.nlt_text: Now do what I say, and let me give you a little something to eat so you can regain your strength for the trip back."

verses.kjv_text: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened unto their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.
verses.nlt_text: But Saul refused. The men who were with him also urged him to eat, so he finally yielded and got up from the ground and sat on the couch.

verses.kjv_text: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded {it}, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:
verses.nlt_text: The woman had been fattening a calf, so she hurried out and killed it. She took some flour, kneaded it into dough and baked unleavened bread.

verses.kjv_text: And she brought {it} before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.
verses.nlt_text: She brought the meal to Saul and his men, and they ate it. Then they went out into the night.

verses.kjv_text: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek: and the Israelites pitched by a fountain which {is} in Jezreel.
verses.nlt_text: The entire Philistine army now mobilized at Aphek, and the Israelites camped at the spring in Jezreel.

verses.kjv_text: And the lords of the Philistines passed on by hundreds, and by thousands: but David and his men passed on in the rereward with Achish.
verses.nlt_text: As the Philistine rulers were leading out their troops in groups of hundreds and thousands, David and his men marched at the rear with King Achish.

verses.kjv_text: Then said the princes of the Philistines, What {do} these Hebrews {here}? And Achish said unto the princes of the Philistines, {Is} not this David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, which hath been with me these days, or these years, and I have found no fault in him since he fell {unto me} unto this day?
verses.nlt_text: But the Philistine commanders demanded, "What are these Hebrews doing here?" And Achish told them, "This is David, the servant of King Saul of Israel. He's been with me for years, and I've never found a single fault in him from the day he arrived until today."

verses.kjv_text: And the princes of the Philistines were wroth with him; and the princes of the Philistines said unto him, Make this fellow return, that he may go again to his place which thou hast appointed him, and let him not go down with us to battle, lest in the battle he be an adversary to us: for wherewith should he reconcile himself unto his master? {should it} not {be} with the heads of these men?
verses.nlt_text: But the Philistine commanders were angry. "Send him back to the town you've given him!" they demanded. "He can't go into the battle with us. What if he turns against us in battle and becomes our adversary? Is there any better way for him to reconcile himself with his master than by handing our heads over to him?

verses.kjv_text: {Is} not this David, of whom they sang one to another in dances, saying, Saul slew his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
verses.nlt_text: Isn't this the same David about whom the women of Israel sing in their dances, 'Saul has killed his thousands, and David his ten thousands'?"

verses.kjv_text: Then Achish called David, and said unto him, Surely, {as} the LORD liveth, thou hast been upright, and thy going out and thy coming in with me in the host {is} good in my sight: for I have not found evil in thee since the day of thy coming unto me unto this day: nevertheless the lords favour thee not. {the lords...: Heb. thou art not good in the eyes of the lords}
verses.nlt_text: So Achish finally summoned David and said to him, "I swear by the LORD that you have been a trustworthy ally. I think you should go with me into battle, for I've never found a single flaw in you from the day you arrived until today. But the other Philistine rulers won't hear of it.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore now return, and go in peace, that thou displease not the lords of the Philistines. {displease...: Heb. do not evil in the eyes of the lords}
verses.nlt_text: Please don't upset them, but go back quietly."

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto Achish, But what have I done? and what hast thou found in thy servant so long as I have been with thee unto this day, that I may not go fight against the enemies of my lord the king? {with...: Heb. before thee}
verses.nlt_text: "What have I done to deserve this treatment?" David demanded. "What have you ever found in your servant, that I can't go and fight the enemies of my lord the king?"

verses.kjv_text: And Achish answered and said to David, I know that thou {art} good in my sight, as an angel of God: notwithstanding the princes of the Philistines have said, He shall not go up with us to the battle.
verses.nlt_text: But Achish insisted, "As far as I'm concerned, you're as perfect as an angel of God. But the Philistine commanders are afraid to have you with them in the battle.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore now rise up early in the morning with thy master's servants that are come with thee: and as soon as ye be up early in the morning, and have light, depart.
verses.nlt_text: Now get up early in the morning, and leave with your men as soon as it gets light."

verses.kjv_text: So David and his men rose up early to depart in the morning, to return into the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
verses.nlt_text: So David and his men headed back into the land of the Philistines, while the Philistine army went on to Jezreel.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when David and his men were come to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire;
verses.nlt_text: Three days later, when David and his men arrived home at their town of Ziklag, they found that the Amalekites had made a raid into the Negev and Ziklag; they had crushed Ziklag and burned it to the ground.

verses.kjv_text: And had taken the women captives, that {were} therein: they slew not any, either great or small, but carried {them} away, and went on their way.
verses.nlt_text: They had carried off the women and children and everyone else but without killing anyone.

verses.kjv_text: So David and his men came to the city, and, behold, {it was} burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives.
verses.nlt_text: When David and his men saw the ruins and realized what had happened to their families,

verses.kjv_text: Then David and the people that {were} with him lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.
verses.nlt_text: they wept until they could weep no more.

verses.kjv_text: And David's two wives were taken captives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
verses.nlt_text: David's two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel, were among those captured.

verses.kjv_text: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God. {grieved: Heb. bitter}
verses.nlt_text: David was now in great danger because all his men were very bitter about losing their sons and daughters, and they began to talk of stoning him. But David found strength in the LORD his God.

verses.kjv_text: And David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, I pray thee, bring me hither the ephod. And Abiathar brought thither the ephod to David.
verses.nlt_text: Then he said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring me the ephod!" So Abiathar brought it.

verses.kjv_text: And David enquired at the LORD, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? And he answered him, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake {them}, and without fail recover {all}.
verses.nlt_text: Then David asked the LORD, "Should I chase after this band of raiders? Will I catch them?" And the LORD told him, "Yes, go after them. You will surely recover everything that was taken from you!"

verses.kjv_text: So David went, he and the six hundred men that {were} with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed.
verses.nlt_text: So David and his 600 men set out, and they came to the brook Besor.

verses.kjv_text: But David pursued, he and four hundred men: for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.
verses.nlt_text: But 200 of the men were too exhausted to cross the brook, so David continued the pursuit with 400 men.

verses.kjv_text: And they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he did eat; and they made him drink water;
verses.nlt_text: Along the way they found an Egyptian man in a field and brought him to David. They gave him some bread to eat and water to drink.

verses.kjv_text: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins: and when he had eaten, his spirit came again to him: for he had eaten no bread, nor drunk {any} water, three days and three nights.
verses.nlt_text: They also gave him part of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins, for he hadn't had anything to eat or drink for three days and nights. Before long his strength returned.

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto him, To whom {belongest} thou? and whence {art} thou? And he said, I {am} a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days agone I fell sick.
verses.nlt_text: "To whom do you belong, and where do you come from?" David asked him."I am an Egyptian-- the slave of an Amalekite," he replied. "My master abandoned me three days ago because I was sick.

verses.kjv_text: We made an invasion {upon} the south of the Cherethites, and upon {the coast} which {belongeth} to Judah, and upon the south of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.
verses.nlt_text: We were on our way back from raiding the Kerethites in the Negev, the territory of Judah, and the land of Caleb, and we had just burned Ziklag."

verses.kjv_text: And David said to him, Canst thou bring me down to this company? And he said, Swear unto me by God, that thou wilt neither kill me, nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company.
verses.nlt_text: "Will you lead me to this band of raiders?" David asked.The young man replied, "If you take an oath in God's name that you will not kill me or give me back to my master, then I will guide you to them."

verses.kjv_text: And when he had brought him down, behold, {they were} spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking, and dancing, because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
verses.nlt_text: So he led David to them, and they found the Amalekites spread out across the fields, eating and drinking and dancing with joy because of the vast amount of plunder they had taken from the Philistines and the land of Judah.

verses.kjv_text: And David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day: and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men, which rode upon camels, and fled. {the next...: Heb. their morrow}
verses.nlt_text: David and his men rushed in among them and slaughtered them throughout that night and the entire next day until evening. None of the Amalekites escaped except 400 young men who fled on camels.

verses.kjv_text: And David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away: and David rescued his two wives.
verses.nlt_text: David got back everything the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued his two wives.

verses.kjv_text: And there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil, nor any {thing} that they had taken to them: David recovered all.
verses.nlt_text: Nothing was missing: small or great, son or daughter, nor anything else that had been taken. David brought everything back.

verses.kjv_text: And David took all the flocks and the herds, {which} they drave before those {other} cattle, and said, This {is} David's spoil.
verses.nlt_text: He also recovered all the flocks and herds, and his men drove them ahead of the other livestock. "This plunder belongs to David!" they said.

verses.kjv_text: And David came to the two hundred men, which were so faint that they could not follow David, whom they had made also to abide at the brook Besor: and they went forth to meet David, and to meet the people that {were} with him: and when David came near to the people, he saluted them. {saluted...: or, asked them how they did}
verses.nlt_text: Then David returned to the brook Besor and met up with the 200 men who had been left behind because they were too exhausted to go with him. They went out to meet David and his men, and David greeted them joyfully.

verses.kjv_text: Then answered all the wicked men and {men} of Belial, of those that went with David, and said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them {ought} of the spoil that we have recovered, save to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead {them} away, and depart. {those: Heb. men}
verses.nlt_text: But some evil troublemakers among David's men said, "They didn't go with us, so they can't have any of the plunder we recovered. Give them their wives and children, and tell them to be gone."

verses.kjv_text: Then said David, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the LORD hath given us, who hath preserved us, and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.
verses.nlt_text: But David said, "No, my brothers! Don't be selfish with what the LORD has given us. He has kept us safe and helped us defeat the band of raiders that attacked us.

verses.kjv_text: For who will hearken unto you in this matter? but as his part {is} that goeth down to the battle, so {shall} his part {be} that tarrieth by the stuff: they shall part alike.
verses.nlt_text: Who will listen when you talk like this? We share and share alike-- those who go to battle and those who guard the equipment."

verses.kjv_text: And it was {so} from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day. {forward: Heb. and forward}
verses.nlt_text: From then on David made this a decree and regulation for Israel, and it is still followed today.

verses.kjv_text: And when David came to Ziklag, he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Judah, {even} to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the LORD; {present: Heb. blessing}
verses.nlt_text: When he arrived at Ziklag, David sent part of the plunder to the elders of Judah, who were his friends. "Here is a present for you, taken from the LORD's enemies," he said.

verses.kjv_text: To {them} which {were} in Bethel, and to {them} which {were} in south Ramoth, and to {them} which {were} in Jattir,
verses.nlt_text: The gifts were sent to the people of the following towns David had visited: Bethel, Ramoth-negev, Jattir,

verses.kjv_text: And to {them} which {were} in Aroer, and to {them} which {were} in Siphmoth, and to {them} which {were} in Eshtemoa,
verses.nlt_text: Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa,

verses.kjv_text: And to {them} which {were} in Rachal, and to {them} which {were} in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to {them} which {were} in the cities of the Kenites,
verses.nlt_text: Racal, the towns of the Jerahmeelites, the towns of the Kenites,

verses.kjv_text: And to {them} which {were} in Hormah, and to {them} which {were} in Chorashan, and to {them} which {were} in Athach,
verses.nlt_text: Hormah, Bor-ashan, Athach,

verses.kjv_text: And to {them} which {were} in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.
verses.nlt_text: Hebron, and all the other places David and his men had visited.

verses.kjv_text: Now the Philistines fought against Israel: and the men of Israel fled from before the Philistines, and fell down slain in mount Gilboa. {slain: or, wounded}
verses.nlt_text: Now the Philistines attacked Israel, and the men of Israel fled before them. Many were slaughtered on the slopes of Mount Gilboa.

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, Saul's sons.
verses.nlt_text: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed three of his sons-- Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malkishua.

verses.kjv_text: And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers. {and the archers: Heb. and the shooters, men with bows} {hit...: Heb. found him}
verses.nlt_text: The fighting grew very fierce around Saul, and the Philistine archers caught up with him and wounded him severely.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it. {abuse...: or, mock me}
verses.nlt_text: Saul groaned to his armor bearer, "Take your sword and kill me before these pagan Philistines come to run me through and taunt and torture me." But his armor bearer was afraid and would not do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

verses.kjv_text: And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.
verses.nlt_text: When his armor bearer realized that Saul was dead, he fell on his own sword and died beside the king.

verses.kjv_text: So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.
verses.nlt_text: So Saul, his three sons, his armor bearer, and his troops all died together that same day.

verses.kjv_text: And when the men of Israel that {were} on the other side of the valley, and {they} that {were} on the other side Jordan, saw that the men of Israel fled, and that Saul and his sons were dead, they forsook the cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.
verses.nlt_text: When the Israelites on the other side of the Jezreel Valley and beyond the Jordan saw that the Israelite army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled. So the Philistines moved in and occupied their towns.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass on the morrow, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen in mount Gilboa.
verses.nlt_text: The next day, when the Philistines went out to strip the dead, they found the bodies of Saul and his three sons on Mount Gilboa.

verses.kjv_text: And they cut off his head, and stripped off his armour, and sent into the land of the Philistines round about, to publish {it in} the house of their idols, and among the people.
verses.nlt_text: So they cut off Saul's head and stripped off his armor. Then they proclaimed the good news of Saul's death in their pagan temple and to the people throughout the land of Philistia.

verses.kjv_text: And they put his armour in the house of Ashtaroth: and they fastened his body to the wall of Bethshan.
verses.nlt_text: They placed his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths, and they fastened his body to the wall of the city of Beth-shan.

verses.kjv_text: And when the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead heard of that which the Philistines had done to Saul; {of that: or, concerning him that}
verses.nlt_text: But when the people of Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,

verses.kjv_text: All the valiant men arose, and went all night, and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Bethshan, and came to Jabesh, and burnt them there.
verses.nlt_text: all their mighty warriors traveled through the night to Beth-shan and took the bodies of Saul and his sons down from the wall. They brought them to Jabesh, where they burned the bodies.

verses.kjv_text: And they took their bones, and buried {them} under a tree at Jabesh, and fasted seven days.
verses.nlt_text: Then they took their bones and buried them beneath the tamarisk tree at Jabesh, and they fasted for seven days.

verses.kjv_text: Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag;
verses.nlt_text: After the death of Saul, David returned from his victory over the Amalekites and spent two days in Ziklag.

verses.kjv_text: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and {so} it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
verses.nlt_text: On the third day a man arrived from Saul's army camp. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show that he was in mourning. He fell to the ground before David in deep respect.

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
verses.nlt_text: "Where have you come from?" David asked."I escaped from the Israelite camp," the man replied.

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also. {How...: Heb. What was, etc}
verses.nlt_text: "What happened?" David demanded. "Tell me how the battle went." The man replied, "Our entire army fled from the battle. Many of the men are dead, and Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead."

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?
verses.nlt_text: "How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?" David demanded of the young man.

verses.kjv_text: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
verses.nlt_text: The man answered, "I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and there was Saul leaning on his spear with the enemy chariots and charioteers closing in on him.

verses.kjv_text: And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here {am} I. {Here...: Heb. Behold me}
verses.nlt_text: When he turned and saw me, he cried out for me to come to him. 'How can I help?' I asked him.

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto me, Who {art} thou? And I answered him, I {am} an Amalekite.
verses.nlt_text: "He responded, 'Who are you?'" 'I am an Amalekite,' I told him.

verses.kjv_text: He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life {is} yet whole in me. {anguish...: or, my coat of mail (or, my embroidered coat) hindereth me, that my, etc}
verses.nlt_text: "Then he begged me, 'Come over here and put me out of my misery, for I am in terrible pain and want to die.'

verses.kjv_text: So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that {was} upon his head, and the bracelet that {was} on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
verses.nlt_text: "So I killed him," the Amalekite told David, "for I knew he couldn't live. Then I took his crown and his armband, and I have brought them here to you, my lord."

verses.kjv_text: Then David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that {were} with him:
verses.nlt_text: David and his men tore their clothes in sorrow when they heard the news.

verses.kjv_text: And they mourned, and wept, and fasted until even, for Saul, and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of the LORD, and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.
verses.nlt_text: They mourned and wept and fasted all day for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the LORD's army and the nation of Israel, because they had died by the sword that day.

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence {art} thou? And he answered, I {am} the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
verses.nlt_text: Then David said to the young man who had brought the news, "Where are you from?" And he replied, "I am a foreigner, an Amalekite, who lives in your land."

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the LORD'S anointed?
verses.nlt_text: "Why were you not afraid to kill the LORD's anointed one?" David asked.

verses.kjv_text: And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, {and} fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
verses.nlt_text: Then David said to one of his men, "Kill him!" So the man thrust his sword into the Amalekite and killed him.

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto him, Thy blood {be} upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the LORD'S anointed.
verses.nlt_text: "You have condemned yourself," David said, "for you yourself confessed that you killed the LORD's anointed one."

verses.kjv_text: And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:
verses.nlt_text: Then David composed a funeral song for Saul and Jonathan,

verses.kjv_text: (Also he bade them teach the children of Judah {the use of} the bow: behold, {it is} written in the book of Jasher.) {of Jasher: or, of the upright}
verses.nlt_text: and he commanded that it be taught to the people of Judah. It is known as the Song of the Bow, and it is recorded in [The Book of Jashar.]

verses.kjv_text: The beauty of Israel is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!
verses.nlt_text: Your pride and joy, O Israel, lies dead on the hills! Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen!

verses.kjv_text: Tell {it} not in Gath, publish {it} not in the streets of Askelon; lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.
verses.nlt_text: Don't announce the news in Gath, don't proclaim it in the streets of Ashkelon, or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice and the pagans will laugh in triumph.

verses.kjv_text: Ye mountains of Gilboa, {let there be} no dew, neither {let there be} rain, upon you, nor fields of offerings: for there the shield of the mighty is vilely cast away, the shield of Saul, {as though he had} not {been} anointed with oil.
verses.nlt_text: O mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain upon you, nor fruitful fields producing offerings of grain. For there the shield of the mighty heroes was defiled; the shield of Saul will no longer be anointed with oil.

verses.kjv_text: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, the bow of Jonathan turned not back, and the sword of Saul returned not empty.
verses.nlt_text: The bow of Jonathan was powerful, and the sword of Saul did its mighty work. They shed the blood of their enemies and pierced the bodies of mighty heroes.

verses.kjv_text: Saul and Jonathan {were} lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions. {pleasant: or, sweet}
verses.nlt_text: How beloved and gracious were Saul and Jonathan! They were together in life and in death. They were swifter than eagles, stronger than lions.

verses.kjv_text: Ye daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you in scarlet, with {other} delights, who put on ornaments of gold upon your apparel.
verses.nlt_text: O women of Israel, weep for Saul, for he dressed you in luxurious scarlet clothing, in garments decorated with gold.

verses.kjv_text: How are the mighty fallen in the midst of the battle! O Jonathan, {thou wast} slain in thine high places.
verses.nlt_text: Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen in battle! Jonathan lies dead on the hills.

verses.kjv_text: I am distressed for thee, my brother Jonathan: very pleasant hast thou been unto me: thy love to me was wonderful, passing the love of women.
verses.nlt_text: How I weep for you, my brother Jonathan! Oh, how much I loved you! And your love for me was deep, deeper than the love of women!

verses.kjv_text: How are the mighty fallen, and the weapons of war perished!
verses.nlt_text: Oh, how the mighty heroes have fallen! Stripped of their weapons, they lie dead.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after this, that David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.
verses.nlt_text: After this, David asked the LORD, "Should I move back to one of the towns of Judah?" "Yes," the LORD replied.Then David asked, "Which town should I go to?" "To Hebron," the LORD answered.

verses.kjv_text: So David went up thither, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail Nabal's wife the Carmelite.
verses.nlt_text: David's two wives were Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel. So David and his wives

verses.kjv_text: And his men that {were} with him did David bring up, every man with his household: and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.
verses.nlt_text: and his men and their families all moved to Judah, and they settled in the villages near Hebron.

verses.kjv_text: And the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, {That} the men of Jabeshgilead {were they} that buried Saul.
verses.nlt_text: Then the men of Judah came to David and crowned him king over the people of Judah.When David heard that the men of Jabesh-gilead had buried Saul,

verses.kjv_text: And David sent messengers unto the men of Jabeshgilead, and said unto them, Blessed {be} ye of the LORD, that ye have shewed this kindness unto your lord, {even} unto Saul, and have buried him.
verses.nlt_text: he sent them this message: "May the LORD bless you for being so loyal to your master Saul and giving him a decent burial.

verses.kjv_text: And now the LORD shew kindness and truth unto you: and I also will requite you this kindness, because ye have done this thing.
verses.nlt_text: May the LORD be loyal to you in return and reward you with his unfailing love! And I, too, will reward you for what you have done.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore now let your hands be strengthened, and be ye valiant: for your master Saul is dead, and also the house of Judah have anointed me king over them. {be ye...: Heb. be ye the sons of valour}
verses.nlt_text: Now that Saul is dead, I ask you to be my strong and loyal subjects like the people of Judah, who have anointed me as their new king."

verses.kjv_text: But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim; {Saul's host: Heb. the host which was Saul's} {Ishbosheth: or, Eshbaal}
verses.nlt_text: But Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had already gone to Mahanaim with Saul's son Ishbosheth.

verses.kjv_text: And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
verses.nlt_text: There he proclaimed Ishbosheth king over Gilead, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin, the land of the Ashurites, and all the rest of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: Ishbosheth Saul's son {was} forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.
verses.nlt_text: Ishbosheth, Saul's son, was forty years old when he became king, and he ruled from Mahanaim for two years. Meanwhile, the people of Judah remained loyal to David.

verses.kjv_text: And the time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months. {time: Heb. number of days}
verses.nlt_text: David made Hebron his capital, and he ruled as king of Judah for seven and a half years.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner the son of Ner, and the servants of Ishbosheth the son of Saul, went out from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
verses.nlt_text: One day Abner led Ishbosheth's troops from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

verses.kjv_text: And Joab the son of Zeruiah, and the servants of David, went out, and met together by the pool of Gibeon: and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool. {together: Heb. them together}
verses.nlt_text: About the same time, Joab son of Zeruiah led David's troops out and met them at the pool of Gibeon. The two groups sat down there, facing each other from opposite sides of the pool.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner said to Joab, Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.
verses.nlt_text: Then Abner suggested to Joab, "Let's have a few of our warriors fight hand to hand here in front of us." "All right," Joab agreed.

verses.kjv_text: Then there arose and went over by number twelve of Benjamin, which {pertained} to Ishbosheth the son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.
verses.nlt_text: So twelve men were chosen to fight from each side-- twelve men of Benjamin representing Ishbosheth son of Saul, and twelve representing David.

verses.kjv_text: And they caught every one his fellow by the head, and {thrust} his sword in his fellow's side; so they fell down together: wherefore that place was called Helkathhazzurim, which {is} in Gibeon. {Helkathhazzurim: that is, The field of strong men}
verses.nlt_text: Each one grabbed his opponent by the hair and thrust his sword into the other's side so that all of them died. So this place at Gibeon has been known ever since as the Field of Swords.

verses.kjv_text: And there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.
verses.nlt_text: A fierce battle followed that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by the forces of David.

verses.kjv_text: And there were three sons of Zeruiah there, Joab, and Abishai, and Asahel: and Asahel {was as} light of foot as a wild roe. {of foot: Heb. of his feet} {as a wild...: Heb. as one of the roes that is in the field}
verses.nlt_text: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel-- the three sons of Zeruiah-- were among David's forces that day. Asahel could run like a gazelle,

verses.kjv_text: And Asahel pursued after Abner; and in going he turned not to the right hand nor to the left from following Abner. {from...: Heb. from after Abner}
verses.nlt_text: and he began chasing Abner. He pursued him relentlessly, not stopping for anything.

verses.kjv_text: Then Abner looked behind him, and said, {Art} thou Asahel? And he answered, I {am}.
verses.nlt_text: When Abner looked back and saw him coming, he called out, "Is that you, Asahel?" "Yes, it is," he replied.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner said to him, Turn thee aside to thy right hand or to thy left, and lay thee hold on one of the young men, and take thee his armour. But Asahel would not turn aside from following of him. {armour: or, spoil}
verses.nlt_text: "Go fight someone else!" Abner warned. "Take on one of the younger men, and strip him of his weapons." But Asahel kept right on chasing Abner.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner said again to Asahel, Turn thee aside from following me: wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?
verses.nlt_text: Again Abner shouted to him, "Get away from here! I don't want to kill you. How could I ever face your brother Joab again?"

verses.kjv_text: Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth {rib}, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, {that} as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
verses.nlt_text: But Asahel refused to turn back, so Abner thrust the butt end of his spear through Asahel's stomach, and the spear came out through his back. He stumbled to the ground and died there. And everyone who came by that spot stopped and stood still when they saw Asahel lying there.

verses.kjv_text: Joab also and Abishai pursued after Abner: and the sun went down when they were come to the hill of Ammah, that {lieth} before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon.
verses.nlt_text: When Joab and Abishai found out what had happened, they set out after Abner. The sun was just going down as they arrived at the hill of Ammah near Giah, along the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.

verses.kjv_text: And the children of Benjamin gathered themselves together after Abner, and became one troop, and stood on the top of an hill.
verses.nlt_text: Abner's troops from the tribe of Benjamin regrouped there at the top of the hill to take a stand.

verses.kjv_text: Then Abner called to Joab, and said, Shall the sword devour for ever? knowest thou not that it will be bitterness in the latter end? how long shall it be then, ere thou bid the people return from following their brethren?
verses.nlt_text: Abner shouted down to Joab, "Must we always be killing each other? Don't you realize that bitterness is the only result? When will you call off your men from chasing their Israelite brothers?"

verses.kjv_text: And Joab said, {As} God liveth, unless thou hadst spoken, surely then in the morning the people had gone up every one from following his brother. {in the...: Heb. from the morning} {gone...: or, gone away}
verses.nlt_text: Then Joab said, "God only knows what would have happened if you hadn't spoken, for we would have chased you all night if necessary."

verses.kjv_text: So Joab blew a trumpet, and all the people stood still, and pursued after Israel no more, neither fought they any more.
verses.nlt_text: So Joab blew the ram's horn, and his men stopped chasing the troops of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner and his men walked all that night through the plain, and passed over Jordan, and went through all Bithron, and they came to Mahanaim.
verses.nlt_text: All that night Abner and his men retreated through the Jordan Valley. They crossed the Jordan River, traveling all through the morning, and didn't stop until they arrived at Mahanaim.

verses.kjv_text: And Joab returned from following Abner: and when he had gathered all the people together, there lacked of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel.
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Joab and his men also returned home. When Joab counted his casualties, he discovered that only 19 men were missing in addition to Asahel.

verses.kjv_text: But the servants of David had smitten of Benjamin, and of Abner's men, {so that} three hundred and threescore men died.
verses.nlt_text: But 360 of Abner's men had been killed, all from the tribe of Benjamin.

verses.kjv_text: And they took up Asahel, and buried him in the sepulchre of his father, which {was in} Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and they came to Hebron at break of day.
verses.nlt_text: Joab and his men took Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him there in his father's tomb. Then they traveled all night and reached Hebron at daybreak.

verses.kjv_text: Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.
verses.nlt_text: That was the beginning of a long war between those who were loyal to Saul and those loyal to David. As time passed David became stronger and stronger, while Saul's dynasty became weaker and weaker.

verses.kjv_text: And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;
verses.nlt_text: These are the sons who were born to David in Hebron: The oldest was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel.

verses.kjv_text: And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; {Chileab: or, Daniel}
verses.nlt_text: The second was Daniel, whose mother was Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel. The third was Absalom, whose mother was Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur.

verses.kjv_text: And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;
verses.nlt_text: The fourth was Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith. The fifth was Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital.

verses.kjv_text: And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David's wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
verses.nlt_text: The sixth was Ithream, whose mother was Eglah, David's wife. These sons were all born to David in Hebron.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.
verses.nlt_text: As the war between the house of Saul and the house of David went on, Abner became a powerful leader among those loyal to Saul.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul had a concubine, whose name {was} Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and {Ishbosheth} said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father's concubine?
verses.nlt_text: One day Ishbosheth, Saul's son, accused Abner of sleeping with one of his father's concubines, a woman named Rizpah, daughter of Aiah.

verses.kjv_text: Then was Abner very wroth for the words of Ishbosheth, and said, {Am} I a dog's head, which against Judah do shew kindness this day unto the house of Saul thy father, to his brethren, and to his friends, and have not delivered thee into the hand of David, that thou chargest me to day with a fault concerning this woman?
verses.nlt_text: Abner was furious. "Am I some Judean dog to be kicked around like this?" he shouted. "After all I have done for your father, Saul, and his family and friends by not handing you over to David, is this my reward-- that you find fault with me about this woman?

verses.kjv_text: So do God to Abner, and more also, except, as the LORD hath sworn to David, even so I do to him;
verses.nlt_text: May God strike me and even kill me if I don't do everything I can to help David get what the LORD has promised him!

verses.kjv_text: To translate the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to set up the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba.
verses.nlt_text: I'm going to take Saul's kingdom and give it to David. I will establish the throne of David over Israel as well as Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south."

verses.kjv_text: And he could not answer Abner a word again, because he feared him.
verses.nlt_text: Ishbosheth didn't dare say another word because he was afraid of what Abner might do.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner sent messengers to David on his behalf, saying, Whose {is} the land? saying {also}, Make thy league with me, and, behold, my hand {shall be} with thee, to bring about all Israel unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: Then Abner sent messengers to David, saying, "Doesn't the entire land belong to you? Make a solemn pact with me, and I will help turn over all of Israel to you."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal Saul's daughter, when thou comest to see my face. {that is: Heb. saying}
verses.nlt_text: "All right," David replied, "but I will not negotiate with you unless you bring back my wife Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come."

verses.kjv_text: And David sent messengers to Ishbosheth Saul's son, saying, Deliver {me} my wife Michal, which I espoused to me for an hundred foreskins of the Philistines.
verses.nlt_text: David then sent this message to Ishbosheth, Saul's son: "Give me back my wife Michal, for I bought her with the lives of 100 Philistines."

verses.kjv_text: And Ishbosheth sent, and took her from {her} husband, {even} from Phaltiel the son of Laish. {Phaltiel: also called, Phalti}
verses.nlt_text: So Ishbosheth took Michal away from her husband, Palti son of Laish.

verses.kjv_text: And her husband went with her along weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return. And he returned. {along...: Heb. going and weeping}
verses.nlt_text: Palti followed along behind her as far as Bahurim, weeping as he went. Then Abner told him, "Go back home!" So Palti returned.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner had communication with the elders of Israel, saying, Ye sought for David in times past {to be} king over you: {in times...: Heb. both yesterday and the third day}
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Abner had consulted with the elders of Israel. "For some time now," he told them, "you have wanted to make David your king.

verses.kjv_text: Now then do {it}: for the LORD hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
verses.nlt_text: Now is the time! For the LORD has said, 'I have chosen David to save my people Israel from the hands of the Philistines and from all their other enemies.'"

verses.kjv_text: And Abner also spake in the ears of Benjamin: and Abner went also to speak in the ears of David in Hebron all that seemed good to Israel, and that seemed good to the whole house of Benjamin.
verses.nlt_text: Abner also spoke with the men of Benjamin. Then he went to Hebron to tell David that all the people of Israel and Benjamin had agreed to support him.

verses.kjv_text: So Abner came to David to Hebron, and twenty men with him. And David made Abner and the men that {were} with him a feast.
verses.nlt_text: When Abner and twenty of his men came to Hebron, David entertained them with a great feast.

verses.kjv_text: And Abner said unto David, I will arise and go, and will gather all Israel unto my lord the king, that they may make a league with thee, and that thou mayest reign over all that thine heart desireth. And David sent Abner away; and he went in peace.
verses.nlt_text: Then Abner said to David, "Let me go and call an assembly of all Israel to support my lord the king. They will make a covenant with you to make you their king, and you will rule over everything your heart desires." So David sent Abner safely on his way.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, the servants of David and Joab came from {pursuing} a troop, and brought in a great spoil with them: but Abner {was} not with David in Hebron; for he had sent him away, and he was gone in peace.
verses.nlt_text: But just after David had sent Abner away in safety, Joab and some of David's troops returned from a raid, bringing much plunder with them.

verses.kjv_text: When Joab and all the host that {was} with him were come, they told Joab, saying, Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he hath sent him away, and he is gone in peace.
verses.nlt_text: When Joab arrived, he was told that Abner had just been there visiting the king and had been sent away in safety.

verses.kjv_text: Then Joab came to the king, and said, What hast thou done? behold, Abner came unto thee; why {is} it {that} thou hast sent him away, and he is quite gone?
verses.nlt_text: Joab rushed to the king and demanded, "What have you done? What do you mean by letting Abner get away?

verses.kjv_text: Thou knowest Abner the son of Ner, that he came to deceive thee, and to know thy going out and thy coming in, and to know all that thou doest.
verses.nlt_text: You know perfectly well that he came to spy on you and find out everything you're doing!"

verses.kjv_text: And when Joab was come out from David, he sent messengers after Abner, which brought him again from the well of Sirah: but David knew {it} not.
verses.nlt_text: Joab then left David and sent messengers to catch up with Abner, asking him to return. They found him at the well of Sirah and brought him back, though David knew nothing about it.

verses.kjv_text: And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the fifth {rib}, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother. {quietly: or, peaceably}
verses.nlt_text: When Abner arrived back at Hebron, Joab took him aside at the gateway as if to speak with him privately. But then he stabbed Abner in the stomach and killed him in revenge for killing his brother Asahel.

verses.kjv_text: And afterward when David heard {it}, he said, I and my kingdom {are} guiltless before the LORD for ever from the blood of Abner the son of Ner: {blood: Heb. bloods}
verses.nlt_text: When David heard about it, he declared, "I vow by the LORD that I and my kingdom are forever innocent of this crime against Abner son of Ner.

verses.kjv_text: Let it rest on the head of Joab, and on all his father's house; and let there not fail from the house of Joab one that hath an issue, or that is a leper, or that leaneth on a staff, or that falleth on the sword, or that lacketh bread. {fail: Heb. be cut off}
verses.nlt_text: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. May the family of Joab be cursed in every generation with a man who has open sores or leprosy or who walks on crutches or dies by the sword or begs for food!"

verses.kjv_text: So Joab and Abishai his brother slew Abner, because he had slain their brother Asahel at Gibeon in the battle.
verses.nlt_text: So Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because Abner had killed their brother Asahel at the battle of Gibeon.

verses.kjv_text: And David said to Joab, and to all the people that {were} with him, Rend your clothes, and gird you with sackcloth, and mourn before Abner. And king David {himself} followed the bier. {bier: Heb. bed}
verses.nlt_text: Then David said to Joab and all those who were with him, "Tear your clothes and put on burlap. Mourn for Abner." And King David himself walked behind the procession to the grave.

verses.kjv_text: And they buried Abner in Hebron: and the king lifted up his voice, and wept at the grave of Abner; and all the people wept.
verses.nlt_text: They buried Abner in Hebron, and the king and all the people wept at his graveside.

verses.kjv_text: And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Died Abner as a fool dieth?
verses.nlt_text: Then the king sang this funeral song for Abner: "Should Abner have died as fools die?

verses.kjv_text: Thy hands {were} not bound, nor thy feet put into fetters: as a man falleth before wicked men, {so} fellest thou. And all the people wept again over him. {wicked...: Heb. children of iniquity}
verses.nlt_text: Your hands were not bound; your feet were not chained. No, you were murdered-- the victim of a wicked plot." All the people wept again for Abner.

verses.kjv_text: And when all the people came to cause David to eat meat while it was yet day, David sware, saying, So do God to me, and more also, if I taste bread, or ought else, till the sun be down.
verses.nlt_text: David had refused to eat anything on the day of the funeral, and now everyone begged him to eat. But David had made a vow, saying, "May God strike me and even kill me if I eat anything before sundown."

verses.kjv_text: And all the people took notice {of it}, and it pleased them: as whatsoever the king did pleased all the people. {pleased them: Heb. was good in their eyes}
verses.nlt_text: This pleased the people very much. In fact, everything the king did pleased them!

verses.kjv_text: For all the people and all Israel understood that day that it was not of the king to slay Abner the son of Ner.
verses.nlt_text: So everyone in Judah and all Israel understood that David was not responsible for Abner's murder.

verses.kjv_text: And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Israel?
verses.nlt_text: Then King David said to his officials, "Don't you realize that a great commander has fallen today in Israel?

verses.kjv_text: And I {am} this day weak, though anointed king; and these men the sons of Zeruiah {be} too hard for me: the LORD shall reward the doer of evil according to his wickedness. {weak: Heb. tender}
verses.nlt_text: And even though I am the anointed king, these two sons of Zeruiah-- Joab and Abishai-- are too strong for me to control. So may the LORD repay these evil men for their evil deeds."

verses.kjv_text: And when Saul's son heard that Abner was dead in Hebron, his hands were feeble, and all the Israelites were troubled.
verses.nlt_text: When Ishbosheth, Saul's son, heard about Abner's death at Hebron, he lost all courage, and all Israel became paralyzed with fear.

verses.kjv_text: And Saul's son had two men {that were} captains of bands: the name of the one {was} Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, the sons of Rimmon a Beerothite, of the children of Benjamin: (for Beeroth also was reckoned to Benjamin: {other: Heb. second}
verses.nlt_text: Now there were two brothers, Baanah and Recab, who were captains of Ishbosheth's raiding parties. They were sons of Rimmon, a member of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Beeroth. The town of Beeroth is now part of Benjamin's territory

verses.kjv_text: And the Beerothites fled to Gittaim, and were sojourners there until this day.)
verses.nlt_text: because the original people of Beeroth fled to Gittaim, where they still live as foreigners.

verses.kjv_text: And Jonathan, Saul's son, had a son {that was} lame of {his} feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name {was} Mephibosheth. {Mephibosheth: or, Meribbaal}
verses.nlt_text: (Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who was crippled as a child. He was five years old when the report came from Jezreel that Saul and Jonathan had been killed in battle. When the child's nurse heard the news, she picked him up and fled. But as she hurried away, she dropped him, and he became crippled.)

verses.kjv_text: And the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, went, and came about the heat of the day to the house of Ishbosheth, who lay on a bed at noon.
verses.nlt_text: One day Recab and Baanah, the sons of Rimmon from Beeroth, went to Ishbosheth's house around noon as he was taking his midday rest.

verses.kjv_text: And they came thither into the midst of the house, {as though} they would have fetched wheat; and they smote him under the fifth {rib}: and Rechab and Baanah his brother escaped.
verses.nlt_text: The doorkeeper, who had been sifting wheat, became drowsy and fell asleep. So Recab and Baanah slipped past her.

verses.kjv_text: For when they came into the house, he lay on his bed in his bedchamber, and they smote him, and slew him, and beheaded him, and took his head, and gat them away through the plain all night.
verses.nlt_text: They went into the house and found Ishbosheth sleeping on his bed. They struck and killed him and cut off his head. Then, taking his head with them, they fled across the Jordan Valley through the night.

verses.kjv_text: And they brought the head of Ishbosheth unto David to Hebron, and said to the king, Behold the head of Ishbosheth the son of Saul thine enemy, which sought thy life; and the LORD hath avenged my lord the king this day of Saul, and of his seed.
verses.nlt_text: When they arrived at Hebron, they presented Ishbosheth's head to David. "Look!" they exclaimed to the king. "Here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you. Today the LORD has given my lord the king revenge on Saul and his entire family!"

verses.kjv_text: And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, {As} the LORD liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
verses.nlt_text: But David said to Recab and Baanah, "The LORD, who saves me from all my enemies, is my witness.

verses.kjv_text: When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who {thought} that I would have given him a reward for his tidings: {thinking...: Heb. he was in his own eyes as a bringer, etc} {who...: or, which was the reward I gave him for his tidings}
verses.nlt_text: Someone once told me, 'Saul is dead,' thinking he was bringing me good news. But I seized him and killed him at Ziklag. That's the reward I gave him for his news!

verses.kjv_text: How much more, when wicked men have slain a righteous person in his own house upon his bed? shall I not therefore now require his blood of your hand, and take you away from the earth?
verses.nlt_text: How much more should I reward evil men who have killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed? Shouldn't I hold you responsible for his blood and rid the earth of you?"

verses.kjv_text: And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged {them} up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ishbosheth, and buried {it} in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.
verses.nlt_text: So David ordered his young men to kill them, and they did. They cut off their hands and feet and hung their bodies beside the pool in Hebron. Then they took Ishbosheth's head and buried it in Abner's tomb in Hebron.

verses.kjv_text: Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we {are} thy bone and thy flesh.
verses.nlt_text: Then all the tribes of Israel went to David at Hebron and told him, "We are your own flesh and blood.

verses.kjv_text: Also in time past, when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel: and the LORD said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.
verses.nlt_text: In the past, when Saul was our king, you were the one who really led the forces of Israel. And the LORD told you, 'You will be the shepherd of my people Israel. You will be Israel's leader.' "

verses.kjv_text: So all the elders of Israel came to the king to Hebron; and king David made a league with them in Hebron before the LORD: and they anointed David king over Israel.
verses.nlt_text: So there at Hebron, King David made a covenant before the LORD with all the elders of Israel. And they anointed him king of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: David {was} thirty years old when he began to reign, {and} he reigned forty years.
verses.nlt_text: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years in all.

verses.kjv_text: In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.
verses.nlt_text: He had reigned over Judah from Hebron for seven years and six months, and from Jerusalem he reigned over all Israel and Judah for thirty-three years.

verses.kjv_text: And the king and his men went to Jerusalem unto the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land: which spake unto David, saying, Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither: thinking, David cannot come in hither. {thinking...: or, saying David shall not, etc}
verses.nlt_text: David then led his men to Jerusalem to fight against the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of the land who were living there. The Jebusites taunted David, saying, "You'll never get in here! Even the blind and lame could keep you out!" For the Jebusites thought they were safe.

verses.kjv_text: Nevertheless David took the strong hold of Zion: the same {is} the city of David.
verses.nlt_text: But David captured the fortress of Zion, which is now called the City of David.

verses.kjv_text: And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, {that are} hated of David's soul, {he shall be chief and captain}. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. {Wherefore...: or, Because they had said, even the blind and the lame, He shall not}
verses.nlt_text: On the day of the attack, David said to his troops, "I hate those 'lame' and 'blind' Jebusites. Whoever attacks them should strike by going into the city through the water tunnel. " That is the origin of the saying, "The blind and the lame may not enter the house."

verses.kjv_text: So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David. And David built round about from Millo and inward.
verses.nlt_text: So David made the fortress his home, and he called it the City of David. He extended the city, starting at the supporting terraces and working inward.

verses.kjv_text: And David went on, and grew great, and the LORD God of hosts {was} with him. {went...: Heb. went, going and growing}
verses.nlt_text: And David became more and more powerful, because the LORD God of Heaven's Armies was with him.

verses.kjv_text: And Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, and cedar trees, and carpenters, and masons: and they built David an house. {masons: Heb. hewers of the stone of the wall}
verses.nlt_text: Then King Hiram of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar timber and carpenters and stonemasons, and they built David a palace.

verses.kjv_text: And David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, and that he had exalted his kingdom for his people Israel's sake.
verses.nlt_text: And David realized that the LORD had confirmed him as king over Israel and had blessed his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And David took {him} more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he was come from Hebron: and there were yet sons and daughters born to David.
verses.nlt_text: After moving from Hebron to Jerusalem, David married more concubines and wives, and they had more sons and daughters.

verses.kjv_text: And these {be} the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon,
verses.nlt_text: These are the names of David's sons who were born in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

verses.kjv_text: Ibhar also, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia,
verses.nlt_text: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

verses.kjv_text: And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
verses.nlt_text: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

verses.kjv_text: But when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines came up to seek David; and David heard {of it}, and went down to the hold.
verses.nlt_text: When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king of Israel, they mobilized all their forces to capture him. But David was told they were coming, so he went into the stronghold.

verses.kjv_text: The Philistines also came and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.nlt_text: The Philistines arrived and spread out across the valley of Rephaim.

verses.kjv_text: And David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into mine hand? And the LORD said unto David, Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand.
verses.nlt_text: So David asked the LORD, "Should I go out to fight the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD replied to David, "Yes, go ahead. I will certainly hand them over to you."

verses.kjv_text: And David came to Baalperazim, and David smote them there, and said, The LORD hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters. Therefore he called the name of that place Baalperazim. {Baalperazim: that is, the plain of breaches}
verses.nlt_text: So David went to Baal-perazim and defeated the Philistines there. "The LORD did it!" David exclaimed. "He burst through my enemies like a raging flood!" So he named that place Baal-perazim (which means "the Lord who bursts through").

verses.kjv_text: And there they left their images, and David and his men burned them. {burned...: or, took them away}
verses.nlt_text: The Philistines had abandoned their idols there, so David and his men confiscated them.

verses.kjv_text: And the Philistines came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rephaim.
verses.nlt_text: But after a while the Philistines returned and again spread out across the valley of Rephaim.

verses.kjv_text: And when David enquired of the LORD, he said, Thou shalt not go up; {but} fetch a compass behind them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.
verses.nlt_text: And again David asked the LORD what to do. "Do not attack them straight on," the LORD replied. "Instead, circle around behind and attack them near the poplar trees.

verses.kjv_text: And let it be, when thou hearest the sound of a going in the tops of the mulberry trees, that then thou shalt bestir thyself: for then shall the LORD go out before thee, to smite the host of the Philistines.
verses.nlt_text: When you hear a sound like marching feet in the tops of the poplar trees, be on the alert! That will be the signal that the LORD is moving ahead of you to strike down the Philistine army."

verses.kjv_text: And David did so, as the LORD had commanded him; and smote the Philistines from Geba until thou come to Gazer. {Geba: also called, Gibeon}
verses.nlt_text: So David did what the LORD commanded, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer.

verses.kjv_text: Again, David gathered together all {the} chosen {men} of Israel, thirty thousand.
verses.nlt_text: Then David again gathered all the elite troops in Israel, 30,000 in all.

verses.kjv_text: And David arose, and went with all the people that {were} with him from Baale of Judah, to bring up from thence the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the LORD of hosts that dwelleth {between} the cherubims. {Baale: or, Baalah, that is, Kirjathjearim} {whose name...: or, at which the name, even the name of the LORD of hosts, was called upon}
verses.nlt_text: He led them to Baalah of Judah to bring back the Ark of God, which bears the name of the LORD of Heaven's Armies, who is enthroned between the cherubim.

verses.kjv_text: And they set the ark of God upon a new cart, and brought it out of the house of Abinadab that {was} in Gibeah: and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart. {set: Heb. made to ride} {Gibeah: or, the hill}
verses.nlt_text: They placed the Ark of God on a new cart and brought it from Abinadab's house, which was on a hill. Uzzah and Ahio, Abinadab's sons, were guiding the cart as it left the house,

verses.kjv_text: And they brought it out of the house of Abinadab which {was} at Gibeah, accompanying the ark of God: and Ahio went before the ark. {accompanying: Heb. with}
verses.nlt_text: carrying the Ark of God. Ahio walked in front of the Ark.

verses.kjv_text: And David and all the house of Israel played before the LORD on all manner of {instruments made of} fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.
verses.nlt_text: David and all the people of Israel were celebrating before the LORD, singing songs and playing all kinds of musical instruments-- lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets, and cymbals.

verses.kjv_text: And when they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth {his hand} to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook {it}. {Nachon: also called Chidon} {shook it: or, stumbled}
verses.nlt_text: But when they arrived at the threshing floor of Nacon, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out his hand and steadied the Ark of God.

verses.kjv_text: And the anger of the LORD was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for {his} error; and there he died by the ark of God. {error: or, rashness}
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD's anger was aroused against Uzzah, and God struck him dead because of this. So Uzzah died right there beside the Ark of God.

verses.kjv_text: And David was displeased, because the LORD had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perezuzzah to this day. {made: Heb. broken} {Perezuzzah: that is, the breach of Uzzah}
verses.nlt_text: David was angry because the LORD's anger had burst out against Uzzah. He named that place Perez-uzzah (which means "to burst out against Uzzah"), as it is still called today.

verses.kjv_text: And David was afraid of the LORD that day, and said, How shall the ark of the LORD come to me?
verses.nlt_text: David was now afraid of the LORD, and he asked, "How can I ever bring the Ark of the LORD back into my care?"

verses.kjv_text: So David would not remove the ark of the LORD unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obededom the Gittite.
verses.nlt_text: So David decided not to move the Ark of the LORD into the City of David. Instead, he took it to the house of Obed-edom of Gath.

verses.kjv_text: And the ark of the LORD continued in the house of Obededom the Gittite three months: and the LORD blessed Obededom, and all his household.
verses.nlt_text: The Ark of the LORD remained there in Obed-edom's house for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and his entire household.

verses.kjv_text: And it was told king David, saying, The LORD hath blessed the house of Obededom, and all that {pertaineth} unto him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obededom into the city of David with gladness.
verses.nlt_text: Then King David was told, "The LORD has blessed Obed-edom's household and everything he has because of the Ark of God." So David went there and brought the Ark of God from the house of Obed-edom to the City of David with a great celebration.

verses.kjv_text: And it was {so}, that when they that bare the ark of the LORD had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings.
verses.nlt_text: After the men who were carrying the Ark of the LORD had gone six steps, David sacrificed a bull and a fattened calf.

verses.kjv_text: And David danced before the LORD with all {his} might; and David {was} girded with a linen ephod.
verses.nlt_text: And David danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing a priestly garment.

verses.kjv_text: So David and all the house of Israel brought up the ark of the LORD with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
verses.nlt_text: So David and all the people of Israel brought up the Ark of the LORD with shouts of joy and the blowing of rams' horns.

verses.kjv_text: And as the ark of the LORD came into the city of David, Michal Saul's daughter looked through a window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she despised him in her heart.
verses.nlt_text: But as the Ark of the LORD entered the City of David, Michal, the daughter of Saul, looked down from her window. When she saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD, she was filled with contempt for him.

verses.kjv_text: And they brought in the ark of the LORD, and set it in his place, in the midst of the tabernacle that David had pitched for it: and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD. {pitched: Heb. stretched}
verses.nlt_text: They brought the Ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the special tent David had prepared for it. And David sacrificed burnt offerings and peace offerings to the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And as soon as David had made an end of offering burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts.
verses.nlt_text: When he had finished his sacrifices, David blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Heaven's Armies.

verses.kjv_text: And he dealt among all the people, {even} among the whole multitude of Israel, as well to the women as men, to every one a cake of bread, and a good piece {of flesh}, and a flagon {of wine}. So all the people departed every one to his house.
verses.nlt_text: Then he gave to every Israelite man and woman in the crowd a loaf of bread, a cake of dates, and a cake of raisins. Then all the people returned to their homes.

verses.kjv_text: Then David returned to bless his household. And Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, How glorious was the king of Israel to day, who uncovered himself to day in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself! {shamelessly: or, openly}
verses.nlt_text: When David returned home to bless his own family, Michal, the daughter of Saul, came out to meet him. She said in disgust, "How distinguished the king of Israel looked today, shamelessly exposing himself to the servant girls like any vulgar person might do!"

verses.kjv_text: And David said unto Michal, {It was} before the LORD, which chose me before thy father, and before all his house, to appoint me ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel: therefore will I play before the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: David retorted to Michal, "I was dancing before the LORD, who chose me above your father and all his family! He appointed me as the leader of Israel, the people of the LORD, so I celebrate before the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And I will yet be more vile than thus, and will be base in mine own sight: and of the maidservants which thou hast spoken of, of them shall I be had in honour. {of the...: or, of the handmaids of my servants}
verses.nlt_text: Yes, and I am willing to look even more foolish than this, even to be humiliated in my own eyes! But those servant girls you mentioned will indeed think I am distinguished!"

verses.kjv_text: Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.
verses.nlt_text: So Michal, the daughter of Saul, remained childless throughout her entire life.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when the king sat in his house, and the LORD had given him rest round about from all his enemies;
verses.nlt_text: When King David was settled in his palace and the LORD had given him rest from all the surrounding enemies,

verses.kjv_text: That the king said unto Nathan the prophet, See now, I dwell in an house of cedar, but the ark of God dwelleth within curtains.
verses.nlt_text: the king summoned Nathan the prophet. "Look," David said, "I am living in a beautiful cedar palace, but the Ark of God is out there in a tent!"

verses.kjv_text: And Nathan said to the king, Go, do all that {is} in thine heart; for the LORD {is} with thee.
verses.nlt_text: Nathan replied to the king, "Go ahead and do whatever you have in mind, for the LORD is with you."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass that night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan, saying,
verses.nlt_text: But that same night the LORD said to Nathan,

verses.kjv_text: Go and tell my servant David, Thus saith the LORD, Shalt thou build me an house for me to dwell in? {my servant...: Heb. to my servant, to David}
verses.nlt_text: "Go and tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD has declared: Are you the one to build a house for me to live in?

verses.kjv_text: Whereas I have not dwelt in {any} house since the time that I brought up the children of Israel out of Egypt, even to this day, but have walked in a tent and in a tabernacle.
verses.nlt_text: I have never lived in a house, from the day I brought the Israelites out of Egypt until this very day. I have always moved from one place to another with a tent and a Tabernacle as my dwelling.

verses.kjv_text: In all {the places} wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build ye not me an house of cedar? {any of...: any of the judges}
verses.nlt_text: Yet no matter where I have gone with the Israelites, I have never once complained to Israel's tribal leaders, the shepherds of my people Israel. I have never asked them, "Why haven't you built me a beautiful cedar house?"'

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore so shalt thou say unto my servant David, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people, over Israel: {from following: Heb. from after}
verses.nlt_text: "Now go and say to my servant David, 'This is what the LORD of Heaven's Armies has declared: I took you from tending sheep in the pasture and selected you to be the leader of my people Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And I was with thee whithersoever thou wentest, and have cut off all thine enemies out of thy sight, and have made thee a great name, like unto the name of the great {men} that {are} in the earth. {out of...: Heb. from thy face}
verses.nlt_text: I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have destroyed all your enemies before your eyes. Now I will make your name as famous as anyone who has ever lived on the earth!

verses.kjv_text: Moreover I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in a place of their own, and move no more; neither shall the children of wickedness afflict them any more, as beforetime,
verses.nlt_text: And I will provide a homeland for my people Israel, planting them in a secure place where they will never be disturbed. Evil nations won't oppress them as they've done in the past,

verses.kjv_text: And as since the time that I commanded judges {to be} over my people Israel, and have caused thee to rest from all thine enemies. Also the LORD telleth thee that he will make thee an house.
