verses.nlt_text: When David reached the summit of the Mount of Olives where people worshiped God, Hushai the Arkite was waiting there for him. Hushai had torn his clothing and put dirt on his head as a sign of mourning.

verses.kjv_text: Unto whom David said, If thou passest on with me, then thou shalt be a burden unto me:
verses.nlt_text: But David told him, "If you go with me, you will only be a burden.

verses.kjv_text: But if thou return to the city, and say unto Absalom, I will be thy servant, O king; {as} I {have been} thy father's servant hitherto, so {will} I now also {be} thy servant: then mayest thou for me defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
verses.nlt_text: Return to Jerusalem and tell Absalom, 'I will now be your adviser, O king, just as I was your father's adviser in the past.' Then you can frustrate and counter Ahithophel's advice.

verses.kjv_text: And {hast thou} not there with thee Zadok and Abiathar the priests? therefore it shall be, {that} what thing soever thou shalt hear out of the king's house, thou shalt tell {it} to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.
verses.nlt_text: Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, will be there. Tell them about the plans being made in the king's palace,

verses.kjv_text: Behold, {they have} there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz Zadok's {son}, and Jonathan Abiathar's {son}; and by them ye shall send unto me every thing that ye can hear.
verses.nlt_text: and they will send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what is going on."

verses.kjv_text: So Hushai David's friend came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: So David's friend Hushai returned to Jerusalem, getting there just as Absalom arrived.

verses.kjv_text: And when David was a little past the top {of the hill}, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him, with a couple of asses saddled, and upon them two hundred {loaves} of bread, and an hundred bunches of raisins, and an hundred of summer fruits, and a bottle of wine.
verses.nlt_text: When David had gone a little beyond the summit of the Mount of Olives, Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, was waiting there for him. He had two donkeys loaded with 200 loaves of bread, 100 clusters of raisins, 100 bunches of summer fruit, and a wineskin full of wine.

verses.kjv_text: And the king said unto Ziba, What meanest thou by these? And Ziba said, The asses {be} for the king's household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that such as be faint in the wilderness may drink.
verses.nlt_text: "What are these for?" the king asked Ziba.Ziba replied, "The donkeys are for the king's people to ride on, and the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat. The wine is for those who become exhausted in the wilderness."

verses.kjv_text: And the king said, And where {is} thy master's son? And Ziba said unto the king, Behold, he abideth at Jerusalem: for he said, To day shall the house of Israel restore me the kingdom of my father.
verses.nlt_text: "And where is Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson?" the king asked him."He stayed in Jerusalem," Ziba replied. "He said, 'Today I will get back the kingdom of my grandfather Saul.'"

verses.kjv_text: Then said the king to Ziba, Behold, thine {are} all that {pertained} unto Mephibosheth. And Ziba said, I humbly beseech thee {that} I may find grace in thy sight, my lord, O king. {I humbly...: Heb. I do obeisance}
verses.nlt_text: "In that case," the king told Ziba, "I give you everything Mephibosheth owns." "I bow before you," Ziba replied. "May I always be pleasing to you, my lord the king."

verses.kjv_text: And when king David came to Bahurim, behold, thence came out a man of the family of the house of Saul, whose name {was} Shimei, the son of Gera: he came forth, and cursed still as he came. {he came forth...: or, he still came forth and cursed}
verses.nlt_text: As King David came to Bahurim, a man came out of the village cursing them. It was Shimei son of Gera, from the same clan as Saul's family.

verses.kjv_text: And he cast stones at David, and at all the servants of king David: and all the people and all the mighty men {were} on his right hand and on his left.
verses.nlt_text: He threw stones at the king and the king's officers and all the mighty warriors who surrounded him.

verses.kjv_text: And thus said Shimei when he cursed, Come out, come out, thou bloody man, and thou man of Belial: {bloody...: Heb. man of blood}
verses.nlt_text: "Get out of here, you murderer, you scoundrel!" he shouted at David.

verses.kjv_text: The LORD hath returned upon thee all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose stead thou hast reigned; and the LORD hath delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom thy son: and, behold, thou {art taken} in thy mischief, because thou {art} a bloody man. {behold...: Heb. behold thee in thy evil}
verses.nlt_text: "The LORD is paying you back for all the bloodshed in Saul's clan. You stole his throne, and now the LORD has given it to your son Absalom. At last you will taste some of your own medicine, for you are a murderer!"

verses.kjv_text: Then said Abishai the son of Zeruiah unto the king, Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? let me go over, I pray thee, and take off his head.
verses.nlt_text: "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king?" Abishai son of Zeruiah demanded. "Let me go over and cut off his head!"

verses.kjv_text: And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the LORD hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?
verses.nlt_text: "No!" the king said. "Who asked your opinion, you sons of Zeruiah! If the LORD has told him to curse me, who are you to stop him?"

verses.kjv_text: And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now {may this} Benjamite {do it}? let him alone, and let him curse; for the LORD hath bidden him.
verses.nlt_text: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "My own son is trying to kill me. Doesn't this relative of Saul have even more reason to do so? Leave him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has told him to do it.

verses.kjv_text: It may be that the LORD will look on mine affliction, and that the LORD will requite me good for his cursing this day. {affliction: or, tears: Heb. eye}
verses.nlt_text: And perhaps the LORD will see that I am being wronged and will bless me because of these curses today."

verses.kjv_text: And as David and his men went by the way, Shimei went along on the hill's side over against him, and cursed as he went, and threw stones at him, and cast dust. {cast...: Heb. dusted him with dust}
verses.nlt_text: So David and his men continued down the road, and Shimei kept pace with them on a nearby hillside, cursing as he went and throwing stones at David and tossing dust into the air.

verses.kjv_text: And the king, and all the people that {were} with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.
verses.nlt_text: The king and all who were with him grew weary along the way, so they rested when they reached the Jordan River.

verses.kjv_text: And Absalom, and all the people the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Absalom and all the army of Israel arrived at Jerusalem, accompanied by Ahithophel.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Hushai the Archite, David's friend, was come unto Absalom, that Hushai said unto Absalom, God save the king, God save the king. {God...: Heb. Let the king live}
verses.nlt_text: When David's friend Hushai the Arkite arrived, he went immediately to see Absalom. "Long live the king!" he exclaimed. "Long live the king!"

verses.kjv_text: And Absalom said to Hushai, {Is} this thy kindness to thy friend? why wentest thou not with thy friend?
verses.nlt_text: "Is this the way you treat your friend David?" Absalom asked him. "Why aren't you with him?"

verses.kjv_text: And Hushai said unto Absalom, Nay; but whom the LORD, and this people, and all the men of Israel, choose, his will I be, and with him will I abide.
verses.nlt_text: "I'm here because I belong to the man who is chosen by the LORD and by all the men of Israel," Hushai replied.

verses.kjv_text: And again, whom should I serve? {should I} not {serve} in the presence of his son? as I have served in thy father's presence, so will I be in thy presence.
verses.nlt_text: "And anyway, why shouldn't I serve you? Just as I was your father's adviser, now I will be your adviser!"

verses.kjv_text: Then said Absalom to Ahithophel, Give counsel among you what we shall do.
verses.nlt_text: Then Absalom turned to Ahithophel and asked him, "What should I do next?"

verses.kjv_text: And Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Go in unto thy father's concubines, which he hath left to keep the house; and all Israel shall hear that thou art abhorred of thy father: then shall the hands of all that {are} with thee be strong.
verses.nlt_text: Ahithophel told him, "Go and sleep with your father's concubines, for he has left them here to look after the palace. Then all Israel will know that you have insulted your father beyond hope of reconciliation, and they will throw their support to you."

verses.kjv_text: So they spread Absalom a tent upon the top of the house; and Absalom went in unto his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.
verses.nlt_text: So they set up a tent on the palace roof where everyone could see it, and Absalom went in and had sex with his father's concubines.

verses.kjv_text: And the counsel of Ahithophel, which he counselled in those days, {was} as if a man had enquired at the oracle of God: so {was} all the counsel of Ahithophel both with David and with Absalom. {oracle: Heb. word}
verses.nlt_text: Absalom followed Ahithophel's advice, just as David had done. For every word Ahithophel spoke seemed as wise as though it had come directly from the mouth of God.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover Ahithophel said unto Absalom, Let me now choose out twelve thousand men, and I will arise and pursue after David this night:
verses.nlt_text: Now Ahithophel urged Absalom, "Let me choose 12,000 men to start out after David tonight.

verses.kjv_text: And I will come upon him while he {is} weary and weak handed, and will make him afraid: and all the people that {are} with him shall flee; and I will smite the king only:
verses.nlt_text: I will catch up with him while he is weary and discouraged. He and his troops will panic, and everyone will run away. Then I will kill only the king,

verses.kjv_text: And I will bring back all the people unto thee: the man whom thou seekest {is} as if all returned: {so} all the people shall be in peace.
verses.nlt_text: and I will bring all the people back to you as a bride returns to her husband. After all, it is only one man's life that you seek. Then you will be at peace with all the people."

verses.kjv_text: And the saying pleased Absalom well, and all the elders of Israel. {pleased...: Heb. was right in the eyes of, etc}
verses.nlt_text: This plan seemed good to Absalom and to all the elders of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Absalom, Call now Hushai the Archite also, and let us hear likewise what he saith. {what...: Heb. what is in his mouth}
verses.nlt_text: But then Absalom said, "Bring in Hushai the Arkite. Let's see what he thinks about this."

verses.kjv_text: And when Hushai was come to Absalom, Absalom spake unto him, saying, Ahithophel hath spoken after this manner: shall we do {after} his saying? if not; speak thou. {his saying: Heb. his word}
verses.nlt_text: When Hushai arrived, Absalom told him what Ahithophel had said. Then he asked, "What is your opinion? Should we follow Ahithophel's advice? If not, what do you suggest?"

verses.kjv_text: And Hushai said unto Absalom, The counsel that Ahithophel hath given {is} not good at this time. {given: Heb. counselled}
verses.nlt_text: "Well," Hushai replied to Absalom, "this time Ahithophel has made a mistake.

verses.kjv_text: For, said Hushai, thou knowest thy father and his men, that they {be} mighty men, and they {be} chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field: and thy father {is} a man of war, and will not lodge with the people. {chafed...: Heb. bitter of soul}
verses.nlt_text: You know your father and his men; they are mighty warriors. Right now they are as enraged as a mother bear who has been robbed of her cubs. And remember that your father is an experienced man of war. He won't be spending the night among the troops.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he is hid now in some pit, or in some {other} place: and it will come to pass, when some of them be overthrown at the first, that whosoever heareth it will say, There is a slaughter among the people that follow Absalom. {overthrown: Heb. fallen}
verses.nlt_text: He has probably already hidden in some pit or cave. And when he comes out and attacks and a few of your men fall, there will be panic among your troops, and the word will spread that Absalom's men are being slaughtered.

verses.kjv_text: And he also {that is} valiant, whose heart {is} as the heart of a lion, shall utterly melt: for all Israel knoweth that thy father {is} a mighty man, and {they} which {be} with him {are} valiant men.
verses.nlt_text: Then even the bravest soldiers, though they have the heart of a lion, will be paralyzed with fear. For all Israel knows what a mighty warrior your father is and how courageous his men are.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore I counsel that all Israel be generally gathered unto thee, from Dan even to Beersheba, as the sand that {is} by the sea for multitude; and that thou go to battle in thine own person. {that thou...: Heb. that thy face, or, presence go, etc}
verses.nlt_text: "I recommend that you mobilize the entire army of Israel, bringing them from as far away as Dan in the north and Beersheba in the south. That way you will have an army as numerous as the sand on the seashore. And I advise that you personally lead the troops.

verses.kjv_text: So shall we come upon him in some place where he shall be found, and we will light upon him as the dew falleth on the ground: and of him and of all the men that {are} with him there shall not be left so much as one.
verses.nlt_text: When we find David, we'll fall on him like dew that falls on the ground. Then neither he nor any of his men will be left alive.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover, if he be gotten into a city, then shall all Israel bring ropes to that city, and we will draw it into the river, until there be not one small stone found there.
verses.nlt_text: And if David were to escape into some town, you will have all Israel there at your command. Then we can take ropes and drag the walls of the town into the nearest valley until every stone is torn down."

verses.kjv_text: And Absalom and all the men of Israel said, The counsel of Hushai the Archite {is} better than the counsel of Ahithophel. For the LORD had appointed to defeat the good counsel of Ahithophel, to the intent that the LORD might bring evil upon Absalom. {appointed: Heb. commanded}
verses.nlt_text: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "Hushai's advice is better than Ahithophel's." For the LORD had determined to defeat the counsel of Ahithophel, which really was the better plan, so that he could bring disaster on Absalom!

verses.kjv_text: Then said Hushai unto Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, Thus and thus did Ahithophel counsel Absalom and the elders of Israel; and thus and thus have I counselled.
verses.nlt_text: Hushai told Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, what Ahithophel had said to Absalom and the elders of Israel and what he himself had advised instead.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore send quickly, and tell David, saying, Lodge not this night in the plains of the wilderness, but speedily pass over; lest the king be swallowed up, and all the people that {are} with him.
verses.nlt_text: "Quick!" he told them. "Find David and urge him not to stay at the shallows of the Jordan River tonight. He must go across at once into the wilderness beyond. Otherwise he will die and his entire army with him."

verses.kjv_text: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed by Enrogel; for they might not be seen to come into the city: and a wench went and told them; and they went and told king David.
verses.nlt_text: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been staying at En-rogel so as not to be seen entering and leaving the city. Arrangements had been made for a servant girl to bring them the message they were to take to King David.

verses.kjv_text: Nevertheless a lad saw them, and told Absalom: but they went both of them away quickly, and came to a man's house in Bahurim, which had a well in his court; whither they went down.
verses.nlt_text: But a boy spotted them at En-rogel, and he told Absalom about it. So they quickly escaped to Bahurim, where a man hid them down inside a well in his courtyard.

verses.kjv_text: And the woman took and spread a covering over the well's mouth, and spread ground corn thereon; and the thing was not known.
verses.nlt_text: The man's wife put a cloth over the top of the well and scattered grain on it to dry in the sun; so no one suspected they were there.

verses.kjv_text: And when Absalom's servants came to the woman to the house, they said, Where {is} Ahimaaz and Jonathan? And the woman said unto them, They be gone over the brook of water. And when they had sought and could not find {them}, they returned to Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: When Absalom's men arrived, they asked her, "Have you seen Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman replied, "They were here, but they crossed over the brook." Absalom's men looked for them without success and returned to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, after they were departed, that they came up out of the well, and went and told king David, and said unto David, Arise, and pass quickly over the water: for thus hath Ahithophel counselled against you.
verses.nlt_text: Then the two men crawled out of the well and hurried on to King David. "Quick!" they told him, "cross the Jordan tonight!" And they told him how Ahithophel had advised that he be captured and killed.

verses.kjv_text: Then David arose, and all the people that {were} with him, and they passed over Jordan: by the morning light there lacked not one of them that was not gone over Jordan.
verses.nlt_text: So David and all the people with him went across the Jordan River during the night, and they were all on the other bank before dawn.

verses.kjv_text: And when Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled {his} ass, and arose, and gat him home to his house, to his city, and put his household in order, and hanged himself, and died, and was buried in the sepulchre of his father. {followed: Heb. done} {put his...: Heb. gave charge concerning his house}
verses.nlt_text: When Ahithophel realized that his advice had not been followed, he saddled his donkey, went to his hometown, set his affairs in order, and hanged himself. He died there and was buried in the family tomb.

verses.kjv_text: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom passed over Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.
verses.nlt_text: David soon arrived at Mahanaim. By now, Absalom had mobilized the entire army of Israel and was leading his troops across the Jordan River.

verses.kjv_text: And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa {was} a man's son, whose name {was} Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab's mother. {Ithra an Israelite: or, Jether an Ishmaelite} {Abigail: Heb. Abigal} {Nahash: or, Jesse}
verses.nlt_text: Absalom had appointed Amasa as commander of his army, replacing Joab, who had been commander under David. (Amasa was Joab's cousin. His father was Jether, an Ishmaelite. His mother, Abigail daughter of Nahash, was the sister of Joab's mother, Zeruiah.)

verses.kjv_text: So Israel and Absalom pitched in the land of Gilead.
verses.nlt_text: Absalom and the Israelite army set up camp in the land of Gilead.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
verses.nlt_text: When David arrived at Mahanaim, he was warmly greeted by Shobi son of Nahash, who came from Rabbah of the Ammonites, and by Makir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and by Barzillai of Gilead from Rogelim.

verses.kjv_text: Brought beds, and basons, and earthen vessels, and wheat, and barley, and flour, and parched {corn}, and beans, and lentiles, and parched {pulse}, {basons: or, cups}
verses.nlt_text: They brought sleeping mats, cooking pots, serving bowls, wheat and barley, flour and roasted grain, beans, lentils,

verses.kjv_text: And honey, and butter, and sheep, and cheese of kine, for David, and for the people that {were} with him, to eat: for they said, The people {is} hungry, and weary, and thirsty, in the wilderness.
verses.nlt_text: honey, butter, sheep, goats, and cheese for David and those who were with him. For they said, "You must all be very hungry and tired and thirsty after your long march through the wilderness."

verses.kjv_text: And David numbered the people that {were} with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.
verses.nlt_text: David now mustered the men who were with him and appointed generals and captains to lead them.

verses.kjv_text: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.
verses.nlt_text: He sent the troops out in three groups, placing one group under Joab, one under Joab's brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and one under Ittai, the man from Gath. The king told his troops, "I am going out with you."

verses.kjv_text: But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now {thou art} worth ten thousand of us: therefore now {it is} better that thou succour us out of the city. {care...: Heb. set their heart on us} {worth...: Heb. as ten thousand of us} {succour: Heb. be to succour or help}
verses.nlt_text: But his men objected strongly. "You must not go," they urged. "If we have to turn and run-- and even if half of us die-- it will make no difference to Absalom's troops; they will be looking only for you. You are worth 10,000 of us, and it is better that you stay here in the town and send help if we need it."

verses.kjv_text: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.
verses.nlt_text: "If you think that's the best plan, I'll do it," the king answered. So he stood alongside the gate of the town as all the troops marched out in groups of hundreds and of thousands.

verses.kjv_text: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, {Deal} gently for my sake with the young man, {even} with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.
verses.nlt_text: And the king gave this command to Joab, Abishai, and Ittai: "For my sake, deal gently with young Absalom." And all the troops heard the king give this order to his commanders.

verses.kjv_text: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;
verses.nlt_text: So the battle began in the forest of Ephraim,

verses.kjv_text: Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand {men}.
verses.nlt_text: and the Israelite troops were beaten back by David's men. There was a great slaughter that day, and 20,000 men laid down their lives.

verses.kjv_text: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured. {devoured: Heb. multiplied to devour}
verses.nlt_text: The battle raged all across the countryside, and more men died because of the forest than were killed by the sword.

verses.kjv_text: And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that {was} under him went away.
verses.nlt_text: During the battle, Absalom happened to come upon some of David's men. He tried to escape on his mule, but as he rode beneath the thick branches of a great tree, his hair got caught in the tree. His mule kept going and left him dangling in the air.

verses.kjv_text: And a certain man saw {it}, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.
verses.nlt_text: One of David's men saw what had happened and told Joab, "I saw Absalom dangling from a great tree."

verses.kjv_text: And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest {him}, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten {shekels} of silver, and a girdle.
verses.nlt_text: "What?" Joab demanded. "You saw him there and didn't kill him? I would have rewarded you with ten pieces of silver and a hero's belt!"

verses.kjv_text: And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand {shekels} of silver in mine hand, {yet} would I not put forth mine hand against the king's son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none {touch} the young man Absalom. {receive: Heb. weigh upon mine hand} {Beware...: Heb. Beware whosoever ye be of, etc}
verses.nlt_text: "I would not kill the king's son for even a thousand pieces of silver, " the man replied to Joab. "We all heard the king say to you and Abishai and Ittai, 'For my sake, please spare young Absalom.'

verses.kjv_text: Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against {me}.
verses.nlt_text: And if I had betrayed the king by killing his son-- and the king would certainly find out who did it-- you yourself would be the first to abandon me."

verses.kjv_text: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he {was} yet alive in the midst of the oak. {with...: Heb. before thee} {midst: Heb. heart}
verses.nlt_text: "Enough of this nonsense," Joab said. Then he took three daggers and plunged them into Absalom's heart as he dangled, still alive, in the great tree.

verses.kjv_text: And ten young men that bare Joab's armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.
verses.nlt_text: Ten of Joab's young armor bearers then surrounded Absalom and killed him.

verses.kjv_text: And Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing after Israel: for Joab held back the people.
verses.nlt_text: Then Joab blew the ram's horn, and his men returned from chasing the army of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.
verses.nlt_text: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and piled a great heap of stones over it. And all Israel fled to their homes.

verses.kjv_text: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which {is} in the king's dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom's place.
verses.nlt_text: During his lifetime, Absalom had built a monument to himself in the King's Valley, for he said, "I have no son to carry on my name." He named the monument after himself, and it is known as Absalom's Monument to this day.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies. {avenged...: Heb. judged him from the hand, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Then Zadok's son Ahimaaz said, "Let me run to the king with the good news that the LORD has rescued him from his enemies."

verses.kjv_text: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king's son is dead. {bear tidings this: Heb. be a man of tidings, etc}
verses.nlt_text: "No," Joab told him, "it wouldn't be good news to the king that his son is dead. You can be my messenger another time, but not today."

verses.kjv_text: Then said Joab to Cushi, Go tell the king what thou hast seen. And Cushi bowed himself unto Joab, and ran.
verses.nlt_text: Then Joab said to a man from Ethiopia, "Go tell the king what you have seen." The man bowed and ran off.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready? {howsoever: Heb. be what may} {ready: or, convenient}
verses.nlt_text: But Ahimaaz continued to plead with Joab, "Whatever happens, please let me go, too." "Why should you go, my son?" Joab replied. "There will be no reward for your news."

verses.kjv_text: But howsoever, {said he}, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes, but let me go anyway," he begged.Joab finally said, "All right, go ahead." So Ahimaaz took the less demanding route by way of the plain and ran to Mahanaim ahead of the Ethiopian.

verses.kjv_text: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.
verses.nlt_text: While David was sitting between the inner and outer gates of the town, the watchman climbed to the roof of the gateway by the wall. As he looked, he saw a lone man running toward them.

verses.kjv_text: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he {be} alone, {there is} tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.
verses.nlt_text: He shouted the news down to David, and the king replied, "If he is alone, he has news." As the messenger came closer,

verses.kjv_text: And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold {another} man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.
verses.nlt_text: the watchman saw another man running toward them. He shouted down, "Here comes another one!" The king replied, "He also will have news."

verses.kjv_text: And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He {is} a good man, and cometh with good tidings. {Me...: Heb. I see the running}
verses.nlt_text: "The first man runs like Ahimaaz son of Zadok," the watchman said."He is a good man and comes with good news," the king replied.

verses.kjv_text: And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed {be} the LORD thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king. {All...: or, Peace be to thee: Heb. Peace} {delivered...: Heb. shut up}
verses.nlt_text: Then Ahimaaz cried out to the king, "Everything is all right!" He bowed before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Praise to the LORD your God, who has handed over the rebels who dared to stand against my lord the king."

verses.kjv_text: And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king's servant, and {me} thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what {it was}. {Is...: Heb. Is there peace?}
verses.nlt_text: "What about young Absalom?" the king demanded. "Is he all right?" Ahimaaz replied, "When Joab told me to come, there was a lot of commotion. But I didn't know what was happening."

verses.kjv_text: And the king said {unto him}, Turn aside, {and} stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.
verses.nlt_text: "Wait here," the king told him. So Ahimaaz stepped aside.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee. {Tidings: Heb. Tidings is brought}
verses.nlt_text: Then the man from Ethiopia arrived and said, "I have good news for my lord the king. Today the LORD has rescued you from all those who rebelled against you."

verses.kjv_text: And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do {thee} hurt, be as {that} young man {is}.
verses.nlt_text: "What about young Absalom?" the king demanded. "Is he all right?" And the Ethiopian replied, "May all of your enemies, my lord the king, both now and in the future, share the fate of that young man!"

verses.kjv_text: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!
verses.nlt_text: The king was overcome with emotion. He went up to the room over the gateway and burst into tears. And as he went, he cried, "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you! O Absalom, my son, my son."

verses.kjv_text: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.
verses.nlt_text: Word soon reached Joab that the king was weeping and mourning for Absalom.

verses.kjv_text: And the victory that day was {turned} into mourning unto all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son. {victory: Heb. salvation, or, deliverance}
verses.nlt_text: As all the people heard of the king's deep grief for his son, the joy of that day's victory was turned into deep sadness.

verses.kjv_text: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.
verses.nlt_text: They crept back into the town that day as though they were ashamed and had deserted in battle.

verses.kjv_text: But the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!
verses.nlt_text: The king covered his face with his hands and kept on crying, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!"

verses.kjv_text: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, which this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;
verses.nlt_text: Then Joab went to the king's room and said to him, "We saved your life today and the lives of your sons, your daughters, and your wives and concubines. Yet you act like this, making us feel ashamed of ourselves.

verses.kjv_text: In that thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends. For thou hast declared this day, that thou regardest neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well. {in...: Heb. By loving, etc} {that thou regardest...: Heb. that princes or servants are not to thee}
verses.nlt_text: You seem to love those who hate you and hate those who love you. You have made it clear today that your commanders and troops mean nothing to you. It seems that if Absalom had lived and all of us had died, you would be pleased.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants: for I swear by the LORD, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that befell thee from thy youth until now. {comfortably...: Heb. to the heart of thy servants}
verses.nlt_text: Now go out there and congratulate your troops, for I swear by the LORD that if you don't go out, not a single one of them will remain here tonight. Then you will be worse off than ever before."

verses.kjv_text: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king doth sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent.
verses.nlt_text: So the king went out and took his seat at the town gate, and as the news spread throughout the town that he was there, everyone went to him.Meanwhile, the Israelites who had supported Absalom fled to their homes.

verses.kjv_text: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.
verses.nlt_text: And throughout all the tribes of Israel there was much discussion and argument going on. The people were saying, "The king rescued us from our enemies and saved us from the Philistines, but Absalom chased him out of the country.

verses.kjv_text: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back? {speak...: Heb. are ye silent?}
verses.nlt_text: Now Absalom, whom we anointed to rule over us, is dead. Why not ask David to come back and be our king again?"

verses.kjv_text: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, {even} to his house.
verses.nlt_text: Then King David sent Zadok and Abiathar, the priests, to say to the elders of Judah, "Why are you the last ones to welcome back the king into his palace? For I have heard that all Israel is ready.

verses.kjv_text: Ye {are} my brethren, ye {are} my bones and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?
verses.nlt_text: You are my relatives, my own tribe, my own flesh and blood! So why are you the last ones to welcome back the king?"

verses.kjv_text: And say ye to Amasa, {Art} thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
verses.nlt_text: And David told them to tell Amasa, "Since you are my own flesh and blood, like Joab, may God strike me and even kill me if I do not appoint you as commander of my army in his place."

verses.kjv_text: And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as {the heart of} one man; so that they sent {this word} unto the king, Return thou, and all thy servants.
verses.nlt_text: Then Amasa convinced all the men of Judah, and they responded unanimously. They sent word to the king, "Return to us, and bring back all who are with you."

verses.kjv_text: So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.
verses.nlt_text: So the king started back to Jerusalem. And when he arrived at the Jordan River, the people of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the river.

verses.kjv_text: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which {was} of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.
verses.nlt_text: Shimei son of Gera, the man from Bahurim in Benjamin, hurried across with the men of Judah to welcome King David.

verses.kjv_text: And {there were} a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.
verses.nlt_text: A thousand other men from the tribe of Benjamin were with him, including Ziba, the chief servant of the house of Saul, and Ziba's fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan to meet the king. They crossed the shallows of the Jordan to bring the king's household across the river, helping him in every way they could.

verses.kjv_text: And there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king's household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan; {what...: Heb. the good in his eyes}
verses.nlt_text: As the king was about to cross the river, Shimei fell down before him.

verses.kjv_text: And said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.
verses.nlt_text: "My lord the king, please forgive me," he pleaded. "Forget the terrible thing your servant did when you left Jerusalem. May the king put it out of his mind.

verses.kjv_text: For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.
verses.nlt_text: I know how much I sinned. That is why I have come here today, the very first person in all Israel to greet my lord the king."

verses.kjv_text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD'S anointed?
verses.nlt_text: Then Abishai son of Zeruiah said, "Shimei should die, for he cursed the LORD's anointed king!"

verses.kjv_text: And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I {am} this day king over Israel?
verses.nlt_text: "Who asked your opinion, you sons of Zeruiah!" David exclaimed. "Why have you become my adversary today? This is not a day for execution but for celebration! Today I am once again the king of Israel!"

verses.kjv_text: Therefore the king said unto Shimei, Thou shalt not die. And the king sware unto him.
verses.nlt_text: Then, turning to Shimei, David vowed, "Your life will be spared."

verses.kjv_text: And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king, and had neither dressed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king departed until the day he came {again} in peace.
verses.nlt_text: Now Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, came down from Jerusalem to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet, trimmed his beard, or washed his clothes since the day the king left Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he was come to Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said unto him, Wherefore wentest not thou with me, Mephibosheth?
verses.nlt_text: "Why didn't you come with me, Mephibosheth?" the king asked him.

verses.kjv_text: And he answered, My lord, O king, my servant deceived me: for thy servant said, I will saddle me an ass, that I may ride thereon, and go to the king; because thy servant {is} lame.
verses.nlt_text: Mephibosheth replied, "My lord the king, my servant Ziba deceived me. I told him, 'Saddle my donkey so I can go with the king.' For as you know I am crippled.

verses.kjv_text: And he hath slandered thy servant unto my lord the king; but my lord the king {is} as an angel of God: do therefore {what is} good in thine eyes.
verses.nlt_text: Ziba has slandered me by saying that I refused to come. But I know that my lord the king is like an angel of God, so do what you think is best.

verses.kjv_text: For all {of} my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king: yet didst thou set thy servant among them that did eat at thine own table. What right therefore have I yet to cry any more unto the king? {dead...: Heb. men of death}
verses.nlt_text: All my relatives and I could expect only death from you, my lord, but instead you have honored me by allowing me to eat at your own table! What more can I ask?"

verses.kjv_text: And the king said unto him, Why speakest thou any more of thy matters? I have said, Thou and Ziba divide the land.
verses.nlt_text: "You've said enough," David replied. "I've decided that you and Ziba will divide your land equally between you."

verses.kjv_text: And Mephibosheth said unto the king, Yea, let him take all, forasmuch as my lord the king is come again in peace unto his own house.
verses.nlt_text: "Give him all of it," Mephibosheth said. "I am content just to have you safely back again, my lord the king!"

verses.kjv_text: And Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim, and went over Jordan with the king, to conduct him over Jordan.
verses.nlt_text: Barzillai of Gilead had come down from Rogelim to escort the king across the Jordan.

verses.kjv_text: Now Barzillai was a very aged man, {even} fourscore years old: and he had provided the king of sustenance while he lay at Mahanaim; for he {was} a very great man.
verses.nlt_text: He was very old, about eighty, and very wealthy. He was the one who had provided food for the king during his stay in Mahanaim.

verses.kjv_text: And the king said unto Barzillai, Come thou over with me, and I will feed thee with me in Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: "Come across with me and live in Jerusalem," the king said to Barzillai. "I will take care of you there."

verses.kjv_text: And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem? {How...: Heb. How many days are the years of my life}
verses.nlt_text: "No," he replied, "I am far too old to go with the king to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: I {am} this day fourscore years old: {and} can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women? wherefore then should thy servant be yet a burden unto my lord the king?
verses.nlt_text: I am eighty years old today, and I can no longer enjoy anything. Food and wine are no longer tasty, and I cannot hear the singers as they sing. I would only be a burden to my lord the king.

verses.kjv_text: Thy servant will go a little way over Jordan with the king: and why should the king recompense it me with such a reward?
verses.nlt_text: Just to go across the Jordan River with the king is all the honor I need!

verses.kjv_text: Let thy servant, I pray thee, turn back again, that I may die in mine own city, {and be buried} by the grave of my father and of my mother. But behold thy servant Chimham; let him go over with my lord the king; and do to him what shall seem good unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: Then let me return again to die in my own town, where my father and mother are buried. But here is your servant, my son Kimham. Let him go with my lord the king and receive whatever you want to give him."

verses.kjv_text: And the king answered, Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem good unto thee: and whatsoever thou shalt require of me, {that} will I do for thee. {require: Heb. choose}
verses.nlt_text: "Good," the king agreed. "Kimham will go with me, and I will help him in any way you would like. And I will do for you anything you want."

verses.kjv_text: And all the people went over Jordan. And when the king was come over, the king kissed Barzillai, and blessed him; and he returned unto his own place.
verses.nlt_text: So all the people crossed the Jordan with the king. After David had blessed and embraced him, Barzillai returned to his own home.

verses.kjv_text: Then the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him: and all the people of Judah conducted the king, and also half the people of Israel. {Chimham: Heb. Chimhan}
verses.nlt_text: The king then crossed over to Gilgal, taking Kimham with him. All the troops of Judah and half the troops of Israel escorted the king on his way.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, all the men of Israel came to the king, and said unto the king, Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away, and have brought the king, and his household, and all David's men with him, over Jordan?
verses.nlt_text: But all the men of Israel complained to the king, "The men of Judah stole the  vnumber="2"> He sent the troopsr of helping take you, your household, and all your men across the Jordan."

verses.kjv_text: And all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, Because the king {is} near of kin to us: wherefore then be ye angry for this matter? have we eaten at all of the king's {cost}? or hath he given us any gift?
verses.nlt_text: The men of Judah replied, "The king is one of our own kinsmen. Why should this make you angry? We haven't eaten any of the king's food or received any special favors!"

verses.kjv_text: And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more {right} in David than ye: why then did ye despise us, that our advice should not be first had in bringing back our king? And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel. {despise...: Heb. set us at light}
verses.nlt_text: "But there are ten tribes in Israel," the others replied. "So we have ten times as much right to the king as you do. What right do you have to treat us with such contempt? Weren't we the first to speak of bringing him back to be our king again?" The argument continued back and forth, and the men of Judah spoke even more harshly than the men of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And there happened to be there a man of Belial, whose name {was} Sheba, the son of Bichri, a Benjamite: and he blew a trumpet, and said, We have no part in David, neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to his tents, O Israel.
verses.nlt_text: There happened to be a troublemaker there named Sheba son of Bicri, a man from the tribe of Benjamin. Sheba blew a ram's horn and began to chant: "Down with the dynasty of David! We have no interest in the son of Jesse. Come on, you men of Israel, back to your homes!"

verses.kjv_text: So every man of Israel went up from after David, {and} followed Sheba the son of Bichri: but the men of Judah clave unto their king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: So all the men of Israel deserted David and followed Sheba son of Bicri. But the men of Judah stayed with their king and escorted him from the Jordan River to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: And David came to his house at Jerusalem; and the king took the ten women {his} concubines, whom he had left to keep the house, and put them in ward, and fed them, but went not in unto them. So they were shut up unto the day of their death, living in widowhood. {ward: Heb. an house of ward} {shut...: Heb. bound} {living...: Heb. in widowhood of life}
verses.nlt_text: When David came to his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to look after the palace and placed them in seclusion. Their needs were provided for, but he no longer slept with them. So each of them lived like a widow until she died.

verses.kjv_text: Then said the king to Amasa, Assemble me the men of Judah within three days, and be thou here present. {Assemble: Heb. Call}
verses.nlt_text: Then the king told Amasa, "Mobilize the army of Judah within three days, and report back at that time."

verses.kjv_text: So Amasa went to assemble {the men of} Judah: but he tarried longer than the set time which he had appointed him. {Assemble: Heb. Call}
verses.nlt_text: So Amasa went out to notify Judah, but it took him longer than the time he had been given.

verses.kjv_text: And David said to Abishai, Now shall Sheba the son of Bichri do us more harm than {did} Absalom: take thou thy lord's servants, and pursue after him, lest he get him fenced cities, and escape us. {escape...: Heb. deliver himself from our eyes}
verses.nlt_text: Then David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bicri is going to hurt us more than Absalom did. Quick, take my troops and chase after him before he gets into a fortified town where we can't reach him."

verses.kjv_text: And there went out after him Joab's men, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, and all the mighty men: and they went out of Jerusalem, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.nlt_text: So Abishai and Joab, together with the king's bodyguard and all the mighty warriors, set out from Jerusalem to go after Sheba.

verses.kjv_text: When they {were} at the great stone which {is} in Gibeon, Amasa went before them. And Joab's garment that he had put on was girded unto him, and upon it a girdle {with} a sword fastened upon his loins in the sheath thereof; and as he went forth it fell out.
verses.nlt_text: As they arrived at the great stone in Gibeon, Amasa met them. Joab was wearing his military tunic with a dagger strapped to his belt. As he stepped forward to greet Amasa, he slipped the dagger from its sheath.

verses.kjv_text: And Joab said to Amasa, {Art} thou in health, my brother? And Joab took Amasa by the beard with the right hand to kiss him.
verses.nlt_text: "How are you, my cousin?" Joab said and took him by the beard with his right hand as though to kiss him.

verses.kjv_text: But Amasa took no heed to the sword that {was} in Joab's hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth {rib}, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri. {struck...: Heb. doubled not his stroke}
verses.nlt_text: Amasa didn't notice the dagger in his left hand, and Joab stabbed him in the stomach with it so that his insides gushed out onto the ground. Joab did not need to strike again, and Amasa soon died. Joab and his brother Abishai left him lying there and continued after Sheba.

verses.kjv_text: And one of Joab's men stood by him, and said, He that favoureth Joab, and he that {is} for David, {let him go} after Joab.
verses.nlt_text: One of Joab's young men shouted to Amasa's troops, "If you are for Joab and David, come and follow Joab."

verses.kjv_text: And Amasa wallowed in blood in the midst of the highway. And when the man saw that all the people stood still, he removed Amasa out of the highway into the field, and cast a cloth upon him, when he saw that every one that came by him stood still.
verses.nlt_text: But Amasa lay in his blood in the middle of the road, and Joab's man saw that everyone was stopping to stare at him. So he pulled him off the road into a field and threw a cloak over him.

verses.kjv_text: When he was removed out of the highway, all the people went on after Joab, to pursue after Sheba the son of Bichri.
verses.nlt_text: With Amasa's body out of the way, everyone went on with Joab to capture Sheba son of Bicri.

verses.kjv_text: And he went through all the tribes of Israel unto Abel, and to Bethmaachah, and all the Berites: and they were gathered together, and went also after him.
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Sheba traveled through all the tribes of Israel and eventually came to the town of Abel-beth-maacah. All the members of his own clan, the Bicrites, assembled for battle and followed him into the town.

verses.kjv_text: And they came and besieged him in Abel of Bethmaachah, and they cast up a bank against the city, and it stood in the trench: and all the people that {were} with Joab battered the wall, to throw it down. {in the trench: or, against the outmost wall} {battered: Heb. marred to throw down}
verses.nlt_text: When Joab's forces arrived, they attacked Abel-beth-maacah. They built a siege ramp against the town's fortifications and began battering down the wall.

verses.kjv_text: Then cried a wise woman out of the city, Hear, hear; say, I pray you, unto Joab, Come near hither, that I may speak with thee.
verses.nlt_text: But a wise woman in the town called out to Joab, "Listen to me, Joab. Come over here so I can talk to you."

verses.kjv_text: And when he was come near unto her, the woman said, {Art} thou Joab? And he answered, I {am he}. Then she said unto him, Hear the words of thine handmaid. And he answered, I do hear.
verses.nlt_text: As he approached, the woman asked, "Are you Joab?" "I am," he replied.So she said, "Listen carefully to your servant." "I'm listening," he said.

verses.kjv_text: Then she spake, saying, They were wont to speak in old time, saying, They shall surely ask {counsel} at Abel: and so they ended {the matter}. {They were...: or, They plainly spake in the beginning, saying, Surely they will ask of Abel, and so make an end}
verses.nlt_text: Then she continued, "There used to be a saying, 'If you want to settle an argument, ask advice at the town of Abel.'

verses.kjv_text: I {am one of them that are} peaceable {and} faithful in Israel: thou seekest to destroy a city and a mother in Israel: why wilt thou swallow up the inheritance of the LORD?
verses.nlt_text: I am one who is peace loving and faithful in Israel. But you are destroying an important town in Israel. Why do you want to devour what belongs to the LORD?"

verses.kjv_text: And Joab answered and said, Far be it, far be it from me, that I should swallow up or destroy.
verses.nlt_text: And Joab replied, "Believe me, I don't want to devour or destroy your town!

verses.kjv_text: The matter {is} not so: but a man of mount Ephraim, Sheba the son of Bichri by name, hath lifted up his hand against the king, {even} against David: deliver him only, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said unto Joab, Behold, his head shall be thrown to thee over the wall. {by name: Heb. by his name}
verses.nlt_text: That's not my purpose. All I want is a man named Sheba son of Bicri from the hill country of Ephraim, who has revolted against King David. If you hand over this one man to me, I will leave the town in peace." "All right," the woman replied, "we will throw his head over the wall to you."

verses.kjv_text: Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and cast {it} out to Joab. And he blew a trumpet, and they retired from the city, every man to his tent. And Joab returned to Jerusalem unto the king. {retired: Heb. were scattered}
verses.nlt_text: Then the woman went to all the people with her wise advice, and they cut off Sheba's head and threw it out to Joab. So he blew the ram's horn and called his troops back from the attack. They all returned to their homes, and Joab returned to the king at Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: Now Joab {was} over all the host of Israel: and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada {was} over the Cherethites and over the Pelethites:
verses.nlt_text: Now Joab was the commander of the army of Israel. Benaiah son of Jehoiada was captain of the king's bodyguard.

verses.kjv_text: And Adoram {was} over the tribute: and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud {was} recorder: {recorder: or, remembrancer}
verses.nlt_text: Adoniram was in charge of the labor force. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the royal historian.

verses.kjv_text: And Sheva {was} scribe: and Zadok and Abiathar {were} the priests:
verses.nlt_text: Sheva was the court secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.

verses.kjv_text: And Ira also the Jairite was a chief ruler about David. {a chief...: or, a prince}
verses.nlt_text: And Ira, a descendant of Jair, was David's personal priest.

verses.kjv_text: Then there was a famine in the days of David three years, year after year; and David enquired of the LORD. And the LORD answered, {It is} for Saul, and for {his} bloody house, because he slew the Gibeonites. {enquired...: Heb. sought the face, etc}
verses.nlt_text: There was a famine during David's reign that lasted for three years, so David asked the LORD about it. And the LORD said, "The famine has come because Saul and his family are guilty of murdering the Gibeonites."

verses.kjv_text: And the king called the Gibeonites, and said unto them; (now the Gibeonites {were} not of the children of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; and the children of Israel had sworn unto them: and Saul sought to slay them in his zeal to the children of Israel and Judah.)
verses.nlt_text: So the king summoned the Gibeonites. They were not part of Israel but were all that was left of the nation of the Amorites. The people of Israel had sworn not to kill them, but Saul, in his zeal for Israel and Judah, had tried to wipe them out.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore David said unto the Gibeonites, What shall I do for you? and wherewith shall I make the atonement, that ye may bless the inheritance of the LORD?
verses.nlt_text: David asked them, "What can I do for you? How can I make amends so that you will bless the LORD's people again?"

verses.kjv_text: And the Gibeonites said unto him, We will have no silver nor gold of Saul, nor of his house; neither for us shalt thou kill any man in Israel. And he said, What ye shall say, {that} will I do for you. {We will...: or, It is not silver nor gold that we have to do with Saul or his house, neither pertains it to us to kill, etc}
verses.nlt_text: "Well, money can't settle this matter between us and the family of Saul," the Gibeonites replied. "Neither can we demand the life of anyone in Israel." "What can I do then?" David asked. "Just tell me and I will do it for you."

verses.kjv_text: And they answered the king, The man that consumed us, and that devised against us {that} we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the coasts of Israel, {devised...: or, cut us off}
verses.nlt_text: Then they replied, "It was Saul who planned to destroy us, to keep us from having any place at all in the territory of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: Let seven men of his sons be delivered unto us, and we will hang them up unto the LORD in Gibeah of Saul, {whom} the LORD did choose. And the king said, I will give {them}. {whom...: or, chosen of the LORD}
verses.nlt_text: So let seven of Saul's sons be handed over to us, and we will execute them before the LORD at Gibeon, on the mountain of the LORD. " "All right," the king said, "I will do it."

verses.kjv_text: But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the LORD'S oath that {was} between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.
verses.nlt_text: The king spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, who was Saul's grandson, because of the oath David and Jonathan had sworn before the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite: {Michal: or, Michal's sister} {brought...: Heb. bear to Adriel}
verses.nlt_text: But he gave them Saul's two sons Armoni and Mephibosheth, whose mother was Rizpah daughter of Aiah. He also gave them the five sons of Saul's daughter Merab, the wife of Adriel son of Barzillai from Meholah.

verses.kjv_text: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the LORD: and they fell {all} seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first {days}, in the beginning of barley harvest.
verses.nlt_text: The men of Gibeon executed them on the mountain before the LORD. So all seven of them died together at the beginning of the barley harvest.

verses.kjv_text: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for her upon the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water dropped upon them out of heaven, and suffered neither the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
verses.nlt_text: Then Rizpah daughter of Aiah, the mother of two of the men, spread burlap on a rock and stayed there the entire harvest season. She prevented the scavenger birds from tearing at their bodies during the day and stopped wild animals from eating them at night.

verses.kjv_text: And it was told David what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.
verses.nlt_text: When David learned what Rizpah, Saul's concubine, had done,

verses.kjv_text: And David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabeshgilead, which had stolen them from the street of Bethshan, where the Philistines had hanged them, when the Philistines had slain Saul in Gilboa:
verses.nlt_text: he went to the people of Jabesh-gilead and retrieved the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan. (When the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa, the people of Jabesh-gilead stole their bodies from the public square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hung them.)

verses.kjv_text: And he brought up from thence the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son; and they gathered the bones of them that were hanged.
verses.nlt_text: So David obtained the bones of Saul and Jonathan, as well as the bones of the men the Gibeonites had executed.

verses.kjv_text: And the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son buried they in the country of Benjamin in Zelah, in the sepulchre of Kish his father: and they performed all that the king commanded. And after that God was intreated for the land.
verses.nlt_text: Then the king ordered that they bury the bones in the tomb of Kish, Saul's father, at the town of Zela in the land of Benjamin. After that, God ended the famine in the land.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover the Philistines had yet war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines: and David waxed faint.
verses.nlt_text: Once again the Philistines were at war with Israel. And when David and his men were in the thick of battle, David became weak and exhausted.

verses.kjv_text: And Ishbibenob, which {was} of the sons of the giant, the weight of whose spear {weighed} three hundred {shekels} of brass in weight, he being girded with a new {sword}, thought to have slain David. {the giant: or, Rapha} {spear: Heb. the staff, or, the head}
verses.nlt_text: Ishbi-benob was a descendant of the giants; his bronze spearhead weighed more than seven pounds, and he was armed with a new sword. He had cornered David and was about to kill him.

verses.kjv_text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him, and smote the Philistine, and killed him. Then the men of David sware unto him, saying, Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the light of Israel. {light: Heb. candle, or, lamp}
verses.nlt_text: But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David's rescue and killed the Philistine. Then David's men declared, "You are not going out to battle with us again! Why risk snuffing out the light of Israel?"

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after this, that there was again a battle with the Philistines at Gob: then Sibbechai the Hushathite slew Saph, which {was} of the sons of the giant. {the giant: or, Rapha} {Saph: or, Sippai}
verses.nlt_text: After this, there was another battle against the Philistines at Gob. As they fought, Sibbecai from Hushah killed Saph, another descendant of the giants.

verses.kjv_text: And there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines, where Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim, a Bethlehemite, slew {the brother of} Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear {was} like a weaver's beam. {Jaareoregim: or, Jair}
verses.nlt_text: During another battle at Gob, Elhanan son of Jair from Bethlehem killed the brother of Goliath of Gath. The handle of his spear was as thick as a weaver's beam!

verses.kjv_text: And there was yet a battle in Gath, where was a man of {great} stature, that had on every hand six fingers, and on every foot six toes, four and twenty in number; and he also was born to the giant. {the giant: or, Rapha}
verses.nlt_text: In another battle with the Philistines at Gath, they encountered a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all, who was also a descendant of the giants.

verses.kjv_text: And when he defied Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea the brother of David slew him. {defied: or, reproached} {Shimea: also called, Shammah}
verses.nlt_text: But when he defied and taunted Israel, he was killed by Jonathan, the son of David's brother Shimea.

verses.kjv_text: These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
verses.nlt_text: These four Philistines were descendants of the giants of Gath, but David and his warriors killed them.

verses.kjv_text: And David spake unto the LORD the words of this song in the day {that} the LORD had delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul:
verses.nlt_text: David sang this song to the LORD on the day the LORD rescued him from all his enemies and from Saul.

verses.kjv_text: And he said, The LORD {is} my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer;
verses.nlt_text: He sang: "The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my savior;

verses.kjv_text: The God of my rock; in him will I trust: {he is} my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge, my saviour; thou savest me from violence.
verses.nlt_text: my God is my rock, in whom I find protection. He is my shield, the power that saves me, and my place of safety. He is my refuge, my savior, the one who saves me from violence.

verses.kjv_text: I will call on the LORD, {who is} worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies.
verses.nlt_text: I called on the LORD, who is worthy of praise, and he saved me from my enemies.

verses.kjv_text: When the waves of death compassed me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid; {waves: or, pangs} {ungodly...: Heb. Belial}
verses.nlt_text: "The waves of death overwhelmed me; floods of destruction swept over me.

verses.kjv_text: The sorrows of hell compassed me about; the snares of death prevented me; {sorrows: or, cords}
verses.nlt_text: The grave wrapped its ropes around me; death laid a trap in my path.

verses.kjv_text: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried to my God: and he did hear my voice out of his temple, and my cry {did enter} into his ears.
verses.nlt_text: But in my distress I cried out to the LORD; yes, I cried to my God for help. He heard me from his sanctuary; my cry reached his ears.

verses.kjv_text: Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of heaven moved and shook, because he was wroth.
verses.nlt_text: "Then the earth quaked and trembled. The foundations of the heavens shook; they quaked because of his anger.

verses.kjv_text: There went up a smoke out of his nostrils, and fire out of his mouth devoured: coals were kindled by it. {out of his nostrils: Heb. by, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Smoke poured from his nostrils; fierce flames leaped from his mouth. Glowing coals blazed forth from him.

verses.kjv_text: He bowed the heavens also, and came down; and darkness {was} under his feet.
verses.nlt_text: He opened the heavens and came down; dark storm clouds were beneath his feet.

verses.kjv_text: And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly: and he was seen upon the wings of the wind.
verses.nlt_text: Mounted on a mighty angelic being, he flew, soaring on the wings of the wind.

verses.kjv_text: And he made darkness pavilions round about him, dark waters, {and} thick clouds of the skies. {dark...: Heb. binding of waters}
verses.nlt_text: He shrouded himself in darkness, veiling his approach with dense rain clouds.

verses.kjv_text: Through the brightness before him were coals of fire kindled.
verses.nlt_text: A great brightness shone around him, and burning coals blazed forth.

verses.kjv_text: The LORD thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD thundered from heaven; the voice of the Most High resounded.

verses.kjv_text: And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.
verses.nlt_text: He shot arrows and scattered his enemies; his lightning flashed, and they were confused.

verses.kjv_text: And the channels of the sea appeared, the foundations of the world were discovered, at the rebuking of the LORD, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.
verses.nlt_text: Then at the command of the LORD, at the blast of his breath, the bottom of the sea could be seen, and the foundations of the earth were laid bare.

verses.kjv_text: He sent from above, he took me; he drew me out of many waters; {many: or, great}
verses.nlt_text: "He reached down from heaven and rescued me; he drew me out of deep waters.

verses.kjv_text: He delivered me from my strong enemy, {and} from them that hated me: for they were too strong for me.
verses.nlt_text: He rescued me from my powerful enemies, from those who hated me and were too strong for me.

verses.kjv_text: They prevented me in the day of my calamity: but the LORD was my stay.
verses.nlt_text: They attacked me at a moment when I was in distress, but the LORD supported me.

verses.kjv_text: He brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me, because he delighted in me.
verses.nlt_text: He led me to a place of safety; he rescued me because he delights in me.

verses.kjv_text: The LORD rewarded me according to my righteousness: according to the cleanness of my hands hath he recompensed me.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD rewarded me for doing right; he restored me because of my innocence.

verses.kjv_text: For I have kept the ways of the LORD, and have not wickedly departed from my God.
verses.nlt_text: For I have kept the ways of the LORD; I have not turned from my God to follow evil.

verses.kjv_text: For all his judgments {were} before me: and {as for} his statutes, I did not depart from them.
verses.nlt_text: I have followed all his regulations; I have never abandoned his decrees.

verses.kjv_text: I was also upright before him, and have kept myself from mine iniquity. {before: Heb. to}
verses.nlt_text: I am blameless before God; I have kept myself from sin.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore the LORD hath recompensed me according to my righteousness; according to my cleanness in his eye sight. {in...: Heb. before his eyes}
verses.nlt_text: The LORD rewarded me for doing right. He has seen my innocence.

verses.kjv_text: With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful, {and} with the upright man thou wilt shew thyself upright.
verses.nlt_text: "To the faithful you show yourself faithful; to those with integrity you show integrity.

verses.kjv_text: With the pure thou wilt shew thyself pure; and with the froward thou wilt shew thyself unsavoury. {shew thyself unsavoury: or, wrestle}
verses.nlt_text: To the pure you show yourself pure, but to the wicked you show yourself hostile.

verses.kjv_text: And the afflicted people thou wilt save: but thine eyes {are} upon the haughty, {that} thou mayest bring {them} down.
verses.nlt_text: You rescue the humble, but your eyes watch the proud and humiliate them.

verses.kjv_text: For thou {art} my lamp, O LORD: and the LORD will lighten my darkness. {lamp: or, candle}
verses.nlt_text: O LORD, you are my lamp. The LORD lights up my darkness.

verses.kjv_text: For by thee I have run through a troop: by my God have I leaped over a wall. {run: or, broken}
verses.nlt_text: In your strength I can crush an army; with my God I can scale any wall.

verses.kjv_text: {As for} God, his way {is} perfect; the word of the LORD {is} tried: he {is} a buckler to all them that trust in him. {tried: or, refined}
verses.nlt_text: "God's way is perfect. All the LORD's promises prove true. He is a shield for all who look to him for protection.

verses.kjv_text: For who {is} God, save the LORD? and who {is} a rock, save our God?
verses.nlt_text: For who is God except the LORD? Who but our God is a solid rock?

verses.kjv_text: God {is} my strength {and} power: and he maketh my way perfect. {maketh: Heb. riddeth, or, looseth}
verses.nlt_text: God is my strong fortress, and he makes my way perfect.

verses.kjv_text: He maketh my feet like hinds' {feet}: and setteth me upon my high places. {maketh: Heb. equalleth}
verses.nlt_text: He makes me as surefooted as a deer, enabling me to stand on mountain heights.

verses.kjv_text: He teacheth my hands to war; so that a bow of steel is broken by mine arms. {to war: Heb. for the war}
verses.nlt_text: He trains my hands for battle; he strengthens my arm to draw a bronze bow.

verses.kjv_text: Thou hast also given me the shield of thy salvation: and thy gentleness hath made me great. {made...: Heb. multiplied me}
verses.nlt_text: You have given me your shield of victory; your help has made me great.

verses.kjv_text: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me; so that my feet did not slip. {feet: Heb. ankles}
verses.nlt_text: You have made a wide path for my feet to keep them from slipping.

verses.kjv_text: I have pursued mine enemies, and destroyed them; and turned not again until I had consumed them.
verses.nlt_text: "I chased my enemies and destroyed them; I did not stop until they were conquered.

verses.kjv_text: And I have consumed them, and wounded them, that they could not arise: yea, they are fallen under my feet.
verses.nlt_text: I consumed them; I struck them down so they did not get up; they fell beneath my feet.

verses.kjv_text: For thou hast girded me with strength to battle: them that rose up against me hast thou subdued under me. {subdued: Heb. caused to bow}
verses.nlt_text: You have armed me with strength for the battle; you have subdued my enemies under my feet.

verses.kjv_text: Thou hast also given me the necks of mine enemies, that I might destroy them that hate me.
verses.nlt_text: You placed my foot on their necks. I have destroyed all who hated me.

verses.kjv_text: They looked, but {there was} none to save; {even} unto the LORD, but he answered them not.
verses.nlt_text: They looked for help, but no one came to their rescue. They even cried to the LORD, but he refused to answer.

verses.kjv_text: Then did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I did stamp them as the mire of the street, {and} did spread them abroad.
verses.nlt_text: I ground them as fine as the dust of the earth; I trampled them in the gutter like dirt.

verses.kjv_text: Thou also hast delivered me from the strivings of my people, thou hast kept me {to be} head of the heathen: a people {which} I knew not shall serve me.
verses.nlt_text: "You gave me victory over my accusers. You preserved me as the ruler over nations; people I don't even know now serve me.

verses.kjv_text: Strangers shall submit themselves unto me: as soon as they hear, they shall be obedient unto me. {Strangers: Heb. Sons of the stranger} {submit...: or, yield feigned obedience: Heb. lie}
verses.nlt_text: Foreign nations cringe before me; as soon as they hear of me, they submit.

verses.kjv_text: Strangers shall fade away, and they shall be afraid out of their close places.
verses.nlt_text: They all lose their courage and come trembling from their strongholds.

verses.kjv_text: The LORD liveth; and blessed {be} my rock; and exalted be the God of the rock of my salvation.
verses.nlt_text: "The LORD lives! Praise to my Rock! May God, the Rock of my salvation, be exalted!

verses.kjv_text: It {is} God that avengeth me, and that bringeth down the people under me, {avengeth: Heb. giveth avengement for}
verses.nlt_text: He is the God who pays back those who harm me; he brings down the nations under me

verses.kjv_text: And that bringeth me forth from mine enemies: thou also hast lifted me up on high above them that rose up against me: thou hast delivered me from the violent man.
verses.nlt_text: and delivers me from my enemies. You hold me safe beyond the reach of my enemies; you save me from violent opponents.
