verses.nlt_text: Joab and the army of Israel had stayed there for six months, killing them.

verses.kjv_text: That Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father's servants with him, to go into Egypt; Hadad {being} yet a little child.
verses.nlt_text: But Hadad and a few of his father's royal officials escaped and headed for Egypt. (Hadad was just a boy at the time.)

verses.kjv_text: And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran: and they took men with them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, unto Pharaoh king of Egypt; which gave him an house, and appointed him victuals, and gave him land.
verses.nlt_text: They set out from Midian and went to Paran, where others joined them. Then they traveled to Egypt and went to Pharaoh, who gave them a home, food, and some land.

verses.kjv_text: And Hadad found great favour in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
verses.nlt_text: Pharaoh grew very fond of Hadad, and he gave him his wife's sister in marriage-- the sister of Queen Tahpenes.

verses.kjv_text: And the sister of Tahpenes bare him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house: and Genubath was in Pharaoh's household among the sons of Pharaoh.
verses.nlt_text: She bore him a son named Genubath. Tahpenes raised him in Pharaoh's palace among Pharaoh's own sons.

verses.kjv_text: And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to mine own country. {Let...: Heb. Send me away}
verses.nlt_text: When the news reached Hadad in Egypt that David and his commander Joab were both dead, he said to Pharaoh, "Let me return to my own country."

verses.kjv_text: Then Pharaoh said unto him, But what hast thou lacked with me, that, behold, thou seekest to go to thine own country? And he answered, Nothing: howbeit let me go in any wise. {Nothing: Heb. Not}
verses.nlt_text: "Why?" Pharaoh asked him. "What do you lack here that makes you want to go home?" "Nothing," he replied. "But even so, please let me return home."

verses.kjv_text: And God stirred him up {another} adversary, Rezon the son of Eliadah, which fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah:
verses.nlt_text: God also raised up Rezon son of Eliada as Solomon's adversary. Rezon had fled from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah,

verses.kjv_text: And he gathered men unto him, and became captain over a band, when David slew them {of Zobah}: and they went to Damascus, and dwelt therein, and reigned in Damascus.
verses.nlt_text: and had become the leader of a gang of rebels. After David conquered Hadadezer, Rezon and his men fled to Damascus, where he became king.

verses.kjv_text: And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, beside the mischief that Hadad {did}: and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.
verses.nlt_text: Rezon was Israel's bitter adversary for the rest of Solomon's reign, and he made trouble, just as Hadad did. Rezon hated Israel intensely and continued to reign in Aram.

verses.kjv_text: And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon's servant, whose mother's name {was} Zeruah, a widow woman, even he lifted up {his} hand against the king.
verses.nlt_text: Another rebel leader was Jeroboam son of Nebat, one of Solomon's own officials. He came from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim, and his mother was Zeruah, a widow.

verses.kjv_text: And this {was} the cause that he lifted up {his} hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, {and} repaired the breaches of the city of David his father. {repaired: Heb. closed}
verses.nlt_text: This is the story behind his rebellion. Solomon was rebuilding the supporting terraces and repairing the walls of the city of his father, David.

verses.kjv_text: And the man Jeroboam {was} a mighty man of valour: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph. {was industrious: Heb. did work} {charge: Heb. burden}
verses.nlt_text: Jeroboam was a very capable young man, and when Solomon saw how industrious he was, he put him in charge of the labor force from the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, the descendants of Joseph.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass at that time when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two {were} alone in the field:
verses.nlt_text: One day as Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh met him along the way. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak. The two of them were alone in a field,

verses.kjv_text: And Ahijah caught the new garment that {was} on him, and rent it {in} twelve pieces:
verses.nlt_text: and Ahijah took hold of the new cloak he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.

verses.kjv_text: And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the LORD, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:
verses.nlt_text: Then he said to Jeroboam, "Take ten of these pieces, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I am about to tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon, and I will give ten of the tribes to you!

verses.kjv_text: (But he shall have one tribe for my servant David's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel:)
verses.nlt_text: But I will leave him one tribe for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do {that which is} right in mine eyes, and {to keep} my statutes and my judgments, as {did} David his father.
verses.nlt_text: For Solomon has abandoned me and worshiped Ashtoreth, the goddess of the Sidonians; Chemosh, the god of Moab; and Molech, the god of the Ammonites. He has not followed my ways and done what is pleasing in my sight. He has not obeyed my decrees and regulations as David his father did.

verses.kjv_text: Howbeit I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand: but I will make him prince all the days of his life for David my servant's sake, whom I chose, because he kept my commandments and my statutes:
verses.nlt_text: " 'But I will not take the entire kingdom from Solomon at this time. For the sake of my servant David, the one whom I chose and who obeyed my commands and decrees, I will keep Solomon as leader for the rest of his life.

verses.kjv_text: But I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand, and will give it unto thee, {even} ten tribes.
verses.nlt_text: But I will take the kingdom away from his son and give ten of the tribes to you.

verses.kjv_text: And unto his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there. {light: Heb. lamp, or, candle}
verses.nlt_text: His son will have one tribe so that the descendants of David my servant will continue to reign, shining like a lamp in Jerusalem, the city I have chosen to be the place for my name.

verses.kjv_text: And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.
verses.nlt_text: And I will place you on the throne of Israel, and you will rule over all that your heart desires.

verses.kjv_text: And it shall be, if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do {that is} right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: If you listen to what I tell you and follow my ways and do whatever I consider to be right, and if you obey my decrees and commands, as my servant David did, then I will always be with you. I will establish an enduring dynasty for you as I did for David, and I will give Israel to you.

verses.kjv_text: And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.
verses.nlt_text: Because of Solomon's sin I will punish the descendants of David-- though not forever.'"

verses.kjv_text: Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. And Jeroboam arose, and fled into Egypt, unto Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
verses.nlt_text: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but he fled to King Shishak of Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died.

verses.kjv_text: And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, {are} they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon? {acts: or, words, or, things}
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Solomon's reign, including all his deeds and his wisdom, are recorded in [The Book of the Acts of Solomon.]

verses.kjv_text: And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel {was} forty years. {time: Heb. days}
verses.nlt_text: Solomon ruled in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.

verses.kjv_text: And Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead. {Rehoboam: Gr. Roboam}
verses.nlt_text: When he died, he was buried in the City of David, named for his father. Then his son Rehoboam became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.
verses.nlt_text: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was yet in Egypt, heard {of it}, (for he was fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam dwelt in Egypt;)
verses.nlt_text: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of this, he returned from Egypt, for he had fled to Egypt to escape from King Solomon.

verses.kjv_text: That they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came, and spake unto Rehoboam, saying,
verses.nlt_text: The leaders of Israel summoned him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel went to speak with Rehoboam.

verses.kjv_text: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee.
verses.nlt_text: "Your father was a hard master," they said. "Lighten the harsh labor demands and heavy taxes that your father imposed on us. Then we will be your loyal subjects."

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, Depart yet {for} three days, then come again to me. And the people departed.
verses.nlt_text: Rehoboam replied, "Give me three days to think this over. Then come back for my answer." So the people went away.

verses.kjv_text: And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do ye advise that I may answer this people?
verses.nlt_text: Then King Rehoboam discussed the matter with the older men who had counseled his father, Solomon. "What is your advice?" he asked. "How should I answer these people?"

verses.kjv_text: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.
verses.nlt_text: The older counselors replied, "If you are willing to be a servant to these people today and give them a favorable answer, they will always be your loyal subjects."

verses.kjv_text: But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, {and} which stood before him:
verses.nlt_text: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the older men and instead asked the opinion of the young men who had grown up with him and were now his advisers.

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, What counsel give ye that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which thy father did put upon us lighter?
verses.nlt_text: "What is your advice?" he asked them. "How should I answer these people who want me to lighten the burdens imposed by my father?"

verses.kjv_text: And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou {it} lighter unto us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little {finger} shall be thicker than my father's loins.
verses.nlt_text: The young men replied, "This is what you should tell those complainers who want a lighter burden: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist!

verses.kjv_text: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, my father laid heavy burdens on you, but I'm going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!'"

verses.kjv_text: So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.
verses.nlt_text: Three days later Jeroboam and all the people returned to hear Rehoboam's decision, just as the king had ordered.

verses.kjv_text: And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men's counsel that they gave him; {roughly: Heb. hardly}
verses.nlt_text: But Rehoboam spoke harshly to the people, for he rejected the advice of the older counselors

verses.kjv_text: And spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father {also} chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
verses.nlt_text: and followed the counsel of his younger advisers. He told the people, "My father laid heavy burdens on you, but I'm going to make them even heavier! My father beat you with whips, but I will beat you with scorpions!"

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore the king hearkened not unto the people; for the cause was from the LORD, that he might perform his saying, which the LORD spake by Ahijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.nlt_text: So the king paid no attention to the people. This turn of events was the will of the LORD, for it fulfilled the LORD's message to Jeroboam son of Nebat through the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh.

verses.kjv_text: So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither {have we} inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.
verses.nlt_text: When all Israel realized that the king had refused to listen to them, they responded, "Down with the dynasty of David! We have no interest in the son of Jesse. Back to your homes, O Israel! Look out for your own house, O David!" So the people of Israel returned home.

verses.kjv_text: But {as for} the children of Israel which dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
verses.nlt_text: But Rehoboam continued to rule over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.

verses.kjv_text: Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who {was} over the tribute; and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. Therefore king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem. {made...: Heb. strengthened himself}
verses.nlt_text: King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, who was in charge of the labor force, to restore order, but the people of Israel stoned him to death. When this news reached King Rehoboam, he quickly jumped into his chariot and fled to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day. {rebelled: or, fell away}
verses.nlt_text: And to this day the northern tribes of Israel have refused to be ruled by a descendant of David.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.
verses.nlt_text: When the people of Israel learned of Jeroboam's return from Egypt, they called an assembly and made him king over all Israel. So only the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the family of David.

verses.kjv_text: And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
verses.nlt_text: When Rehoboam arrived at Jerusalem, he mobilized the men of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin-- 180,000 select troops-- to fight against the men of Israel and to restore the kingdom to himself.

verses.kjv_text: But the word of God came unto Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
verses.nlt_text: But God said to Shemaiah, the man of God,

verses.kjv_text: Speak unto Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and unto all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying,
verses.nlt_text: "Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the people of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people,

verses.kjv_text: Thus saith the LORD, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They hearkened therefore to the word of the LORD, and returned to depart, according to the word of the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not fight against your relatives, the Israelites. Go back home, for what has happened is my doing!' " So they obeyed the message of the LORD and went home, as the LORD had commanded.

verses.kjv_text: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim, and dwelt therein; and went out from thence, and built Penuel.
verses.nlt_text: Jeroboam then built up the city of Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and it became his capital. Later he went and built up the town of Peniel.

verses.kjv_text: And Jeroboam said in his heart, Now shall the kingdom return to the house of David:
verses.nlt_text: Jeroboam thought to himself, "Unless I am careful, the kingdom will return to the dynasty of David.

verses.kjv_text: If this people go up to do sacrifice in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, then shall the heart of this people turn again unto their lord, {even} unto Rehoboam king of Judah, and they shall kill me, and go again to Rehoboam king of Judah.
verses.nlt_text: When these people go to Jerusalem to offer sacrifices at the Temple of the LORD, they will again give their allegiance to King Rehoboam of Judah. They will kill me and make him their king instead."

verses.kjv_text: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves {of} gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.nlt_text: So on the advice of his counselors, the king made two gold calves. He said to the people, "It is too much trouble for you to worship in Jerusalem. Look, Israel, these are the gods who brought you out of Egypt!"

verses.kjv_text: And he set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan.
verses.nlt_text: He placed these calf idols in Bethel and in Dan-- at either end of his kingdom.

verses.kjv_text: And this thing became a sin: for the people went {to worship} before the one, {even} unto Dan.
verses.nlt_text: But this became a great sin, for the people worshiped the idols, traveling as far north as Dan to worship the one there.

verses.kjv_text: And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.
verses.nlt_text: Jeroboam also erected buildings at the pagan shrines and ordained priests from the common people-- those who were not from the priestly tribe of Levi.

verses.kjv_text: And Jeroboam ordained a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like unto the feast that {is} in Judah, and he offered upon the altar. So did he in Bethel, sacrificing unto the calves that he had made: and he placed in Bethel the priests of the high places which he had made. {offered...: or, went up to the altar, etc} {sacrificing: or, to sacrifice}
verses.nlt_text: And Jeroboam instituted a religious festival in Bethel, held on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in imitation of the annual Festival of Shelters in Judah. There at Bethel he himself offered sacrifices to the calves he had made, and he appointed priests for the pagan shrines he had made.

verses.kjv_text: So he offered upon the altar which he had made in Bethel the fifteenth day of the eighth month, {even} in the month which he had devised of his own heart; and ordained a feast unto the children of Israel: and he offered upon the altar, and burnt incense. {offered...: or, went up to the altar, etc} {and burnt...: Heb. to burn incense}
verses.nlt_text: So on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a day that he himself had designated, Jeroboam offered sacrifices on the altar at Bethel. He instituted a religious festival for Israel, and he went up to the altar to burn incense.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, there came a man of God out of Judah by the word of the LORD unto Bethel: and Jeroboam stood by the altar to burn incense. {burn: or, offer}
verses.nlt_text: At the LORD's command, a man of God from Judah went to Bethel, arriving there just as Jeroboam was approaching the altar to burn incense.

verses.kjv_text: And he cried against the altar in the word of the LORD, and said, O altar, altar, thus saith the LORD; Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he offer the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men's bones shall be burnt upon thee.
verses.nlt_text: Then at the LORD's command, he shouted, "O altar, altar! This is what the LORD says: A child named Josiah will be born into the dynasty of David. On you he will sacrifice the priests from the pagan shrines who come here to burn incense, and human bones will be burned on you."

verses.kjv_text: And he gave a sign the same day, saying, This {is} the sign which the LORD hath spoken; Behold, the altar shall be rent, and the ashes that {are} upon it shall be poured out.
verses.nlt_text: That same day the man of God gave a sign to prove his message. He said, "The LORD has promised to give this sign: This altar will split apart, and its ashes will be poured out on the ground."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when king Jeroboam heard the saying of the man of God, which had cried against the altar in Bethel, that he put forth his hand from the altar, saying, Lay hold on him. And his hand, which he put forth against him, dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him.
verses.nlt_text: When King Jeroboam heard the man of God speaking against the altar at Bethel, he pointed at him and shouted, "Seize that man!" But instantly the king's hand became paralyzed in that position, and he couldn't pull it back.

verses.kjv_text: The altar also was rent, and the ashes poured out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God had given by the word of the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: At the same time a wide crack appeared in the altar, and the ashes poured out, just as the man of God had predicted in his message from the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: And the king answered and said unto the man of God, Intreat now the face of the LORD thy God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again. And the man of God besought the LORD, and the king's hand was restored him again, and became as {it was} before. {the LORD, and: Heb. the face of the LORD, etc}
verses.nlt_text: The king cried out to the man of God, "Please ask the LORD your God to restore my hand again!" So the man of God prayed to the LORD, and the king's hand was restored and he could move it again.

verses.kjv_text: And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward.
verses.nlt_text: Then the king said to the man of God, "Come to the palace with me and have something to eat, and I will give you a gift."

verses.kjv_text: And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thine house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place:
verses.nlt_text: But the man of God said to the king, "Even if you gave me half of everything you own, I would not go with you. I would not eat or drink anything in this place.

verses.kjv_text: For so was it charged me by the word of the LORD, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.
verses.nlt_text: For the LORD gave me this command: 'You must not eat or drink anything while you are there, and do not return to Judah by the same way you came.'"

verses.kjv_text: So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Bethel.
verses.nlt_text: So he left Bethel and went home another way.

verses.kjv_text: Now there dwelt an old prophet in Bethel; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Bethel: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father.
verses.nlt_text: As it happened, there was an old prophet living in Bethel, and his sons came home and told him what the man of God had done in Bethel that day. They also told their father what the man had said to the king.

verses.kjv_text: And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.
verses.nlt_text: The old prophet asked them, "Which way did he go?" So they showed their father which road the man of God had taken.

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon,
verses.nlt_text: "Quick, saddle the donkey," the old man said. So they saddled the donkey for him, and he mounted it.

verses.kjv_text: And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, {Art} thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I {am}.
verses.nlt_text: Then he rode after the man of God and found him sitting under a great tree. The old prophet asked him, "Are you the man of God who came from Judah?" "Yes, I am," he replied.

verses.kjv_text: Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.
verses.nlt_text: Then he said to the man of God, "Come home with me and eat some food."

verses.kjv_text: And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:
verses.nlt_text: "No, I cannot," he replied. "I am not allowed to eat or drink anything here in this place.

verses.kjv_text: For it was said to me by the word of the LORD, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest. {it...: Heb. a word was}
verses.nlt_text: For the LORD gave me this command: 'You must not eat or drink anything while you are there, and do not return to Judah by the same way you came.'"

verses.kjv_text: He said unto him, I {am} a prophet also as thou {art}; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the LORD, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. {But} he lied unto him.
verses.nlt_text: But the old prophet answered, "I am a prophet, too, just as you are. And an angel gave me this command from the LORD: 'Bring him home with you so he can have something to eat and drink.' " But the old man was lying to him.

verses.kjv_text: So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.
verses.nlt_text: So they went back together, and the man of God ate and drank at the prophet's home.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the LORD came unto the prophet that brought him back:
verses.nlt_text: Then while they were sitting at the table, a command from the LORD came to the old prophet.

verses.kjv_text: And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the LORD, and hast not kept the commandment which the LORD thy God commanded thee,
verses.nlt_text: He cried out to the man of God from Judah, "This is what the LORD says: You have defied the word of the LORD and have disobeyed the command the LORD your God gave you.

verses.kjv_text: But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which {the LORD} did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.
verses.nlt_text: You came back to this place and ate and drank where he told you not to eat or drink. Because of this, your body will not be buried in the grave of your ancestors."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, {to wit}, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
verses.nlt_text: After the man of God had finished eating and drinking, the old prophet saddled his own donkey for him,

verses.kjv_text: And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase.
verses.nlt_text: and the man of God started off again. But as he was traveling along, a lion came out and killed him. His body lay there on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside it.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told {it} in the city where the old prophet dwelt.
verses.nlt_text: People who passed by saw the body lying in the road and the lion standing beside it, and they went and reported it in Bethel, where the old prophet lived.

verses.kjv_text: And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard {thereof}, he said, It {is} the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the LORD: therefore the LORD hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake unto him. {torn: Heb. broken}
verses.nlt_text: When the prophet heard the report, he said, "It is the man of God who disobeyed the LORD's command. The LORD has fulfilled his word by causing the lion to attack and kill him."

verses.kjv_text: And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled {him}.
verses.nlt_text: Then the prophet said to his sons, "Saddle a donkey for me." So they saddled a donkey,

verses.kjv_text: And he went and found his carcase cast in the way, and the ass and the lion standing by the carcase: the lion had not eaten the carcase, nor torn the ass. {torn: Heb. broken}
verses.nlt_text: and he went out and found the body lying in the road. The donkey and lion were still standing there beside it, for the lion had not eaten the body nor attacked the donkey.

verses.kjv_text: And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.
verses.nlt_text: So the prophet laid the body of the man of God on the donkey and took it back to the town to mourn over him and bury him.

verses.kjv_text: And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, {saying}, Alas, my brother!
verses.nlt_text: He laid the body in his own grave, crying out in grief, "Oh, my brother!"

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God {is} buried; lay my bones beside his bones:
verses.nlt_text: Afterward the prophet said to his sons, "When I die, bury me in the grave where the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones.

verses.kjv_text: For the saying which he cried by the word of the LORD against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places which {are} in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.
verses.nlt_text: For the message the LORD told him to proclaim against the altar in Bethel and against the pagan shrines in the towns of Samaria will certainly come true."

verses.kjv_text: After this thing Jeroboam returned not from his evil way, but made again of the lowest of the people priests of the high places: whosoever would, he consecrated him, and he became {one} of the priests of the high places. {made...: Heb. returned and made} {consecrated...: Heb. filled his hand}
verses.nlt_text: But even after this, Jeroboam did not turn from his evil ways. He continued to choose priests from the common people. He appointed anyone who wanted to become a priest for the pagan shrines.

verses.kjv_text: And this thing became sin unto the house of Jeroboam, even to cut {it} off, and to destroy {it} from off the face of the earth.
verses.nlt_text: This became a great sin and resulted in the utter destruction of Jeroboam's dynasty from the face of the earth.

verses.kjv_text: At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam fell sick.
verses.nlt_text: At that time Jeroboam's son Abijah became very sick.

verses.kjv_text: And Jeroboam said to his wife, Arise, I pray thee, and disguise thyself, that thou be not known to be the wife of Jeroboam; and get thee to Shiloh: behold, there {is} Ahijah the prophet, which told me that {I should be} king over this people.
verses.nlt_text: So Jeroboam told his wife, "Disguise yourself so that no one will recognize you as my wife. Then go to the prophet Ahijah at Shiloh-- the man who told me I would become king.

verses.kjv_text: And take with thee ten loaves, and cracknels, and a cruse of honey, and go to him: he shall tell thee what shall become of the child. {with...: Heb. in thine hand} {cracknels: or, cakes} {cruse: or, bottle}
verses.nlt_text: Take him a gift of ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and ask him what will happen to the boy."

verses.kjv_text: And Jeroboam's wife did so, and arose, and went to Shiloh, and came to the house of Ahijah. But Ahijah could not see; for his eyes were set by reason of his age. {were...: Heb. stood for his hoariness}
verses.nlt_text: So Jeroboam's wife went to Ahijah's home at Shiloh. He was an old man now and could no longer see.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Ahijah, Behold, the wife of Jeroboam cometh to ask a thing of thee for her son; for he {is} sick: thus and thus shalt thou say unto her: for it shall be, when she cometh in, that she shall feign herself {to be} another {woman}.
verses.nlt_text: But the LORD had told Ahijah, "Jeroboam's wife will come here, pretending to be someone else. She will ask you about her son, for he is very sick. Give her the answer I give you."

verses.kjv_text: And it was {so}, when Ahijah heard the sound of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, Come in, thou wife of Jeroboam; why feignest thou thyself {to be} another? for I {am} sent to thee {with} heavy {tidings}. {heavy: Heb. hard}
verses.nlt_text: So when Ahijah heard her footsteps at the door, he called out, "Come in, wife of Jeroboam! Why are you pretending to be someone else?" Then he told her, "I have bad news for you.

verses.kjv_text: Go, tell Jeroboam, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Forasmuch as I exalted thee from among the people, and made thee prince over my people Israel,
verses.nlt_text: Give your husband, Jeroboam, this message from the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I promoted you from the ranks of the common people and made you ruler over my people Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And rent the kingdom away from the house of David, and gave it thee: and {yet} thou hast not been as my servant David, who kept my commandments, and who followed me with all his heart, to do {that} only {which was} right in mine eyes;
verses.nlt_text: I ripped the kingdom away from the family of David and gave it to you. But you have not been like my servant David, who obeyed my commands and followed me with all his heart and always did whatever I wanted.

verses.kjv_text: But hast done evil above all that were before thee: for thou hast gone and made thee other gods, and molten images, to provoke me to anger, and hast cast me behind thy back:
verses.nlt_text: You have done more evil than all who lived before you. You have made other gods for yourself and have made me furious with your gold calves. And since you have turned your back on me,

verses.kjv_text: Therefore, behold, I will bring evil upon the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam him that pisseth against the wall, {and} him that is shut up and left in Israel, and will take away the remnant of the house of Jeroboam, as a man taketh away dung, till it be all gone.
verses.nlt_text: I will bring disaster on your dynasty and will destroy every one of your male descendants, slave and free alike, anywhere in Israel. I will burn up your royal dynasty as one burns up trash until it is all gone.

verses.kjv_text: Him that dieth of Jeroboam in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat: for the LORD hath spoken {it}.
verses.nlt_text: The members of Jeroboam's family who die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and those who die in the field will be eaten by vultures. I, the LORD, have spoken.'"

verses.kjv_text: Arise thou therefore, get thee to thine own house: {and} when thy feet enter into the city, the child shall die.
verses.nlt_text: Then Ahijah said to Jeroboam's wife, "Go on home, and when you enter the city, the child will die.

verses.kjv_text: And all Israel shall mourn for him, and bury him: for he only of Jeroboam shall come to the grave, because in him there is found {some} good thing toward the LORD God of Israel in the house of Jeroboam.
verses.nlt_text: All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He is the only member of your family who will have a proper burial, for this child is the only good thing that the LORD, the God of Israel, sees in the entire family of Jeroboam.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover the LORD shall raise him up a king over Israel, who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam that day: but what? even now.
verses.nlt_text: "In addition, the LORD will raise up a king over Israel who will destroy the family of Jeroboam. This will happen today, even now!

verses.kjv_text: For the LORD shall smite Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water, and he shall root up Israel out of this good land, which he gave to their fathers, and shall scatter them beyond the river, because they have made their groves, provoking the LORD to anger.
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD will shake Israel like a reed whipped about in a stream. He will uproot the people of Israel from this good land that he gave their ancestors and will scatter them beyond the Euphrates River, for they have angered the LORD with the Asherah poles they have set up for worship.

verses.kjv_text: And he shall give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, who did sin, and who made Israel to sin.
verses.nlt_text: He will abandon Israel because Jeroboam sinned and made Israel sin along with him."

verses.kjv_text: And Jeroboam's wife arose, and departed, and came to Tirzah: {and} when she came to the threshold of the door, the child died;
verses.nlt_text: So Jeroboam's wife returned to Tirzah, and the child died just as she walked through the door of her home.

verses.kjv_text: And they buried him; and all Israel mourned for him, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by the hand of his servant Ahijah the prophet.
verses.nlt_text: And all Israel buried him and mourned for him, as the LORD had promised through the prophet Ahijah.

verses.kjv_text: And the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they {are} written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Jeroboam's reign, including all his wars and how he ruled, are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.]

verses.kjv_text: And the days which Jeroboam reigned {were} two and twenty years: and he slept with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigned in his stead. {slept: Heb. lay down}
verses.nlt_text: Jeroboam reigned in Israel twenty-two years. When Jeroboam died, his son Nadab became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: And Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam {was} forty and one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which the LORD did choose out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. And his mother's name {was} Naamah an Ammonitess.
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, Rehoboam son of Solomon was king in Judah. He was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen from among all the tribes of Israel as the place to honor his name. Rehoboam's mother was Naamah, an Ammonite woman.

verses.kjv_text: And Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD, and they provoked him to jealousy with their sins which they had committed, above all that their fathers had done.
verses.nlt_text: During Rehoboam's reign, the people of Judah did what was evil in the LORD's sight, provoking his anger with their sin, for it was even worse than that of their ancestors.

verses.kjv_text: For they also built them high places, and images, and groves, on every high hill, and under every green tree. {images: or, standing images, or, statues}
verses.nlt_text: For they also built for themselves pagan shrines and set up sacred pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree.

verses.kjv_text: And there were also sodomites in the land: {and} they did according to all the abominations of the nations which the LORD cast out before the children of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: There were even male and female shrine prostitutes throughout the land. The people imitated the detestable practices of the pagan nations the LORD had driven from the land ahead of the Israelites.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rehoboam, {that} Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem:
verses.nlt_text: In the fifth year of King Rehoboam's reign, King Shishak of Egypt came up and attacked Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: And he took away the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king's house; he even took away all: and he took away all the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
verses.nlt_text: He ransacked the treasuries of the LORD's Temple and the royal palace; he stole everything, including all the gold shields Solomon had made.

verses.kjv_text: And king Rehoboam made in their stead brasen shields, and committed {them} unto the hands of the chief of the guard, which kept the door of the king's house. {guard: Heb. runners}
verses.nlt_text: King Rehoboam later replaced them with bronze shields as substitutes, and he entrusted them to the care of the commanders of the guard who protected the entrance to the royal palace.

verses.kjv_text: And it was {so}, when the king went into the house of the LORD, that the guard bare them, and brought them back into the guard chamber.
verses.nlt_text: Whenever the king went to the Temple of the LORD, the guards would also take the shields and then return them to the guardroom.

verses.kjv_text: Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he did, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Rehoboam's reign and everything he did are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.]

verses.kjv_text: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all {their} days.
verses.nlt_text: There was constant war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam.

verses.kjv_text: And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. And his mother's name {was} Naamah an Ammonitess. And Abijam his son reigned in his stead. {Abijam: also called, Abijah: Gr. Abia}
verses.nlt_text: When Rehoboam died, he was buried among his ancestors in the City of David. His mother was Naamah, an Ammonite woman. Then his son Abijam became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat reigned Abijam over Judah.
verses.nlt_text: Abijam began to rule over Judah in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam's reign in Israel.

verses.kjv_text: Three years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother's name {was} Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom. {Maachah...: also called, Michaiah the daughter of Uriel} {Abishalom: also called, Absalom}
verses.nlt_text: He reigned in Jerusalem three years. His mother was Maacah, the daughter of Absalom.

verses.kjv_text: And he walked in all the sins of his father, which he had done before him: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father.
verses.nlt_text: He committed the same sins as his father before him, and he was not faithful to the LORD his God, as his ancestor David had been.

verses.kjv_text: Nevertheless for David's sake did the LORD his God give him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem: {lamp: or, candle}
verses.nlt_text: But for David's sake, the LORD his God allowed his descendants to continue ruling, shining like a lamp, and he gave Abijam a son to rule after him in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: Because David did {that which was} right in the eyes of the LORD, and turned not aside from any {thing} that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.
verses.nlt_text: For David had done what was pleasing in the LORD's sight and had obeyed the LORD's commands throughout his life, except in the affair concerning Uriah the Hittite.

verses.kjv_text: And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.
verses.nlt_text: There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam throughout Abijam's reign.

verses.kjv_text: Now the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Abijam's reign and everything he did are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.] There was constant war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

verses.kjv_text: And Abijam slept with his fathers; and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his stead.
verses.nlt_text: When Abijam died, he was buried in the City of David. Then his son Asa became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel reigned Asa over Judah.
verses.nlt_text: Asa began to rule over Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's reign in Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And forty and one years reigned he in Jerusalem. And his mother's name {was} Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom. {mother's: that is, grandmother's}
verses.nlt_text: He reigned in Jerusalem forty-one years. His grandmother was Maacah, the daughter of Absalom.

verses.kjv_text: And Asa did {that which was} right in the eyes of the LORD, as {did} David his father.
verses.nlt_text: Asa did what was pleasing in the LORD's sight, as his ancestor David had done.

verses.kjv_text: And he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.
verses.nlt_text: He banished the male and female shrine prostitutes from the land and got rid of all the idols his ancestors had made.

verses.kjv_text: And also Maachah his mother, even her he removed from {being} queen, because she had made an idol in a grove; and Asa destroyed her idol, and burnt {it} by the brook Kidron. {destroyed: Heb. cut off}
verses.nlt_text: He even deposed his grandmother Maacah from her position as queen mother because she had made an obscene Asherah pole. He cut down her obscene pole and burned it in the Kidron Valley.

verses.kjv_text: But the high places were not removed: nevertheless Asa's heart was perfect with the LORD all his days.
verses.nlt_text: Although the pagan shrines were not removed, Asa's heart remained completely faithful to the LORD throughout his life.

verses.kjv_text: And he brought in the things which his father had dedicated, and the things which himself had dedicated, into the house of the LORD, silver, and gold, and vessels. {things: Heb. holy}
verses.nlt_text: He brought into the Temple of the LORD the silver and gold and the various items that he and his father had dedicated.

verses.kjv_text: And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
verses.nlt_text: There was constant war between King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
verses.nlt_text: King Baasha of Israel invaded Judah and fortified Ramah in order to prevent anyone from entering or leaving King Asa's territory in Judah.

verses.kjv_text: Then Asa took all the silver and the gold {that were} left in the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king's house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants: and king Asa sent them to Benhadad, the son of Tabrimon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Asa responded by removing all the silver and gold that was left in the treasuries of the Temple of the LORD and the royal palace. He sent it with some of his officials to Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon, son of Hezion, the king of Aram, who was ruling in Damascus, along with this message:

verses.kjv_text: {There is} a league between me and thee, {and} between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold; come and break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me. {depart: Heb. go up}
verses.nlt_text: "Let there be a treaty between you and me like the one between your father and my father. See, I am sending you a gift of silver and gold. Break your treaty with King Baasha of Israel so that he will leave me alone."

verses.kjv_text: So Benhadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of the hosts which he had against the cities of Israel, and smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abelbethmaachah, and all Cinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali.
verses.nlt_text: Ben-hadad agreed to King Asa's request and sent the commanders of his army to attack the towns of Israel. They conquered the towns of Ijon, Dan, Abel-beth-maacah, and all Kinnereth, and all the land of Naphtali.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Baasha heard {thereof}, that he left off building of Ramah, and dwelt in Tirzah.
verses.nlt_text: As soon as Baasha of Israel heard what was happening, he abandoned his project of fortifying Ramah and withdrew to Tirzah.

verses.kjv_text: Then king Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah; none {was} exempted: and they took away the stones of Ramah, and the timber thereof, wherewith Baasha had builded; and king Asa built with them Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah. {exempted: Heb. free}
verses.nlt_text: Then King Asa sent an order throughout Judah, requiring that everyone, without exception, help to carry away the building stones and timbers that Baasha had been using to fortify Ramah. Asa used these materials to fortify the town of Geba in Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.

verses.kjv_text: The rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the cities which he built, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Nevertheless in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Asa's reign-- the extent of his power, everything he did, and the names of the cities he built-- are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Judah.] In his old age his feet became diseased.

verses.kjv_text: And Asa slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father: and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his stead. {Jehoshaphat: Gr. Josaphat}
verses.nlt_text: When Asa died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of David.Then Jehoshaphat, Asa's son, became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned over Israel two years. {began...: Heb. reigned}
verses.nlt_text: Nadab son of Jeroboam began to rule over Israel in the second year of King Asa's reign in Judah. He reigned in Israel two years.

verses.kjv_text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.
verses.nlt_text: But he did what was evil in the LORD's sight and followed the example of his father, continuing the sins that Jeroboam had led Israel to commit.

verses.kjv_text: And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, which {belonged} to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel laid siege to Gibbethon.
verses.nlt_text: Then Baasha son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, plotted against Nadab and assassinated him while he and the Israelite army were laying siege to the Philistine town of Gibbethon.

verses.kjv_text: Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.
verses.nlt_text: Baasha killed Nadab in the third year of King Asa's reign in Judah, and he became the next king of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he reigned, {that} he smote all the house of Jeroboam; he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him, according unto the saying of the LORD, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite:
verses.nlt_text: He immediately slaughtered all the descendants of King Jeroboam, so that not one of the royal family was left, just as the LORD had promised concerning Jeroboam by the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh.

verses.kjv_text: Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger.
verses.nlt_text: This was done because Jeroboam had provoked the anger of the LORD, the God of Israel, by the sins he had committed and the sins he had led Israel to commit.

verses.kjv_text: Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Nadab's reign and everything he did are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.]

verses.kjv_text: In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasha the son of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty and four years.
verses.nlt_text: Baasha son of Ahijah began to rule over all Israel in the third year of King Asa's reign in Judah. Baasha reigned in Tirzah twenty-four years.

verses.kjv_text: And he did evil in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.
verses.nlt_text: But he did what was evil in the LORD's sight and followed the example of Jeroboam, continuing the sins that Jeroboam had led Israel to commit.

verses.kjv_text: Then the word of the LORD came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,
verses.nlt_text: This message from the LORD was delivered to King Baasha by the prophet Jehu son of Hanani:

verses.kjv_text: Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel; and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;
verses.nlt_text: "I lifted you out of the dust to make you ruler of my people Israel, but you have followed the evil example of Jeroboam. You have provoked my anger by causing my people Israel to sin.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, I will take away the posterity of Baasha, and the posterity of his house; and will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
verses.nlt_text: So now I will destroy you and your family, just as I destroyed the descendants of Jeroboam son of Nebat.

verses.kjv_text: Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the fields shall the fowls of the air eat.
verses.nlt_text: The members of Baasha's family who die in the city will be eaten by dogs, and those who die in the field will be eaten by vultures."

verses.kjv_text: Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Baasha's reign and the extent of his power are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.]

verses.kjv_text: So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah: and Elah his son reigned in his stead.
verses.nlt_text: When Baasha died, he was buried in Tirzah. Then his son Elah became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: And also by the hand of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the LORD against Baasha, and against his house, even for all the evil that he did in the sight of the LORD, in provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam; and because he killed him.
verses.nlt_text: The message from the LORD against Baasha and his family came through the prophet Jehu son of Hanani. It was delivered because Baasha had done what was evil in the LORD's sight (just as the family of Jeroboam had done), and also because Baasha had destroyed the family of Jeroboam. The LORD's anger was provoked by Baasha's sins.

verses.kjv_text: In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
verses.nlt_text: Elah son of Baasha began to rule over Israel in the twenty-sixth year of King Asa's reign in Judah. He reigned in the city of Tirzah for two years.

verses.kjv_text: And his servant Zimri, captain of half {his} chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of {his} house in Tirzah. {steward...: Heb. which was over}
verses.nlt_text: Then Zimri, who commanded half of the royal chariots, made plans to kill him. One day in Tirzah, Elah was getting drunk at the home of Arza, the supervisor of the palace.

verses.kjv_text: And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.
verses.nlt_text: Zimri walked in and struck him down and killed him. This happened in the twenty-seventh year of King Asa's reign in Judah. Then Zimri became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, {that} he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends. {neither...: or, both his kinsmen and his friends}
verses.nlt_text: Zimri immediately killed the entire royal family of Baasha, leaving him not even a single male child. He even destroyed distant relatives and friends.

verses.kjv_text: Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet, {by: Heb. by the hand of}
verses.nlt_text: So Zimri destroyed the dynasty of Baasha as the LORD had promised through the prophet Jehu.

verses.kjv_text: For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the LORD God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
verses.nlt_text: This happened because of all the sins Baasha and his son Elah had committed, and because of the sins they led Israel to commit. They provoked the anger of the LORD, the God of Israel, with their worthless idols.

verses.kjv_text: Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he did, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Elah's reign and everything he did are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.]

verses.kjv_text: In the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah did Zimri reign seven days in Tirzah. And the people {were} encamped against Gibbethon, which {belonged} to the Philistines.
verses.nlt_text: Zimri began to rule over Israel in the twenty-seventh year of King Asa's reign in Judah, but his reign in Tirzah lasted only seven days. The army of Israel was then attacking the Philistine town of Gibbethon.

verses.kjv_text: And the people {that were} encamped heard say, Zimri hath conspired, and hath also slain the king: wherefore all Israel made Omri, the captain of the host, king over Israel that day in the camp.
verses.nlt_text: When they heard that Zimri had committed treason and had assassinated the king, that very day they chose Omri, commander of the army, as the new king of Israel.

verses.kjv_text: And Omri went up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besieged Tirzah.
verses.nlt_text: So Omri led the entire army of Israel up from Gibbethon to attack Tirzah, Israel's capital.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Zimri saw that the city was taken, that he went into the palace of the king's house, and burnt the king's house over him with fire, and died,
verses.nlt_text: When Zimri saw that the city had been taken, he went into the citadel of the palace and burned it down over himself and died in the flames.

verses.kjv_text: For his sins which he sinned in doing evil in the sight of the LORD, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he did, to make Israel to sin.
verses.nlt_text: For he, too, had done what was evil in the LORD's sight. He followed the example of Jeroboam in all the sins he had committed and led Israel to commit.

verses.kjv_text: Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he wrought, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Zimri's reign and his conspiracy are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.]

verses.kjv_text: Then were the people of Israel divided into two parts: half of the people followed Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half followed Omri.
verses.nlt_text: But now the people of Israel were split into two factions. Half the people tried to make Tibni son of Ginath their king, while the other half supported Omri.

verses.kjv_text: But the people that followed Omri prevailed against the people that followed Tibni the son of Ginath: so Tibni died, and Omri reigned.
verses.nlt_text: But Omri's supporters defeated the supporters of Tibni. So Tibni was killed, and Omri became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign over Israel, twelve years: six years reigned he in Tirzah.
verses.nlt_text: Omri began to rule over Israel in the thirty-first year of King Asa's reign in Judah. He reigned twelve years in all, six of them in Tirzah.

verses.kjv_text: And he bought the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, owner of the hill, Samaria. {Samaria: Heb. Shomeron}
verses.nlt_text: Then Omri bought the hill now known as Samaria from its owner, Shemer, for 150 pounds of silver. He built a city on it and called the city Samaria in honor of Shemer.

verses.kjv_text: But Omri wrought evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did worse than all that {were} before him.
verses.nlt_text: But Omri did what was evil in the LORD's sight, even more than any of the kings before him.

verses.kjv_text: For he walked in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin, to provoke the LORD God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
verses.nlt_text: He followed the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat in all the sins he had committed and led Israel to commit. The people provoked the anger of the LORD, the God of Israel, with their worthless idols.

verses.kjv_text: Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he did, and his might that he shewed, {are} they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
verses.nlt_text: The rest of the events in Omri's reign, the extent of his power, and everything he did are recorded in [The Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.]

verses.kjv_text: So Omri slept with his fathers, and was buried in Samaria: and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.
verses.nlt_text: When Omri died, he was buried in Samaria. Then his son Ahab became the next king.

verses.kjv_text: And in the thirty and eighth year of Asa king of Judah began Ahab the son of Omri to reign over Israel: and Ahab the son of Omri reigned over Israel in Samaria twenty and two years.
verses.nlt_text: Ahab son of Omri began to rule over Israel in the thirty-eighth year of King Asa's reign in Judah. He reigned in Samaria twenty-two years.

verses.kjv_text: And Ahab the son of Omri did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that {were} before him.
verses.nlt_text: But Ahab son of Omri did what was evil in the LORD's sight, even more than any of the kings before him.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as if it had been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, that he took to wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, and went and served Baal, and worshipped him. {as if...: Heb. was it a light thing, etc}
verses.nlt_text: And as though it were not enough to follow the example of Jeroboam, he married Jezebel, the daughter of King Ethbaal of the Sidonians, and he began to bow down in worship of Baal.

verses.kjv_text: And he reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he had built in Samaria.
verses.nlt_text: First Ahab built a temple and an altar for Baal in Samaria.

verses.kjv_text: And Ahab made a grove; and Ahab did more to provoke the LORD God of Israel to anger than all the kings of Israel that were before him.
verses.nlt_text: Then he set up an Asherah pole. He did more to provoke the anger of the LORD, the God of Israel, than any of the other kings of Israel before him.

verses.kjv_text: In his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest {son} Segub, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun.
verses.nlt_text: It was during his reign that Hiel, a man from Bethel, rebuilt Jericho. When he laid its foundations, it cost him the life of his oldest son, Abiram. And when he completed it and set up its gates, it cost him the life of his youngest son, Segub. This all happened according to the message from the LORD concerning Jericho spoken by Joshua son of Nun.

verses.kjv_text: And Elijah the Tishbite, {who was} of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, {As} the LORD God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word. {Elijah: Heb. Elijahu: Gr. Elias}
verses.nlt_text: Now Elijah, who was from Tishbe in Gilead, told King Ahab, "As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives-- the God I serve-- there will be no dew or rain during the next few years until I give the word!"

verses.kjv_text: And the word of the LORD came unto him, saying,
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said to Elijah,

verses.kjv_text: Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that {is} before Jordan.
verses.nlt_text: "Go to the east and hide by Kerith Brook, near where it enters the Jordan River.

verses.kjv_text: And it shall be, {that} thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.
verses.nlt_text: Drink from the brook and eat what the ravens bring you, for I have commanded them to bring you food."

verses.kjv_text: So he went and did according unto the word of the LORD: for he went and dwelt by the brook Cherith, that {is} before Jordan.
verses.nlt_text: So Elijah did as the LORD told him and camped beside Kerith Brook, east of the Jordan.

verses.kjv_text: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
verses.nlt_text: The ravens brought him bread and meat each morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land. {after...: Heb. at the end of days}
verses.nlt_text: But after a while the brook dried up, for there was no rainfall anywhere in the land.

verses.kjv_text: Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which {belongeth} to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee. {Zarephath: Gr. Sarepta}
verses.nlt_text: "Go and live in the village of Zarephath, near the city of Sidon. I have instructed a widow there to feed you."

verses.kjv_text: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman {was} there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
verses.nlt_text: So he went to Zarephath. As he arrived at the gates of the village, he saw a widow gathering sticks, and he asked her, "Would you please bring me a little water in a cup?"

verses.kjv_text: And as she was going to fetch {it}, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.
verses.nlt_text: As she was going to get it, he called to her, "Bring me a bite of bread, too."

verses.kjv_text: And she said, {As} the LORD thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I {am} gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
verses.nlt_text: But she said, "I swear by the LORD your God that I don't have a single piece of bread in the house. And I have only a handful of flour left in the jar and a little cooking oil in the bottom of the jug. I was just gathering a few sticks to cook this last meal, and then my son and I will die."

verses.kjv_text: And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go {and} do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring {it} unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.
verses.nlt_text: But Elijah said to her, "Don't be afraid! Go ahead and do just what you've said, but make a little bread for me first. Then use what's left to prepare a meal for yourself and your son.

verses.kjv_text: For thus saith the LORD God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day {that} the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth. {sendeth: Heb. giveth}
verses.nlt_text: For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: There will always be flour and olive oil left in your containers until the time when the LORD sends rain and the crops grow again!"

verses.kjv_text: And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat {many} days. {many...: or, a full year}
verses.nlt_text: So she did as Elijah said, and she and Elijah and her son continued to eat for many days.

verses.kjv_text: {And} the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Elijah. {by: Heb. by the hand of}
verses.nlt_text: There was always enough flour and olive oil left in the containers, just as the LORD had promised through Elijah.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass after these things, {that} the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.
verses.nlt_text: Some time later the woman's son became sick. He grew worse and worse, and finally he died.

verses.kjv_text: And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?
verses.nlt_text: Then she said to Elijah, "O man of God, what have you done to me? Have you come here to point out my sins and kill my son?"

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
verses.nlt_text: But Elijah replied, "Give me your son." And he took the child's body from her arms, carried him up the stairs to the room where he was staying, and laid the body on his bed.

verses.kjv_text: And he cried unto the LORD, and said, O LORD my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
verses.nlt_text: Then Elijah cried out to the LORD, "O LORD my God, why have you brought tragedy to this widow who has opened her home to me, causing her son to die?"

verses.kjv_text: And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the LORD, and said, O LORD my God, I pray thee, let this child's soul come into him again. {stretched: Heb. measured} {into...: Heb. into his inward parts}
verses.nlt_text: And he stretched himself out over the child three times and cried out to the LORD, "O LORD my God, please let this child's life return to him."

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
verses.nlt_text: The LORD heard Elijah's prayer, and the life of the child returned, and he revived!

verses.kjv_text: And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother: and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.
verses.nlt_text: Then Elijah brought him down from the upper room and gave him to his mother. "Look!" he said. "Your son is alive!"

verses.kjv_text: And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that thou {art} a man of God, {and} that the word of the LORD in thy mouth {is} truth.
verses.nlt_text: Then the woman told Elijah, "Now I know for sure that you are a man of God, and that the LORD truly speaks through you."

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass {after} many days, that the word of the LORD came to Elijah in the third year, saying, Go, shew thyself unto Ahab; and I will send rain upon the earth.
verses.nlt_text: Later on, in the third year of the drought, the LORD said to Elijah, "Go and present yourself to King Ahab. Tell him that I will soon send rain!"

verses.kjv_text: And Elijah went to shew himself unto Ahab. And {there was} a sore famine in Samaria.
verses.nlt_text: So Elijah went to appear before Ahab.Meanwhile, the famine had become very severe in Samaria.

verses.kjv_text: And Ahab called Obadiah, which {was} the governor of {his} house. (Now Obadiah feared the LORD greatly: {Obadiah: Heb. Obadiahu} {the governor...: Heb. over his house}
verses.nlt_text: So Ahab summoned Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (Obadiah was a devoted follower of the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: For it was {so}, when Jezebel cut off the prophets of the LORD, that Obadiah took an hundred prophets, and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water.) {Jezebel: Heb. Izebel}
verses.nlt_text: Once when Jezebel had tried to kill all the LORD's prophets, Obadiah had hidden 100 of them in two caves. He put fifty prophets in each cave and supplied them with food and water.)

verses.kjv_text: And Ahab said unto Obadiah, Go into the land, unto all fountains of water, and unto all brooks: peradventure we may find grass to save the horses and mules alive, that we lose not all the beasts. {that...: Heb. that we cut not off ourselves from the beasts}
verses.nlt_text: Ahab said to Obadiah, "We must check every spring and valley in the land to see if we can find enough grass to save at least some of my horses and mules."

verses.kjv_text: So they divided the land between them to pass throughout it: Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.
verses.nlt_text: So they divided the land between them. Ahab went one way by himself, and Obadiah went another way by himself.

verses.kjv_text: And as Obadiah was in the way, behold, Elijah met him: and he knew him, and fell on his face, and said, {Art} thou that my lord Elijah?
verses.nlt_text: As Obadiah was walking along, he suddenly saw Elijah coming toward him. Obadiah recognized him at once and bowed low to the ground before him. "Is it really you, my lord Elijah?" he asked.

verses.kjv_text: And he answered him, I {am}: go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah {is here}.
verses.nlt_text: "Yes, it is," Elijah replied. "Now go and tell your master, 'Elijah is here.'"

verses.kjv_text: And he said, What have I sinned, that thou wouldest deliver thy servant into the hand of Ahab, to slay me?
verses.nlt_text: "Oh, sir," Obadiah protested, "what harm have I done to you that you are sending me to my death at the hands of Ahab?

verses.kjv_text: {As} the LORD thy God liveth, there is no nation or kingdom, whither my lord hath not sent to seek thee: and when they said, {He is} not {there}; he took an oath of the kingdom and nation, that they found thee not.
verses.nlt_text: For I swear by the LORD your God that the king has searched every nation and kingdom on earth from end to end to find you. And each time he was told, 'Elijah isn't here,' King Ahab forced the king of that nation to swear to the truth of his claim.

verses.kjv_text: And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah {is here}.
verses.nlt_text: And now you say, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here."'

verses.kjv_text: And it shall come to pass, {as soon as} I am gone from thee, that the Spirit of the LORD shall carry thee whither I know not; and {so} when I come and tell Ahab, and he cannot find thee, he shall slay me: but I thy servant fear the LORD from my youth.
verses.nlt_text: But as soon as I leave you, the Spirit of the LORD will carry you away to who knows where. When Ahab comes and cannot find you, he will kill me. Yet I have been a true servant of the LORD all my life.

verses.kjv_text: Was it not told my lord what I did when Jezebel slew the prophets of the LORD, how I hid an hundred men of the LORD'S prophets by fifty in a cave, and fed them with bread and water?
verses.nlt_text: Has no one told you, my lord, about the time when Jezebel was trying to kill the LORD's prophets? I hid 100 of them in two caves and supplied them with food and water.

verses.kjv_text: And now thou sayest, Go, tell thy lord, Behold, Elijah {is here}: and he shall slay me.
verses.nlt_text: And now you say, 'Go and tell your master, "Elijah is here." ' Sir, if I do that, Ahab will certainly kill me."

verses.kjv_text: And Elijah said, {As} the LORD of hosts liveth, before whom I stand, I will surely shew myself unto him to day.
verses.nlt_text: But Elijah said, "I swear by the LORD Almighty, in whose presence I stand, that I will present myself to Ahab this very day."

verses.kjv_text: So Obadiah went to meet Ahab, and told him: and Ahab went to meet Elijah.
verses.nlt_text: So Obadiah went to tell Ahab that Elijah had come, and Ahab went out to meet Elijah.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, {Art} thou he that troubleth Israel?
verses.nlt_text: When Ahab saw him, he exclaimed, "So, is it really you, you troublemaker of Israel?"
