verses.kjv_text: While he {was} yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The fire of God is fallen from heaven, and hath burned up the sheep, and the servants, and consumed them; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. {The fire...: or, A great fire}
verses.nlt_text: While he was still speaking, another messenger arrived with this news: "The fire of God has fallen from heaven and burned up your sheep and all the shepherds. I am the only one who escaped to tell you."

verses.kjv_text: While he {was} yet speaking, there came also another, and said, The Chaldeans made out three bands, and fell upon the camels, and have carried them away, yea, and slain the servants with the edge of the sword; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. {fell: Heb. rushed}
verses.nlt_text: While he was still speaking, a third messenger arrived with this news: "Three bands of Chaldean raiders have stolen your camels and killed your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you."

verses.kjv_text: While he {was} yet speaking, there came also another, and said, Thy sons and thy daughters {were} eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother's house:
verses.nlt_text: While he was still speaking, another messenger arrived with this news: "Your sons and daughters were feasting in their oldest brother's home.

verses.kjv_text: And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead; and I only am escaped alone to tell thee. {from...: Heb. from aside, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Suddenly, a powerful wind swept in from the wilderness and hit the house on all sides. The house collapsed, and all your children are dead. I am the only one who escaped to tell you."

verses.kjv_text: Then Job arose, and rent his mantle, and shaved his head, and fell down upon the ground, and worshipped, {mantle: or, robe}
verses.nlt_text: Job stood up and tore his robe in grief. Then he shaved his head and fell to the ground to worship.

verses.kjv_text: And said, Naked came I out of my mother's womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: He said, "I came naked from my mother's womb, and I will be naked when I leave. The LORD gave me what I had, and the LORD has taken it away. Praise the name of the LORD!"

verses.kjv_text: In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly. {charged...: or, attributed folly to God}
verses.nlt_text: In all of this, Job did not sin by blaming God.

verses.kjv_text: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.
verses.nlt_text: One day the members of the heavenly court came again to present themselves before the LORD, and the Accuser, Satan, came with them.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.
verses.nlt_text: "Where have you come from?" the LORD asked Satan.Satan answered the LORD, "I have been patrolling the earth, watching everything that's going on."

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that {there is} none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause. {to destroy...: Heb. to swallow him up}
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD asked Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job? He is the finest man in all the earth. He is blameless-- a man of complete integrity. He fears God and stays away from evil. And he has maintained his integrity, even though you urged me to harm him without cause."

verses.kjv_text: And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.
verses.nlt_text: Satan replied to the LORD, "Skin for skin! A man will give up everything he has to save his life.

verses.kjv_text: But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.
verses.nlt_text: But reach out and take away his health, and he will surely curse you to your face!"

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he {is} in thine hand; but save his life. {but: or, only}
verses.nlt_text: "All right, do with him as you please," the LORD said to Satan. "But spare his life."

verses.kjv_text: So went Satan forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.
verses.nlt_text: So Satan left the LORD's presence, and he struck Job with terrible boils from head to foot.

verses.kjv_text: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.
verses.nlt_text: Job scraped his skin with a piece of broken pottery as he sat among the ashes.

verses.kjv_text: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.
verses.nlt_text: His wife said to him, "Are you still trying to maintain your integrity? Curse God and die."

verses.kjv_text: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.
verses.nlt_text: But Job replied, "You talk like a foolish woman. Should we accept only good things from the hand of God and never anything bad?" So in all this, Job said nothing wrong.

verses.kjv_text: Now when Job's three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
verses.nlt_text: When three of Job's friends heard of the tragedy he had suffered, they got together and traveled from their homes to comfort and console him. Their names were Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite.

verses.kjv_text: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
verses.nlt_text: When they saw Job from a distance, they scarcely recognized him. Wailing loudly, they tore their robes and threw dust into the air over their heads to show their grief.

verses.kjv_text: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that {his} grief was very great.
verses.nlt_text: Then they sat on the ground with him for seven days and nights. No one said a word to Job, for they saw that his suffering was too great for words.

verses.kjv_text: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.
verses.nlt_text: At last Job spoke, and he cursed the day of his birth.

verses.kjv_text: And Job spake, and said, {spake: Heb. answered}
verses.nlt_text: He said:

verses.kjv_text: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night {in which} it was said, There is a man child conceived.
verses.nlt_text: "Let the day of my birth be erased, and the night I was conceived.

verses.kjv_text: Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.
verses.nlt_text: Let that day be turned to darkness. Let it be lost even to God on high, and let no light shine on it.

verses.kjv_text: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. {stain: or, challenge} {let the...: or, let them terrify it, as those who have a bitter day}
verses.nlt_text: Let the darkness and utter gloom claim that day for its own. Let a black cloud overshadow it, and let the darkness terrify it.

verses.kjv_text: As {for} that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months. {let it not be...: or, let it not rejoice among the days}
verses.nlt_text: Let that night be blotted off the calendar, never again to be counted among the days of the year, never again to appear among the months.

verses.kjv_text: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.
verses.nlt_text: Let that night be childless. Let it have no joy.

verses.kjv_text: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning. {their...: or, leviathan}
verses.nlt_text: Let those who are experts at cursing-- whose cursing could rouse Leviathan-- curse that day.

verses.kjv_text: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but {have} none; neither let it see the dawning of the day: {the dawning...: Heb. the eyelids of the morning}
verses.nlt_text: Let its morning stars remain dark. Let it hope for light, but in vain; may it never see the morning light.

verses.kjv_text: Because it shut not up the doors of my {mother's} womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.
verses.nlt_text: Curse that day for failing to shut my mother's womb, for letting me be born to see all this trouble.

verses.kjv_text: Why died I not from the womb? {why} did I {not} give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?
verses.nlt_text: "Why wasn't I born dead? Why didn't I die as I came from the womb?

verses.kjv_text: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?
verses.nlt_text: Why was I laid on my mother's lap? Why did she nurse me at her breasts?

verses.kjv_text: For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,
verses.nlt_text: Had I died at birth, I would now be at peace. I would be asleep and at rest.

verses.kjv_text: With kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves;
verses.nlt_text: I would rest with the world's kings and prime ministers, whose great buildings now lie in ruins.

verses.kjv_text: Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver:
verses.nlt_text: I would rest with princes, rich in gold, whose palaces were filled with silver.

verses.kjv_text: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants {which} never saw light.
verses.nlt_text: Why wasn't I buried like a stillborn child, like a baby who never lives to see the light?

verses.kjv_text: There the wicked cease {from} troubling; and there the weary be at rest. {weary: Heb. wearied in strength}
verses.nlt_text: For in death the wicked cause no trouble, and the weary are at rest.

verses.kjv_text: {There} the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.
verses.nlt_text: Even captives are at ease in death, with no guards to curse them.

verses.kjv_text: The small and great are there; and the servant {is} free from his master.
verses.nlt_text: Rich and poor are both there, and the slave is free from his master.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter {in} soul;
verses.nlt_text: "Oh, why give light to those in misery, and life to those who are bitter?

verses.kjv_text: Which long for death, but it {cometh} not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures; {long: Heb. wait}
verses.nlt_text: They long for death, and it won't come. They search for death more eagerly than for hidden treasure.

verses.kjv_text: Which rejoice exceedingly, {and} are glad, when they can find the grave?
verses.nlt_text: They're filled with joy when they finally die, and rejoice when they find the grave.

verses.kjv_text: {Why is light given} to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?
verses.nlt_text: Why is life given to those with no future, those God has surrounded with difficulties?

verses.kjv_text: For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters. {I eat: Heb. my meat}
verses.nlt_text: I cannot eat for sighing; my groans pour out like water.

verses.kjv_text: For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me. {the thing...: Heb. I feared a fear, and it came upon me}
verses.nlt_text: What I always feared has happened to me. What I dreaded has come true.

verses.kjv_text: I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.
verses.nlt_text: I have no peace, no quietness. I have no rest; only trouble comes."

verses.kjv_text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied to Job:

verses.kjv_text: {If} we assay to commune with thee, wilt thou be grieved? but who can withhold himself from speaking? {to...: Heb. a word} {withhold...: Heb. refrain from words?}
verses.nlt_text: "Will you be patient and let me say a word? For who could keep from speaking out?

verses.kjv_text: Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
verses.nlt_text: "In the past you have encouraged many people; you have strengthened those who were weak.

verses.kjv_text: Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.
verses.nlt_text: Your words have supported those who were falling; you encouraged those with shaky knees.

verses.kjv_text: But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
verses.nlt_text: But now when trouble strikes, you lose heart. You are terrified when it touches you.

verses.kjv_text: {Is} not {this} thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?
verses.nlt_text: Doesn't your reverence for God give you confidence? Doesn't your life of integrity give you hope?

verses.kjv_text: Remember, I pray thee, who {ever} perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?
verses.nlt_text: "Stop and think! Do the innocent die? When have the upright been destroyed?

verses.kjv_text: Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.
verses.nlt_text: My experience shows that those who plant trouble and cultivate evil will harvest the same.

verses.kjv_text: By the blast of God they perish, and by the breath of his nostrils are they consumed. {by the breath...: that is, by his anger}
verses.nlt_text: A breath from God destroys them. They vanish in a blast of his anger.

verses.kjv_text: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, and the teeth of the young lions, are broken.
verses.nlt_text: The lion roars and the wildcat snarls, but the teeth of strong lions will be broken.

verses.kjv_text: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey, and the stout lion's whelps are scattered abroad.
verses.nlt_text: The fierce lion will starve for lack of prey, and the cubs of the lioness will be scattered.

verses.kjv_text: Now a thing was secretly brought to me, and mine ear received a little thereof. {secretly: Heb. by stealth}
verses.nlt_text: "This truth was given to me in secret, as though whispered in my ear.

verses.kjv_text: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falleth on men,
verses.nlt_text: It came to me in a disturbing vision at night, when people are in a deep sleep.

verses.kjv_text: Fear came upon me, and trembling, which made all my bones to shake. {came...: Heb. met} {all: Heb. the multitude of}
verses.nlt_text: Fear gripped me, and my bones trembled.

verses.kjv_text: Then a spirit passed before my face; the hair of my flesh stood up:
verses.nlt_text: A spirit swept past my face, and my hair stood on end.

verses.kjv_text: It stood still, but I could not discern the form thereof: an image {was} before mine eyes, {there was} silence, and I heard a voice, {saying}, {there...: or, I heard a still voice}
verses.nlt_text: The spirit stopped, but I couldn't see its shape. There was a form before my eyes. In the silence I heard a voice say,

verses.kjv_text: Shall mortal man be more just than God? shall a man be more pure than his maker?
verses.nlt_text: 'Can a mortal be innocent before God? Can anyone be pure before the Creator?'

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he put no trust in his servants; and his angels he charged with folly: {and his...: or, nor in his angels, in whom he put light}
verses.nlt_text: "If God does not trust his own angels and has charged his messengers with foolishness,

verses.kjv_text: How much less {in} them that dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation {is} in the dust, {which} are crushed before the moth?
verses.nlt_text: how much less will he trust people made of clay! They are made of dust, crushed as easily as a moth.

verses.kjv_text: They are destroyed from morning to evening: they perish for ever without any regarding {it}. {destroyed: Heb. beaten in pieces}
verses.nlt_text: They are alive in the morning but dead by evening, gone forever without a trace.

verses.kjv_text: Doth not their excellency {which is} in them go away? they die, even without wisdom.
verses.nlt_text: Their tent-cords are pulled and the tent collapses, and they die in ignorance.

verses.kjv_text: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn? {turn: or, look?}
verses.nlt_text: "Cry for help, but will anyone answer you? Which of the angels will help you?

verses.kjv_text: For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one. {envy: or, indignation}
verses.nlt_text: Surely resentment destroys the fool, and jealousy kills the simple.

verses.kjv_text: I have seen the foolish taking root: but suddenly I cursed his habitation.
verses.nlt_text: I have seen that fools may be successful for the moment, but then comes sudden disaster.

verses.kjv_text: His children are far from safety, and they are crushed in the gate, neither {is there} any to deliver {them}.
verses.nlt_text: Their children are abandoned far from help; they are crushed in court with no one to defend them.

verses.kjv_text: Whose harvest the hungry eateth up, and taketh it even out of the thorns, and the robber swalloweth up their substance.
verses.nlt_text: The hungry devour their harvest, even when it is guarded by brambles. The thirsty pant after their wealth.

verses.kjv_text: Although affliction cometh not forth of the dust, neither doth trouble spring out of the ground; {affliction: or, iniquity}
verses.nlt_text: But evil does not spring from the soil, and trouble does not sprout from the earth.

verses.kjv_text: Yet man is born unto trouble, as the sparks fly upward. {trouble: or, labour} {sparks...: Heb. the sons of the burning coal lift up to fly}
verses.nlt_text: People are born for trouble as readily as sparks fly up from a fire.

verses.kjv_text: I would seek unto God, and unto God would I commit my cause:
verses.nlt_text: "If I were you, I would go to God and present my case to him.

verses.kjv_text: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number: {unsearchable: Heb. there is no search} {without...: Heb. till there be no number}
verses.nlt_text: He does great things too marvelous to understand. He performs countless miracles.

verses.kjv_text: Who giveth rain upon the earth, and sendeth waters upon the fields: {fields: Heb. outplaces}
verses.nlt_text: He gives rain for the earth and water for the fields.

verses.kjv_text: To set up on high those that be low; that those which mourn may be exalted to safety.
verses.nlt_text: He gives prosperity to the poor and protects those who suffer.

verses.kjv_text: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform {their} enterprise. {their enterprise: or, any thing}
verses.nlt_text: He frustrates the plans of schemers so the work of their hands will not succeed.

verses.kjv_text: He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.
verses.nlt_text: He traps the wise in their own cleverness so their cunning schemes are thwarted.

verses.kjv_text: They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night. {meet...: or, run into}
verses.nlt_text: They find it is dark in the daytime, and they grope at noon as if it were night.

verses.kjv_text: But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.
verses.nlt_text: He rescues the poor from the cutting words of the strong, and rescues them from the clutches of the powerful.

verses.kjv_text: So the poor hath hope, and iniquity stoppeth her mouth.
verses.nlt_text: And so at last the poor have hope, and the snapping jaws of the wicked are shut.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, happy {is} the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty:
verses.nlt_text: "But consider the joy of those corrected by God! Do not despise the discipline of the Almighty when you sin.

verses.kjv_text: For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.
verses.nlt_text: For though he wounds, he also bandages. He strikes, but his hands also heal.

verses.kjv_text: He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.
verses.nlt_text: From six disasters he will rescue you; even in the seventh, he will keep you from evil.

verses.kjv_text: In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword. {power: Heb. hands}
verses.nlt_text: He will save you from death in time of famine, from the power of the sword in time of war.

verses.kjv_text: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue: neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh. {from...: or, when the tongue scourgeth}
verses.nlt_text: You will be safe from slander and have no fear when destruction comes.

verses.kjv_text: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.
verses.nlt_text: You will laugh at destruction and famine; wild animals will not terrify you.

verses.kjv_text: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field: and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
verses.nlt_text: You will be at peace with the stones of the field, and its wild animals will be at peace with you.

verses.kjv_text: And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle {shall be} in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin. {thy tabernacle...: or, peace is thy tabernacle} {sin: or, err}
verses.nlt_text: You will know that your home is safe. When you survey your possessions, nothing will be missing.

verses.kjv_text: Thou shalt know also that thy seed {shall be} great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth. {great: or, much}
verses.nlt_text: You will have many children; your descendants will be as plentiful as grass!

verses.kjv_text: Thou shalt come to {thy} grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season. {cometh in: Heb. ascendeth}
verses.nlt_text: You will go to the grave at a ripe old age, like a sheaf of grain harvested at the proper time!

verses.kjv_text: Lo this, we have searched it, so it {is}; hear it, and know thou {it} for thy good. {for...: Heb. for thyself}
verses.nlt_text: "We have studied life and found all this to be true. Listen to my counsel, and apply it to yourself."

verses.kjv_text: But Job answered and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Job spoke again:

verses.kjv_text: Oh that my grief were throughly weighed, and my calamity laid in the balances together! {laid: Heb. lifted up}
verses.nlt_text: "If my misery could be weighed and my troubles be put on the scales,

verses.kjv_text: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the sea: therefore my words are swallowed up. {my words...: that is, I want words to express my grief}
verses.nlt_text: they would outweigh all the sands of the sea. That is why I spoke impulsively.

verses.kjv_text: For the arrows of the Almighty {are} within me, the poison whereof drinketh up my spirit: the terrors of God do set themselves in array against me.
verses.nlt_text: For the Almighty has struck me down with his arrows. Their poison infects my spirit. God's terrors are lined up against me.

verses.kjv_text: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass? or loweth the ox over his fodder? {when he...: Heb. at grass?}
verses.nlt_text: Don't I have a right to complain? Don't wild donkeys bray when they find no grass, and oxen bellow when they have no food?

verses.kjv_text: Can that which is unsavoury be eaten without salt? or is there {any} taste in the white of an egg?
verses.nlt_text: Don't people complain about unsalted food? Does anyone want the tasteless white of an egg?

verses.kjv_text: The things {that} my soul refused to touch {are} as my sorrowful meat.
verses.nlt_text: My appetite disappears when I look at it; I gag at the thought of eating it!

verses.kjv_text: Oh that I might have my request; and that God would grant {me} the thing that I long for! {the thing...: Heb. my expectation}
verses.nlt_text: "Oh, that I might have my request, that God would grant my desire.

verses.kjv_text: Even that it would please God to destroy me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!
verses.nlt_text: I wish he would crush me. I wish he would reach out his hand and kill me.

verses.kjv_text: Then should I yet have comfort; yea, I would harden myself in sorrow: let him not spare; for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.
verses.nlt_text: At least I can take comfort in this: Despite the pain, I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

verses.kjv_text: What {is} my strength, that I should hope? and what {is} mine end, that I should prolong my life?
verses.nlt_text: But I don't have the strength to endure. I have nothing to live for.

verses.kjv_text: {Is} my strength the strength of stones? or {is} my flesh of brass? {of brass: Heb. brasen?}
verses.nlt_text: Do I have the strength of a stone? Is my body made of bronze?

verses.kjv_text: {Is} not my help in me? and is wisdom driven quite from me?
verses.nlt_text: No, I am utterly helpless, without any chance of success.

verses.kjv_text: To him that is afflicted pity {should be shewed} from his friend; but he forsaketh the fear of the Almighty. {is afflicted: Heb. melteth}
verses.nlt_text: "One should be kind to a fainting friend, but you accuse me without any fear of the Almighty.

verses.kjv_text: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook, {and} as the stream of brooks they pass away;
verses.nlt_text: My brothers, you have proved as unreliable as a seasonal brook that overflows its banks in the spring

verses.kjv_text: Which are blackish by reason of the ice, {and} wherein the snow is hid:
verses.nlt_text: when it is swollen with ice and melting snow.

verses.kjv_text: What time they wax warm, they vanish: when it is hot, they are consumed out of their place. {vanish: Heb. are cut off} {when...: Heb. in the heat thereof} {consumed: Heb. extinguished}
verses.nlt_text: But when the hot weather arrives, the water disappears. The brook vanishes in the heat.

verses.kjv_text: The paths of their way are turned aside; they go to nothing, and perish.
verses.nlt_text: The caravans turn aside to be refreshed, but there is nothing to drink, so they die.

verses.kjv_text: The troops of Tema looked, the companies of Sheba waited for them.
verses.nlt_text: The caravans from Tema search for this water; the travelers from Sheba hope to find it.

verses.kjv_text: They were confounded because they had hoped; they came thither, and were ashamed.
verses.nlt_text: They count on it but are disappointed. When they arrive, their hopes are dashed.

verses.kjv_text: For now ye are nothing; ye see {my} casting down, and are afraid. {ye are...: or, ye are like to them: Heb. to it} {nothing: Heb. not}
verses.nlt_text: You, too, have given no help. You have seen my calamity, and you are afraid.

verses.kjv_text: Did I say, Bring unto me? or, Give a reward for me of your substance?
verses.nlt_text: But why? Have I ever asked you for a gift? Have I begged for anything of yours for myself?

verses.kjv_text: Or, Deliver me from the enemy's hand? or, Redeem me from the hand of the mighty?
verses.nlt_text: Have I asked you to rescue me from my enemies, or to save me from ruthless people?

verses.kjv_text: Teach me, and I will hold my tongue: and cause me to understand wherein I have erred.
verses.nlt_text: Teach me, and I will keep quiet. Show me what I have done wrong.

verses.kjv_text: How forcible are right words! but what doth your arguing reprove?
verses.nlt_text: Honest words can be painful, but what do your criticisms amount to?

verses.kjv_text: Do ye imagine to reprove words, and the speeches of one that is desperate, {which are} as wind?
verses.nlt_text: Do you think your words are convincing when you disregard my cry of desperation?

verses.kjv_text: Yea, ye overwhelm the fatherless, and ye dig {a pit} for your friend. {ye overwhelm: Heb. ye cause to fall upon}
verses.nlt_text: You would even send an orphan into slavery or sell a friend.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore be content, look upon me; for {it is} evident unto you if I lie. {evident...: Heb. before your face}
verses.nlt_text: Look at me! Would I lie to your face?

verses.kjv_text: Return, I pray you, let it not be iniquity; yea, return again, my righteousness {is} in it. {in it: that is, in this matter}
verses.nlt_text: Stop assuming my guilt, for I have done no wrong.

verses.kjv_text: Is there iniquity in my tongue? cannot my taste discern perverse things? {my taste: Heb. my palate}
verses.nlt_text: Do you think I am lying? Don't I know the difference between right and wrong?

verses.kjv_text: {Is there} not an appointed time to man upon earth? {are not} his days also like the days of an hireling? {an appointed...: or, a warfare}
verses.nlt_text: "Is not all human life a struggle? Our lives are like that of a hired hand,

verses.kjv_text: As a servant earnestly desireth the shadow, and as an hireling looketh for {the reward of} his work: {earnestly...: Heb. gapeth after}
verses.nlt_text: like a worker who longs for the shade, like a servant waiting to be paid.

verses.kjv_text: So am I made to possess months of vanity, and wearisome nights are appointed to me.
verses.nlt_text: I, too, have been assigned months of futility, long and weary nights of misery.

verses.kjv_text: When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day. {the night...: Heb. the evening be measured?}
verses.nlt_text: Lying in bed, I think, 'When will it be morning?' But the night drags on, and I toss till dawn.

verses.kjv_text: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; my skin is broken, and become loathsome.
verses.nlt_text: My body is covered with maggots and scabs. My skin breaks open, oozing with pus.

verses.kjv_text: My days are swifter than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent without hope.
verses.nlt_text: "My days fly faster than a weaver's shuttle. They end without hope.

verses.kjv_text: O remember that my life {is} wind: mine eye shall no more see good. {shall...: Heb. shall not return} {see: to see, that is, to enjoy}
verses.nlt_text: O God, remember that my life is but a breath, and I will never again feel happiness.

verses.kjv_text: The eye of him that hath seen me shall see me no {more}: thine eyes {are} upon me, and I {am} not. {I am...: that is, I can live no longer}
verses.nlt_text: You see me now, but not for long. You will look for me, but I will be gone.

verses.kjv_text: {As} the cloud is consumed and vanisheth away: so he that goeth down to the grave shall come up no {more}.
verses.nlt_text: Just as a cloud dissipates and vanishes, those who die will not come back.

verses.kjv_text: He shall return no more to his house, neither shall his place know him any more.
verses.nlt_text: They are gone forever from their home-- never to be seen again.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth; I will speak in the anguish of my spirit; I will complain in the bitterness of my soul.
verses.nlt_text: "I cannot keep from speaking. I must express my anguish. My bitter soul must complain.

verses.kjv_text: {Am} I a sea, or a whale, that thou settest a watch over me?
verses.nlt_text: Am I a sea monster or a dragon that you must place me under guard?

verses.kjv_text: When I say, My bed shall comfort me, my couch shall ease my complaint;
verses.nlt_text: I think, 'My bed will comfort me, and sleep will ease my misery,'

verses.kjv_text: Then thou scarest me with dreams, and terrifiest me through visions:
verses.nlt_text: but then you shatter me with dreams and terrify me with visions.

verses.kjv_text: So that my soul chooseth strangling, {and} death rather than my life. {life: Heb. bones}
verses.nlt_text: I would rather be strangled-- rather die than suffer like this.

verses.kjv_text: I loathe {it}; I would not live alway: let me alone; for my days {are} vanity.
verses.nlt_text: I hate my life and don't want to go on living. Oh, leave me alone for my few remaining days.

verses.kjv_text: What {is} man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him?
verses.nlt_text: "What are people, that you should make so much of us, that you should think of us so often?

verses.kjv_text: And {that} thou shouldest visit him every morning, {and} try him every moment?
verses.nlt_text: For you examine us every morning and test us every moment.

verses.kjv_text: How long wilt thou not depart from me, nor let me alone till I swallow down my spittle?
verses.nlt_text: Why won't you leave me alone, at least long enough for me to swallow!

verses.kjv_text: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?
verses.nlt_text: If I have sinned, what have I done to you, O watcher of all humanity? Why make me your target? Am I a burden to you?

verses.kjv_text: And why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I {shall} not {be}.
verses.nlt_text: Why not just forgive my sin and take away my guilt? For soon I will lie down in the dust and die. When you look for me, I will be gone."

verses.kjv_text: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Bildad the Shuhite replied to Job:

verses.kjv_text: How long wilt thou speak these {things}? and {how long shall} the words of thy mouth {be like} a strong wind?
verses.nlt_text: "How long will you go on like this? You sound like a blustering wind.

verses.kjv_text: Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
verses.nlt_text: Does God twist justice? Does the Almighty twist what is right?

verses.kjv_text: If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression; {for...: Heb. in the hand of their transgression}
verses.nlt_text: Your children must have sinned against him, so their punishment was well deserved.

verses.kjv_text: If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
verses.nlt_text: But if you pray to God and seek the favor of the Almighty,

verses.kjv_text: If thou {wert} pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
verses.nlt_text: and if you are pure and live with integrity, he will surely rise up and restore your happy home.

verses.kjv_text: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.
verses.nlt_text: And though you started with little, you will end with much.

verses.kjv_text: For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers:
verses.nlt_text: "Just ask the previous generation. Pay attention to the experience of our ancestors.

verses.kjv_text: (For we {are but of} yesterday, and know nothing, because our days upon earth {are} a shadow:) {nothing: Heb. not}
verses.nlt_text: For we were born but yesterday and know nothing. Our days on earth are as fleeting as a shadow.

verses.kjv_text: Shall not they teach thee, {and} tell thee, and utter words out of their heart?
verses.nlt_text: But those who came before us will teach you. They will teach you the wisdom of old.

verses.kjv_text: Can the rush grow up without mire? can the flag grow without water?
verses.nlt_text: "Can papyrus reeds grow tall without a marsh? Can marsh grass flourish without water?

verses.kjv_text: Whilst it {is} yet in his greenness, {and} not cut down, it withereth before any {other} herb.
verses.nlt_text: While they are still flowering, not ready to be cut, they begin to wither more quickly than grass.

verses.kjv_text: So {are} the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish:
verses.nlt_text: The same happens to all who forget God. The hopes of the godless evaporate.

verses.kjv_text: Whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust {shall be} a spider's web. {web: Heb. house}
verses.nlt_text: Their confidence hangs by a thread. They are leaning on a spider's web.

verses.kjv_text: He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.
verses.nlt_text: They cling to their home for security, but it won't last. They try to hold it tight, but it will not endure.

verses.kjv_text: He {is} green before the sun, and his branch shooteth forth in his garden.
verses.nlt_text: The godless seem like a lush plant growing in the sunshine, its branches spreading across the garden.

verses.kjv_text: His roots are wrapped about the heap, {and} seeth the place of stones.
verses.nlt_text: Its roots grow down through a pile of stones; it takes hold on a bed of rocks.

verses.kjv_text: If he destroy him from his place, then {it} shall deny him, {saying}, I have not seen thee.
verses.nlt_text: But when it is uprooted, it's as though it never existed!

verses.kjv_text: Behold, this {is} the joy of his way, and out of the earth shall others grow.
verses.nlt_text: That's the end of its life, and others spring up from the earth to replace it.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, God will not cast away a perfect {man}, neither will he help the evil doers: {help...: Heb. take the ungodly by the hand} {come: Heb. shall not be}
verses.nlt_text: "But look, God will not reject a person of integrity, nor will he lend a hand to the wicked.

verses.kjv_text: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing. {rejoicing: Heb. shouting for joy}
verses.nlt_text: He will once again fill your mouth with laughter and your lips with shouts of joy.

verses.kjv_text: They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought. {shall come...: Heb. shall not be}
verses.nlt_text: Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, and the home of the wicked will be destroyed."

verses.kjv_text: Then Job answered and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Job spoke again:

verses.kjv_text: I know {it is} so of a truth: but how should man be just with God? {with God: or, before God?}
verses.nlt_text: "Yes, I know all this is true in principle. But how can a person be declared innocent in God's sight?

verses.kjv_text: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.
verses.nlt_text: If someone wanted to take God to court, would it be possible to answer him even once in a thousand times?

verses.kjv_text: {He is} wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened {himself} against him, and hath prospered?
verses.nlt_text: For God is so wise and so mighty. Who has ever challenged him successfully?

verses.kjv_text: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.
verses.nlt_text: "Without warning, he moves the mountains, overturning them in his anger.

verses.kjv_text: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.
verses.nlt_text: He shakes the earth from its place, and its foundations tremble.

verses.kjv_text: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.
verses.nlt_text: If he commands it, the sun won't rise and the stars won't shine.

verses.kjv_text: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea. {waves: Heb. heights}
verses.nlt_text: He alone has spread out the heavens and marches on the waves of the sea.

verses.kjv_text: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south. {Arcturus...: Heb. Ash, Cesil, and Cimah}
verses.nlt_text: He made all the stars-- the Bear and Orion, the Pleiades and the constellations of the southern sky.

verses.kjv_text: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.
verses.nlt_text: He does great things too marvelous to understand. He performs countless miracles.

verses.kjv_text: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see {him} not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
verses.nlt_text: "Yet when he comes near, I cannot see him. When he moves by, I do not see him go.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou? {hinder...: Heb. turn him away?}
verses.nlt_text: If he snatches someone in death, who can stop him? Who dares to ask, 'What are you doing?'

verses.kjv_text: {If} God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him. {proud...: Heb. helpers of pride, or, strength}
verses.nlt_text: And God does not restrain his anger. Even the monsters of the sea are crushed beneath his feet.

verses.kjv_text: How much less shall I answer him, {and} choose out my words {to reason} with him?
verses.nlt_text: "So who am I, that I should try to answer God or even reason with him?

verses.kjv_text: Whom, though I were righteous, {yet} would I not answer, {but} I would make supplication to my judge.
verses.nlt_text: Even if I were right, I would have no defense. I could only plead for mercy.

verses.kjv_text: If I had called, and he had answered me; {yet} would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.
verses.nlt_text: And even if I summoned him and he responded, I'm not sure he would listen to me.

verses.kjv_text: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.
verses.nlt_text: For he attacks me with a storm and repeatedly wounds me without cause.

verses.kjv_text: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.
verses.nlt_text: He will not let me catch my breath, but fills me instead with bitter sorrows.

verses.kjv_text: If {I speak} of strength, lo, {he is} strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time {to plead}?
verses.nlt_text: If it's a question of strength, he's the strong one. If it's a matter of justice, who dares to summon him to court?

verses.kjv_text: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: {if I say}, I {am} perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.
verses.nlt_text: Though I am innocent, my own mouth would pronounce me guilty. Though I am blameless, it would prove me wicked.

verses.kjv_text: {Though} I {were} perfect, {yet} would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.
verses.nlt_text: "I am innocent, but it makes no difference to me-- I despise my life.

verses.kjv_text: This {is} one {thing}, therefore I said {it}, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
verses.nlt_text: Innocent or wicked, it is all the same to God. That's why I say, 'He destroys both the blameless and the wicked.'

verses.kjv_text: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.
verses.nlt_text: When a plague sweeps through, he laughs at the death of the innocent.

verses.kjv_text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, {and} who {is} he?
verses.nlt_text: The whole earth is in the hands of the wicked, and God blinds the eyes of the judges. If he's not the one who does it, who is?

verses.kjv_text: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.
verses.nlt_text: "My life passes more swiftly than a runner. It flees away without a glimpse of happiness.

verses.kjv_text: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle {that} hasteth to the prey. {swift...: or, ships of Ebeh: Heb. ships of desire}
verses.nlt_text: It disappears like a swift papyrus boat, like an eagle swooping down on its prey.

verses.kjv_text: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort {myself}:
verses.nlt_text: If I decided to forget my complaints, to put away my sad face and be cheerful,

verses.kjv_text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
verses.nlt_text: I would still dread all the pain, for I know you will not find me innocent, O God.

verses.kjv_text: {If} I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?
verses.nlt_text: Whatever happens, I will be found guilty. So what's the use of trying?

verses.kjv_text: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;
verses.nlt_text: Even if I were to wash myself with soap and clean my hands with lye,

verses.kjv_text: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me. {abhor...: or, make me to be abhorred}
verses.nlt_text: you would plunge me into a muddy ditch, and my own filthy clothing would hate me.

verses.kjv_text: For {he is} not a man, as I {am, that} I should answer him, {and} we should come together in judgment.
verses.nlt_text: "God is not a mortal like me, so I cannot argue with him or take him to trial.

verses.kjv_text: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, {that} might lay his hand upon us both. {any...: Heb. one that should argue} {daysman: or, umpire}
verses.nlt_text: If only there were a mediator between us, someone who could bring us together.

verses.kjv_text: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:
verses.nlt_text: The mediator could make God stop beating me, and I would no longer live in terror of his punishment.

verses.kjv_text: {Then} would I speak, and not fear him; but {it is} not so with me. {it is...: Heb. I am not so with myself}
verses.nlt_text: Then I could speak to him without fear, but I cannot do that in my own strength.

verses.kjv_text: My soul is weary of my life; I will leave my complaint upon myself; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul. {weary...: or, cut off while I live}
verses.nlt_text: "I am disgusted with my life. Let me complain freely. My bitter soul must complain.

verses.kjv_text: I will say unto God, Do not condemn me; shew me wherefore thou contendest with me.
verses.nlt_text: I will say to God, 'Don't simply condemn me-- tell me the charge you are bringing against me.

verses.kjv_text: {Is it} good unto thee that thou shouldest oppress, that thou shouldest despise the work of thine hands, and shine upon the counsel of the wicked? {work: Heb. labour}
verses.nlt_text: What do you gain by oppressing me? Why do you reject me, the work of your own hands, while smiling on the schemes of the wicked?

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou eyes of flesh? or seest thou as man seeth?
verses.nlt_text: Are your eyes like those of a human? Do you see things only as people see them?

verses.kjv_text: {Are} thy days as the days of man? {are} thy years as man's days,
verses.nlt_text: Is your lifetime only as long as ours? Is your life so short

verses.kjv_text: That thou enquirest after mine iniquity, and searchest after my sin?
verses.nlt_text: that you must quickly probe for my guilt and search for my sin?

verses.kjv_text: Thou knowest that I am not wicked; and {there is} none that can deliver out of thine hand. {Thou...: Heb. It is upon thy knowledge}
verses.nlt_text: Although you know I am not guilty, no one can rescue me from your hands.

verses.kjv_text: Thine hands have made me and fashioned me together round about; yet thou dost destroy me. {have...: Heb. took pains about me}
verses.nlt_text: " 'You formed me with your hands; you made me, yet now you completely destroy me.

verses.kjv_text: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?
verses.nlt_text: Remember that you made me from dust-- will you turn me back to dust so soon?

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou not poured me out as milk, and curdled me like cheese?
verses.nlt_text: You guided my conception and formed me in the womb.

verses.kjv_text: Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh, and hast fenced me with bones and sinews. {fenced: Heb. hedged}
verses.nlt_text: You clothed me with skin and flesh, and you knit my bones and sinews together.

verses.kjv_text: Thou hast granted me life and favour, and thy visitation hath preserved my spirit.
verses.nlt_text: You gave me life and showed me your unfailing love. My life was preserved by your care.

verses.kjv_text: And these {things} hast thou hid in thine heart: I know that this {is} with thee.
verses.nlt_text: " 'Yet your real motive-- your true intent--

verses.kjv_text: If I sin, then thou markest me, and thou wilt not acquit me from mine iniquity.
verses.nlt_text: was to watch me, and if I sinned, you would not forgive my guilt.

verses.kjv_text: If I be wicked, woe unto me; and {if} I be righteous, {yet} will I not lift up my head. {I am} full of confusion; therefore see thou mine affliction;
verses.nlt_text: If I am guilty, too bad for me; and even if I'm innocent, I can't hold my head high, because I am filled with shame and misery.

verses.kjv_text: For it increaseth. Thou huntest me as a fierce lion: and again thou shewest thyself marvellous upon me.
verses.nlt_text: And if I hold my head high, you hunt me like a lion and display your awesome power against me.

verses.kjv_text: Thou renewest thy witnesses against me, and increasest thine indignation upon me; changes and war {are} against me. {witnesses: that is, plagues}
verses.nlt_text: Again and again you witness against me. You pour out your growing anger on me and bring fresh armies against me.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore then hast thou brought me forth out of the womb? Oh that I had given up the ghost, and no eye had seen me!
verses.nlt_text: " 'Why, then, did you deliver me from my mother's womb? Why didn't you let me die at birth?

verses.kjv_text: I should have been as though I had not been; I should have been carried from the womb to the grave.
verses.nlt_text: It would be as though I had never existed, going directly from the womb to the grave.

verses.kjv_text: {Are} not my days few? cease {then, and} let me alone, that I may take comfort a little,
verses.nlt_text: I have only a few days left, so leave me alone, that I may have a moment of comfort

verses.kjv_text: Before I go {whence} I shall not return, {even} to the land of darkness and the shadow of death;
verses.nlt_text: before I leave-- never to return-- for the land of darkness and utter gloom.

verses.kjv_text: A land of darkness, as darkness {itself; and} of the shadow of death, without any order, and {where} the light {is} as darkness.
verses.nlt_text: It is a land as dark as midnight, a land of gloom and confusion, where even the light is dark as midnight.'"

verses.kjv_text: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Zophar the Naamathite replied to Job:

verses.kjv_text: Should not the multitude of words be answered? and should a man full of talk be justified? {full...: Heb. of lips}
verses.nlt_text: "Shouldn't someone answer this torrent of words? Is a person proved innocent just by a lot of talking?

verses.kjv_text: Should thy lies make men hold their peace? and when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed? {lies: or, devices}
verses.nlt_text: Should I remain silent while you babble on? When you mock God, shouldn't someone make you ashamed?

verses.kjv_text: For thou hast said, My doctrine {is} pure, and I am clean in thine eyes.
verses.nlt_text: You claim, 'My beliefs are pure,' and 'I am clean in the sight of God.'

verses.kjv_text: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against thee;
verses.nlt_text: If only God would speak; if only he would tell you what he thinks!

verses.kjv_text: And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that {they are} double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee {less} than thine iniquity {deserveth}.
verses.nlt_text: If only he would tell you the secrets of wisdom, for true wisdom is not a simple matter. Listen! God is doubtless punishing you far less than you deserve!

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou by searching find out God? canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
verses.nlt_text: "Can you solve the mysteries of God? Can you discover everything about the Almighty?

verses.kjv_text: {It is} as high as heaven; what canst thou do? deeper than hell; what canst thou know? {as high...: Heb. the heights of heaven}
verses.nlt_text: Such knowledge is higher than the heavens-- and who are you? It is deeper than the underworld-- what do you know?

verses.kjv_text: The measure thereof {is} longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
verses.nlt_text: It is broader than the earth and wider than the sea.

verses.kjv_text: If he cut off, and shut up, or gather together, then who can hinder him? {cut...: or, make a change} {hinder...: Heb. turn him away?}
verses.nlt_text: If God comes and puts a person in prison or calls the court to order, who can stop him?

verses.kjv_text: For he knoweth vain men: he seeth wickedness also; will he not then consider {it}?
verses.nlt_text: For he knows those who are false, and he takes note of all their sins.

verses.kjv_text: For vain man would be wise, though man be born {like} a wild ass's colt. {vain: Heb. empty}
verses.nlt_text: An empty-headed person won't become wise any more than a wild donkey can bear a human child.

verses.kjv_text: If thou prepare thine heart, and stretch out thine hands toward him;
verses.nlt_text: "If only you would prepare your heart and lift up your hands to him in prayer!

verses.kjv_text: If iniquity {be} in thine hand, put it far away, and let not wickedness dwell in thy tabernacles.
verses.nlt_text: Get rid of your sins, and leave all iniquity behind you.

verses.kjv_text: For then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:
verses.nlt_text: Then your face will brighten with innocence. You will be strong and free of fear.

verses.kjv_text: Because thou shalt forget {thy} misery, {and} remember {it} as waters {that} pass away:
verses.nlt_text: You will forget your misery; it will be like water flowing away.

verses.kjv_text: And {thine} age shall be clearer than the noonday; thou shalt shine forth, thou shalt be as the morning. {be clearer...: Heb. arise above}
verses.nlt_text: Your life will be brighter than the noonday. Even darkness will be as bright as morning.

verses.kjv_text: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; yea, thou shalt dig {about thee, and} thou shalt take thy rest in safety.
verses.nlt_text: Having hope will give you courage. You will be protected and will rest in safety.

verses.kjv_text: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make {thee} afraid; yea, many shall make suit unto thee. {make suit...: Heb. intreat thy face}
verses.nlt_text: You will lie down unafraid, and many will look to you for help.

verses.kjv_text: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, and they shall not escape, and their hope {shall be as} the giving up of the ghost. {they shall...: Heb. flight shall perish from them} {the giving...: or, a puff of breath}
verses.nlt_text: But the wicked will be blinded. They will have no escape. Their only hope is death."

verses.kjv_text: And Job answered and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Job spoke again:

verses.kjv_text: No doubt but ye {are} the people, and wisdom shall die with you.
verses.nlt_text: "You people really know everything, don't you? And when you die, wisdom will die with you!

verses.kjv_text: But I have understanding as well as you; I {am} not inferior to you: yea, who knoweth not such things as these? {understanding: Heb. an heart} {I am...: Heb. I fall not lower than you} {who...: Heb. with whom are not such as these?}
verses.nlt_text: Well, I know a few things myself-- and you're no better than I am. Who doesn't know these things you've been saying?

verses.kjv_text: I am {as} one mocked of his neighbour, who calleth upon God, and he answereth him: the just upright {man is} laughed to scorn.
verses.nlt_text: Yet my friends laugh at me, for I call on God and expect an answer. I am a just and blameless man, yet they laugh at me.

verses.kjv_text: He that is ready to slip with {his} feet {is as} a lamp despised in the thought of him that is at ease.
verses.nlt_text: People who are at ease mock those in trouble. They give a push to people who are stumbling.

verses.kjv_text: The tabernacles of robbers prosper, and they that provoke God are secure; into whose hand God bringeth {abundantly}.
verses.nlt_text: But robbers are left in peace, and those who provoke God live in safety-- though God keeps them in his power.

verses.kjv_text: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee:
verses.nlt_text: "Just ask the animals, and they will teach you. Ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.

verses.kjv_text: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: Speak to the earth, and it will instruct you. Let the fish in the sea speak to you.

verses.kjv_text: Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this?
verses.nlt_text: For they all know that my disaster has come from the hand of the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: In whose hand {is} the soul of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind. {soul: or, life} {all...: Heb. all flesh of man}
verses.nlt_text: For the life of every living thing is in his hand, and the breath of every human being.

verses.kjv_text: Doth not the ear try words? and the mouth taste his meat? {mouth: Heb. palate}
verses.nlt_text: The ear tests the words it hears just as the mouth distinguishes between foods.

verses.kjv_text: With the ancient {is} wisdom; and in length of days understanding.
verses.nlt_text: Wisdom belongs to the aged, and understanding to the old.

verses.kjv_text: With him {is} wisdom and strength, he hath counsel and understanding. {With...: that is, With God}
verses.nlt_text: "But true wisdom and power are found in God; counsel and understanding are his.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he breaketh down, and it cannot be built again: he shutteth up a man, and there can be no opening. {up: Heb. upon}
verses.nlt_text: What he destroys cannot be rebuilt. When he puts someone in prison, there is no escape.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he withholdeth the waters, and they dry up: also he sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth.
verses.nlt_text: If he holds back the rain, the earth becomes a desert. If he releases the waters, they flood the earth.

verses.kjv_text: With him {is} strength and wisdom: the deceived and the deceiver {are} his.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, strength and wisdom are his; deceivers and deceived are both in his power.

verses.kjv_text: He leadeth counsellors away spoiled, and maketh the judges fools.
verses.nlt_text: He leads counselors away, stripped of good judgment; wise judges become fools.

verses.kjv_text: He looseth the bond of kings, and girdeth their loins with a girdle.
verses.nlt_text: He removes the royal robe of kings. They are led away with ropes around their waist.

verses.kjv_text: He leadeth princes away spoiled, and overthroweth the mighty.
verses.nlt_text: He leads priests away, stripped of status; he overthrows those with long years in power.

verses.kjv_text: He removeth away the speech of the trusty, and taketh away the understanding of the aged. {speech...: Heb. lip of the faithful}
verses.nlt_text: He silences the trusted adviser and removes the insight of the elders.

verses.kjv_text: He poureth contempt upon princes, and weakeneth the strength of the mighty. {weakeneth...: or, looseth the girdle of the strong}
verses.nlt_text: He pours disgrace upon princes and disarms the strong.

verses.kjv_text: He discovereth deep things out of darkness, and bringeth out to light the shadow of death.
verses.nlt_text: "He uncovers mysteries hidden in darkness; he brings light to the deepest gloom.

verses.kjv_text: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them: he enlargeth the nations, and straiteneth them {again}. {straiteneth: Heb. leadeth in}
verses.nlt_text: He builds up nations, and he destroys them. He expands nations, and he abandons them.

verses.kjv_text: He taketh away the heart of the chief of the people of the earth, and causeth them to wander in a wilderness {where there is} no way.
verses.nlt_text: He strips kings of understanding and leaves them wandering in a pathless wasteland.

verses.kjv_text: They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like {a} drunken {man}. {stagger: Heb. wander}
verses.nlt_text: They grope in the darkness without a light. He makes them stagger like drunkards.

verses.kjv_text: Lo, mine eye hath seen all {this}, mine ear hath heard and understood it.
verses.nlt_text: "Look, I have seen all this with my own eyes and heard it with my own ears, and now I understand.

verses.kjv_text: What ye know, {the same} do I know also: I {am} not inferior unto you.
verses.nlt_text: I know as much as you do. You are no better than I am.

verses.kjv_text: Surely I would speak to the Almighty, and I desire to reason with God.
verses.nlt_text: As for me, I would speak directly to the Almighty. I want to argue my case with God himself.

verses.kjv_text: But ye {are} forgers of lies, ye {are} all physicians of no value.
verses.nlt_text: As for you, you smear me with lies. As physicians, you are worthless quacks.

verses.kjv_text: O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom.
verses.nlt_text: If only you could be silent! That's the wisest thing you could do.

verses.kjv_text: Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
verses.nlt_text: Listen to my charge; pay attention to my arguments.

verses.kjv_text: Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?
verses.nlt_text: "Are you defending God with lies? Do you make your dishonest arguments for his sake?

verses.kjv_text: Will ye accept his person? will ye contend for God?
verses.nlt_text: Will you slant your testimony in his favor? Will you argue God's case for him?

verses.kjv_text: Is it good that he should search you out? or as one man mocketh another, do ye {so} mock him?
verses.nlt_text: What will happen when he finds out what you are doing? Can you fool him as easily as you fool people?

verses.kjv_text: He will surely reprove you, if ye do secretly accept persons.
verses.nlt_text: No, you will be in trouble with him if you secretly slant your testimony in his favor.

verses.kjv_text: Shall not his excellency make you afraid? and his dread fall upon you?
verses.nlt_text: Doesn't his majesty terrify you? Doesn't your fear of him overwhelm you?

verses.kjv_text: Your remembrances {are} like unto ashes, your bodies to bodies of clay.
verses.nlt_text: Your platitudes are as valuable as ashes. Your defense is as fragile as a clay pot.

verses.kjv_text: Hold your peace, let me alone, that I may speak, and let come on me what {will}. {Hold...: Heb. Be silent from me}
verses.nlt_text: "Be silent now and leave me alone. Let me speak, and I will face the consequences.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in mine hand?
verses.nlt_text: Yes, I will take my life in my hands and say what I really think.

verses.kjv_text: Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him: but I will maintain mine own ways before him. {maintain: Heb. prove, or, argue}
verses.nlt_text: God might kill me, but I have no other hope. I am going to argue my case with him.

verses.kjv_text: He also {shall be} my salvation: for an hypocrite shall not come before him.
verses.nlt_text: But this is what will save me-- I am not godless. If I were, I could not stand before him.

verses.kjv_text: Hear diligently my speech, and my declaration with your ears.
verses.nlt_text: "Listen closely to what I am about to say. Hear me out.

verses.kjv_text: Behold now, I have ordered {my} cause; I know that I shall be justified.
verses.nlt_text: I have prepared my case; I will be proved innocent.

verses.kjv_text: Who {is} he {that} will plead with me? for now, if I hold my tongue, I shall give up the ghost.
verses.nlt_text: Who can argue with me over this? And if you prove me wrong, I will remain silent and die.

verses.kjv_text: Only do not two {things} unto me: then will I not hide myself from thee.
verses.nlt_text: "O God, grant me these two things, and then I will be able to face you.

verses.kjv_text: Withdraw thine hand far from me: and let not thy dread make me afraid.
verses.nlt_text: Remove your heavy hand from me, and don't terrify me with your awesome presence.

verses.kjv_text: Then call thou, and I will answer: or let me speak, and answer thou me.
verses.nlt_text: Now summon me, and I will answer! Or let me speak to you, and you reply.

verses.kjv_text: How many {are} mine iniquities and sins? make me to know my transgression and my sin.
verses.nlt_text: Tell me, what have I done wrong? Show me my rebellion and my sin.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and holdest me for thine enemy?
verses.nlt_text: Why do you turn away from me? Why do you treat me as your enemy?

verses.kjv_text: Wilt thou break a leaf driven to and fro? and wilt thou pursue the dry stubble?
verses.nlt_text: Would you terrify a leaf blown by the wind? Would you chase dry straw?

verses.kjv_text: For thou writest bitter things against me, and makest me to possess the iniquities of my youth.
verses.nlt_text: "You write bitter accusations against me and bring up all the sins of my youth.

verses.kjv_text: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks, and lookest narrowly unto all my paths; thou settest a print upon the heels of my feet. {lookest...: Heb. observest} {heels: Heb. roots}
verses.nlt_text: You put my feet in stocks. You examine all my paths. You trace all my footprints.

verses.kjv_text: And he, as a rotten thing, consumeth, as a garment that is moth eaten.
verses.nlt_text: I waste away like rotting wood, like a moth-eaten coat.

verses.kjv_text: Man {that is} born of a woman {is} of few days, and full of trouble. {few...: Heb. short of days}
verses.nlt_text: "How frail is humanity! How short is life, how full of trouble!

verses.kjv_text: He cometh forth like a flower, and is cut down: he fleeth also as a shadow, and continueth not.
verses.nlt_text: We blossom like a flower and then wither. Like a passing shadow, we quickly disappear.

verses.kjv_text: And dost thou open thine eyes upon such an one, and bringest me into judgment with thee?
verses.nlt_text: Must you keep an eye on such a frail creature and demand an accounting from me?

verses.kjv_text: Who can bring a clean {thing} out of an unclean? not one. {can...: Heb. will give}
verses.nlt_text: Who can bring purity out of an impure person? No one!

verses.kjv_text: Seeing his days {are} determined, the number of his months {are} with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;
verses.nlt_text: You have decided the length of our lives. You know how many months we will live, and we are not given a minute longer.

verses.kjv_text: Turn from him, that he may rest, till he shall accomplish, as an hireling, his day. {rest: Heb. cease}
verses.nlt_text: So leave us alone and let us rest! We are like hired hands, so let us finish our work in peace.

verses.kjv_text: For there is hope of a tree, if it be cut down, that it will sprout again, and that the tender branch thereof will not cease.
verses.nlt_text: "Even a tree has more hope! If it is cut down, it will sprout again and grow new branches.

verses.kjv_text: Though the root thereof wax old in the earth, and the stock thereof die in the ground;
verses.nlt_text: Though its roots have grown old in the earth and its stump decays,

verses.kjv_text: {Yet} through the scent of water it will bud, and bring forth boughs like a plant.
verses.nlt_text: at the scent of water it will bud and sprout again like a new seedling.

verses.kjv_text: But man dieth, and wasteth away: yea, man giveth up the ghost, and where {is} he? {wasteth...: Heb. is weakened, or, cut off}
verses.nlt_text: "But when people die, their strength is gone. They breathe their last, and then where are they?

verses.kjv_text: {As} the waters fail from the sea, and the flood decayeth and drieth up:
verses.nlt_text: As water evaporates from a lake and a river disappears in drought,

verses.kjv_text: So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens {be} no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep.
verses.nlt_text: people are laid to rest and do not rise again. Until the heavens are no more, they will not wake up nor be roused from their sleep.

verses.kjv_text: O that thou wouldest hide me in the grave, that thou wouldest keep me secret, until thy wrath be past, that thou wouldest appoint me a set time, and remember me!
verses.nlt_text: "I wish you would hide me in the grave and forget me there until your anger has passed. But mark your calendar to think of me again!

verses.kjv_text: If a man die, shall he live {again}? all the days of my appointed time will I wait, till my change come.
verses.nlt_text: Can the dead live again? If so, this would give me hope through all my years of struggle, and I would eagerly await the release of death.

verses.kjv_text: Thou shalt call, and I will answer thee: thou wilt have a desire to the work of thine hands.
verses.nlt_text: You would call and I would answer, and you would yearn for me, your handiwork.

verses.kjv_text: For now thou numberest my steps: dost thou not watch over my sin?
verses.nlt_text: For then you would guard my steps, instead of watching for my sins.

verses.kjv_text: My transgression {is} sealed up in a bag, and thou sewest up mine iniquity.
verses.nlt_text: My sins would be sealed in a pouch, and you would cover my guilt.

verses.kjv_text: And surely the mountain falling cometh to nought, and the rock is removed out of his place. {cometh...: Heb. fadeth}
verses.nlt_text: "But instead, as mountains fall and crumble and as rocks fall from a cliff,

verses.kjv_text: The waters wear the stones: thou washest away the things which grow {out} of the dust of the earth; and thou destroyest the hope of man. {washest...: Heb. overflowest}
verses.nlt_text: as water wears away the stones and floods wash away the soil, so you destroy people's hope.

verses.kjv_text: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth: thou changest his countenance, and sendest him away.
verses.nlt_text: You always overpower them, and they pass from the scene. You disfigure them in death and send them away.

verses.kjv_text: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth {it} not; and they are brought low, but he perceiveth {it} not of them.
verses.nlt_text: They never know if their children grow up in honor or sink to insignificance.

verses.kjv_text: But his flesh upon him shall have pain, and his soul within him shall mourn.
verses.nlt_text: They suffer painfully; their life is full of trouble."

verses.kjv_text: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:

verses.kjv_text: Should a wise man utter vain knowledge, and fill his belly with the east wind? {vain...: Heb. knowledge of wind}
verses.nlt_text: "A wise man wouldn't answer with such empty talk! You are nothing but a windbag.

verses.kjv_text: Should he reason with unprofitable talk? or with speeches wherewith he can do no good?
verses.nlt_text: The wise don't engage in empty chatter. What good are such words?

verses.kjv_text: Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God. {castest...: Heb. makest void} {prayer: or, speech}
verses.nlt_text: Have you no fear of God, no reverence for him?

verses.kjv_text: For thy mouth uttereth thine iniquity, and thou choosest the tongue of the crafty. {uttereth: Heb. teacheth}
verses.nlt_text: Your sins are telling your mouth what to say. Your words are based on clever deception.

verses.kjv_text: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I: yea, thine own lips testify against thee.
verses.nlt_text: Your own mouth condemns you, not I. Your own lips testify against you.

verses.kjv_text: {Art} thou the first man {that} was born? or wast thou made before the hills?
verses.nlt_text: "Were you the first person ever born? Were you born before the hills were made?

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou heard the secret of God? and dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself?
verses.nlt_text: Were you listening at God's secret council? Do you have a monopoly on wisdom?

verses.kjv_text: What knowest thou, that we know not? {what} understandest thou, which {is} not in us?
verses.nlt_text: What do you know that we don't? What do you understand that we do not?

verses.kjv_text: With us {are} both the grayheaded and very aged men, much elder than thy father.
verses.nlt_text: On our side are aged, gray-haired men much older than your father!

verses.kjv_text: {Are} the consolations of God small with thee? is there any secret thing with thee?
verses.nlt_text: "Is God's comfort too little for you? Is his gentle word not enough?

verses.kjv_text: Why doth thine heart carry thee away? and what do thy eyes wink at,
verses.nlt_text: What has taken away your reason? What has weakened your vision,

verses.kjv_text: That thou turnest thy spirit against God, and lettest {such} words go out of thy mouth?
verses.nlt_text: that you turn against God and say all these evil things?

verses.kjv_text: What {is} man, that he should be clean? and {he which is} born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
verses.nlt_text: Can any mortal be pure? Can anyone born of a woman be just?

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he putteth no trust in his saints; yea, the heavens are not clean in his sight.
verses.nlt_text: Look, God does not even trust the angels. Even the heavens are not absolutely pure in his sight.

verses.kjv_text: How much more abominable and filthy {is} man, which drinketh iniquity like water?
verses.nlt_text: How much less pure is a corrupt and sinful person with a thirst for wickedness!

verses.kjv_text: I will shew thee, hear me; and that {which} I have seen I will declare;
verses.nlt_text: "If you will listen, I will show you. I will answer you from my own experience.

verses.kjv_text: Which wise men have told from their fathers, and have not hid {it}:
verses.nlt_text: And it is confirmed by the reports of wise men who have heard the same thing from their fathers--

verses.kjv_text: Unto whom alone the earth was given, and no stranger passed among them.
verses.nlt_text: from those to whom the land was given long before any foreigners arrived.

verses.kjv_text: The wicked man travaileth with pain all {his} days, and the number of years is hidden to the oppressor.
verses.nlt_text: "The wicked writhe in pain throughout their lives. Years of trouble are stored up for the ruthless.

verses.kjv_text: A dreadful sound {is} in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. {A dreadful...: Heb. A sound of fears}
verses.nlt_text: The sound of terror rings in their ears, and even on good days they fear the attack of the destroyer.

verses.kjv_text: He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.
verses.nlt_text: They dare not go out into the darkness for fear they will be murdered.

verses.kjv_text: He wandereth abroad for bread, {saying}, Where {is it}? he knoweth that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
verses.nlt_text: They wander around, saying, 'Where can I find bread?' They know their day of destruction is near.

verses.kjv_text: Trouble and anguish shall make him afraid; they shall prevail against him, as a king ready to the battle.
verses.nlt_text: That dark day terrifies them. They live in distress and anguish, like a king preparing for battle.

verses.kjv_text: For he stretcheth out his hand against God, and strengtheneth himself against the Almighty.
verses.nlt_text: For they shake their fists at God, defying the Almighty.

verses.kjv_text: He runneth upon him, {even} on {his} neck, upon the thick bosses of his bucklers:
verses.nlt_text: Holding their strong shields, they defiantly charge against him.

verses.kjv_text: Because he covereth his face with his fatness, and maketh collops of fat on {his} flanks.
verses.nlt_text: "These wicked people are heavy and prosperous; their waists bulge with fat.

verses.kjv_text: And he dwelleth in desolate cities, {and} in houses which no man inhabiteth, which are ready to become heaps.
verses.nlt_text: But their cities will be ruined. They will live in abandoned houses that are ready to tumble down.

verses.kjv_text: He shall not be rich, neither shall his substance continue, neither shall he prolong the perfection thereof upon the earth.
verses.nlt_text: Their riches will not last, and their wealth will not endure. Their possessions will no longer spread across the horizon.

verses.kjv_text: He shall not depart out of darkness; the flame shall dry up his branches, and by the breath of his mouth shall he go away.
verses.nlt_text: "They will not escape the darkness. The burning sun will wither their shoots, and the breath of God will destroy them.

verses.kjv_text: Let not him that is deceived trust in vanity: for vanity shall be his recompence.
verses.nlt_text: Let them no longer fool themselves by trusting in empty riches, for emptiness will be their only reward.

verses.kjv_text: It shall be accomplished before his time, and his branch shall not be green. {accomplished: or, cut off}
verses.nlt_text: Like trees, they will be cut down in the prime of life; their branches will never again be green.

verses.kjv_text: He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive.
verses.nlt_text: They will be like a vine whose grapes are harvested too early, like an olive tree that loses its blossoms before the fruit can form.

verses.kjv_text: For the congregation of hypocrites {shall be} desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.
verses.nlt_text: For the godless are barren. Their homes, enriched through bribery, will burn.

verses.kjv_text: They conceive mischief, and bring forth vanity, and their belly prepareth deceit. {vanity: or, iniquity}
verses.nlt_text: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil. Their womb produces deceit."

verses.kjv_text: Then Job answered and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Job spoke again:

verses.kjv_text: I have heard many such things: miserable comforters {are} ye all. {miserable: or, troublesome}
verses.nlt_text: "I have heard all this before. What miserable comforters you are!

verses.kjv_text: Shall vain words have an end? or what emboldeneth thee that thou answerest? {vain...: Heb. words of wind}
verses.nlt_text: Won't you ever stop blowing hot air? What makes you keep on talking?

verses.kjv_text: I also could speak as ye {do}: if your soul were in my soul's stead, I could heap up words against you, and shake mine head at you.
verses.nlt_text: I could say the same things if you were in my place. I could spout off criticism and shake my head at you.

verses.kjv_text: {But} I would strengthen you with my mouth, and the moving of my lips should asswage {your grief}.
verses.nlt_text: But if it were me, I would encourage you. I would try to take away your grief.

verses.kjv_text: Though I speak, my grief is not asswaged: and {though} I forbear, what am I eased? {what...: Heb. what goeth from me?}
