verses.nlt_text: "My servants have never said, 'He let others go hungry.'

verses.kjv_text: The stranger did not lodge in the street: {but} I opened my doors to the traveller. {traveller: or, way}
verses.nlt_text: I have never turned away a stranger but have opened my doors to everyone.

verses.kjv_text: If I covered my transgressions as Adam, by hiding mine iniquity in my bosom: {as Adam: or, after the manner of men}
verses.nlt_text: "Have I tried to hide my sins like other people do, concealing my guilt in my heart?

verses.kjv_text: Did I fear a great multitude, or did the contempt of families terrify me, that I kept silence, {and} went not out of the door?
verses.nlt_text: Have I feared the crowd or the contempt of the masses, so that I kept quiet and stayed indoors?

verses.kjv_text: Oh that one would hear me! behold, my desire {is, that} the Almighty would answer me, and {that} mine adversary had written a book. {my...: or, my sign is that the Almighty will}
verses.nlt_text: "If only someone would listen to me! Look, I will sign my name to my defense. Let the Almighty answer me. Let my accuser write out the charges against me.

verses.kjv_text: Surely I would take it upon my shoulder, {and} bind it {as} a crown to me.
verses.nlt_text: I would face the accusation proudly. I would wear it like a crown.

verses.kjv_text: I would declare unto him the number of my steps; as a prince would I go near unto him.
verses.nlt_text: For I would tell him exactly what I have done. I would come before him like a prince.

verses.kjv_text: If my land cry against me, or that the furrows likewise thereof complain; {complain: Heb. weep}
verses.nlt_text: "If my land accuses me and all its furrows cry out together,

verses.kjv_text: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money, or have caused the owners thereof to lose their life: {fruits: Heb. strength} {the owners...: Heb. the soul of the owners thereof to expire, or, breathe out}
verses.nlt_text: or if I have stolen its crops or murdered its owners,

verses.kjv_text: Let thistles grow instead of wheat, and cockle instead of barley. The words of Job are ended. {cockle: or, noisome weeds}
verses.nlt_text: then let thistles grow on that land instead of wheat, and weeds instead of barley." Job's words are ended.

verses.kjv_text: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he {was} righteous in his own eyes. {to...: Heb. from answering}
verses.nlt_text: Job's three friends refused to reply further to him because he kept insisting on his innocence.

verses.kjv_text: Then was kindled the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram: against Job was his wrath kindled, because he justified himself rather than God. {himself: Heb. his soul}
verses.nlt_text: Then Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, of the clan of Ram, became angry. He was angry because Job refused to admit that he had sinned and that God was right in punishing him.

verses.kjv_text: Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and {yet} had condemned Job.
verses.nlt_text: He was also angry with Job's three friends, for they made God appear to be wrong by their inability to answer Job's arguments.

verses.kjv_text: Now Elihu had waited till Job had spoken, because they {were} elder than he. {waited...: Heb. expected Job in words} {elder: Heb. elder for days}
verses.nlt_text: Elihu had waited for the others to speak to Job because they were older than he.

verses.kjv_text: When Elihu saw that {there was} no answer in the mouth of {these} three men, then his wrath was kindled.
verses.nlt_text: But when he saw that they had no further reply, he spoke out angrily.

verses.kjv_text: And Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered and said, I {am} young, and ye {are} very old; wherefore I was afraid, and durst not shew you mine opinion. {young: Heb. few of days} {durst...: Heb. feared}
verses.nlt_text: Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite said, "I am young and you are old, so I held back from telling you what I think.

verses.kjv_text: I said, Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.
verses.nlt_text: I thought, 'Those who are older should speak, for wisdom comes with age.'

verses.kjv_text: But {there is} a spirit in man: and the inspiration of the Almighty giveth them understanding.
verses.nlt_text: But there is a spirit within people, the breath of the Almighty within them, that makes them intelligent.

verses.kjv_text: Great men are not {always} wise: neither do the aged understand judgment.
verses.nlt_text: Sometimes the elders are not wise. Sometimes the aged do not understand justice.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore I said, Hearken to me; I also will shew mine opinion.
verses.nlt_text: So listen to me, and let me tell you what I think.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, I waited for your words; I gave ear to your reasons, whilst ye searched out what to say. {reasons: Heb. understandings} {what...: Heb. words}
verses.nlt_text: "I have waited all this time, listening very carefully to your arguments, listening to you grope for words.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, I attended unto you, and, behold, {there was} none of you that convinced Job, {or} that answered his words:
verses.nlt_text: I have listened, but not one of you has refuted Job or answered his arguments.

verses.kjv_text: Lest ye should say, We have found out wisdom: God thrusteth him down, not man.
verses.nlt_text: And don't tell me, 'He is too wise for us. Only God can convince him.'

verses.kjv_text: Now he hath not directed {his} words against me: neither will I answer him with your speeches. {directed: or, ordered}
verses.nlt_text: If Job had been arguing with me, I would not answer with your kind of logic!

verses.kjv_text: They were amazed, they answered no more: they left off speaking. {left...: Heb. removed speeches from themselves}
verses.nlt_text: You sit there baffled, with nothing more to say.

verses.kjv_text: When I had waited, (for they spake not, but stood still, {and} answered no more;)
verses.nlt_text: Should I continue to wait, now that you are silent? Must I also remain silent?

verses.kjv_text: {I said}, I will answer also my part, I also will shew mine opinion.
verses.nlt_text: No, I will say my piece. I will speak my mind.

verses.kjv_text: For I am full of matter, the spirit within me constraineth me. {matter: Heb. words} {spirit...: Heb. spirit of my belly}
verses.nlt_text: For I am full of pent-up words, and the spirit within me urges me on.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, my belly {is} as wine {which} hath no vent; it is ready to burst like new bottles. {hath...: Heb. is not opened}
verses.nlt_text: I am like a cask of wine without a vent, like a new wineskin ready to burst!

verses.kjv_text: I will speak, that I may be refreshed: I will open my lips and answer. {be...: Heb. breathe}
verses.nlt_text: I must speak to find relief, so let me give my answers.

verses.kjv_text: Let me not, I pray you, accept any man's person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.
verses.nlt_text: I won't play favorites or try to flatter anyone.

verses.kjv_text: For I know not to give flattering titles; {in so doing} my maker would soon take me away.
verses.nlt_text: For if I tried flattery, my Creator would soon destroy me.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore, Job, I pray thee, hear my speeches, and hearken to all my words.
verses.nlt_text: "Listen to my words, Job; pay attention to what I have to say.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, now I have opened my mouth, my tongue hath spoken in my mouth. {in my mouth: Heb. in my palate}
verses.nlt_text: Now that I have begun to speak, let me continue.

verses.kjv_text: My words {shall be of} the uprightness of my heart: and my lips shall utter knowledge clearly.
verses.nlt_text: I speak with all sincerity; I speak the truth.

verses.kjv_text: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
verses.nlt_text: For the Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

verses.kjv_text: If thou canst answer me, set {thy words} in order before me, stand up.
verses.nlt_text: Answer me, if you can; make your case and take your stand.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, I {am} according to thy wish in God's stead: I also am formed out of the clay. {wish: Heb. mouth} {formed: Heb. cut}
verses.nlt_text: Look, you and I both belong to God. I, too, was formed from clay.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, my terror shall not make thee afraid, neither shall my hand be heavy upon thee.
verses.nlt_text: So you don't need to be afraid of me. I won't come down hard on you.

verses.kjv_text: Surely thou hast spoken in mine hearing, and I have heard the voice of {thy} words, {saying}, {hearing: Heb. ears}
verses.nlt_text: "You have spoken in my hearing, and I have heard your very words.

verses.kjv_text: I am clean without transgression, I {am} innocent; neither {is there} iniquity in me.
verses.nlt_text: You said, 'I am pure; I am without sin; I am innocent; I have no guilt.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he findeth occasions against me, he counteth me for his enemy,
verses.nlt_text: God is picking a quarrel with me, and he considers me his enemy.

verses.kjv_text: He putteth my feet in the stocks, he marketh all my paths.
verses.nlt_text: He puts my feet in the stocks and watches my every move.'

verses.kjv_text: Behold, {in} this thou art not just: I will answer thee, that God is greater than man.
verses.nlt_text: "But you are wrong, and I will show you why. For God is greater than any human being.

verses.kjv_text: Why dost thou strive against him? for he giveth not account of any of his matters. {he giveth...: Heb. he answereth not}
verses.nlt_text: So why are you bringing a charge against him? Why say he does not respond to people's complaints?

verses.kjv_text: For God speaketh once, yea twice, {yet man} perceiveth it not.
verses.nlt_text: For God speaks again and again, though people do not recognize it.

verses.kjv_text: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed;
verses.nlt_text: He speaks in dreams, in visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they lie in their beds.

verses.kjv_text: Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction, {he...: Heb. he revealeth, or, uncovereth}
verses.nlt_text: He whispers in their ears and terrifies them with warnings.

verses.kjv_text: That he may withdraw man {from his} purpose, and hide pride from man. {purpose: Heb. work}
verses.nlt_text: He makes them turn from doing wrong; he keeps them from pride.

verses.kjv_text: He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword. {from perishing: Heb. from passing}
verses.nlt_text: He protects them from the grave, from crossing over the river of death.

verses.kjv_text: He is chastened also with pain upon his bed, and the multitude of his bones with strong {pain}:
verses.nlt_text: "Or God disciplines people with pain on their sickbeds, with ceaseless aching in their bones.

verses.kjv_text: So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat. {dainty...: Heb. meat of desire}
verses.nlt_text: They lose their appetite for even the most delicious food.

verses.kjv_text: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen; and his bones {that} were not seen stick out.
verses.nlt_text: Their flesh wastes away, and their bones stick out.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.
verses.nlt_text: They are at death's door; the angels of death wait for them.

verses.kjv_text: If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to shew unto man his uprightness:
verses.nlt_text: "But if an angel from heaven appears-- a special messenger to intercede for a person and declare that he is upright--

verses.kjv_text: Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom. {a ransom: or, an atonement}
verses.nlt_text: he will be gracious and say, 'Rescue him from the grave, for I have found a ransom for his life.'

verses.kjv_text: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's: he shall return to the days of his youth: {a child's: Heb. childhood}
verses.nlt_text: Then his body will become as healthy as a child's, firm and youthful again.

verses.kjv_text: He shall pray unto God, and he will be favourable unto him: and he shall see his face with joy: for he will render unto man his righteousness.
verses.nlt_text: When he prays to God, he will be accepted. And God will receive him with joy and restore him to good standing.

verses.kjv_text: He looketh upon men, and {if any} say, I have sinned, and perverted {that which was} right, and it profited me not; {He...: or, He shall look upon men, and say}
verses.nlt_text: He will declare to his friends, 'I sinned and twisted the truth, but it was not worth it.

verses.kjv_text: He will deliver his soul from going into the pit, and his life shall see the light. {He...: or, He hath delivered my soul, etc, and my life}
verses.nlt_text: God rescued me from the grave, and now my life is filled with light.'

verses.kjv_text: Lo, all these {things} worketh God oftentimes with man, {oftentimes: Heb. twice and thrice}
verses.nlt_text: "Yes, God does these things again and again for people.

verses.kjv_text: To bring back his soul from the pit, to be enlightened with the light of the living.
verses.nlt_text: He rescues them from the grave so they may enjoy the light of life.

verses.kjv_text: Mark well, O Job, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I will speak.
verses.nlt_text: Mark this well, Job. Listen to me, for I have more to say.

verses.kjv_text: If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak, for I desire to justify thee.
verses.nlt_text: But if you have anything to say, go ahead. Speak, for I am anxious to see you justified.

verses.kjv_text: If not, hearken unto me: hold thy peace, and I shall teach thee wisdom.
verses.nlt_text: But if not, then listen to me. Keep silent and I will teach you wisdom!"

verses.kjv_text: Furthermore Elihu answered and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Elihu said:

verses.kjv_text: Hear my words, O ye wise {men}; and give ear unto me, ye that have knowledge.
verses.nlt_text: "Listen to me, you wise men. Pay attention, you who have knowledge.

verses.kjv_text: For the ear trieth words, as the mouth tasteth meat. {mouth: Heb. palate}
verses.nlt_text: Job said, 'The ear tests the words it hears just as the mouth distinguishes between foods.'

verses.kjv_text: Let us choose to us judgment: let us know among ourselves what {is} good.
verses.nlt_text: So let us discern for ourselves what is right; let us learn together what is good.

verses.kjv_text: For Job hath said, I am righteous: and God hath taken away my judgment.
verses.nlt_text: For Job also said, 'I am innocent, but God has taken away my rights.

verses.kjv_text: Should I lie against my right? my wound {is} incurable without transgression. {my wound: Heb. mine arrow}
verses.nlt_text: I am innocent, but they call me a liar. My suffering is incurable, though I have not sinned.'

verses.kjv_text: What man {is} like Job, {who} drinketh up scorning like water?
verses.nlt_text: "Tell me, has there ever been a man like Job, with his thirst for irreverent talk?

verses.kjv_text: Which goeth in company with the workers of iniquity, and walketh with wicked men.
verses.nlt_text: He chooses evil people as companions. He spends his time with wicked men.

verses.kjv_text: For he hath said, It profiteth a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.
verses.nlt_text: He has even said, 'Why waste time trying to please God?'

verses.kjv_text: Therefore hearken unto me, ye men of understanding: far be it from God, {that he should do} wickedness; and {from} the Almighty, {that he should commit} iniquity. {men...: Heb. men of heart}
verses.nlt_text: "Listen to me, you who have understanding. Everyone knows that God doesn't sin! The Almighty can do no wrong.

verses.kjv_text: For the work of a man shall he render unto him, and cause every man to find according to {his} ways.
verses.nlt_text: He repays people according to their deeds. He treats people as they deserve.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, surely God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert judgment.
verses.nlt_text: Truly, God will not do wrong. The Almighty will not twist justice.

verses.kjv_text: Who hath given him a charge over the earth? or who hath disposed the whole world? {the whole: Heb. all of it?}
verses.nlt_text: Did someone else put the world in his care? Who set the whole world in place?

verses.kjv_text: If he set his heart upon man, {if} he gather unto himself his spirit and his breath; {man: Heb. him}
verses.nlt_text: If God were to take back his spirit and withdraw his breath,

verses.kjv_text: All flesh shall perish together, and man shall turn again unto dust.
verses.nlt_text: all life would cease, and humanity would turn again to dust.

verses.kjv_text: If now {thou hast} understanding, hear this: hearken to the voice of my words.
verses.nlt_text: "Now listen to me if you are wise. Pay attention to what I say.

verses.kjv_text: Shall even he that hateth right govern? and wilt thou condemn him that is most just? {govern: Heb. bind?}
verses.nlt_text: Could God govern if he hated justice? Are you going to condemn the almighty judge?

verses.kjv_text: {Is it fit} to say to a king, {Thou art} wicked? {and} to princes, {Ye are} ungodly?
verses.nlt_text: For he says to kings, 'You are wicked,' and to nobles, 'You are unjust.'

verses.kjv_text: {How much less to him} that accepteth not the persons of princes, nor regardeth the rich more than the poor? for they all {are} the work of his hands.
verses.nlt_text: He doesn't care how great a person may be, and he pays no more attention to the rich than to the poor. He made them all.

verses.kjv_text: In a moment shall they die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight, and pass away: and the mighty shall be taken away without hand. {the mighty...: Heb. they shall take away the mighty}
verses.nlt_text: In a moment they die. In the middle of the night they pass away; the mighty are removed without human hand.

verses.kjv_text: For his eyes {are} upon the ways of man, and he seeth all his goings.
verses.nlt_text: "For God watches how people live; he sees everything they do.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.
verses.nlt_text: No darkness is thick enough to hide the wicked from his eyes.

verses.kjv_text: For he will not lay upon man more {than right}; that he should enter into judgment with God. {enter: Heb. go}
verses.nlt_text: We don't set the time when we will come before God in judgment.

verses.kjv_text: He shall break in pieces mighty men without number, and set others in their stead. {number: Heb. searching out}
verses.nlt_text: He brings the mighty to ruin without asking anyone, and he sets up others in their place.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore he knoweth their works, and he overturneth {them} in the night, so that they are destroyed. {destroyed: Heb. crushed}
verses.nlt_text: He knows what they do, and in the night he overturns and destroys them.

verses.kjv_text: He striketh them as wicked men in the open sight of others; {open...: Heb. place of beholders}
verses.nlt_text: He strikes them down because they are wicked, doing it openly for all to see.

verses.kjv_text: Because they turned back from him, and would not consider any of his ways: {him: Heb. after him}
verses.nlt_text: For they turned away from following him. They have no respect for any of his ways.

verses.kjv_text: So that they cause the cry of the poor to come unto him, and he heareth the cry of the afflicted.
verses.nlt_text: They cause the poor to cry out, catching God's attention. He hears the cries of the needy.

verses.kjv_text: When he giveth quietness, who then can make trouble? and when he hideth {his} face, who then can behold him? whether {it be done} against a nation, or against a man only:
verses.nlt_text: But if he chooses to remain quiet, who can criticize him? When he hides his face, no one can find him, whether an individual or a nation.

verses.kjv_text: That the hypocrite reign not, lest the people be ensnared.
verses.nlt_text: He prevents the godless from ruling so they cannot be a snare to the people.

verses.kjv_text: Surely it is meet to be said unto God, I have borne {chastisement}, I will not offend {any more}:
verses.nlt_text: "Why don't people say to God, 'I have sinned, but I will sin no more'?

verses.kjv_text: {That which} I see not teach thou me: if I have done iniquity, I will do no more.
verses.nlt_text: Or 'I don't know what evil I have done-- tell me. If I have done wrong, I will stop at once'?

verses.kjv_text: {Should it be} according to thy mind? he will recompense it, whether thou refuse, or whether thou choose; and not I: therefore speak what thou knowest. {according...: Heb. from with thee?}
verses.nlt_text: "Must God tailor his justice to your demands? But you have rejected him! The choice is yours, not mine. Go ahead, share your wisdom with us.

verses.kjv_text: Let men of understanding tell me, and let a wise man hearken unto me. {of...: Heb. of heart}
verses.nlt_text: After all, bright people will tell me, and wise people will hear me say,

verses.kjv_text: Job hath spoken without knowledge, and his words {were} without wisdom.
verses.nlt_text: 'Job speaks out of ignorance; his words lack insight.'

verses.kjv_text: My desire {is that} Job may be tried unto the end because of {his} answers for wicked men. {My...: or, My father, let Job be tried}
verses.nlt_text: Job, you deserve the maximum penalty for the wicked way you have talked.

verses.kjv_text: For he addeth rebellion unto his sin, he clappeth {his hands} among us, and multiplieth his words against God.
verses.nlt_text: For you have added rebellion to your sin; you show no respect, and you speak many angry words against God."

verses.kjv_text: Elihu spake moreover, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Elihu said:

verses.kjv_text: Thinkest thou this to be right, {that} thou saidst, My righteousness {is} more than God's?
verses.nlt_text: "Do you think it is right for you to claim, 'I am righteous before God'?

verses.kjv_text: For thou saidst, What advantage will it be unto thee? {and}, What profit shall I have, {if I be cleansed} from my sin? {if...: or, by it more than by my sin}
verses.nlt_text: For you also ask, 'What's in it for me? What's the use of living a righteous life?'

verses.kjv_text: I will answer thee, and thy companions with thee. {answer...: Heb. return to thee words}
verses.nlt_text: "I will answer you and all your friends, too.

verses.kjv_text: Look unto the heavens, and see; and behold the clouds {which} are higher than thou.
verses.nlt_text: Look up into the sky, and see the clouds high above you.

verses.kjv_text: If thou sinnest, what doest thou against him? or {if} thy transgressions be multiplied, what doest thou unto him?
verses.nlt_text: If you sin, how does that affect God? Even if you sin again and again, what effect will it have on him?

verses.kjv_text: If thou be righteous, what givest thou him? or what receiveth he of thine hand?
verses.nlt_text: If you are good, is this some great gift to him? What could you possibly give him?

verses.kjv_text: Thy wickedness {may hurt} a man as thou {art}; and thy righteousness {may profit} the son of man.
verses.nlt_text: No, your sins affect only people like yourself, and your good deeds also affect only humans.

verses.kjv_text: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make {the oppressed} to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.
verses.nlt_text: "People cry out when they are oppressed. They groan beneath the power of the mighty.

verses.kjv_text: But none saith, Where {is} God my maker, who giveth songs in the night;
verses.nlt_text: Yet they don't ask, 'Where is God my Creator, the one who gives songs in the night?

verses.kjv_text: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth, and maketh us wiser than the fowls of heaven?
verses.nlt_text: Where is the one who makes us smarter than the animals and wiser than the birds of the sky?'

verses.kjv_text: There they cry, but none giveth answer, because of the pride of evil men.
verses.nlt_text: And when they cry out, God does not answer because of their pride.

verses.kjv_text: Surely God will not hear vanity, neither will the Almighty regard it.
verses.nlt_text: But it is wrong to say God doesn't listen, to say the Almighty isn't concerned.

verses.kjv_text: Although thou sayest thou shalt not see him, {yet} judgment {is} before him; therefore trust thou in him.
verses.nlt_text: You say you can't see him, but he will bring justice if you will only wait.

verses.kjv_text: But now, because {it is} not {so}, he hath visited in his anger; yet he knoweth {it} not in great extremity: {he hath: that is, God hath} {he knoweth: that is, Job knoweth}
verses.nlt_text: You say he does not respond to sinners with anger and is not greatly concerned about wickedness.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore doth Job open his mouth in vain; he multiplieth words without knowledge.
verses.nlt_text: But you are talking nonsense, Job. You have spoken like a fool."

verses.kjv_text: Elihu also proceeded, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Elihu continued speaking:

verses.kjv_text: Suffer me a little, and I will shew thee that {I have} yet to speak on God's behalf. {I have...: Heb. there are yet words for God}
verses.nlt_text: "Let me go on, and I will show you the truth. For I have not finished defending God!

verses.kjv_text: I will fetch my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
verses.nlt_text: I will present profound arguments for the righteousness of my Creator.

verses.kjv_text: For truly my words {shall} not {be} false: he that is perfect in knowledge {is} with thee.
verses.nlt_text: I am telling you nothing but the truth, for I am a man of great knowledge.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, God {is} mighty, and despiseth not {any: he is} mighty in strength {and} wisdom. {wisdom: Heb. heart}
verses.nlt_text: "God is mighty, but he does not despise anyone! He is mighty in both power and understanding.

verses.kjv_text: He preserveth not the life of the wicked: but giveth right to the poor. {poor: or, afflicted}
verses.nlt_text: He does not let the wicked live but gives justice to the afflicted.

verses.kjv_text: He withdraweth not his eyes from the righteous: but with kings {are they} on the throne; yea, he doth establish them for ever, and they are exalted.
verses.nlt_text: He never takes his eyes off the innocent, but he sets them on thrones with kings and exalts them forever.

verses.kjv_text: And if {they be} bound in fetters, {and} be holden in cords of affliction;
verses.nlt_text: If they are bound in chains and caught up in a web of trouble,

verses.kjv_text: Then he sheweth them their work, and their transgressions that they have exceeded.
verses.nlt_text: he shows them the reason. He shows them their sins of pride.

verses.kjv_text: He openeth also their ear to discipline, and commandeth that they return from iniquity.
verses.nlt_text: He gets their attention and commands that they turn from evil.

verses.kjv_text: If they obey and serve {him}, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.
verses.nlt_text: "If they listen and obey God, they will be blessed with prosperity throughout their lives. All their years will be pleasant.

verses.kjv_text: But if they obey not, they shall perish by the sword, and they shall die without knowledge. {perish: Heb. pass away}
verses.nlt_text: But if they refuse to listen to him, they will be killed by the sword and die from lack of understanding.

verses.kjv_text: But the hypocrites in heart heap up wrath: they cry not when he bindeth them.
verses.nlt_text: For the godless are full of resentment. Even when he punishes them, they refuse to cry out to him for help.

verses.kjv_text: They die in youth, and their life {is} among the unclean. {They...: Heb. Their soul dieth} {unclean: or, sodomites}
verses.nlt_text: They die when they are young, after wasting their lives in immoral living.

verses.kjv_text: He delivereth the poor in his affliction, and openeth their ears in oppression. {poor: or, afflicted}
verses.nlt_text: But by means of their suffering, he rescues those who suffer. For he gets their attention through adversity.

verses.kjv_text: Even so would he have removed thee out of the strait {into} a broad place, where {there is} no straitness; and that which should be set on thy table {should be} full of fatness. {that...: Heb. the rest of thy table}
verses.nlt_text: "God is leading you away from danger, Job, to a place free from distress. He is setting your table with the best food.

verses.kjv_text: But thou hast fulfilled the judgment of the wicked: judgment and justice take hold {on thee}. {take...: or, should uphold thee}
verses.nlt_text: But you are obsessed with whether the godless will be judged. Don't worry, judgment and justice will be upheld.

verses.kjv_text: Because {there is} wrath, {beware} lest he take thee away with {his} stroke: then a great ransom cannot deliver thee. {deliver...: Heb. turn thee aside}
verses.nlt_text: But watch out, or you may be seduced by wealth. Don't let yourself be bribed into sin.

verses.kjv_text: Will he esteem thy riches? {no}, not gold, nor all the forces of strength.
verses.nlt_text: Could all your wealth or all your mighty efforts keep you from distress?

verses.kjv_text: Desire not the night, when people are cut off in their place.
verses.nlt_text: Do not long for the cover of night, for that is when people will be destroyed.

verses.kjv_text: Take heed, regard not iniquity: for this hast thou chosen rather than affliction.
verses.nlt_text: Be on guard! Turn back from evil, for God sent this suffering to keep you from a life of evil.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, God exalteth by his power: who teacheth like him?
verses.nlt_text: "Look, God is all-powerful. Who is a teacher like him?

verses.kjv_text: Who hath enjoined him his way? or who can say, Thou hast wrought iniquity?
verses.nlt_text: No one can tell him what to do, or say to him, 'You have done wrong.'

verses.kjv_text: Remember that thou magnify his work, which men behold.
verses.nlt_text: Instead, glorify his mighty works, singing songs of praise.

verses.kjv_text: Every man may see it; man may behold {it} afar off.
verses.nlt_text: Everyone has seen these things, though only from a distance.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, God {is} great, and we know {him} not, neither can the number of his years be searched out.
verses.nlt_text: "Look, God is greater than we can understand. His years cannot be counted.

verses.kjv_text: For he maketh small the drops of water: they pour down rain according to the vapour thereof:
verses.nlt_text: He draws up the water vapor and then distills it into rain.

verses.kjv_text: Which the clouds do drop {and} distil upon man abundantly.
verses.nlt_text: The rain pours down from the clouds, and everyone benefits.

verses.kjv_text: Also can {any} understand the spreadings of the clouds, {or} the noise of his tabernacle?
verses.nlt_text: Who can understand the spreading of the clouds and the thunder that rolls forth from heaven?

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he spreadeth his light upon it, and covereth the bottom of the sea. {bottom: Heb. roots}
verses.nlt_text: See how he spreads the lightning around him and how it lights up the depths of the sea.

verses.kjv_text: For by them judgeth he the people; he giveth meat in abundance.
verses.nlt_text: By these mighty acts he nourishes the people, giving them food in abundance.

verses.kjv_text: With clouds he covereth the light; and commandeth it {not to shine} by {the cloud} that cometh betwixt.
verses.nlt_text: He fills his hands with lightning bolts and hurls each at its target.

verses.kjv_text: The noise thereof sheweth concerning it, the cattle also concerning the vapour. {the vapour: Heb. that which goeth up}
verses.nlt_text: The thunder announces his presence; the storm announces his indignant anger.

verses.kjv_text: At this also my heart trembleth, and is moved out of his place.
verses.nlt_text: "My heart pounds as I think of this. It trembles within me.

verses.kjv_text: Hear attentively the noise of his voice, and the sound {that} goeth out of his mouth. {Hear...: Heb. Hear in hearing}
verses.nlt_text: Listen carefully to the thunder of God's voice as it rolls from his mouth.

verses.kjv_text: He directeth it under the whole heaven, and his lightning unto the ends of the earth. {lightning: Heb. light} {ends: Heb. wings}
verses.nlt_text: It rolls across the heavens, and his lightning flashes in every direction.

verses.kjv_text: After it a voice roareth: he thundereth with the voice of his excellency; and he will not stay them when his voice is heard.
verses.nlt_text: Then comes the roaring of the thunder-- the tremendous voice of his majesty. He does not restrain it when he speaks.

verses.kjv_text: God thundereth marvellously with his voice; great things doeth he, which we cannot comprehend.
verses.nlt_text: God's voice is glorious in the thunder. We can't even imagine the greatness of his power.

verses.kjv_text: For he saith to the snow, Be thou {on} the earth; likewise to the small rain, and to the great rain of his strength. {likewise...: Heb. and to the shower of rain, and to the showers of rain of his strength}
verses.nlt_text: "He directs the snow to fall on the earth and tells the rain to pour down.

verses.kjv_text: He sealeth up the hand of every man; that all men may know his work.
verses.nlt_text: Then everyone stops working so they can watch his power.

verses.kjv_text: Then the beasts go into dens, and remain in their places.
verses.nlt_text: The wild animals take cover and stay inside their dens.

verses.kjv_text: Out of the south cometh the whirlwind: and cold out of the north. {south: Heb. chamber} {north: Heb. scattering winds}
verses.nlt_text: The stormy wind comes from its chamber, and the driving winds bring the cold.

verses.kjv_text: By the breath of God frost is given: and the breadth of the waters is straitened.
verses.nlt_text: God's breath sends the ice, freezing wide expanses of water.

verses.kjv_text: Also by watering he wearieth the thick cloud: he scattereth his bright cloud: {his...: Heb. the cloud of his light}
verses.nlt_text: He loads the clouds with moisture, and they flash with his lightning.

verses.kjv_text: And it is turned round about by his counsels: that they may do whatsoever he commandeth them upon the face of the world in the earth.
verses.nlt_text: The clouds churn about at his direction. They do whatever he commands throughout the earth.

verses.kjv_text: He causeth it to come, whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy. {correction: Heb. a rod}
verses.nlt_text: He makes these things happen either to punish people or to show his unfailing love.

verses.kjv_text: Hearken unto this, O Job: stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.
verses.nlt_text: "Pay attention to this, Job. Stop and consider the wonderful miracles of God!

verses.kjv_text: Dost thou know when God disposed them, and caused the light of his cloud to shine?
verses.nlt_text: Do you know how God controls the storm and causes the lightning to flash from his clouds?

verses.kjv_text: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him which is perfect in knowledge?
verses.nlt_text: Do you understand how he moves the clouds with wonderful perfection and skill?

verses.kjv_text: How thy garments {are} warm, when he quieteth the earth by the south {wind}?
verses.nlt_text: When you are sweltering in your clothes and the south wind dies down and everything is still,

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou with him spread out the sky, {which is} strong, {and} as a molten looking glass?
verses.nlt_text: he makes the skies reflect the heat like a bronze mirror. Can you do that?

verses.kjv_text: Teach us what we shall say unto him; {for} we cannot order {our speech} by reason of darkness.
verses.nlt_text: "So teach the rest of us what to say to God. We are too ignorant to make our own arguments.

verses.kjv_text: Shall it be told him that I speak? if a man speak, surely he shall be swallowed up.
verses.nlt_text: Should God be notified that I want to speak? Can people even speak when they are confused?

verses.kjv_text: And now {men} see not the bright light which {is} in the clouds: but the wind passeth, and cleanseth them.
verses.nlt_text: We cannot look at the sun, for it shines brightly in the sky when the wind clears away the clouds.

verses.kjv_text: Fair weather cometh out of the north: with God {is} terrible majesty. {Fair...: Heb. Gold}
verses.nlt_text: So also, golden splendor comes from the mountain of God. He is clothed in dazzling splendor.

verses.kjv_text: {Touching} the Almighty, we cannot find him out: {he is} excellent in power, and in judgment, and in plenty of justice: he will not afflict.
verses.nlt_text: We cannot imagine the power of the Almighty; but even though he is just and righteous, he does not destroy us.

verses.kjv_text: Men do therefore fear him: he respecteth not any {that are} wise of heart.
verses.nlt_text: No wonder people everywhere fear him. All who are wise show him reverence."

verses.kjv_text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind:

verses.kjv_text: Who {is} this that darkeneth counsel by words without knowledge?
verses.nlt_text: "Who is this that questions my wisdom with such ignorant words?

verses.kjv_text: Gird up now thy loins like a man; for I will demand of thee, and answer thou me. {answer...: Heb. make me know}
verses.nlt_text: Brace yourself like a man, because I have some questions for you, and you must answer them.

verses.kjv_text: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding. {hast...: Heb. knowest understanding}
verses.nlt_text: "Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you know so much.

verses.kjv_text: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest? or who hath stretched the line upon it?
verses.nlt_text: Who determined its dimensions and stretched out the surveying line?

verses.kjv_text: Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; {foundations: Heb. sockets} {fastened: Heb. made to sink?}
verses.nlt_text: What supports its foundations, and who laid its cornerstone

verses.kjv_text: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
verses.nlt_text: as the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?

verses.kjv_text: Or {who} shut up the sea with doors, when it brake forth, {as if} it had issued out of the womb?
verses.nlt_text: "Who kept the sea inside its boundaries as it burst from the womb,

verses.kjv_text: When I made the cloud the garment thereof, and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it,
verses.nlt_text: and as I clothed it with clouds and wrapped it in thick darkness?

verses.kjv_text: And brake up for it my decreed {place}, and set bars and doors, {brake...: or, established my decree upon it}
verses.nlt_text: For I locked it behind barred gates, limiting its shores.

verses.kjv_text: And said, Hitherto shalt thou come, but no further: and here shall thy proud waves be stayed? {thy...: Heb. the pride of thy waves}
verses.nlt_text: I said, 'This far and no farther will you come. Here your proud waves must stop!'

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou commanded the morning since thy days; {and} caused the dayspring to know his place;
verses.nlt_text: "Have you ever commanded the morning to appear and caused the dawn to rise in the east?

verses.kjv_text: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth, that the wicked might be shaken out of it? {ends: Heb. wings}
verses.nlt_text: Have you made daylight spread to the ends of the earth, to bring an end to the night's wickedness?

verses.kjv_text: It is turned as clay {to} the seal; and they stand as a garment.
verses.nlt_text: As the light approaches, the earth takes shape like clay pressed beneath a seal; it is robed in brilliant colors.

verses.kjv_text: And from the wicked their light is withholden, and the high arm shall be broken.
verses.nlt_text: The light disturbs the wicked and stops the arm that is raised in violence.

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou entered into the springs of the sea? or hast thou walked in the search of the depth?
verses.nlt_text: "Have you explored the springs from which the seas come? Have you explored their depths?

verses.kjv_text: Have the gates of death been opened unto thee? or hast thou seen the doors of the shadow of death?
verses.nlt_text: Do you know where the gates of death are located? Have you seen the gates of utter gloom?

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou perceived the breadth of the earth? declare if thou knowest it all.
verses.nlt_text: Do you realize the extent of the earth? Tell me about it if you know!

verses.kjv_text: Where {is} the way {where} light dwelleth? and {as for} darkness, where {is} the place thereof,
verses.nlt_text: "Where does light come from, and where does darkness go?

verses.kjv_text: That thou shouldest take it to the bound thereof, and that thou shouldest know the paths {to} the house thereof? {to the bound: or, at, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Can you take each to its home? Do you know how to get there?

verses.kjv_text: Knowest thou {it}, because thou wast then born? or {because} the number of thy days {is} great?
verses.nlt_text: But of course you know all this! For you were born before it was all created, and you are so very experienced!

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou entered into the treasures of the snow? or hast thou seen the treasures of the hail,
verses.nlt_text: "Have you visited the storehouses of the snow or seen the storehouses of hail?

verses.kjv_text: Which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?
verses.nlt_text: (I have reserved them as weapons for the time of trouble, for the day of battle and war.)

verses.kjv_text: By what way is the light parted, {which} scattereth the east wind upon the earth?
verses.nlt_text: Where is the path to the source of light? Where is the home of the east wind?

verses.kjv_text: Who hath divided a watercourse for the overflowing of waters, or a way for the lightning of thunder;
verses.nlt_text: "Who created a channel for the torrents of rain? Who laid out the path for the lightning?

verses.kjv_text: To cause it to rain on the earth, {where} no man {is; on} the wilderness, wherein {there is} no man;
verses.nlt_text: Who makes the rain fall on barren land, in a desert where no one lives?

verses.kjv_text: To satisfy the desolate and waste {ground}; and to cause the bud of the tender herb to spring forth?
verses.nlt_text: Who sends rain to satisfy the parched ground and make the tender grass spring up?

verses.kjv_text: Hath the rain a father? or who hath begotten the drops of dew?
verses.nlt_text: "Does the rain have a father? Who gives birth to the dew?

verses.kjv_text: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the hoary frost of heaven, who hath gendered it?
verses.nlt_text: Who is the mother of the ice? Who gives birth to the frost from the heavens?

verses.kjv_text: The waters are hid as {with} a stone, and the face of the deep is frozen. {is...: Heb. is taken}
verses.nlt_text: For the water turns to ice as hard as rock, and the surface of the water freezes.

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou bind the sweet influences of Pleiades, or loose the bands of Orion? {Pleiades: or, the seven stars: Heb. Cimah} {Orion: Heb. Cesil?}
verses.nlt_text: "Can you direct the movement of the stars-- binding the cluster of the Pleiades or loosening the cords of Orion?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou bring forth Mazzaroth in his season? or canst thou guide Arcturus with his sons? {Mazzaroth: or, the twelve signs} {guide: Heb. guide them}
verses.nlt_text: Can you direct the sequence of the seasons or guide the Bear with her cubs across the heavens?

verses.kjv_text: Knowest thou the ordinances of heaven? canst thou set the dominion thereof in the earth?
verses.nlt_text: Do you know the laws of the universe? Can you use them to regulate the earth?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that abundance of waters may cover thee?
verses.nlt_text: "Can you shout to the clouds and make it rain?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou send lightnings, that they may go, and say unto thee, Here we {are}? {Here...: Heb. Behold us?}
verses.nlt_text: Can you make lightning appear and cause it to strike as you direct?

verses.kjv_text: Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts? or who hath given understanding to the heart?
verses.nlt_text: Who gives intuition to the heart and instinct to the mind?

verses.kjv_text: Who can number the clouds in wisdom? or who can stay the bottles of heaven, {stay: Heb. cause to lie down}
verses.nlt_text: Who is wise enough to count all the clouds? Who can tilt the water jars of heaven

verses.kjv_text: When the dust groweth into hardness, and the clods cleave fast together? {groweth...: or, is turned into mire: Heb. is poured}
verses.nlt_text: when the parched ground is dry and the soil has hardened into clods?

verses.kjv_text: Wilt thou hunt the prey for the lion? or fill the appetite of the young lions, {the appetite: Heb. the life}
verses.nlt_text: "Can you stalk prey for a lioness and satisfy the young lions' appetites

verses.kjv_text: When they couch in {their} dens, {and} abide in the covert to lie in wait?
verses.nlt_text: as they lie in their dens or crouch in the thicket?

verses.kjv_text: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.
verses.nlt_text: Who provides food for the ravens when their young cry out to God and wander about in hunger?

verses.kjv_text: Knowest thou the time when the wild goats of the rock bring forth? {or} canst thou mark when the hinds do calve?
verses.nlt_text: "Do you know when the wild goats give birth? Have you watched as deer are born in the wild?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou number the months {that} they fulfil? or knowest thou the time when they bring forth?
verses.nlt_text: Do you know how many months they carry their young? Are you aware of the time of their delivery?

verses.kjv_text: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young ones, they cast out their sorrows.
verses.nlt_text: They crouch down to give birth to their young and deliver their offspring.

verses.kjv_text: Their young ones are in good liking, they grow up with corn; they go forth, and return not unto them.
verses.nlt_text: Their young grow up in the open fields, then leave home and never return.

verses.kjv_text: Who hath sent out the wild ass free? or who hath loosed the bands of the wild ass?
verses.nlt_text: "Who gives the wild donkey its freedom? Who untied its ropes?

verses.kjv_text: Whose house I have made the wilderness, and the barren land his dwellings. {barren...: Heb. salt places}
verses.nlt_text: I have placed it in the wilderness; its home is the wasteland.

verses.kjv_text: He scorneth the multitude of the city, neither regardeth he the crying of the driver. {of the driver: Heb. of the exactor}
verses.nlt_text: It hates the noise of the city and has no driver to shout at it.

verses.kjv_text: The range of the mountains {is} his pasture, and he searcheth after every green thing.
verses.nlt_text: The mountains are its pastureland, where it searches for every blade of grass.

verses.kjv_text: Will the unicorn be willing to serve thee, or abide by thy crib?
verses.nlt_text: "Will the wild ox consent to being tamed? Will it spend the night in your stall?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou bind the unicorn with his band in the furrow? or will he harrow the valleys after thee?
verses.nlt_text: Can you hitch a wild ox to a plow? Will it plow a field for you?

verses.kjv_text: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength {is} great? or wilt thou leave thy labour to him?
verses.nlt_text: Given its strength, can you trust it? Can you leave and trust the ox to do your work?

verses.kjv_text: Wilt thou believe him, that he will bring home thy seed, and gather {it into} thy barn?
verses.nlt_text: Can you rely on it to bring home your grain and deliver it to your threshing floor?

verses.kjv_text: {Gavest thou} the goodly wings unto the peacocks? or wings and feathers unto the ostrich? {wings and...: or, the feathers of the stork and ostrich}
verses.nlt_text: "The ostrich flaps her wings grandly, but they are no match for the feathers of the stork.

verses.kjv_text: Which leaveth her eggs in the earth, and warmeth them in dust,
verses.nlt_text: She lays her eggs on top of the earth, letting them be warmed in the dust.

verses.kjv_text: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them, or that the wild beast may break them.
verses.nlt_text: She doesn't worry that a foot might crush them or a wild animal might destroy them.

verses.kjv_text: She is hardened against her young ones, as though {they were} not hers: her labour is in vain without fear;
verses.nlt_text: She is harsh toward her young, as if they were not her own. She doesn't care if they die.

verses.kjv_text: Because God hath deprived her of wisdom, neither hath he imparted to her understanding.
verses.nlt_text: For God has deprived her of wisdom. He has given her no understanding.

verses.kjv_text: What time she lifteth up herself on high, she scorneth the horse and his rider.
verses.nlt_text: But whenever she jumps up to run, she passes the swiftest horse with its rider.

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou given the horse strength? hast thou clothed his neck with thunder?
verses.nlt_text: "Have you given the horse its strength or clothed its neck with a flowing mane?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou make him afraid as a grasshopper? the glory of his nostrils {is} terrible. {terrible: Heb. terror}
verses.nlt_text: Did you give it the ability to leap like a locust? Its majestic snorting is terrifying!

verses.kjv_text: He paweth in the valley, and rejoiceth in {his} strength: he goeth on to meet the armed men. {He paweth: or, His feet dig} {the armed...: Heb. the armour}
verses.nlt_text: It paws the earth and rejoices in its strength when it charges out to battle.

verses.kjv_text: He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted; neither turneth he back from the sword.
verses.nlt_text: It laughs at fear and is unafraid. It does not run from the sword.

verses.kjv_text: The quiver rattleth against him, the glittering spear and the shield.
verses.nlt_text: The arrows rattle against it, and the spear and javelin flash.

verses.kjv_text: He swalloweth the ground with fierceness and rage: neither believeth he that {it is} the sound of the trumpet.
verses.nlt_text: It paws the ground fiercely and rushes forward into battle when the ram's horn blows.

verses.kjv_text: He saith among the trumpets, Ha, ha; and he smelleth the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.
verses.nlt_text: It snorts at the sound of the horn. It senses the battle in the distance. It quivers at the captain's commands and the noise of battle.

verses.kjv_text: Doth the hawk fly by thy wisdom, {and} stretch her wings toward the south?
verses.nlt_text: "Is it your wisdom that makes the hawk soar and spread its wings toward the south?

verses.kjv_text: Doth the eagle mount up at thy command, and make her nest on high? {at...: Heb. by thy mouth}
verses.nlt_text: Is it at your command that the eagle rises to the heights to make its nest?

verses.kjv_text: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock, upon the crag of the rock, and the strong place.
verses.nlt_text: It lives on the cliffs, making its home on a distant, rocky crag.

verses.kjv_text: From thence she seeketh the prey, {and} her eyes behold afar off.
verses.nlt_text: From there it hunts its prey, keeping watch with piercing eyes.

verses.kjv_text: Her young ones also suck up blood: and where the slain {are}, there {is} she.
verses.nlt_text: Its young gulp down blood. Where there's a carcass, there you'll find it."

verses.kjv_text: Moreover the LORD answered Job, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD said to Job,

verses.kjv_text: Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct {him}? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.
verses.nlt_text: "Do you still want to argue with the Almighty? You are God's critic, but do you have the answers?"

verses.kjv_text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Job replied to the LORD,

verses.kjv_text: Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.
verses.nlt_text: "I am nothing-- how could I ever find the answers? I will cover my mouth with my hand.

verses.kjv_text: Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.
verses.nlt_text: I have said too much already. I have nothing more to say."

verses.kjv_text: Then answered the LORD unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then the LORD answered Job from the whirlwind:

verses.kjv_text: Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
verses.nlt_text: "Brace yourself like a man, because I have some questions for you, and you must answer them.

verses.kjv_text: Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?
verses.nlt_text: "Will you discredit my justice and condemn me just to prove you are right?

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
verses.nlt_text: Are you as strong as God? Can you thunder with a voice like his?

verses.kjv_text: Deck thyself now {with} majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.
verses.nlt_text: All right, put on your glory and splendor, your honor and majesty.

verses.kjv_text: Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one {that is} proud, and abase him.
verses.nlt_text: Give vent to your anger. Let it overflow against the proud.

verses.kjv_text: Look on every one {that is} proud, {and} bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.
verses.nlt_text: Humiliate the proud with a glance; walk on the wicked where they stand.

verses.kjv_text: Hide them in the dust together; {and} bind their faces in secret.
verses.nlt_text: Bury them in the dust. Imprison them in the world of the dead.

verses.kjv_text: Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.
verses.nlt_text: Then even I would praise you, for your own strength would save you.

verses.kjv_text: Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox. {behemoth: probably an extinct animal of some kind}
verses.nlt_text: "Take a look at Behemoth, which I made, just as I made you. It eats grass like an ox.

verses.kjv_text: Lo now, his strength {is} in his loins, and his force {is} in the navel of his belly.
verses.nlt_text: See its powerful loins and the muscles of its belly.

verses.kjv_text: He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together. {He...: or, He setteth up}
verses.nlt_text: Its tail is as strong as a cedar. The sinews of its thighs are knit tightly together.

verses.kjv_text: His bones {are as} strong pieces of brass; his bones {are} like bars of iron.
verses.nlt_text: Its bones are tubes of bronze. Its limbs are bars of iron.

verses.kjv_text: He {is} the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach {unto him}.
verses.nlt_text: It is a prime example of God's handiwork, and only its Creator can threaten it.

verses.kjv_text: Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.
verses.nlt_text: The mountains offer it their best food, where all the wild animals play.

verses.kjv_text: He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.
verses.nlt_text: It lies under the lotus plants, hidden by the reeds in the marsh.

verses.kjv_text: The shady trees cover him {with} their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.
verses.nlt_text: The lotus plants give it shade among the willows beside the stream.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, he drinketh up a river, {and} hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth. {he drinketh up: Heb. he oppresseth}
verses.nlt_text: It is not disturbed by the raging river, not concerned when the swelling Jordan rushes around it.

verses.kjv_text: He taketh it with his eyes: {his} nose pierceth through snares. {He...: or, Will any take him in his sight, or, bore his nose with a gin?}
verses.nlt_text: No one can catch it off guard or put a ring in its nose and lead it away.

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord {which} thou lettest down? {leviathan: probably an extinct animal of some kind} {which...: Heb. which thou drownest?}
verses.nlt_text: "Can you catch Leviathan with a hook or put a noose around its jaw?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou put an hook into his nose? or bore his jaw through with a thorn?
verses.nlt_text: Can you tie it with a rope through the nose or pierce its jaw with a spike?

verses.kjv_text: Will he make many supplications unto thee? will he speak soft {words} unto thee?
verses.nlt_text: Will it beg you for mercy or implore you for pity?

verses.kjv_text: Will he make a covenant with thee? wilt thou take him for a servant for ever?
verses.nlt_text: Will it agree to work for you, to be your slave for life?

verses.kjv_text: Wilt thou play with him as {with} a bird? or wilt thou bind him for thy maidens?
verses.nlt_text: Can you make it a pet like a bird, or give it to your little girls to play with?

verses.kjv_text: Shall the companions make a banquet of him? shall they part him among the merchants?
verses.nlt_text: Will merchants try to buy it to sell it in their shops?

verses.kjv_text: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons? or his head with fish spears?
verses.nlt_text: Will its hide be hurt by spears or its head by a harpoon?

verses.kjv_text: Lay thine hand upon him, remember the battle, do no more.
verses.nlt_text: If you lay a hand on it, you will certainly remember the battle that follows. You won't try that again!

verses.kjv_text: Behold, the hope of him is in vain: shall not {one} be cast down even at the sight of him?
verses.nlt_text: No, it is useless to try to capture it. The hunter who attempts it will be knocked down.

verses.kjv_text: None {is so} fierce that dare stir him up: who then is able to stand before me?
verses.nlt_text: And since no one dares to disturb it, who then can stand up to me?

verses.kjv_text: Who hath prevented me, that I should repay {him? whatsoever is} under the whole heaven is mine.
verses.nlt_text: Who has given me anything that I need to pay back? Everything under heaven is mine.

verses.kjv_text: I will not conceal his parts, nor his power, nor his comely proportion.
verses.nlt_text: "I want to emphasize Leviathan's limbs and its enormous strength and graceful form.

verses.kjv_text: Who can discover the face of his garment? {or} who can come {to him} with his double bridle? {with: or, within}
verses.nlt_text: Who can strip off its hide, and who can penetrate its double layer of armor?

verses.kjv_text: Who can open the doors of his face? his teeth {are} terrible round about.
verses.nlt_text: Who could pry open its jaws? For its teeth are terrible!

verses.kjv_text: {His} scales {are his} pride, shut up together {as with} a close seal. {scales: Heb. strong pieces of shields}
verses.nlt_text: Its scales are like rows of shields tightly sealed together.

verses.kjv_text: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.
verses.nlt_text: They are so close together that no air can get between them.

verses.kjv_text: They are joined one to another, they stick together, that they cannot be sundered.
verses.nlt_text: Each scale sticks tight to the next. They interlock and cannot be penetrated.

verses.kjv_text: By his neesings a light doth shine, and his eyes {are} like the eyelids of the morning.
verses.nlt_text: "When it sneezes, it flashes light! Its eyes are like the red of dawn.

verses.kjv_text: Out of his mouth go burning lamps, {and} sparks of fire leap out.
verses.nlt_text: Lightning leaps from its mouth; flames of fire flash out.

verses.kjv_text: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke, as {out} of a seething pot or caldron.
verses.nlt_text: Smoke streams from its nostrils like steam from a pot heated over burning rushes.

verses.kjv_text: His breath kindleth coals, and a flame goeth out of his mouth.
verses.nlt_text: Its breath would kindle coals, for flames shoot from its mouth.

verses.kjv_text: In his neck remaineth strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him. {is turned into joy: Heb. rejoiceth}
verses.nlt_text: "The tremendous strength in Leviathan's neck strikes terror wherever it goes.

verses.kjv_text: The flakes of his flesh are joined together: they are firm in themselves; they cannot be moved. {flakes: Heb. fallings}
verses.nlt_text: Its flesh is hard and firm and cannot be penetrated.

verses.kjv_text: His heart is as firm as a stone; yea, as hard as a piece of the nether {millstone}.
verses.nlt_text: Its heart is hard as rock, hard as a millstone.

verses.kjv_text: When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves.
verses.nlt_text: When it rises, the mighty are afraid, gripped by terror.

verses.kjv_text: The sword of him that layeth at him cannot hold: the spear, the dart, nor the habergeon. {habergeon: or, breastplate}
verses.nlt_text: No sword can stop it, no spear, dart, or javelin.

verses.kjv_text: He esteemeth iron as straw, {and} brass as rotten wood.
verses.nlt_text: Iron is nothing but straw to that creature, and bronze is like rotten wood.

verses.kjv_text: The arrow cannot make him flee: slingstones are turned with him into stubble.
verses.nlt_text: Arrows cannot make it flee. Stones shot from a sling are like bits of grass.

verses.kjv_text: Darts are counted as stubble: he laugheth at the shaking of a spear.
verses.nlt_text: Clubs are like a blade of grass, and it laughs at the swish of javelins.

verses.kjv_text: Sharp stones {are} under him: he spreadeth sharp pointed things upon the mire. {Sharp stones: Heb. Sharp pieces of potsherd}
verses.nlt_text: Its belly is covered with scales as sharp as glass. It plows up the ground as it drags through the mud.

verses.kjv_text: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot: he maketh the sea like a pot of ointment.
verses.nlt_text: "Leviathan makes the water boil with its commotion. It stirs the depths like a pot of ointment.

verses.kjv_text: He maketh a path to shine after him; {one} would think the deep {to be} hoary.
verses.nlt_text: The water glistens in its wake, making the sea look white.

verses.kjv_text: Upon earth there is not his like, who is made without fear. {is made without fear: or, behave themselves without fear}
verses.nlt_text: Nothing on earth is its equal, no other creature so fearless.

verses.kjv_text: He beholdeth all high {things}: he {is} a king over all the children of pride.
verses.nlt_text: Of all the creatures, it is the proudest. It is the king of beasts."

verses.kjv_text: Then Job answered the LORD, and said,
verses.nlt_text: Then Job replied to the LORD:

verses.kjv_text: I know that thou canst do every {thing}, and {that} no thought can be withholden from thee. {no thought can be...: or, no thought of thine can be hindered}
verses.nlt_text: "I know that you can do anything, and no one can stop you.

verses.kjv_text: Who {is} he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not.
verses.nlt_text: You asked, 'Who is this that questions my wisdom with such ignorance?' It is I-- and I was talking about things I knew nothing about, things far too wonderful for me.

verses.kjv_text: Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
verses.nlt_text: You said, 'Listen and I will speak! I have some questions for you, and you must answer them.'

verses.kjv_text: I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.
verses.nlt_text: I had only heard about you before, but now I have seen you with my own eyes.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore I abhor {myself}, and repent in dust and ashes.
verses.nlt_text: I take back everything I said, and I sit in dust and ashes to show my repentance."

verses.kjv_text: And it was {so}, that after the LORD had spoken these words unto Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me {the thing that is} right, as my servant Job {hath}.
verses.nlt_text: After the LORD had finished speaking to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Temanite: "I am angry with you and your two friends, for you have not spoken accurately about me, as my servant Job has.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you {after your} folly, in that ye have not spoken of me {the thing which is} right, like my servant Job. {him: Heb. his face, or, person}
verses.nlt_text: So take seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer on your behalf. I will not treat you as you deserve, for you have not spoken accurately about me, as my servant Job has."

verses.kjv_text: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite {and} Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the LORD commanded them: the LORD also accepted Job. {Job: Heb. the face of Job}
verses.nlt_text: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite did as the LORD commanded them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.

verses.kjv_text: And the LORD turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before. {gave...: Heb. added all that had been to Job unto the double}
verses.nlt_text: When Job prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his fortunes. In fact, the LORD gave him twice as much as before!

verses.kjv_text: Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the LORD had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.
verses.nlt_text: Then all his brothers, sisters, and former friends came and feasted with him in his home. And they consoled him and comforted him because of all the trials the LORD had brought against him. And each of them brought him a gift of money and a gold ring.

verses.kjv_text: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.
verses.nlt_text: So the LORD blessed Job in the second half of his life even more than in the beginning. For now he had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 teams of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

verses.kjv_text: He had also seven sons and three daughters.
verses.nlt_text: He also gave Job seven more sons and three more daughters.

verses.kjv_text: And he called the name of the first, Jemima; and the name of the second, Kezia; and the name of the third, Kerenhappuch.
verses.nlt_text: He named his first daughter Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.

verses.kjv_text: And in all the land were no women found {so} fair as the daughters of Job: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren.
verses.nlt_text: In all the land no women were as lovely as the daughters of Job. And their father put them into his will along with their brothers.

verses.kjv_text: After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, {even} four generations.
verses.nlt_text: Job lived 140 years after that, living to see four generations of his children and grandchildren.

verses.kjv_text: So Job died, {being} old and full of days.
verses.nlt_text: Then he died, an old man who had lived a long, full life.

verses.kjv_text: Blessed {is} the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. {ungodly: or, wicked}
But his delight {is} in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.
And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper. {wither: Heb. fade}
The ungodly {are} not so: but {are} like the chaff which the wind driveth away.
Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.
For the LORD knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.
Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing? {rage: or, tumultuously assemble} {imagine: Heb. meditate}
The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed, {saying},
Let us break their bands asunder, and cast away their cords from us.
He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: the Lord shall have them in derision.
Then shall he speak unto them in his wrath, and vex them in his sore displeasure. {vex: or, trouble}
Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion. {set: Heb. anointed} {upon...: Heb. upon Zion, the hill of my holiness}
I will declare the decree: the LORD hath said unto me, Thou {art} my Son; this day have I begotten thee. {the decree: or, for a decree}
Ask of me, and I shall give {thee} the heathen {for} thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth {for} thy possession.
Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.
Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish {from} the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed {are} all they that put their trust in him.
[A Psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.] LORD, how are they increased that trouble me! many {are} they that rise up against me.
Many {there be} which say of my soul, {There is} no help for him in God. Selah.
But thou, O LORD, {art} a shield for me; my glory, and the lifter up of mine head. {for: or, about}
I cried unto the LORD with my voice, and he heard me out of his holy hill. Selah.
I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.
I will not be afraid of ten thousands of people, that have set {themselves} against me round about.
Arise, O LORD; save me, O my God: for thou hast smitten all mine enemies {upon} the cheek bone; thou hast broken the teeth of the ungodly.
Salvation {belongeth} unto the LORD: thy blessing {is} upon thy people. Selah.

[To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm of David.] Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness: thou hast enlarged me {when I was} in distress; have mercy upon me, and hear my prayer. {chief...: or, overseer} {have...: or, be gracious unto me}
O ye sons of men, how long {will ye turn} my glory into shame? {how long} will ye love vanity, {and} seek after leasing? Selah.
But know that the LORD hath set apart him that is godly for himself: the LORD will hear when I call unto him.
Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.
Offer the sacrifices of righteousness, and put your trust in the LORD.
{There be} many that say, Who will shew us {any} good? LORD, lift thou up the light of thy countenance upon us.
Thou hast put gladness in my heart, more than in the time {that} their corn and their wine increased.
I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
[To the chief Musician upon Nehiloth, A Psalm of David.] Give ear to my words, O LORD, consider my meditation.
Hearken unto the voice of my cry, my King, and my God: for unto thee will I pray.
My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct {my prayer} unto thee, and will look up.
For thou {art} not a God that hath pleasure in wickedness: neither shall evil dwell with thee.
The foolish shall not stand in thy sight: thou hatest all workers of iniquity. {in...: Heb. before thine eyes}
Thou shalt destroy them that speak leasing: the LORD will abhor the bloody and deceitful man. {bloody...: Heb. man of bloods and deceit}
But as for me, I will come {into} thy house in the multitude of thy mercy: {and} in thy fear will I worship toward thy holy temple. {thy holy...: Heb. the temple of thy holiness}
Lead me, O LORD, in thy righteousness because of mine enemies; make thy way straight before my face. {mine...: Heb. those which observe me}

For {there is} no faithfulness in their mouth; their inward part {is} very wickedness; their throat {is} an open sepulchre; they flatter with their tongue. {faithfulness: or, stedfastness} {their mouth: Heb. his mouth, that is, the mouth of any of them} {very...: Heb. wickednesses}

Destroy thou them, O God; let them fall by their own counsels; cast them out in the multitude of their transgressions; for they have rebelled against thee. {Destroy...: or, Make them guilty} {by...: or, from their counsels}

But let all those that put their trust in thee rejoice: let them ever shout for joy, because thou defendest them: let them also that love thy name be joyful in thee. {defendest...: Heb. coverest over, or, protectest them}
For thou, LORD, wilt bless the righteous; with favour wilt thou compass him as {with} a shield. {compass: Heb. crown}

[To the chief Musician on Neginoth upon Sheminith, A Psalm of David.] O LORD, rebuke me not in thine anger, neither chasten me in thy hot displeasure. {chief...: or, overseer} {Sheminith: or, the eighth}
Have mercy upon me, O LORD; for I {am} weak: O LORD, heal me; for my bones are vexed.
My soul is also sore vexed: but thou, O LORD, how long?
Return, O LORD, deliver my soul: oh save me for thy mercies' sake.
For in death {there is} no remembrance of thee: in the grave who shall give thee thanks?
I am weary with my groaning; all the night make I my bed to swim; I water my couch with my tears. {all...: or, every night}
Mine eye is consumed because of grief; it waxeth old because of all mine enemies.
Depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity; for the LORD hath heard the voice of my weeping.
The LORD hath heard my supplication; the LORD will receive my prayer.
Let all mine enemies be ashamed and sore vexed: let them return {and} be ashamed suddenly.

[Shiggaion of David, which he sang unto the LORD, concerning the words of Cush the Benjamite.] O LORD my God, in thee do I put my trust: save me from all them that persecute me, and deliver me: {words: or, business}
Lest he tear my soul like a lion, rending {it} in pieces, while {there is} none to deliver. {none...: Heb. not a deliverer}
O LORD my God, if I have done this; if there be iniquity in my hands;
If I have rewarded evil unto him that was at peace with me; (yea, I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy:)
Let the enemy persecute my soul, and take {it}; yea, let him tread down my life upon the earth, and lay mine honour in the dust. Selah.
Arise, O LORD, in thine anger, lift up thyself because of the rage of mine enemies: and awake for me {to} the judgment {that} thou hast commanded.
So shall the congregation of the people compass thee about: for their sakes therefore return thou on high.
The LORD shall judge the people: judge me, O LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to mine integrity {that is} in me.
Oh let the wickedness of the wicked come to an end; but establish the just: for the righteous God trieth the hearts and reins.
My defence {is} of God, which saveth the upright in heart. {My...: Heb. My buckler is upon God}
God judgeth the righteous, and God is angry {with the wicked} every day. {judgeth...: or, is a righteous judge}
If he turn not, he will whet his sword; he hath bent his bow, and made it ready.
He hath also prepared for him the instruments of death; he ordaineth his arrows against the persecutors.
Behold, he travaileth with iniquity, and hath conceived mischief, and brought forth falsehood.
He made a pit, and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch {which} he made. {He made a pit: Heb. He hath digged a pit}
His mischief shall return upon his own head, and his violent dealing shall come down upon his own pate.
I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness: and will sing praise to the name of the LORD most high.
[To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David.] O LORD our Lord, how excellent {is} thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.
Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou ordained strength because of thine enemies, that thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger. {ordained: Heb. founded}
When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained;
What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?
For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.
Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all {things} under his feet:
All sheep and oxen, yea, and the beasts of the field; {All...: Heb. Flocks and oxen all of them}
The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, {and whatsoever} passeth through the paths of the seas.
O LORD our Lord, how excellent {is} thy name in all the earth!
[To the chief Musician upon Muthlabben, A Psalm of David.] I will praise {thee}, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
I will be glad and rejoice in thee: I will sing praise to thy name, O thou most High.
When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence.
For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right. {maintained...: Heb. made my judgment} {judging right: Heb. judging in righteousness}
Thou hast rebuked the heathen, thou hast destroyed the wicked, thou hast put out their name for ever and ever.

O thou enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end: and thou hast destroyed cities; their memorial is perished with them. {O thou...: or, The destructions of the enemy are come to a perpetual end: and their cities hast thou destroyed, etc}
But the LORD shall endure for ever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment.
And he shall judge the world in righteousness, he shall minister judgment to the people in uprightness.
The LORD also will be a refuge for the oppressed, a refuge in times of trouble. {a refuge: Heb. an high place}
And they that know thy name will put their trust in thee: for thou, LORD, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.
Sing praises to the LORD, which dwelleth in Zion: declare among the people his doings.
When he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble. {humble: or, afflicted}
