verses.nlt_text: Get the truth and never sell it; also get wisdom, discipline, and good judgment.

verses.kjv_text: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise {child} shall have joy of him.
verses.nlt_text: The father of godly children has cause for joy. What a pleasure to have children who are wise.

verses.kjv_text: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.
verses.nlt_text: So give your father and mother joy! May she who gave you birth be happy.

verses.kjv_text: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.
verses.nlt_text: O my son, give me your heart. May your eyes take delight in following my ways.

verses.kjv_text: For a whore {is} a deep ditch; and a strange woman {is} a narrow pit.
verses.nlt_text: A prostitute is a dangerous trap; a promiscuous woman is as dangerous as falling into a narrow well.

verses.kjv_text: She also lieth in wait as {for} a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men. {as for...: or, as a robber}
verses.nlt_text: She hides and waits like a robber, eager to make more men unfaithful.

verses.kjv_text: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?
verses.nlt_text: Who has anguish? Who has sorrow? Who is always fighting? Who is always complaining? Who has unnecessary bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?

verses.kjv_text: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.
verses.nlt_text: It is the one who spends long hours in the taverns, trying out new drinks.

verses.kjv_text: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, {when} it moveth itself aright.
verses.nlt_text: Don't gaze at the wine, seeing how red it is, how it sparkles in the cup, how smoothly it goes down.

verses.kjv_text: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder. {an...: or, a cockatrice}
verses.nlt_text: For in the end it bites like a poisonous snake; it stings like a viper.

verses.kjv_text: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.
verses.nlt_text: You will see hallucinations, and you will say crazy things.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast. {the midst...: Heb. the heart of the sea}
verses.nlt_text: You will stagger like a sailor tossed at sea, clinging to a swaying mast.

verses.kjv_text: They have stricken me, {shalt thou say, and} I was not sick; they have beaten me, {and} I felt {it} not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again. {I felt...: Heb. I knew it not}
verses.nlt_text: And you will say, "They hit me, but I didn't feel it. I didn't even know it when they beat me up. When will I wake up so I can look for another drink?"

verses.kjv_text: Be not thou envious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
verses.nlt_text: Don't envy evil people or desire their company.

verses.kjv_text: For their heart studieth destruction, and their lips talk of mischief.
verses.nlt_text: For their hearts plot violence, and their words always stir up trouble.

verses.kjv_text: Through wisdom is an house builded; and by understanding it is established:
verses.nlt_text: A house is built by wisdom and becomes strong through good sense.

verses.kjv_text: And by knowledge shall the chambers be filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
verses.nlt_text: Through knowledge its rooms are filled with all sorts of precious riches and valuables.

verses.kjv_text: A wise man {is} strong; yea, a man of knowledge increaseth strength. {is strong: Heb. is in strength} {increaseth...: Heb. strengtheneth might}
verses.nlt_text: The wise are mightier than the strong, and those with knowledge grow stronger and stronger.

verses.kjv_text: For by wise counsel thou shalt make thy war: and in multitude of counsellors {there is} safety.
verses.nlt_text: So don't go to war without wise guidance; victory depends on having many advisers.

verses.kjv_text: Wisdom {is} too high for a fool: he openeth not his mouth in the gate.
verses.nlt_text: Wisdom is too lofty for fools. Among leaders at the city gate, they have nothing to say.

verses.kjv_text: He that deviseth to do evil shall be called a mischievous person.
verses.nlt_text: A person who plans evil will get a reputation as a troublemaker.

verses.kjv_text: The thought of foolishness {is} sin: and the scorner {is} an abomination to men.
verses.nlt_text: The schemes of a fool are sinful; everyone detests a mocker.

verses.kjv_text: {If} thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength {is} small. {small: Heb. narrow}
verses.nlt_text: If you fail under pressure, your strength is too small.

verses.kjv_text: If thou forbear to deliver {them that are} drawn unto death, and {those that are} ready to be slain;
verses.nlt_text: Rescue those who are unjustly sentenced to die; save them as they stagger to their death.

verses.kjv_text: If thou sayest, Behold, we knew it not; doth not he that pondereth the heart consider {it}? and he that keepeth thy soul, doth {not} he know {it}? and shall {not} he render to {every} man according to his works?
verses.nlt_text: Don't excuse yourself by saying, "Look, we didn't know." For God understands all hearts, and he sees you. He who guards your soul knows you knew. He will repay all people as their actions deserve.

verses.kjv_text: My son, eat thou honey, because {it is} good; and the honeycomb, {which is} sweet to thy taste: {to...: Heb. upon thy palate}
verses.nlt_text: My child, eat honey, for it is good, and the honeycomb is sweet to the taste.

verses.kjv_text: So {shall} the knowledge of wisdom {be} unto thy soul: when thou hast found {it}, then there shall be a reward, and thy expectation shall not be cut off.
verses.nlt_text: In the same way, wisdom is sweet to your soul. If you find it, you will have a bright future, and your hopes will not be cut short.

verses.kjv_text: Lay not wait, O wicked {man}, against the dwelling of the righteous; spoil not his resting place:
verses.nlt_text: Don't wait in ambush at the home of the godly, and don't raid the house where the godly live.

verses.kjv_text: For a just {man} falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
verses.nlt_text: The godly may trip seven times, but they will get up again. But one disaster is enough to overthrow the wicked.

verses.kjv_text: Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth:
verses.nlt_text: Don't rejoice when your enemies fall; don't be happy when they stumble.

verses.kjv_text: Lest the LORD see {it}, and it displease him, and he turn away his wrath from him. {it displeaseth...: Heb. it be evil in his eyes}
verses.nlt_text: For the LORD will be displeased with you and will turn his anger away from them.

verses.kjv_text: Fret not thyself because of evil {men}, neither be thou envious at the wicked; {Fret...: or, Keep not company with the wicked}
verses.nlt_text: Don't fret because of evildoers; don't envy the wicked.

verses.kjv_text: For there shall be no reward to the evil {man}; the candle of the wicked shall be put out. {candle: or, lamp}
verses.nlt_text: For evil people have no future; the light of the wicked will be snuffed out.

verses.kjv_text: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king: {and} meddle not with them that are given to change: {them...: Heb. changers}
verses.nlt_text: My child, fear the LORD and the king. Don't associate with rebels,

verses.kjv_text: For their calamity shall rise suddenly; and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
verses.nlt_text: for disaster will hit them suddenly. Who knows what punishment will come from the LORD and the king?

verses.kjv_text: These {things} also {belong} to the wise. {It is} not good to have respect of persons in judgment.
verses.nlt_text: Here are some further sayings of the wise: It is wrong to show favoritism when passing judgment.

verses.kjv_text: He that saith unto the wicked, Thou {art} righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him:
verses.nlt_text: A judge who says to the wicked, "You are innocent," will be cursed by many people and denounced by the nations.

verses.kjv_text: But to them that rebuke {him} shall be delight, and a good blessing shall come upon them. {a good...: Heb. a blessing of good}
verses.nlt_text: But it will go well for those who convict the guilty; rich blessings will be showered on them.

verses.kjv_text: {Every man} shall kiss {his} lips that giveth a right answer. {that...: Heb. that answereth right words}
verses.nlt_text: An honest answer is like a kiss of friendship.

verses.kjv_text: Prepare thy work without, and make it fit for thyself in the field; and afterwards build thine house.
verses.nlt_text: Do your planning and prepare your fields before building your house.

verses.kjv_text: Be not a witness against thy neighbour without cause; and deceive {not} with thy lips.
verses.nlt_text: Don't testify against your neighbors without cause; don't lie about them.

verses.kjv_text: Say not, I will do so to him as he hath done to me: I will render to the man according to his work.
verses.nlt_text: And don't say, "Now I can pay them back for what they've done to me! I'll get even with them!"

verses.kjv_text: I went by the field of the slothful, and by the vineyard of the man void of understanding;
verses.nlt_text: I walked by the field of a lazy person, the vineyard of one with no common sense.

verses.kjv_text: And, lo, it was all grown over with thorns, {and} nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
verses.nlt_text: I saw that it was overgrown with nettles. It was covered with weeds, and its walls were broken down.

verses.kjv_text: Then I saw, {and} considered {it} well: I looked upon {it, and} received instruction. {considered...: Heb. set my heart}
verses.nlt_text: Then, as I looked and thought about it, I learned this lesson:

verses.kjv_text: {Yet} a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:
verses.nlt_text: A little extra sleep, a little more slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest--

verses.kjv_text: So shall thy poverty come {as} one that travelleth; and thy want as an armed man. {an...: Heb. a man of shield}
verses.nlt_text: then poverty will pounce on you like a bandit; scarcity will attack you like an armed robber.

verses.kjv_text: These {are} also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
verses.nlt_text: These are more proverbs of Solomon, collected by the advisers of King Hezekiah of Judah.

verses.kjv_text: {It is} the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings {is} to search out a matter.
verses.nlt_text: It is God's privilege to conceal things and the king's privilege to discover them.

verses.kjv_text: The heaven for height, and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings {is} unsearchable. {is...: Heb. there is no searching}
verses.nlt_text: No one can comprehend the height of heaven, the depth of the earth, or all that goes on in the king's mind!

verses.kjv_text: Take away the dross from the silver, and there shall come forth a vessel for the finer.
verses.nlt_text: Remove the impurities from silver, and the sterling will be ready for the silversmith.

verses.kjv_text: Take away the wicked {from} before the king, and his throne shall be established in righteousness.
verses.nlt_text: Remove the wicked from the king's court, and his reign will be made secure by justice.

verses.kjv_text: Put not forth thyself in the presence of the king, and stand not in the place of great {men}: {Put...: Heb. Set not out thy glory}
verses.nlt_text: Don't demand an audience with the king or push for a place among the great.

verses.kjv_text: For better {it is} that it be said unto thee, Come up hither; than that thou shouldest be put lower in the presence of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
verses.nlt_text: It's better to wait for an invitation to the head table than to be sent away in public disgrace. Just because you've seen something,

verses.kjv_text: Go not forth hastily to strive, lest {thou know not} what to do in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
verses.nlt_text: don't be in a hurry to go to court. For what will you do in the end if your neighbor deals you a shameful defeat?

verses.kjv_text: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour {himself}; and discover not a secret to another: {a secret...: or, the secret of}
verses.nlt_text: When arguing with your neighbor, don't betray another person's secret.

verses.kjv_text: Lest he that heareth {it} put thee to shame, and thine infamy turn not away.
verses.nlt_text: Others may accuse you of gossip, and you will never regain your good reputation.

verses.kjv_text: A word fitly spoken {is like} apples of gold in pictures of silver. {fitly...: Heb. spoken upon his wheels}
verses.nlt_text: Timely advice is lovely, like golden apples in a silver basket.

verses.kjv_text: {As} an earring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold, {so is} a wise reprover upon an obedient ear.
verses.nlt_text: To one who listens, valid criticism is like a gold earring or other gold jewelry.

verses.kjv_text: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, {so is} a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
verses.nlt_text: Trustworthy messengers refresh like snow in summer. They revive the spirit of their employer.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso boasteth himself of a false gift {is like} clouds and wind without rain. {of a...: Heb. in a gift of falsehood}
verses.nlt_text: A person who promises a gift but doesn't give it is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.

verses.kjv_text: By long forbearing is a prince persuaded, and a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
verses.nlt_text: Patience can persuade a prince, and soft speech can break bones.

verses.kjv_text: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.
verses.nlt_text: Do you like honey? Don't eat too much, or it will make you sick!

verses.kjv_text: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbour's house; lest he be weary of thee, and {so} hate thee. {Withdraw...: or, Let thy foot be seldom in} {weary...: Heb. full of thee}
verses.nlt_text: Don't visit your neighbors too often, or you will wear out your welcome.

verses.kjv_text: A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour {is} a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
verses.nlt_text: Telling lies about others is as harmful as hitting them with an ax, wounding them with a sword, or shooting them with a sharp arrow.

verses.kjv_text: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble {is like} a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
verses.nlt_text: Putting confidence in an unreliable person in times of trouble is like chewing with a broken tooth or walking on a lame foot.

verses.kjv_text: {As} he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, {and as} vinegar upon nitre, so {is} he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
verses.nlt_text: Singing cheerful songs to a person with a heavy heart is like taking someone's coat in cold weather or pouring vinegar in a wound.

verses.kjv_text: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink:
verses.nlt_text: If your enemies are hungry, give them food to eat. If they are thirsty, give them water to drink.

verses.kjv_text: For thou shalt heap coals of fire upon his head, and the LORD shall reward thee.
verses.nlt_text: You will heap burning coals of shame on their heads, and the LORD will reward you.

verses.kjv_text: The north wind driveth away rain: so {doth} an angry countenance a backbiting tongue. {driveth...: or, bringeth forth rain: so doth a backbiting tongue an angry countenance}
verses.nlt_text: As surely as a north wind brings rain, so a gossiping tongue causes anger!

verses.kjv_text: {It is} better to dwell in the corner of the housetop, than with a brawling woman and in a wide house.
verses.nlt_text: It's better to live alone in the corner of an attic than with a quarrelsome wife in a lovely home.

verses.kjv_text: {As} cold waters to a thirsty soul, so {is} good news from a far country.
verses.nlt_text: Good news from far away is like cold water to the thirsty.

verses.kjv_text: A righteous man falling down before the wicked {is as} a troubled fountain, and a corrupt spring.
verses.nlt_text: If the godly give in to the wicked, it's like polluting a fountain or muddying a spring.

verses.kjv_text: {It is} not good to eat much honey: so {for men} to search their own glory {is not} glory.
verses.nlt_text: It's not good to eat too much honey, and it's not good to seek honors for yourself.

verses.kjv_text: He that {hath} no rule over his own spirit {is like} a city {that is} broken down, {and} without walls.
verses.nlt_text: A person without self-control is like a city with broken-down walls.

verses.kjv_text: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.
verses.nlt_text: Honor is no more associated with fools than snow with summer or rain with harvest.

verses.kjv_text: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.
verses.nlt_text: Like a fluttering sparrow or a darting swallow, an undeserved curse will not land on its intended victim.

verses.kjv_text: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool's back.
verses.nlt_text: Guide a horse with a whip, a donkey with a bridle, and a fool with a rod to his back!

verses.kjv_text: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
verses.nlt_text: Don't answer the foolish arguments of fools, or you will become as foolish as they are.

verses.kjv_text: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit. {conceit: Heb. eyes}
verses.nlt_text: Be sure to answer the foolish arguments of fools, or they will become wise in their own estimation.

verses.kjv_text: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, {and} drinketh damage. {damage: or, violence}
verses.nlt_text: Trusting a fool to convey a message is like cutting off one's feet or drinking poison!

verses.kjv_text: The legs of the lame are not equal: so {is} a parable in the mouth of fools. {are...: Heb. are lifted up}
verses.nlt_text: A proverb in the mouth of a fool is as useless as a paralyzed leg.

verses.kjv_text: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so {is} he that giveth honour to a fool. {bindeth...: or, putteth a precious stone in an heap of stones}
verses.nlt_text: Honoring a fool is as foolish as tying a stone to a slingshot.

verses.kjv_text: {As} a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so {is} a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.nlt_text: A proverb in the mouth of a fool is like a thorny branch brandished by a drunk.

verses.kjv_text: The great {God} that formed all {things} both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors. {The great...: or, A great man grieveth all, and he hireth the fool, he hireth also transgressors}
verses.nlt_text: An employer who hires a fool or a bystander is like an archer who shoots at random.

verses.kjv_text: As a dog returneth to his vomit, {so} a fool returneth to his folly. {returneth to his folly: Heb. iterateth his folly}
verses.nlt_text: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his foolishness.

verses.kjv_text: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? {there is} more hope of a fool than of him.
verses.nlt_text: There is more hope for fools than for people who think they are wise.

verses.kjv_text: The slothful {man} saith, {There is} a lion in the way; a lion {is} in the streets.
verses.nlt_text: The lazy person claims, "There's a lion on the road! Yes, I'm sure there's a lion out there!"

verses.kjv_text: {As} the door turneth upon his hinges, so {doth} the slothful upon his bed.
verses.nlt_text: As a door swings back and forth on its hinges, so the lazy person turns over in bed.

verses.kjv_text: The slothful hideth his hand in {his} bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth. {it grieveth...: or, he is weary}
verses.nlt_text: Lazy people take food in their hand but don't even lift it to their mouth.

verses.kjv_text: The sluggard {is} wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
verses.nlt_text: Lazy people consider themselves smarter than seven wise counselors.

verses.kjv_text: He that passeth by, {and} meddleth with strife {belonging} not to him, {is like} one that taketh a dog by the ears. {meddleth: or, is enraged}
verses.nlt_text: Interfering in someone else's argument is as foolish as yanking a dog's ears.

verses.kjv_text: As a mad {man} who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death, {firebrands: Heb. flames, or, sparks}
verses.nlt_text: Just as damaging as a madman shooting a deadly weapon

verses.kjv_text: So {is} the man {that} deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
verses.nlt_text: is someone who lies to a friend and then says, "I was only joking."

verses.kjv_text: Where no wood is, {there} the fire goeth out: so where {there is} no talebearer, the strife ceaseth. {Where no...: Heb. Without wood} {talebearer: or, whisperer} {ceaseth: Heb. is silent}
verses.nlt_text: Fire goes out without wood, and quarrels disappear when gossip stops.

verses.kjv_text: {As} coals {are} to burning coals, and wood to fire; so {is} a contentious man to kindle strife.
verses.nlt_text: A quarrelsome person starts fights as easily as hot embers light charcoal or fire lights wood.

verses.kjv_text: The words of a talebearer {are} as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly. {innermost...: Heb. chambers}
verses.nlt_text: Rumors are dainty morsels that sink deep into one's heart.

verses.kjv_text: Burning lips and a wicked heart {are like} a potsherd covered with silver dross.
verses.nlt_text: Smooth words may hide a wicked heart, just as a pretty glaze covers a clay pot.

verses.kjv_text: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him; {dissembleth: or, is known}
verses.nlt_text: People may cover their hatred with pleasant words, but they're deceiving you.

verses.kjv_text: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for {there are} seven abominations in his heart. {speaketh...: Heb. maketh his voice gracious}
verses.nlt_text: They pretend to be kind, but don't believe them. Their hearts are full of many evils.

verses.kjv_text: {Whose} hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the {whole} congregation. {by...: or, in secret}
verses.nlt_text: While their hatred may be concealed by trickery, their wrongdoing will be exposed in public.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
verses.nlt_text: If you set a trap for others, you will get caught in it yourself. If you roll a boulder down on others, it will crush you instead.

verses.kjv_text: A lying tongue hateth {those that are} afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
verses.nlt_text: A lying tongue hates its victims, and flattering words cause ruin.

verses.kjv_text: Boast not thyself of to morrow; for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth. {to...: Heb. to morrow day}
verses.nlt_text: Don't brag about tomorrow, since you don't know what the day will bring.

verses.kjv_text: Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips.
verses.nlt_text: Let someone else praise you, not your own mouth-- a stranger, not your own lips.

verses.kjv_text: A stone {is} heavy, and the sand weighty; but a fool's wrath {is} heavier than them both. {heavy: Heb. heaviness}
verses.nlt_text: A stone is heavy and sand is weighty, but the resentment caused by a fool is even heavier.

verses.kjv_text: Wrath {is} cruel, and anger {is} outrageous; but who {is} able to stand before envy? {Wrath...: Heb. Wrath is cruelty, and anger an overflowing} {envy: or, jealousy?}
verses.nlt_text: Anger is cruel, and wrath is like a flood, but jealousy is even more dangerous.

verses.kjv_text: Open rebuke {is} better than secret love.
verses.nlt_text: An open rebuke is better than hidden love!

verses.kjv_text: Faithful {are} the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy {are} deceitful. {deceitful: or, earnest, or, frequent}
verses.nlt_text: Wounds from a sincere friend are better than many kisses from an enemy.

verses.kjv_text: The full soul loatheth an honeycomb; but to the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet. {loatheth: Heb. treadeth under foot}
verses.nlt_text: A person who is full refuses honey, but even bitter food tastes sweet to the hungry.

verses.kjv_text: As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so {is} a man that wandereth from his place.
verses.nlt_text: A person who strays from home is like a bird that strays from its nest.

verses.kjv_text: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so {doth} the sweetness of a man's friend by hearty counsel. {by...: Heb. from the counsel of the soul}
verses.nlt_text: The heartfelt counsel of a friend is as sweet as perfume and incense.

verses.kjv_text: Thine own friend, and thy father's friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother's house in the day of thy calamity: {for} better {is} a neighbour {that is} near than a brother far off.
verses.nlt_text: Never abandon a friend-- either yours or your father's. When disaster strikes, you won't have to ask your brother for assistance. It's better to go to a neighbor than to a brother who lives far away.

verses.kjv_text: My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him that reproacheth me.
verses.nlt_text: Be wise, my child, and make my heart glad. Then I will be able to answer my critics.

verses.kjv_text: A prudent {man} foreseeth the evil, {and} hideth himself; {but} the simple pass on, {and} are punished.
verses.nlt_text: A prudent person foresees danger and takes precautions. The simpleton goes blindly on and suffers the consequences.

verses.kjv_text: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and take a pledge of him for a strange woman.
verses.nlt_text: Get security from someone who guarantees a stranger's debt. Get a deposit if he does it for foreigners.

verses.kjv_text: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it shall be counted a curse to him.
verses.nlt_text: A loud and cheerful greeting early in the morning will be taken as a curse!

verses.kjv_text: A continual dropping in a very rainy day and a contentious woman are alike.
verses.nlt_text: A quarrelsome wife is as annoying as constant dripping on a rainy day.

verses.kjv_text: Whosoever hideth her hideth the wind, and the ointment of his right hand, {which} bewrayeth {itself}.
verses.nlt_text: Stopping her complaints is like trying to stop the wind or trying to hold something with greased hands.

verses.kjv_text: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
verses.nlt_text: As iron sharpens iron, so a friend sharpens a friend.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso keepeth the fig tree shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth on his master shall be honoured.
verses.nlt_text: As workers who tend a fig tree are allowed to eat the fruit, so workers who protect their employer's interests will be rewarded.

verses.kjv_text: As in water face {answereth} to face, so the heart of man to man.
verses.nlt_text: As a face is reflected in water, so the heart reflects the real person.

verses.kjv_text: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied. {never: Heb. not}
verses.nlt_text: Just as Death and Destruction are never satisfied, so human desire is never satisfied.

verses.kjv_text: {As} the fining pot for silver, and the furnace for gold; so {is} a man to his praise.
verses.nlt_text: Fire tests the purity of silver and gold, but a person is tested by being praised.

verses.kjv_text: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar among wheat with a pestle, {yet} will not his foolishness depart from him.
verses.nlt_text: You cannot separate fools from their foolishness, even though you grind them like grain with mortar and pestle.

verses.kjv_text: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, {and} look well to thy herds. {look...: Heb. set thy heart}
verses.nlt_text: Know the state of your flocks, and put your heart into caring for your herds,

verses.kjv_text: For riches {are} not for ever: and doth the crown {endure} to every generation? {riches: Heb. strength} {to...: Heb. to generation and generation?}
verses.nlt_text: for riches don't last forever, and the crown might not be passed to the next generation.

verses.kjv_text: The hay appeareth, and the tender grass sheweth itself, and herbs of the mountains are gathered.
verses.nlt_text: After the hay is harvested and the new crop appears and the mountain grasses are gathered in,

verses.kjv_text: The lambs {are} for thy clothing, and the goats {are} the price of the field.
verses.nlt_text: your sheep will provide wool for clothing, and your goats will provide the price of a field.

verses.kjv_text: And {thou shalt have} goats' milk enough for thy food, for the food of thy household, and {for} the maintenance for thy maidens. {maintenance: Heb. life}
verses.nlt_text: And you will have enough goats' milk for yourself, your family, and your servant girls.

verses.kjv_text: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.
verses.nlt_text: The wicked run away when no one is chasing them, but the godly are as bold as lions.

verses.kjv_text: For the transgression of a land many {are} the princes thereof: but by a man of understanding {and} knowledge the state {thereof} shall be prolonged. {by...: or, by men of understanding and wisdom shall they likewise be prolonged}
verses.nlt_text: When there is moral rot within a nation, its government topples easily. But wise and knowledgeable leaders bring stability.

verses.kjv_text: A poor man that oppresseth the poor {is like} a sweeping rain which leaveth no food. {which...: Heb. without food}
verses.nlt_text: A poor person who oppresses the poor is like a pounding rain that destroys the crops.

verses.kjv_text: They that forsake the law praise the wicked: but such as keep the law contend with them.
verses.nlt_text: To reject the law is to praise the wicked; to obey the law is to fight them.

verses.kjv_text: Evil men understand not judgment: but they that seek the LORD understand all {things}.
verses.nlt_text: Evil people don't understand justice, but those who follow the LORD understand completely.

verses.kjv_text: Better {is} the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than {he that is} perverse {in his} ways, though he {be} rich.
verses.nlt_text: Better to be poor and honest than to be dishonest and rich.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso keepeth the law {is} a wise son: but he that is a companion of riotous {men} shameth his father. {is a companion...: or, feedeth gluttons}
verses.nlt_text: Young people who obey the law are wise; those with wild friends bring shame to their parents.

verses.kjv_text: He that by usury and unjust gain increaseth his substance, he shall gather it for him that will pity the poor. {unjust...: Heb. by increase}
verses.nlt_text: Income from charging high interest rates will end up in the pocket of someone who is kind to the poor.

verses.kjv_text: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer {shall be} abomination.
verses.nlt_text: God detests the prayers of a person who ignores the law.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso causeth the righteous to go astray in an evil way, he shall fall himself into his own pit: but the upright shall have good {things} in possession.
verses.nlt_text: Those who lead good people along an evil path will fall into their own trap, but the honest will inherit good things.

verses.kjv_text: The rich man {is} wise in his own conceit; but the poor that hath understanding searcheth him out. {own...: Heb. eyes}
verses.nlt_text: Rich people may think they are wise, but a poor person with discernment can see right through them.

verses.kjv_text: When righteous {men} do rejoice, {there is} great glory: but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden. {hidden: or, sought for}
verses.nlt_text: When the godly succeed, everyone is glad. When the wicked take charge, people go into hiding.

verses.kjv_text: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh {them} shall have mercy.
verses.nlt_text: People who conceal their sins will not prosper, but if they confess and turn from them, they will receive mercy.

verses.kjv_text: Happy {is} the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart shall fall into mischief.
verses.nlt_text: Blessed are those who fear to do wrong, but the stubborn are headed for serious trouble.

verses.kjv_text: {As} a roaring lion, and a ranging bear; {so is} a wicked ruler over the poor people.
verses.nlt_text: A wicked ruler is as dangerous to the poor as a roaring lion or an attacking bear.

verses.kjv_text: The prince that wanteth understanding {is} also a great oppressor: {but} he that hateth covetousness shall prolong {his} days.
verses.nlt_text: A ruler with no understanding will oppress his people, but one who hates corruption will have a long life.

verses.kjv_text: A man that doeth violence to the blood of {any} person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him.
verses.nlt_text: A murderer's tormented conscience will drive him into the grave. Don't protect him!

verses.kjv_text: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but {he that is} perverse {in his} ways shall fall at once.
verses.nlt_text: The blameless will be rescued from harm, but the crooked will be suddenly destroyed.

verses.kjv_text: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain {persons} shall have poverty enough.
verses.nlt_text: A hard worker has plenty of food, but a person who chases fantasies ends up in poverty.

verses.kjv_text: A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent. {innocent: or, unpunished}
verses.nlt_text: The trustworthy person will get a rich reward, but a person who wants quick riches will get into trouble.

verses.kjv_text: To have respect of persons {is} not good: for for a piece of bread {that} man will transgress.
verses.nlt_text: Showing partiality is never good, yet some will do wrong for a mere piece of bread.

verses.kjv_text: He that hasteth to be rich {hath} an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him. {hasteth...: or, hath an evil eye hasteth to be rich}
verses.nlt_text: Greedy people try to get rich quick but don't realize they're headed for poverty.

verses.kjv_text: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue.
verses.nlt_text: In the end, people appreciate honest criticism far more than flattery.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, {It is} no transgression; the same {is} the companion of a destroyer. {a destroyer: Heb. a man destroying}
verses.nlt_text: Anyone who steals from his father and mother and says, "What's wrong with that?" is no better than a murderer.

verses.kjv_text: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat.
verses.nlt_text: Greed causes fighting; trusting the LORD leads to prosperity.

verses.kjv_text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
verses.nlt_text: Those who trust their own insight are foolish, but anyone who walks in wisdom is safe.

verses.kjv_text: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse.
verses.nlt_text: Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing, but those who close their eyes to poverty will be cursed.

verses.kjv_text: When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.
verses.nlt_text: When the wicked take charge, people go into hiding. When the wicked meet disaster, the godly flourish.

verses.kjv_text: He, that being often reproved hardeneth {his} neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy. {He...: Heb. A man of reproofs}
verses.nlt_text: Whoever stubbornly refuses to accept criticism will suddenly be destroyed beyond recovery.

verses.kjv_text: When the righteous are in authority, the people rejoice: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people mourn. {in...: or, increased}
verses.nlt_text: When the godly are in authority, the people rejoice. But when the wicked are in power, they groan.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso loveth wisdom rejoiceth his father: but he that keepeth company with harlots spendeth {his} substance.
verses.nlt_text: The man who loves wisdom brings joy to his father, but if he hangs around with prostitutes, his wealth is wasted.

verses.kjv_text: The king by judgment establisheth the land: but he that receiveth gifts overthroweth it. {he...: Heb. a man of oblations}
verses.nlt_text: A just king gives stability to his nation, but one who demands bribes destroys it.

verses.kjv_text: A man that flattereth his neighbour spreadeth a net for his feet.
verses.nlt_text: To flatter friends is to lay a trap for their feet.

verses.kjv_text: In the transgression of an evil man {there is} a snare: but the righteous doth sing and rejoice.
verses.nlt_text: Evil people are trapped by sin, but the righteous escape, shouting for joy.

verses.kjv_text: The righteous considereth the cause of the poor: {but} the wicked regardeth not to know {it}.
verses.nlt_text: The godly care about the rights of the poor; the wicked don't care at all.

verses.kjv_text: Scornful men bring a city into a snare: but wise {men} turn away wrath. {bring...: or, set a city on fire}
verses.nlt_text: Mockers can get a whole town agitated, but the wise will calm anger.

verses.kjv_text: {If} a wise man contendeth with a foolish man, whether he rage or laugh, {there is} no rest.
verses.nlt_text: If a wise person takes a fool to court, there will be ranting and ridicule but no satisfaction.

verses.kjv_text: The bloodthirsty hate the upright: but the just seek his soul. {The bloodthirsty: Heb. Men of blood}
verses.nlt_text: The bloodthirsty hate blameless people, but the upright seek to help them.

verses.kjv_text: A fool uttereth all his mind: but a wise {man} keepeth it in till afterwards.
verses.nlt_text: Fools vent their anger, but the wise quietly hold it back.

verses.kjv_text: If a ruler hearken to lies, all his servants {are} wicked.
verses.nlt_text: If a ruler pays attention to liars, all his advisers will be wicked.

verses.kjv_text: The poor and the deceitful man meet together: the LORD lighteneth both their eyes. {the deceitful...: or, the usurer}
verses.nlt_text: The poor and the oppressor have this in common-- the LORD gives sight to the eyes of both.

verses.kjv_text: The king that faithfully judgeth the poor, his throne shall be established for ever.
verses.nlt_text: If a king judges the poor fairly, his throne will last forever.

verses.kjv_text: The rod and reproof give wisdom: but a child left {to himself} bringeth his mother to shame.
verses.nlt_text: To discipline a child produces wisdom, but a mother is disgraced by an undisciplined child.

verses.kjv_text: When the wicked are multiplied, transgression increaseth: but the righteous shall see their fall.
verses.nlt_text: When the wicked are in authority, sin flourishes, but the godly will live to see their downfall.

verses.kjv_text: Correct thy son, and he shall give thee rest; yea, he shall give delight unto thy soul.
verses.nlt_text: Discipline your children, and they will give you peace of mind and will make your heart glad.

verses.kjv_text: Where {there is} no vision, the people perish: but he that keepeth the law, happy {is} he. {perish: or, is made naked}
verses.nlt_text: When people do not accept divine guidance, they run wild. But whoever obeys the law is joyful.

verses.kjv_text: A servant will not be corrected by words: for though he understand he will not answer.
verses.nlt_text: Words alone will not discipline a servant; the words may be understood, but they are not heeded.

verses.kjv_text: Seest thou a man {that is} hasty in his words? {there is} more hope of a fool than of him. {words: or, matters?}
verses.nlt_text: There is more hope for a fool than for someone who speaks without thinking.

verses.kjv_text: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child shall have him become {his} son at the length.
verses.nlt_text: A servant pampered from childhood will become a rebel.

verses.kjv_text: An angry man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.
verses.nlt_text: An angry person starts fights; a hot-tempered person commits all kinds of sin.

verses.kjv_text: A man's pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit.
verses.nlt_text: Pride ends in humiliation, while humility brings honor.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth {it} not.
verses.nlt_text: If you assist a thief, you only hurt yourself. You are sworn to tell the truth, but you dare not testify.

verses.kjv_text: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe. {safe: Heb. set on high}
verses.nlt_text: Fearing people is a dangerous trap, but trusting the LORD means safety.

verses.kjv_text: Many seek the ruler's favour; but {every} man's judgment {cometh} from the LORD. {the ruler's...: Heb. the face of a ruler}
verses.nlt_text: Many seek the ruler's favor, but justice comes from the LORD.

verses.kjv_text: An unjust man {is} an abomination to the just: and {he that is} upright in the way {is} abomination to the wicked.
verses.nlt_text: The righteous despise the unjust; the wicked despise the godly.

verses.kjv_text: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, {even} the prophecy: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal,
verses.nlt_text: The sayings of Agur son of Jakeh contain this message. I am weary, O God; I am weary and worn out, O God.

verses.kjv_text: Surely I {am} more brutish than {any} man, and have not the understanding of a man.
verses.nlt_text: I am too stupid to be human, and I lack common sense.

verses.kjv_text: I neither learned wisdom, nor have the knowledge of the holy. {have: Heb. know}
verses.nlt_text: I have not mastered human wisdom, nor do I know the Holy One.

verses.kjv_text: Who hath ascended up into heaven, or descended? who hath gathered the wind in his fists? who hath bound the waters in a garment? who hath established all the ends of the earth? what {is} his name, and what {is} his son's name, if thou canst tell?
verses.nlt_text: Who but God goes up to heaven and comes back down? Who holds the wind in his fists? Who wraps up the oceans in his cloak? Who has created the whole wide world? What is his name-- and his son's name? Tell me if you know!

verses.kjv_text: Every word of God {is} pure: he {is} a shield unto them that put their trust in him. {pure: Heb. purified}
verses.nlt_text: Every word of God proves true. He is a shield to all who come to him for protection.

verses.kjv_text: Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.
verses.nlt_text: Do not add to his words, or he may rebuke you and expose you as a liar.

verses.kjv_text: Two {things} have I required of thee; deny me {them} not before I die: {deny...: Heb. withhold not from me}
verses.nlt_text: O God, I beg two favors from you; let me have them before I die.

verses.kjv_text: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: {convenient...: Heb. of my allowance}
verses.nlt_text: First, help me never to tell a lie. Second, give me neither poverty nor riches! Give me just enough to satisfy my needs.

verses.kjv_text: Lest I be full, and deny {thee}, and say, Who {is} the LORD? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God {in vain}. {deny...: Heb. belie thee}
verses.nlt_text: For if I grow rich, I may deny you and say, "Who is the LORD?" And if I am too poor, I may steal and thus insult God's holy name.

verses.kjv_text: Accuse not a servant unto his master, lest he curse thee, and thou be found guilty. {Accuse...: Heb. Hurt not with thy tongue}
verses.nlt_text: Never slander a worker to the employer, or the person will curse you, and you will pay for it.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} a generation {that} curseth their father, and doth not bless their mother.
verses.nlt_text: Some people curse their father and do not thank their mother.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} a generation {that are} pure in their own eyes, and {yet} is not washed from their filthiness.
verses.nlt_text: They are pure in their own eyes, but they are filthy and unwashed.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} a generation, O how lofty are their eyes! and their eyelids are lifted up.
verses.nlt_text: They look proudly around, casting disdainful glances.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} a generation, whose teeth {are as} swords, and their jaw teeth {as} knives, to devour the poor from off the earth, and the needy from {among} men.
verses.nlt_text: They have teeth like swords and fangs like knives. They devour the poor from the earth and the needy from among humanity.

verses.kjv_text: The horseleach hath two daughters, {crying}, Give, give. There are three {things that} are never satisfied, {yea}, four {things} say not, {It is} enough: {It is...: Heb. Wealth}
verses.nlt_text: The leech has two suckers that cry out, "More, more!" There are three things that are never satisfied-- no, four that never say, "Enough!":

verses.kjv_text: The grave; and the barren womb; the earth {that} is not filled with water; and the fire {that} saith not, {It is} enough.
verses.nlt_text: the grave, the barren womb, the thirsty desert, the blazing fire.

verses.kjv_text: The eye {that} mocketh at {his} father, and despiseth to obey {his} mother, the ravens of the valley shall pick it out, and the young eagles shall eat it. {the valley: or, the brook}
verses.nlt_text: The eye that mocks a father and despises a mother's instructions will be plucked out by ravens of the valley and eaten by vultures.

verses.kjv_text: There be three {things which} are too wonderful for me, yea, four which I know not:
verses.nlt_text: There are three things that amaze me-- no, four things that I don't understand:

verses.kjv_text: The way of an eagle in the air; the way of a serpent upon a rock; the way of a ship in the midst of the sea; and the way of a man with a maid. {midst: Heb. heart}
verses.nlt_text: how an eagle glides through the sky, how a snake slithers on a rock, how a ship navigates the ocean, how a man loves a woman.

verses.kjv_text: Such {is} the way of an adulterous woman; she eateth, and wipeth her mouth, and saith, I have done no wickedness.
verses.nlt_text: An adulterous woman consumes a man, then wipes her mouth and says, "What's wrong with that?"

verses.kjv_text: For three {things} the earth is disquieted, and for four {which} it cannot bear:
verses.nlt_text: There are three things that make the earth tremble-- no, four it cannot endure:

verses.kjv_text: For a servant when he reigneth; and a fool when he is filled with meat;
verses.nlt_text: a slave who becomes a king, an overbearing fool who prospers,

verses.kjv_text: For an odious {woman} when she is married; and an handmaid that is heir to her mistress.
verses.nlt_text: a bitter woman who finally gets a husband, a servant girl who supplants her mistress.

verses.kjv_text: There be four {things which are} little upon the earth, but they {are} exceeding wise: {exceeding...: Heb. wise, made wise}
verses.nlt_text: There are four things on earth that are small but unusually wise:

verses.kjv_text: The ants {are} a people not strong, yet they prepare their meat in the summer;
verses.nlt_text: Ants-- they aren't strong, but they store up food all summer.

verses.kjv_text: The conies {are but} a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks;
verses.nlt_text: Hyraxes-- they aren't powerful, but they make their homes among the rocks.

verses.kjv_text: The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands; {by...: Heb. gathered together}
verses.nlt_text: Locusts-- they have no king, but they march in formation.

verses.kjv_text: The spider taketh hold with her hands, and is in kings' palaces.
verses.nlt_text: Lizards-- they are easy to catch, but they are found even in kings' palaces.

verses.kjv_text: There be three {things} which go well, yea, four are comely in going:
verses.nlt_text: There are three things that walk with stately stride-- no, four that strut about:

verses.kjv_text: A lion {which is} strongest among beasts, and turneth not away for any;
verses.nlt_text: the lion, king of animals, who won't turn aside for anything,

verses.kjv_text: A greyhound; an he goat also; and a king, against whom {there is} no rising up. {greyhound: or, horse: Heb. girt in the loins}
verses.nlt_text: the strutting rooster, the male goat, a king as he leads his army.

verses.kjv_text: If thou hast done foolishly in lifting up thyself, or if thou hast thought evil, {lay} thine hand upon thy mouth.
verses.nlt_text: If you have been a fool by being proud or plotting evil, cover your mouth in shame.

verses.kjv_text: Surely the churning of milk bringeth forth butter, and the wringing of the nose bringeth forth blood: so the forcing of wrath bringeth forth strife.
verses.nlt_text: As the beating of cream yields butter and striking the nose causes bleeding, so stirring up anger causes quarrels.

verses.kjv_text: The words of king Lemuel, the prophecy that his mother taught him.
verses.nlt_text: The sayings of King Lemuel contain this message, which his mother taught him.

verses.kjv_text: What, my son? and what, the son of my womb? and what, the son of my vows?
verses.nlt_text: O my son, O son of my womb, O son of my vows,

verses.kjv_text: Give not thy strength unto women, nor thy ways to that which destroyeth kings.
verses.nlt_text: do not waste your strength on women, on those who ruin kings.

verses.kjv_text: {It is} not for kings, O Lemuel, {it is} not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink:
verses.nlt_text: It is not for kings, O Lemuel, to guzzle wine. Rulers should not crave alcohol.

verses.kjv_text: Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted. {prevert: Heb. alter} {of any...: Heb. of all the sons of affliction}
verses.nlt_text: For if they drink, they may forget the law and not give justice to the oppressed.

verses.kjv_text: Give strong drink unto him that is ready to perish, and wine unto those that be of heavy hearts. {of...: Heb. bitter of soul}
verses.nlt_text: Alcohol is for the dying, and wine for those in bitter distress.

verses.kjv_text: Let him drink, and forget his poverty, and remember his misery no more.
verses.nlt_text: Let them drink to forget their poverty and remember their troubles no more.

verses.kjv_text: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. {such...: Heb. the sons of destruction}
verses.nlt_text: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves; ensure justice for those being crushed.

verses.kjv_text: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, speak up for the poor and helpless, and see that they get justice.

verses.kjv_text: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price {is} far above rubies.
verses.nlt_text: Who can find a virtuous and capable wife? She is more precious than rubies.

verses.kjv_text: The heart of her husband doth safely trust in her, so that he shall have no need of spoil.
verses.nlt_text: Her husband can trust her, and she will greatly enrich his life.

verses.kjv_text: She will do him good and not evil all the days of her life.
verses.nlt_text: She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life.

verses.kjv_text: She seeketh wool, and flax, and worketh willingly with her hands.
verses.nlt_text: She finds wool and flax and busily spins it.

verses.kjv_text: She is like the merchants' ships; she bringeth her food from afar.
verses.nlt_text: She is like a merchant's ship, bringing her food from afar.

verses.kjv_text: She riseth also while it is yet night, and giveth meat to her household, and a portion to her maidens.
verses.nlt_text: She gets up before dawn to prepare breakfast for her household and plan the day's work for her servant girls.

verses.kjv_text: She considereth a field, and buyeth it: with the fruit of her hands she planteth a vineyard. {buyeth: Heb. taketh}
verses.nlt_text: She goes to inspect a field and buys it; with her earnings she plants a vineyard.

verses.kjv_text: She girdeth her loins with strength, and strengtheneth her arms.
verses.nlt_text: She is energetic and strong, a hard worker.

verses.kjv_text: She perceiveth that her merchandise {is} good: her candle goeth not out by night. {She...: Heb. She tasteth}
verses.nlt_text: She makes sure her dealings are profitable; her lamp burns late into the night.

verses.kjv_text: She layeth her hands to the spindle, and her hands hold the distaff.
verses.nlt_text: Her hands are busy spinning thread, her fingers twisting fiber.

verses.kjv_text: She stretcheth out her hand to the poor; yea, she reacheth forth her hands to the needy. {She...: Heb. She spreadeth}
verses.nlt_text: She extends a helping hand to the poor and opens her arms to the needy.

verses.kjv_text: She is not afraid of the snow for her household: for all her household {are} clothed with scarlet. {scarlet: or, double garments}
verses.nlt_text: She has no fear of winter for her household, for everyone has warm clothes.

verses.kjv_text: She maketh herself coverings of tapestry; her clothing {is} silk and purple.
verses.nlt_text: She makes her own bedspreads. She dresses in fine linen and purple gowns.

verses.kjv_text: Her husband is known in the gates, when he sitteth among the elders of the land.
verses.nlt_text: Her husband is well known at the city gates, where he sits with the other civic leaders.

verses.kjv_text: She maketh fine linen, and selleth {it}; and delivereth girdles unto the merchant.
verses.nlt_text: She makes belted linen garments and sashes to sell to the merchants.

verses.kjv_text: Strength and honour {are} her clothing; and she shall rejoice in time to come.
verses.nlt_text: She is clothed with strength and dignity, and she laughs without fear of the future.

verses.kjv_text: She openeth her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue {is} the law of kindness.
verses.nlt_text: When she speaks, her words are wise, and she gives instructions with kindness.

verses.kjv_text: She looketh well to the ways of her household, and eateth not the bread of idleness.
verses.nlt_text: She carefully watches everything in her household and suffers nothing from laziness.

verses.kjv_text: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband {also}, and he praiseth her.
verses.nlt_text: Her children stand and bless her. Her husband praises her:

verses.kjv_text: Many daughters have done virtuously, but thou excellest them all. {have...: or, have gotten riches}
verses.nlt_text: "There are many virtuous and capable women in the world, but you surpass them all!"

verses.kjv_text: Favour {is} deceitful, and beauty {is} vain: {but} a woman {that} feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
verses.nlt_text: Charm is deceptive, and beauty does not last; but a woman who fears the LORD will be greatly praised.

verses.kjv_text: Give her of the fruit of her hands; and let her own works praise her in the gates.
verses.nlt_text: Reward her for all she has done. Let her deeds publicly declare her praise.

verses.kjv_text: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: These are the words of the Teacher, King David's son, who ruled in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all {is} vanity.
verses.nlt_text: "Everything is meaningless," says the Teacher, "completely meaningless!"

verses.kjv_text: What profit hath a man of all his labour which he taketh under the sun?
verses.nlt_text: What do people get for all their hard work under the sun?

verses.kjv_text: {One} generation passeth away, and {another} generation cometh: but the earth abideth for ever.
verses.nlt_text: Generations come and generations go, but the earth never changes.

verses.kjv_text: The sun also ariseth, and the sun goeth down, and hasteth to his place where he arose. {hasteth: Heb. panteth}
verses.nlt_text: The sun rises and the sun sets, then hurries around to rise again.

verses.kjv_text: The wind goeth toward the south, and turneth about unto the north; it whirleth about continually, and the wind returneth again according to his circuits.
verses.nlt_text: The wind blows south, and then turns north. Around and around it goes, blowing in circles.

verses.kjv_text: All the rivers run into the sea; yet the sea {is} not full; unto the place from whence the rivers come, thither they return again. {return...: Heb. return to go}
verses.nlt_text: Rivers run into the sea, but the sea is never full. Then the water returns again to the rivers and flows out again to the sea.

verses.kjv_text: All things {are} full of labour; man cannot utter {it}: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.nlt_text: Everything is wearisome beyond description. No matter how much we see, we are never satisfied. No matter how much we hear, we are not content.

verses.kjv_text: The thing that hath been, it {is that} which shall be; and that which is done {is} that which shall be done: and {there is} no new {thing} under the sun.
verses.nlt_text: History merely repeats itself. It has all been done before. Nothing under the sun is truly new.

verses.kjv_text: Is there {any} thing whereof it may be said, See, this {is} new? it hath been already of old time, which was before us.
verses.nlt_text: Sometimes people say, "Here is something new!" But actually it is old; nothing is ever truly new.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} no remembrance of former {things}; neither shall there be {any} remembrance of {things} that are to come with {those} that shall come after.
verses.nlt_text: We don't remember what happened in the past, and in future generations, no one will remember what we are doing now.

verses.kjv_text: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: I, the Teacher, was king of Israel, and I lived in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: And I gave my heart to seek and search out by wisdom concerning all {things} that are done under heaven: this sore travail hath God given to the sons of man to be exercised therewith. {to be...: or, to afflict them}
verses.nlt_text: I devoted myself to search for understanding and to explore by wisdom everything being done under heaven. I soon discovered that God has dealt a tragic existence to the human race.

verses.kjv_text: I have seen all the works that are done under the sun; and, behold, all {is} vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.nlt_text: I observed everything going on under the sun, and really, it is all meaningless-- like chasing the wind.

verses.kjv_text: {That which is} crooked cannot be made straight: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered. {that which is wanting: Heb. defect}
verses.nlt_text: What is wrong cannot be made right. What is missing cannot be recovered.

verses.kjv_text: I communed with mine own heart, saying, Lo, I am come to great estate, and have gotten more wisdom than all {they} that have been before me in Jerusalem: yea, my heart had great experience of wisdom and knowledge. {had...: Heb. had seen much}
verses.nlt_text: I said to myself, "Look, I am wiser than any of the kings who ruled in Jerusalem before me. I have greater wisdom and knowledge than any of them."

verses.kjv_text: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
verses.nlt_text: So I set out to learn everything from wisdom to madness and folly. But I learned firsthand that pursuing all this is like chasing the wind.

verses.kjv_text: For in much wisdom {is} much grief: and he that increaseth knowledge increaseth sorrow.
verses.nlt_text: The greater my wisdom, the greater my grief. To increase knowledge only increases sorrow.

verses.kjv_text: I said in mine heart, Go to now, I will prove thee with mirth, therefore enjoy pleasure: and, behold, this also {is} vanity.
verses.nlt_text: I said to myself, "Come on, let's try pleasure. Let's look for the 'good things' in life." But I found that this, too, was meaningless.

verses.kjv_text: I said of laughter, {It is} mad: and of mirth, What doeth it?
verses.nlt_text: So I said, "Laughter is silly. What good does it do to seek pleasure?"

verses.kjv_text: I sought in mine heart to give myself unto wine, yet acquainting mine heart with wisdom; and to lay hold on folly, till I might see what {was} that good for the sons of men, which they should do under the heaven all the days of their life. {to give...: Heb. to draw my flesh with wine} {all...: Heb. the number of the days of their life}
verses.nlt_text: After much thought, I decided to cheer myself with wine. And while still seeking wisdom, I clutched at foolishness. In this way, I tried to experience the only happiness most people find during their brief life in this world.

verses.kjv_text: I made me great works; I builded me houses; I planted me vineyards:
verses.nlt_text: I also tried to find meaning by building huge homes for myself and by planting beautiful vineyards.

verses.kjv_text: I made me gardens and orchards, and I planted trees in them of all {kind of} fruits:
verses.nlt_text: I made gardens and parks, filling them with all kinds of fruit trees.

verses.kjv_text: I made me pools of water, to water therewith the wood that bringeth forth trees:
verses.nlt_text: I built reservoirs to collect the water to irrigate my many flourishing groves.

verses.kjv_text: I got {me} servants and maidens, and had servants born in my house; also I had great possessions of great and small cattle above all that were in Jerusalem before me: {servants born...: Heb. sons of my house}
verses.nlt_text: I bought slaves, both men and women, and others were born into my household. I also owned large herds and flocks, more than any of the kings who had lived in Jerusalem before me.

verses.kjv_text: I gathered me also silver and gold, and the peculiar treasure of kings and of the provinces: I gat me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men, {as} musical instruments, and that of all sorts. {musical...: Heb. musical instrument and instruments}
verses.nlt_text: I collected great sums of silver and gold, the treasure of many kings and provinces. I hired wonderful singers, both men and women, and had many beautiful concubines. I had everything a man could desire!

verses.kjv_text: So I was great, and increased more than all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom remained with me.
verses.nlt_text: So I became greater than all who had lived in Jerusalem before me, and my wisdom never failed me.

verses.kjv_text: And whatsoever mine eyes desired I kept not from them, I withheld not my heart from any joy; for my heart rejoiced in all my labour: and this was my portion of all my labour.
verses.nlt_text: Anything I wanted, I would take. I denied myself no pleasure. I even found great pleasure in hard work, a reward for all my labors.

verses.kjv_text: Then I looked on all the works that my hands had wrought, and on the labour that I had laboured to do: and, behold, all {was} vanity and vexation of spirit, and {there was} no profit under the sun.
verses.nlt_text: But as I looked at everything I had worked so hard to accomplish, it was all so meaningless-- like chasing the wind. There was nothing really worthwhile anywhere.

verses.kjv_text: And I turned myself to behold wisdom, and madness, and folly: for what {can} the man {do} that cometh after the king? {even} that which hath been already done. {even...: or, in those things which have been already done}
verses.nlt_text: So I decided to compare wisdom with foolishness and madness (for who can do this better than I, the king?).

verses.kjv_text: Then I saw that wisdom excelleth folly, as far as light excelleth darkness. {that...: Heb. that there is an excellency in wisdom more than in folly, etc}
verses.nlt_text: I thought, "Wisdom is better than foolishness, just as light is better than darkness.

verses.kjv_text: The wise man's eyes {are} in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness: and I myself perceived also that one event happeneth to them all.
verses.nlt_text: For the wise can see where they are going, but fools walk in the dark." Yet I saw that the wise and the foolish share the same fate.

verses.kjv_text: Then said I in my heart, As it happeneth to the fool, so it happeneth even to me; and why was I then more wise? Then I said in my heart, that this also {is} vanity. {happeneth even...: Heb. happeneth to me, even to me}
verses.nlt_text: Both will die. So I said to myself, "Since I will end up the same as the fool, what's the value of all my wisdom? This is all so meaningless!"

verses.kjv_text: For {there is} no remembrance of the wise more than of the fool for ever; seeing that which now {is} in the days to come shall all be forgotten. And how dieth the wise {man}? as the fool.
verses.nlt_text: For the wise and the foolish both die. The wise will not be remembered any longer than the fool. In the days to come, both will be forgotten.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore I hated life; because the work that is wrought under the sun {is} grievous unto me: for all {is} vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.nlt_text: So I came to hate life because everything done here under the sun is so troubling. Everything is meaningless-- like chasing the wind.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, I hated all my labour which I had taken under the sun: because I should leave it unto the man that shall be after me. {taken: Heb. laboured}
verses.nlt_text: I came to hate all my hard work here on earth, for I must leave to others everything I have earned.

verses.kjv_text: And who knoweth whether he shall be a wise {man} or a fool? yet shall he have rule over all my labour wherein I have laboured, and wherein I have shewed myself wise under the sun. This {is} also vanity.
verses.nlt_text: And who can tell whether my successors will be wise or foolish? Yet they will control everything I have gained by my skill and hard work under the sun. How meaningless!

verses.kjv_text: Therefore I went about to cause my heart to despair of all the labour which I took under the sun.
verses.nlt_text: So I gave up in despair, questioning the value of all my hard work in this world.

verses.kjv_text: For there is a man whose labour {is} in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in equity; yet to a man that hath not laboured therein shall he leave it {for} his portion. This also {is} vanity and a great evil. {leave: Heb. give}
verses.nlt_text: Some people work wisely with knowledge and skill, then must leave the fruit of their efforts to someone who hasn't worked for it. This, too, is meaningless, a great tragedy.

verses.kjv_text: For what hath man of all his labour, and of the vexation of his heart, wherein he hath laboured under the sun?
verses.nlt_text: So what do people get in this life for all their hard work and anxiety?

verses.kjv_text: For all his days {are} sorrows, and his travail grief; yea, his heart taketh not rest in the night. This is also vanity.
verses.nlt_text: Their days of labor are filled with pain and grief; even at night their minds cannot rest. It is all meaningless.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} nothing better for a man, {than} that he should eat and drink, and {that} he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it {was} from the hand of God. {should make...: or, delight his senses}
verses.nlt_text: So I decided there is nothing better than to enjoy food and drink and to find satisfaction in work. Then I realized that these pleasures are from the hand of God.

verses.kjv_text: For who can eat, or who else can hasten {hereunto}, more than I?
verses.nlt_text: For who can eat or enjoy anything apart from him?

verses.kjv_text: For {God} giveth to a man that {is} good in his sight wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but to the sinner he giveth travail, to gather and to heap up, that he may give to {him that is} good before God. This also {is} vanity and vexation of spirit. {in his...: Heb. before him}
verses.nlt_text: God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to those who please him. But if a sinner becomes wealthy, God takes the wealth away and gives it to those who please him. This, too, is meaningless-- like chasing the wind.

verses.kjv_text: To every {thing there is} a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
verses.nlt_text: For everything there is a season, a time for every activity under heaven.

verses.kjv_text: A time to be born, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up {that which is} planted; {to be...: Heb. to bear}
verses.nlt_text: A time to be born and a time to die. A time to plant and a time to harvest.

verses.kjv_text: A time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to break down, and a time to build up;
verses.nlt_text: A time to kill and a time to heal. A time to tear down and a time to build up.

verses.kjv_text: A time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
verses.nlt_text: A time to cry and a time to laugh. A time to grieve and a time to dance.

verses.kjv_text: A time to cast away stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to refrain from embracing; {to refrain from: Heb. to be far from}
verses.nlt_text: A time to scatter stones and a time to gather stones. A time to embrace and a time to turn away.

verses.kjv_text: A time to get, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away; {get: or, seek}
verses.nlt_text: A time to search and a time to quit searching. A time to keep and a time to throw away.

verses.kjv_text: A time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to keep silence, and a time to speak;
verses.nlt_text: A time to tear and a time to mend. A time to be quiet and a time to speak.

verses.kjv_text: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
verses.nlt_text: A time to love and a time to hate. A time for war and a time for peace.

verses.kjv_text: What profit hath he that worketh in that wherein he laboureth?
verses.nlt_text: What do people really get for all their hard work?

verses.kjv_text: I have seen the travail, which God hath given to the sons of men to be exercised in it.
verses.nlt_text: I have seen the burden God has placed on us all.

verses.kjv_text: He hath made every {thing} beautiful in his time: also he hath set the world in their heart, so that no man can find out the work that God maketh from the beginning to the end.
verses.nlt_text: Yet God has made everything beautiful for its own time. He has planted eternity in the human heart, but even so, people cannot see the whole scope of God's work from beginning to end.

verses.kjv_text: I know that {there is} no good in them, but for {a man} to rejoice, and to do good in his life.
verses.nlt_text: So I concluded there is nothing better than to be happy and enjoy ourselves as long as we can.

verses.kjv_text: And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it {is} the gift of God.
verses.nlt_text: And people should eat and drink and enjoy the fruits of their labor, for these are gifts from God.

verses.kjv_text: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth {it}, that {men} should fear before him.
verses.nlt_text: And I know that whatever God does is final. Nothing can be added to it or taken from it. God's purpose is that people should fear him.

verses.kjv_text: That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past. {that which is past: Heb. that which is driven away}
verses.nlt_text: What is happening now has happened before, and what will happen in the future has happened before, because God makes the same things happen over and over again.

verses.kjv_text: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, {that} wickedness {was} there; and the place of righteousness, {that} iniquity {was} there.
verses.nlt_text: I also noticed that under the sun there is evil in the courtroom. Yes, even the courts of law are corrupt!

verses.kjv_text: I said in mine heart, God shall judge the righteous and the wicked: for {there is} a time there for every purpose and for every work.
verses.nlt_text: I said to myself, "In due season God will judge everyone, both good and bad, for all their deeds."

verses.kjv_text: I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts. {that God...: or, that they might clear God, and see, etc}
verses.nlt_text: I also thought about the human condition-- how God proves to people that they are like animals.

verses.kjv_text: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts; even one thing befalleth them: as the one dieth, so dieth the other; yea, they have all one breath; so that a man hath no preeminence above a beast: for all {is} vanity.
verses.nlt_text: For people and animals share the same fate-- both breathe and both must die. So people have no real advantage over the animals. How meaningless!

verses.kjv_text: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
verses.nlt_text: Both go to the same place-- they came from dust and they return to dust.

verses.kjv_text: Who knoweth the spirit of man that goeth upward, and the spirit of the beast that goeth downward to the earth? {of man: Heb. of the sons of man} {goeth upward: Heb. is ascending, etc}
verses.nlt_text: For who can prove that the human spirit goes up and the spirit of animals goes down into the earth?

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore I perceive that {there is} nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his own works; for that {is} his portion: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
verses.nlt_text: So I saw that there is nothing better for people than to be happy in their work. That is why we are here! No one will bring us back from death to enjoy life after we die.

verses.kjv_text: So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of {such as were} oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors {there was} power; but they had no comforter. {side: Heb. hand}
verses.nlt_text: Again, I observed all the oppression that takes place under the sun. I saw the tears of the oppressed, with no one to comfort them. The oppressors have great power, and their victims are helpless.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore I praised the dead which are already dead more than the living which are yet alive.
verses.nlt_text: So I concluded that the dead are better off than the living.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, better {is he} than both they, which hath not yet been, who hath not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.nlt_text: But most fortunate of all are those who are not yet born. For they have not seen all the evil that is done under the sun.

verses.kjv_text: Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This {is} also vanity and vexation of spirit. {every...: Heb. all the rightness of work} {for this...: Heb. this is the envy of a man from his neighbour}
verses.nlt_text: Then I observed that most people are motivated to success because they envy their neighbors. But this, too, is meaningless-- like chasing the wind.

verses.kjv_text: The fool foldeth his hands together, and eateth his own flesh.
verses.nlt_text: "Fools fold their idle hands, leading them to ruin."

verses.kjv_text: Better {is} an handful {with} quietness, than both the hands full {with} travail and vexation of spirit.
verses.nlt_text: And yet, "Better to have one handful with quietness than two handfuls with hard work and chasing the wind."

verses.kjv_text: Then I returned, and I saw vanity under the sun.
verses.nlt_text: I observed yet another example of something meaningless under the sun.

verses.kjv_text: There is one {alone}, and {there is} not a second; yea, he hath neither child nor brother: yet {is there} no end of all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with riches; neither {saith he}, For whom do I labour, and bereave my soul of good? This {is} also vanity, yea, it {is} a sore travail.
verses.nlt_text: This is the case of a man who is all alone, without a child or a brother, yet who works hard to gain as much wealth as he can. But then he asks himself, "Who am I working for? Why am I giving up so much pleasure now?" It is all so meaningless and depressing.

verses.kjv_text: Two {are} better than one; because they have a good reward for their labour.
verses.nlt_text: Two people are better off than one, for they can help each other succeed.

verses.kjv_text: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him {that is} alone when he falleth; for {he hath} not another to help him up.
verses.nlt_text: If one person falls, the other can reach out and help. But someone who falls alone is in real trouble.

verses.kjv_text: Again, if two lie together, then they have heat: but how can one be warm {alone}?
verses.nlt_text: Likewise, two people lying close together can keep each other warm. But how can one be warm alone?

verses.kjv_text: And if one prevail against him, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
verses.nlt_text: A person standing alone can be attacked and defeated, but two can stand back-to-back and conquer. Three are even better, for a triple-braided cord is not easily broken.

verses.kjv_text: Better {is} a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished. {who...: Heb. who knoweth not to be admonished}
verses.nlt_text: It is better to be a poor but wise youth than an old and foolish king who refuses all advice.

verses.kjv_text: For out of prison he cometh to reign; whereas also {he that is} born in his kingdom becometh poor.
verses.nlt_text: Such a youth could rise from poverty and succeed. He might even become king, though he has been in prison.

verses.kjv_text: I considered all the living which walk under the sun, with the second child that shall stand up in his stead.
verses.nlt_text: But then everyone rushes to the side of yet another youth who replaces him.

verses.kjv_text: {There is} no end of all the people, {even} of all that have been before them: they also that come after shall not rejoice in him. Surely this also {is} vanity and vexation of spirit.
verses.nlt_text: Endless crowds stand around him, but then another generation grows up and rejects him, too. So it is all meaningless-- like chasing the wind.

verses.kjv_text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
