verses.nlt_text: As you enter the house of God, keep your ears open and your mouth shut. It is evil to make mindless offerings to God.

verses.kjv_text: Be not rash with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be hasty to utter {any} thing before God: for God {is} in heaven, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few. {thing: or, word}
verses.nlt_text: Don't make rash promises, and don't be hasty in bringing matters before God. After all, God is in heaven, and you are here on earth. So let your words be few.

verses.kjv_text: For a dream cometh through the multitude of business; and a fool's voice {is known} by multitude of words.
verses.nlt_text: Too much activity gives you restless dreams; too many words make you a fool.

verses.kjv_text: When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for {he hath} no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed.
verses.nlt_text: When you make a promise to God, don't delay in following through, for God takes no pleasure in fools. Keep all the promises you make to him.

verses.kjv_text: Better {is it} that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.
verses.nlt_text: It is better to say nothing than to make a promise and not keep it.

verses.kjv_text: Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it {was} an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?
verses.nlt_text: Don't let your mouth make you sin. And don't defend yourself by telling the Temple messenger that the promise you made was a mistake. That would make God angry, and he might wipe out everything you have achieved.

verses.kjv_text: For in the multitude of dreams and many words {there are} also {divers} vanities: but fear thou God.
verses.nlt_text: Talk is cheap, like daydreams and other useless activities. Fear God instead.

verses.kjv_text: If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for {he that is} higher than the highest regardeth; and {there be} higher than they. {at the... Heb. at the will, or, purpose}
verses.nlt_text: Don't be surprised if you see a poor person being oppressed by the powerful and if justice is being miscarried throughout the land. For every official is under orders from higher up, and matters of justice get lost in red tape and bureaucracy.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover the profit of the earth is for all: the king {himself} is served by the field.
verses.nlt_text: Even the king milks the land for his own profit!

verses.kjv_text: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver; nor he that loveth abundance with increase: this {is} also vanity.
verses.nlt_text: Those who love money will never have enough. How meaningless to think that wealth brings true happiness!

verses.kjv_text: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them: and what good {is there} to the owners thereof, saving the beholding {of them} with their eyes?
verses.nlt_text: The more you have, the more people come to help you spend it. So what good is wealth-- except perhaps to watch it slip through your fingers!

verses.kjv_text: The sleep of a labouring man {is} sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.
verses.nlt_text: People who work hard sleep well, whether they eat little or much. But the rich seldom get a good night's sleep.

verses.kjv_text: There is a sore evil {which} I have seen under the sun, {namely}, riches kept for the owners thereof to their hurt.
verses.nlt_text: There is another serious problem I have seen under the sun. Hoarding riches harms the saver.

verses.kjv_text: But those riches perish by evil travail: and he begetteth a son, and {there is} nothing in his hand.
verses.nlt_text: Money is put into risky investments that turn sour, and everything is lost. In the end, there is nothing left to pass on to one's children.

verses.kjv_text: As he came forth of his mother's womb, naked shall he return to go as he came, and shall take nothing of his labour, which he may carry away in his hand.
verses.nlt_text: We all come to the end of our lives as naked and empty-handed as on the day we were born. We can't take our riches with us.

verses.kjv_text: And this also {is} a sore evil, {that} in all points as he came, so shall he go: and what profit hath he that hath laboured for the wind?
verses.nlt_text: And this, too, is a very serious problem. People leave this world no better off than when they came. All their hard work is for nothing-- like working for the wind.

verses.kjv_text: All his days also he eateth in darkness, and {he hath} much sorrow and wrath with his sickness.
verses.nlt_text: Throughout their lives, they live under a cloud-- frustrated, discouraged, and angry.

verses.kjv_text: Behold {that} which I have seen: {it is} good and comely {for one} to eat and to drink, and to enjoy the good of all his labour that he taketh under the sun all the days of his life, which God giveth him: for it {is} his portion. {It is good...: Heb. there is a good which is comely, etc} {all the days: Heb. the number of the days}
verses.nlt_text: Even so, I have noticed one thing, at least, that is good. It is good for people to eat, drink, and enjoy their work under the sun during the short life God has given them, and to accept their lot in life.

verses.kjv_text: Every man also to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and hath given him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this {is} the gift of God.
verses.nlt_text: And it is a good thing to receive wealth from God and the good health to enjoy it. To enjoy your work and accept your lot in life-- this is indeed a gift from God.

verses.kjv_text: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; because God answereth {him} in the joy of his heart. {For...: or, Though he give not much, yet he remembereth, etc}
verses.nlt_text: God keeps such people so busy enjoying life that they take no time to brood over the past.

verses.kjv_text: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it {is} common among men:
verses.nlt_text: There is another serious tragedy I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily on humanity.

verses.kjv_text: A man to whom God hath given riches, wealth, and honour, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he desireth, yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof, but a stranger eateth it: this {is} vanity, and it {is} an evil disease.
verses.nlt_text: God gives some people great wealth and honor and everything they could ever want, but then he doesn't give them the chance to enjoy these things. They die, and someone else, even a stranger, ends up enjoying their wealth! This is meaningless-- a sickening tragedy.

verses.kjv_text: If a man beget an hundred {children}, and live many years, so that the days of his years be many, and his soul be not filled with good, and also {that} he have no burial; I say, {that} an untimely birth {is} better than he.
verses.nlt_text: A man might have a hundred children and live to be very old. But if he finds no satisfaction in life and doesn't even get a decent burial, it would have been better for him to be born dead.

verses.kjv_text: For he cometh in with vanity, and departeth in darkness, and his name shall be covered with darkness.
verses.nlt_text: His birth would have been meaningless, and he would have ended in darkness. He wouldn't even have had a name,

verses.kjv_text: Moreover he hath not seen the sun, nor known {any thing}: this hath more rest than the other.
verses.nlt_text: and he would never have seen the sun or known of its existence. Yet he would have had more peace than in growing up to be an unhappy man.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, though he live a thousand years twice {told}, yet hath he seen no good: do not all go to one place?
verses.nlt_text: He might live a thousand years twice over but still not find contentment. And since he must die like everyone else-- well, what's the use?

verses.kjv_text: All the labour of man {is} for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled. {appetite: Heb. soul}
verses.nlt_text: All people spend their lives scratching for food, but they never seem to have enough.

verses.kjv_text: For what hath the wise more than the fool? what hath the poor, that knoweth to walk before the living?
verses.nlt_text: So are wise people really better off than fools? Do poor people gain anything by being wise and knowing how to act in front of others?

verses.kjv_text: Better {is} the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire: this {is} also vanity and vexation of spirit. {than...: Heb. than the walking of the soul}
verses.nlt_text: Enjoy what you have rather than desiring what you don't have. Just dreaming about nice things is meaningless-- like chasing the wind.

verses.kjv_text: That which hath been is named already, and it is known that it {is} man: neither may he contend with him that is mightier than he.
verses.nlt_text: Everything has already been decided. It was known long ago what each person would be. So there's no use arguing with God about your destiny.

verses.kjv_text: Seeing there be many things that increase vanity, what {is} man the better?
verses.nlt_text: The more words you speak, the less they mean. So what good are they?

verses.kjv_text: For who knoweth what {is} good for man in {this} life, all the days of his vain life which he spendeth as a shadow? for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun? {all...: Heb. the number of the days of the life of his vanity}
verses.nlt_text: In the few days of our meaningless lives, who knows how our days can best be spent? Our lives are like a shadow. Who can tell what will happen on this earth after we are gone?

verses.kjv_text: A good name {is} better than precious ointment; and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
verses.nlt_text: A good reputation is more valuable than costly perfume. And the day you die is better than the day you are born.

verses.kjv_text: {It is} better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that {is} the end of all men; and the living will lay {it} to his heart.
verses.nlt_text: Better to spend your time at funerals than at parties. After all, everyone dies-- so the living should take this to heart.

verses.kjv_text: Sorrow {is} better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart is made better. {Sorrow: or, Anger}
verses.nlt_text: Sorrow is better than laughter, for sadness has a refining influence on us.

verses.kjv_text: The heart of the wise {is} in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools {is} in the house of mirth.
verses.nlt_text: A wise person thinks a lot about death, while a fool thinks only about having a good time.

verses.kjv_text: {It is} better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools.
verses.nlt_text: Better to be criticized by a wise person than to be praised by a fool.

verses.kjv_text: For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so {is} the laughter of the fool: this also {is} vanity. {crackling: Heb. sound}
verses.nlt_text: A fool's laughter is quickly gone, like thorns crackling in a fire. This also is meaningless.

verses.kjv_text: Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
verses.nlt_text: Extortion turns wise people into fools, and bribes corrupt the heart.

verses.kjv_text: Better {is} the end of a thing than the beginning thereof: {and} the patient in spirit {is} better than the proud in spirit.
verses.nlt_text: Finishing is better than starting. Patience is better than pride.

verses.kjv_text: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.
verses.nlt_text: Control your temper, for anger labels you a fool.

verses.kjv_text: Say not thou, What is {the cause} that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this. {wisely: Heb. out of wisdom}
verses.nlt_text: Don't long for "the good old days." This is not wise.

verses.kjv_text: Wisdom {is} good with an inheritance: and {by it there is} profit to them that see the sun. {good...: or, as good as an inheritance, yea, better too}
verses.nlt_text: Wisdom is even better when you have money. Both are a benefit as you go through life.

verses.kjv_text: For wisdom {is} a defence, {and} money {is} a defence: but the excellency of knowledge {is, that} wisdom giveth life to them that have it. {defence: Heb. shadow}
verses.nlt_text: Wisdom and money can get you almost anything, but only wisdom can save your life.

verses.kjv_text: Consider the work of God: for who can make {that} straight, which he hath made crooked?
verses.nlt_text: Accept the way God does things, for who can straighten what he has made crooked?

verses.kjv_text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other, to the end that man should find nothing after him. {set: Heb. made}
verses.nlt_text: Enjoy prosperity while you can, but when hard times strike, realize that both come from God. Remember that nothing is certain in this life.

verses.kjv_text: All {things} have I seen in the days of my vanity: there is a just {man} that perisheth in his righteousness, and there is a wicked {man} that prolongeth {his life} in his wickedness.
verses.nlt_text: I have seen everything in this meaningless life, including the death of good young people and the long life of wicked people.

verses.kjv_text: Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself? {destroy...: Heb. be desolate?}
verses.nlt_text: So don't be too good or too wise! Why destroy yourself?

verses.kjv_text: Be not over much wicked, neither be thou foolish: why shouldest thou die before thy time? {before...: Heb. not in thy time?}
verses.nlt_text: On the other hand, don't be too wicked either. Don't be a fool! Why die before your time?

verses.kjv_text: {It is} good that thou shouldest take hold of this; yea, also from this withdraw not thine hand: for he that feareth God shall come forth of them all.
verses.nlt_text: Pay attention to these instructions, for anyone who fears God will avoid both extremes.

verses.kjv_text: Wisdom strengtheneth the wise more than ten mighty {men} which are in the city.
verses.nlt_text: One wise person is stronger than ten leading citizens of a town!

verses.kjv_text: For {there is} not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.
verses.nlt_text: Not a single person on earth is always good and never sins.

verses.kjv_text: Also take no heed unto all words that are spoken; lest thou hear thy servant curse thee: {take...: Heb. give not thine heart}
verses.nlt_text: Don't eavesdrop on others-- you may hear your servant curse you.

verses.kjv_text: For oftentimes also thine own heart knoweth that thou thyself likewise hast cursed others.
verses.nlt_text: For you know how often you yourself have cursed others.

verses.kjv_text: All this have I proved by wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it {was} far from me.
verses.nlt_text: I have always tried my best to let wisdom guide my thoughts and actions. I said to myself, "I am determined to be wise." But it didn't work.

verses.kjv_text: That which is far off, and exceeding deep, who can find it out?
verses.nlt_text: Wisdom is always distant and difficult to find.

verses.kjv_text: I applied mine heart to know, and to search, and to seek out wisdom, and the reason {of things}, and to know the wickedness of folly, even of foolishness {and} madness: {I applied...: Heb. I and mine heart compassed}
verses.nlt_text: I searched everywhere, determined to find wisdom and to understand the reason for things. I was determined to prove to myself that wickedness is stupid and that foolishness is madness.

verses.kjv_text: And I find more bitter than death the woman, whose heart {is} snares and nets, {and} her hands {as} bands: whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her. {whoso...: Heb. he that is good before God}
verses.nlt_text: I discovered that a seductive woman is a trap more bitter than death. Her passion is a snare, and her soft hands are chains. Those who are pleasing to God will escape her, but sinners will be caught in her snare.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, {counting} one by one, to find out the account: {counting...: or, weighing one thing after another, to find out the reason}
verses.nlt_text: "This is my conclusion," says the Teacher. "I discovered this after looking at the matter from every possible angle.

verses.kjv_text: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found; but a woman among all those have I not found.
verses.nlt_text: Though I have searched repeatedly, I have not found what I was looking for. Only one out of a thousand men is virtuous, but not one woman!

verses.kjv_text: Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions.
verses.nlt_text: But I did find this: God created people to be virtuous, but they have each turned to follow their own downward path."

verses.kjv_text: Who {is} as the wise {man}? and who knoweth the interpretation of a thing? a man's wisdom maketh his face to shine, and the boldness of his face shall be changed. {the boldness: Heb. the strength}
verses.nlt_text: How wonderful to be wise, to analyze and interpret things. Wisdom lights up a person's face, softening its harshness.

verses.kjv_text: I {counsel thee} to keep the king's commandment, and {that} in regard of the oath of God.
verses.nlt_text: Obey the king since you vowed to God that you would.

verses.kjv_text: Be not hasty to go out of his sight: stand not in an evil thing; for he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him.
verses.nlt_text: Don't try to avoid doing your duty, and don't stand with those who plot evil, for the king can do whatever he wants.

verses.kjv_text: Where the word of a king {is, there is} power: and who may say unto him, What doest thou?
verses.nlt_text: His command is backed by great power. No one can resist or question it.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso keepeth the commandment shall feel no evil thing: and a wise man's heart discerneth both time and judgment. {shall...: Heb. shall know}
verses.nlt_text: Those who obey him will not be punished. Those who are wise will find a time and a way to do what is right,

verses.kjv_text: Because to every purpose there is time and judgment, therefore the misery of man {is} great upon him.
verses.nlt_text: for there is a time and a way for everything, even when a person is in trouble.

verses.kjv_text: For he knoweth not that which shall be: for who can tell him when it shall be? {when...: or, how it shall be?}
verses.nlt_text: Indeed, how can people avoid what they don't know is going to happen?

verses.kjv_text: {There is} no man that hath power over the spirit to retain the spirit; neither {hath he} power in the day of death: and {there is} no discharge in {that} war; neither shall wickedness deliver those that are given to it. {discharge: or, casting off weapons}
verses.nlt_text: None of us can hold back our spirit from departing. None of us has the power to prevent the day of our death. There is no escaping that obligation, that dark battle. And in the face of death, wickedness will certainly not rescue the wicked.

verses.kjv_text: All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: {there is} a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.
verses.nlt_text: I have thought deeply about all that goes on here under the sun, where people have the power to hurt each other.

verses.kjv_text: And so I saw the wicked buried, who had come and gone from the place of the holy, and they were forgotten in the city where they had so done: this {is} also vanity.
verses.nlt_text: I have seen wicked people buried with honor. Yet they were the very ones who frequented the Temple and are now praised in the same city where they committed their crimes! This, too, is meaningless.

verses.kjv_text: Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.
verses.nlt_text: When a crime is not punished quickly, people feel it is safe to do wrong.

verses.kjv_text: Though a sinner do evil an hundred times, and his {days} be prolonged, yet surely I know that it shall be well with them that fear God, which fear before him:
verses.nlt_text: But even though a person sins a hundred times and still lives a long time, I know that those who fear God will be better off.

verses.kjv_text: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he prolong {his} days, {which are} as a shadow; because he feareth not before God.
verses.nlt_text: The wicked will not prosper, for they do not fear God. Their days will never grow long like the evening shadows.

verses.kjv_text: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there be just {men}, unto whom it happeneth according to the work of the wicked; again, there be wicked {men}, to whom it happeneth according to the work of the righteous: I said that this also {is} vanity.
verses.nlt_text: And this is not all that is meaningless in our world. In this life, good people are often treated as though they were wicked, and wicked people are often treated as though they were good. This is so meaningless!

verses.kjv_text: Then I commended mirth, because a man hath no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be merry: for that shall abide with him of his labour the days of his life, which God giveth him under the sun.
verses.nlt_text: So I recommend having fun, because there is nothing better for people in this world than to eat, drink, and enjoy life. That way they will experience some happiness along with all the hard work God gives them under the sun.

verses.kjv_text: When I applied mine heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done upon the earth: (for also {there is that} neither day nor night seeth sleep with his eyes:)
verses.nlt_text: In my search for wisdom and in my observation of people's burdens here on earth, I discovered that there is ceaseless activity, day and night.

verses.kjv_text: Then I beheld all the work of God, that a man cannot find out the work that is done under the sun: because though a man labour to seek {it} out, yet he shall not find {it}; yea further; though a wise {man} think to know {it}, yet shall he not be able to find {it}.
verses.nlt_text: I realized that no one can discover everything God is doing under the sun. Not even the wisest people discover everything, no matter what they claim.

verses.kjv_text: For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, {are} in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred {by} all {that is} before them. {I considered...: Heb. I gave, or, set to my heart}
verses.nlt_text: This, too, I carefully explored: Even though the actions of godly and wise people are in God's hands, no one knows whether God will show them favor.

verses.kjv_text: All {things come} alike to all: {there is} one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as {is} the good, so {is} the sinner; {and} he that sweareth, as {he} that feareth an oath.
verses.nlt_text: The same destiny ultimately awaits everyone, whether righteous or wicked, good or bad, ceremonially clean or unclean, religious or irreligious. Good people receive the same treatment as sinners, and people who make promises to God are treated like people who don't.

verses.kjv_text: This {is} an evil among all {things} that are done under the sun, that {there is} one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness {is} in their heart while they live, and after that {they go} to the dead.
verses.nlt_text: It seems so tragic that everyone under the sun suffers the same fate. That is why people are not more careful to be good. Instead, they choose their own mad course, for they have no hope. There is nothing ahead but death anyway.

verses.kjv_text: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.nlt_text: There is hope only for the living. As they say, "It's better to be a live dog than a dead lion!"

verses.kjv_text: For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten.
verses.nlt_text: The living at least know they will die, but the dead know nothing. They have no further reward, nor are they remembered.

verses.kjv_text: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any {thing} that is done under the sun.
verses.nlt_text: Whatever they did in their lifetime-- loving, hating, envying-- is all long gone. They no longer play a part in anything here on earth.

verses.kjv_text: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works.
verses.nlt_text: So go ahead. Eat your food with joy, and drink your wine with a happy heart, for God approves of this!

verses.kjv_text: Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment.
verses.nlt_text: Wear fine clothes, with a splash of cologne!

verses.kjv_text: Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that {is} thy portion in {this} life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun. {Live...: Heb. See, or, Enjoy life}
verses.nlt_text: Live happily with the woman you love through all the meaningless days of life that God has given you under the sun. The wife God gives you is your reward for all your earthly toil.

verses.kjv_text: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do {it} with thy might; for {there is} no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
verses.nlt_text: Whatever you do, do well. For when you go to the grave, there will be no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom.

verses.kjv_text: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race {is} not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.
verses.nlt_text: I have observed something else under the sun. The fastest runner doesn't always win the race, and the strongest warrior doesn't always win the battle. The wise sometimes go hungry, and the skillful are not necessarily wealthy. And those who are educated don't always lead successful lives. It is all decided by chance, by being in the right place at the right time.

verses.kjv_text: For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so {are} the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them.
verses.nlt_text: People can never predict when hard times might come. Like fish in a net or birds in a trap, people are caught by sudden tragedy.

verses.kjv_text: This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it {seemed} great unto me:
verses.nlt_text: Here is another bit of wisdom that has impressed me as I have watched the way our world works.

verses.kjv_text: {There was} a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:
verses.nlt_text: There was a small town with only a few people, and a great king came with his army and besieged it.

verses.kjv_text: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man.
verses.nlt_text: A poor, wise man knew how to save the town, and so it was rescued. But afterward no one thought to thank him.

verses.kjv_text: Then said I, Wisdom {is} better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom {is} despised, and his words are not heard.
verses.nlt_text: So even though wisdom is better than strength, those who are wise will be despised if they are poor. What they say will not be appreciated for long.

verses.kjv_text: The words of wise {men are} heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.
verses.nlt_text: Better to hear the quiet words of a wise person than the shouts of a foolish king.

verses.kjv_text: Wisdom {is} better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.
verses.nlt_text: Better to have wisdom than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much that is good.

verses.kjv_text: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: {so doth} a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom {and} honour. {Dead...: Heb. Flies of death}
verses.nlt_text: As dead flies cause even a bottle of perfume to stink, so a little foolishness spoils great wisdom and honor.

verses.kjv_text: A wise man's heart {is} at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.
verses.nlt_text: A wise person chooses the right road; a fool takes the wrong one.

verses.kjv_text: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth {him}, and he saith to every one {that} he {is} a fool. {his...: Heb. his heart}
verses.nlt_text: You can identify fools just by the way they walk down the street!

verses.kjv_text: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
verses.nlt_text: If your boss is angry at you, don't quit! A quiet spirit can overcome even great mistakes.

verses.kjv_text: There is an evil {which} I have seen under the sun, as an error {which} proceedeth from the ruler: {from: Heb. from before}
verses.nlt_text: There is another evil I have seen under the sun. Kings and rulers make a grave mistake

verses.kjv_text: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place. {in great...: Heb. in great heights}
verses.nlt_text: when they give great authority to foolish people and low positions to people of proven worth.

verses.kjv_text: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
verses.nlt_text: I have even seen servants riding horseback like princes-- and princes walking like servants!

verses.kjv_text: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
verses.nlt_text: When you dig a well, you might fall in. When you demolish an old wall, you could be bitten by a snake.

verses.kjv_text: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; {and} he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
verses.nlt_text: When you work in a quarry, stones might fall and crush you. When you chop wood, there is danger with each stroke of your ax.

verses.kjv_text: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom {is} profitable to direct.
verses.nlt_text: Using a dull ax requires great strength, so sharpen the blade. That's the value of wisdom; it helps you succeed.

verses.kjv_text: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better. {a babbler: Heb. the master of the tongue}
verses.nlt_text: If a snake bites before you charm it, what's the use of being a snake charmer?

verses.kjv_text: The words of a wise man's mouth {are} gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself. {gracious: Heb. grace}
verses.nlt_text: Wise words bring approval, but fools are destroyed by their own words.

verses.kjv_text: The beginning of the words of his mouth {is} foolishness: and the end of his talk {is} mischievous madness. {his talk: Heb. his mouth}
verses.nlt_text: Fools base their thoughts on foolish assumptions, so their conclusions will be wicked madness;

verses.kjv_text: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him? {is full...: Heb. multiplieth words}
verses.nlt_text: they chatter on and on. No one really knows what is going to happen; no one can predict the future.

verses.kjv_text: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
verses.nlt_text: Fools are so exhausted by a little work that they can't even find their way home.

verses.kjv_text: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king {is} a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
verses.nlt_text: What sorrow for the land ruled by a servant, the land whose leaders feast in the morning.

verses.kjv_text: Blessed {art} thou, O land, when thy king {is} the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
verses.nlt_text: Happy is the land whose king is a noble leader and whose leaders feast at the proper time to gain strength for their work, not to get drunk.

verses.kjv_text: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
verses.nlt_text: Laziness leads to a sagging roof; idleness leads to a leaky house.

verses.kjv_text: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all {things}. {maketh...: Heb. maketh glad the life}
verses.nlt_text: A party gives laughter, wine gives happiness, and money gives everything!

verses.kjv_text: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter. {thought: or, conscience}
verses.nlt_text: Never make light of the king, even in your thoughts. And don't make fun of the powerful, even in your own bedroom. For a little bird might deliver your message and tell them what you said.

verses.kjv_text: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days. {upon...: Heb. upon the face of the waters}
verses.nlt_text: Send your grain across the seas, and in time, profits will flow back to you.

verses.kjv_text: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth.
verses.nlt_text: But divide your investments among many places, for you do not know what risks might lie ahead.

verses.kjv_text: If the clouds be full of rain, they empty {themselves} upon the earth: and if the tree fall toward the south, or toward the north, in the place where the tree falleth, there it shall be.
verses.nlt_text: When clouds are heavy, the rains come down. Whether a tree falls north or south, it stays where it falls.

verses.kjv_text: He that observeth the wind shall not sow; and he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap.
verses.nlt_text: Farmers who wait for perfect weather never plant. If they watch every cloud, they never harvest.

verses.kjv_text: As thou knowest not what {is} the way of the spirit, {nor} how the bones {do grow} in the womb of her that is with child: even so thou knowest not the works of God who maketh all.
verses.nlt_text: Just as you cannot understand the path of the wind or the mystery of a tiny baby growing in its mother's womb, so you cannot understand the activity of God, who does all things.

verses.kjv_text: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both {shall be} alike good. {shall prosper: Heb. shall be right}
verses.nlt_text: Plant your seed in the morning and keep busy all afternoon, for you don't know if profit will come from one activity or another-- or maybe both.

verses.kjv_text: Truly the light {is} sweet, and a pleasant {thing it is} for the eyes to behold the sun:
verses.nlt_text: Light is sweet; how pleasant to see a new day dawning.

verses.kjv_text: But if a man live many years, {and} rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that cometh {is} vanity.
verses.nlt_text: When people live to be very old, let them rejoice in every day of life. But let them also remember there will be many dark days. Everything still to come is meaningless.

verses.kjv_text: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these {things} God will bring thee into judgment.
verses.nlt_text: Young people, it's wonderful to be young! Enjoy every minute of it. Do everything you want to do; take it all in. But remember that you must give an account to God for everything you do.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for childhood and youth {are} vanity. {sorrow: or, anger}
verses.nlt_text: So refuse to worry, and keep your body healthy. But remember that youth, with a whole life before you, is meaningless.

verses.kjv_text: Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them;
verses.nlt_text: Don't let the excitement of youth cause you to forget your Creator. Honor him in your youth before you grow old and say, "Life is not pleasant anymore."

verses.kjv_text: While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain:
verses.nlt_text: Remember him before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is dim to your old eyes, and rain clouds continually darken your sky.

verses.kjv_text: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, {the grinders...: or, the grinders fail, because they grind little}
verses.nlt_text: Remember him before your legs-- the guards of your house-- start to tremble; and before your shoulders-- the strong men-- stoop. Remember him before your teeth-- your few remaining servants-- stop grinding; and before your eyes-- the women looking through the windows-- see dimly.

verses.kjv_text: And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low;
verses.nlt_text: Remember him before the door to life's opportunities is closed and the sound of work fades. Now you rise at the first chirping of the birds, but then all their sounds will grow faint.

verses.kjv_text: Also {when} they shall be afraid of {that which is} high, and fears {shall be} in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets:
verses.nlt_text: Remember him before you become fearful of falling and worry about danger in the streets; before your hair turns white like an almond tree in bloom, and you drag along without energy like a dying grasshopper, and the caperberry no longer inspires sexual desire. Remember him before you near the grave, your everlasting home, when the mourners will weep at your funeral.

verses.kjv_text: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, remember your Creator now while you are young, before the silver cord of life snaps and the golden bowl is broken. Don't wait until the water jar is smashed at the spring and the pulley is broken at the well.

verses.kjv_text: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.
verses.nlt_text: For then the dust will return to the earth, and the spirit will return to God who gave it.

verses.kjv_text: Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all {is} vanity.
verses.nlt_text: "Everything is meaningless," says the Teacher, "completely meaningless."

verses.kjv_text: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, {and} set in order many proverbs. {moreover...: or, the more wise the preacher was, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Keep this in mind: The Teacher was considered wise, and he taught the people everything he knew. He listened carefully to many proverbs, studying and classifying them.

verses.kjv_text: The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and {that which was} written {was} upright, {even} words of truth. {acceptable...: Heb. words of delight}
verses.nlt_text: The Teacher sought to find just the right words to express truths clearly.

verses.kjv_text: The words of the wise {are} as goads, and as nails fastened {by} the masters of assemblies, {which} are given from one shepherd.
verses.nlt_text: The words of the wise are like cattle prods-- painful but helpful. Their collected sayings are like a nail-studded stick with which a shepherd drives the sheep.

verses.kjv_text: And further, by these, my son, be admonished: of making many books {there is} no end; and much study {is} a weariness of the flesh. {study: or, reading}
verses.nlt_text: But, my child, let me give you some further advice: Be careful, for writing books is endless, and much study wears you out.

verses.kjv_text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this {is} the whole {duty} of man. {Let...: or, The end of the matter, even all that hath been heard, is}
verses.nlt_text: That's the whole story. Here now is my final conclusion: Fear God and obey his commands, for this is everyone's duty.

verses.kjv_text: For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether {it be} good, or whether {it be} evil.
verses.nlt_text: God will judge us for everything we do, including every secret thing, whether good or bad.

verses.kjv_text: The song of songs, which {is} Solomon's.
verses.nlt_text: This is Solomon's song of songs, more wonderful than any other. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love {is} better than wine. {thy...: Heb. thy loves}
verses.nlt_text: Kiss me and kiss me again, for your love is sweeter than wine.

verses.kjv_text: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name {is as} ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.
verses.nlt_text: How fragrant your cologne; your name is like its spreading fragrance. No wonder all the young women love you!

verses.kjv_text: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee. {the upright...: or, they love thee uprightly}
verses.nlt_text: Take me with you; come, let's run! The king has brought me into his bedroom. Young Women of Jerusalem How happy we are for you, O king. We praise your love even more than wine. Young Woman How right they are to adore you.

verses.kjv_text: I {am} black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
verses.nlt_text: I am dark but beautiful, O women of Jerusalem-- dark as the tents of Kedar, dark as the curtains of Solomon's tents.

verses.kjv_text: Look not upon me, because I {am} black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; {but} mine own vineyard have I not kept.
verses.nlt_text: Don't stare at me because I am dark-- the sun has darkened my skin. My brothers were angry with me; they forced me to care for their vineyards, so I couldn't care for myself-- my own vineyard.

verses.kjv_text: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest {thy flock} to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions? {as one...: or, as one that is veiled}
verses.nlt_text: Tell me, my love, where are you leading your flock today? Where will you rest your sheep at noon? For why should I wander like a prostitute among your friends and their flocks? Young Man

verses.kjv_text: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.
verses.nlt_text: If you don't know, O most beautiful woman, follow the trail of my flock, and graze your young goats by the shepherds' tents.

verses.kjv_text: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.
verses.nlt_text: You are as exciting, my darling, as a mare among Pharaoh's stallions.

verses.kjv_text: Thy cheeks are comely with rows {of jewels}, thy neck with chains {of gold}.
verses.nlt_text: How lovely are your cheeks; your earrings set them afire! How lovely is your neck, enhanced by a string of jewels.

verses.kjv_text: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.
verses.nlt_text: We will make for you earrings of gold and beads of silver. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: While the king {sitteth} at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
verses.nlt_text: The king is lying on his couch, enchanted by the fragrance of my perfume.

verses.kjv_text: A bundle of myrrh {is} my wellbeloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
verses.nlt_text: My lover is like a sachet of myrrh lying between my breasts.

verses.kjv_text: My beloved {is} unto me {as} a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi. {camphire: or, cypress}
verses.nlt_text: He is like a bouquet of sweet henna blossoms from the vineyards of En-gedi. Young Man

verses.kjv_text: Behold, thou {art} fair, my love; behold, thou {art} fair; thou {hast} doves' eyes. {my love: or, my companion}
verses.nlt_text: How beautiful you are, my darling, how beautiful! Your eyes are like doves. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: Behold, thou {art} fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed {is} green.
verses.nlt_text: You are so handsome, my love, pleasing beyond words! The soft grass is our bed;

verses.kjv_text: The beams of our house {are} cedar, {and} our rafters of fir. {rafters: or, galleries}
verses.nlt_text: fragrant cedar branches are the beams of our house, and pleasant smelling firs are the rafters. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: I {am} the rose of Sharon, {and} the lily of the valleys.
verses.nlt_text: I am the spring crocus blooming on the Sharon Plain, the lily of the valley. Young Man

verses.kjv_text: As the lily among thorns, so {is} my love among the daughters.
verses.nlt_text: Like a lily among thistles is my darling among young women. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so {is} my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit {was} sweet to my taste. {I sat...: Heb. I delighted and sat down, etc} {taste: Heb. palate}
verses.nlt_text: Like the finest apple tree in the orchard is my lover among other young men. I sit in his delightful shade and taste his delicious fruit.

verses.kjv_text: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me {was} love. {banqueting...: Heb. house of wine}
verses.nlt_text: He escorts me to the banquet hall; it's obvious how much he loves me.

verses.kjv_text: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I {am} sick of love. {comfort...: Heb. straw me with apples}
verses.nlt_text: Strengthen me with raisin cakes, refresh me with apples, for I am weak with love.

verses.kjv_text: His left hand {is} under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.
verses.nlt_text: His left arm is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.

verses.kjv_text: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake {my} love, till he please. {I charge...: Heb. I adjure you}
verses.nlt_text: Promise me, O women of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and wild deer, not to awaken love until the time is right.

verses.kjv_text: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
verses.nlt_text: Ah, I hear my lover coming! He is leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.

verses.kjv_text: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice. {shewing...: Heb. flourishing}
verses.nlt_text: My lover is like a swift gazelle or a young stag. Look, there he is behind the wall, looking through the window, peering into the room.

verses.kjv_text: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.nlt_text: My lover said to me, "Rise up, my darling! Come away with me, my fair one!

verses.kjv_text: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over {and} gone;
verses.nlt_text: Look, the winter is past, and the rains are over and gone.

verses.kjv_text: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing {of birds} is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
verses.nlt_text: The flowers are springing up, the season of singing birds has come, and the cooing of turtledoves fills the air.

verses.kjv_text: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines {with} the tender grape give a {good} smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
verses.nlt_text: The fig trees are forming young fruit, and the fragrant grapevines are blossoming. Rise up, my darling! Come away with me, my fair one!" Young Man

verses.kjv_text: O my dove, {that art} in the clefts of the rock, in the secret {places} of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet {is} thy voice, and thy countenance {is} comely.
verses.nlt_text: My dove is hiding behind the rocks, behind an outcrop on the cliff. Let me see your face; let me hear your voice. For your voice is pleasant, and your face is lovely. Young Women of Jerusalem

verses.kjv_text: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines {have} tender grapes.
verses.nlt_text: Catch all the foxes, those little foxes, before they ruin the vineyard of love, for the grapevines are blossoming! Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: My beloved {is} mine, and I {am} his: he feedeth among the lilies.
verses.nlt_text: My lover is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.

verses.kjv_text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether. {of Bether: or, of division}
verses.nlt_text: Before the dawn breezes blow and the night shadows flee, return to me, my love, like a gazelle or a young stag on the rugged mountains. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.nlt_text: One night as I lay in bed, I yearned for my lover. I yearned for him, but he did not come.

verses.kjv_text: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
verses.nlt_text: So I said to myself, "I will get up and roam the city, searching in all its streets and squares. I will search for the one I love." So I searched everywhere but did not find him.

verses.kjv_text: The watchmen that go about the city found me: {to whom I said}, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
verses.nlt_text: The watchmen stopped me as they made their rounds, and I asked, "Have you seen the one I love?"

verses.kjv_text: {It was} but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
verses.nlt_text: Then scarcely had I left them when I found my love! I caught and held him tightly, then I brought him to my mother's house, into my mother's bed, where I had been conceived.

verses.kjv_text: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake {my} love, till he please.
verses.nlt_text: Promise me, O women of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and wild deer, not to awaken love until the time is right. Young Women of Jerusalem

verses.kjv_text: Who {is} this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
verses.nlt_text: Who is this sweeping in from the wilderness like a cloud of smoke? Who is it, fragrant with myrrh and frankincense and every kind of spice?

verses.kjv_text: Behold his bed, which {is} Solomon's; threescore valiant men {are} about it, of the valiant of Israel.
verses.nlt_text: Look, it is Solomon's carriage, surrounded by sixty heroic men, the best of Israel's soldiers.

verses.kjv_text: They all hold swords, {being} expert in war: every man {hath} his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
verses.nlt_text: They are all skilled swordsmen, experienced warriors. Each wears a sword on his thigh, ready to defend the king against an attack in the night.

verses.kjv_text: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon. {a chariot: or, a bed}
verses.nlt_text: King Solomon's carriage is built of wood imported from Lebanon.

verses.kjv_text: He made the pillars thereof {of} silver, the bottom thereof {of} gold, the covering of it {of} purple, the midst thereof being paved {with} love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: Its posts are silver, its canopy gold; its cushions are purple. It was decorated with love by the young women of Jerusalem. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.nlt_text: Come out to see King Solomon, young women of Jerusalem. He wears the crown his mother gave him on his wedding day, his most joyous day. Young Man

verses.kjv_text: Behold, thou {art} fair, my love; behold, thou {art} fair; thou {hast} doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair {is} as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead. {that...: or, that eat of, etc}
verses.nlt_text: You are beautiful, my darling, beautiful beyond words. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair falls in waves, like a flock of goats winding down the slopes of Gilead.

verses.kjv_text: Thy teeth {are} like a flock {of sheep that are even} shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none {is} barren among them.
verses.nlt_text: Your teeth are as white as sheep, recently shorn and freshly washed. Your smile is flawless, each tooth matched with its twin.

verses.kjv_text: Thy lips {are} like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech {is} comely: thy temples {are} like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.
verses.nlt_text: Your lips are like scarlet ribbon; your mouth is inviting. Your cheeks are like rosy pomegranates behind your veil.

verses.kjv_text: Thy neck {is} like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
verses.nlt_text: Your neck is as beautiful as the tower of David, jeweled with the shields of a thousand heroes.

verses.kjv_text: Thy two breasts {are} like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
verses.nlt_text: Your breasts are like two fawns, twin fawns of a gazelle grazing among the lilies.

verses.kjv_text: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense. {break: Heb. breathe}
verses.nlt_text: Before the dawn breezes blow and the night shadows flee, I will hurry to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.

verses.kjv_text: Thou {art} all fair, my love; {there is} no spot in thee.
verses.nlt_text: You are altogether beautiful, my darling, beautiful in every way.

verses.kjv_text: Come with me from Lebanon, {my} spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
verses.nlt_text: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, come with me from Lebanon. Come down from Mount Amana, from the peaks of Senir and Hermon, where the lions have their dens and leopards live among the hills.

verses.kjv_text: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, {my} spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck. {ravished: or, taken away}
verses.nlt_text: You have captured my heart, my treasure, my bride. You hold it hostage with one glance of your eyes, with a single jewel of your necklace.

verses.kjv_text: How fair is thy love, my sister, {my} spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!
verses.nlt_text: Your love delights me, my treasure, my bride. Your love is better than wine, your perfume more fragrant than spices.

verses.kjv_text: Thy lips, O {my} spouse, drop {as} the honeycomb: honey and milk {are} under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments {is} like the smell of Lebanon.
verses.nlt_text: Your lips are as sweet as nectar, my bride. Honey and milk are under your tongue. Your clothes are scented like the cedars of Lebanon.

verses.kjv_text: A garden inclosed {is} my sister, {my} spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed. {inclosed: Heb. barred} {shut up: Heb. barred}
verses.nlt_text: You are my private garden, my treasure, my bride, a secluded spring, a hidden fountain.

verses.kjv_text: Thy plants {are} an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard, {camphire: or, cypress}
verses.nlt_text: Your thighs shelter a paradise of pomegranates with rare spices-- henna with nard,

verses.kjv_text: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
verses.nlt_text: nard and saffron, fragrant calamus and cinnamon, with all the trees of frankincense, myrrh, and aloes, and every other lovely spice.

verses.kjv_text: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
verses.nlt_text: You are a garden fountain, a well of fresh water streaming down from Lebanon's mountains. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, {that} the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
verses.nlt_text: Awake, north wind! Rise up, south wind! Blow on my garden and spread its fragrance all around. Come into your garden, my love; taste its finest fruits. Young Man

verses.kjv_text: I am come into my garden, my sister, {my} spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved. {yea...: or, and be drunken with loves}
verses.nlt_text: I have entered my garden, my treasure, my bride! I gather myrrh with my spices and eat honeycomb with my honey. I drink wine with my milk. Young Women of Jerusalem Oh, lover and beloved, eat and drink! Yes, drink deeply of your love! Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: I sleep, but my heart waketh: {it is} the voice of my beloved that knocketh, {saying}, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, {and} my locks with the drops of the night.
verses.nlt_text: I slept, but my heart was awake, when I heard my lover knocking and calling: "Open to me, my treasure, my darling, my dove, my perfect one. My head is drenched with dew, my hair with the dampness of the night."

verses.kjv_text: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
verses.nlt_text: But I responded, "I have taken off my robe. Should I get dressed again? I have washed my feet. Should I get them soiled?"

verses.kjv_text: My beloved put in his hand by the hole {of the door}, and my bowels were moved for him. {for him: or, (as some read) in me}
verses.nlt_text: My lover tried to unlatch the door, and my heart thrilled within me.

verses.kjv_text: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped {with} myrrh, and my fingers {with} sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock. {sweet...: Heb. passing, or, running about}
verses.nlt_text: I jumped up to open the door for my love, and my hands dripped with perfume. My fingers dripped with lovely myrrh as I pulled back the bolt.

verses.kjv_text: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, {and} was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
verses.nlt_text: I opened to my lover, but he was gone! My heart sank. I searched for him but could not find him anywhere. I called to him, but there was no reply.

verses.kjv_text: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
verses.nlt_text: The night watchmen found me as they made their rounds. They beat and bruised me and stripped off my veil, those watchmen on the walls.

verses.kjv_text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I {am} sick of love. {that ye: Heb. what, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Make this promise, O women of Jerusalem-- If you find my lover, tell him I am weak with love. Young Women of Jerusalem

verses.kjv_text: What {is} thy beloved more than {another} beloved, O thou fairest among women? what {is} thy beloved more than {another} beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
verses.nlt_text: Why is your lover better than all others, O woman of rare beauty? What makes your lover so special that we must promise this? Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: My beloved {is} white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand. {the chiefest: Heb. a standard-bearer}
verses.nlt_text: My lover is dark and dazzling, better than ten thousand others!

verses.kjv_text: His head {is as} the most fine gold, his locks {are} bushy, {and} black as a raven. {bushy: or, curled}
verses.nlt_text: His head is finest gold, his wavy hair is black as a raven.

verses.kjv_text: His eyes {are} as {the eyes} of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, {and} fitly set. {fitly...: Heb. sitting in fulness, that is, fitly placed, and set as a precious stone in the foil of a ring}
verses.nlt_text: His eyes sparkle like doves beside springs of water; they are set like jewels washed in milk.

verses.kjv_text: His cheeks {are} as a bed of spices, {as} sweet flowers: his lips {like} lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh. {sweet flowers: or, towers of perfumes}
verses.nlt_text: His cheeks are like gardens of spices giving off fragrance. His lips are like lilies, perfumed with myrrh.

verses.kjv_text: His hands {are as} gold rings set with the beryl: his belly {is as} bright ivory overlaid {with} sapphires.
verses.nlt_text: His arms are like rounded bars of gold, set with beryl. His body is like bright ivory, glowing with lapis lazuli.

verses.kjv_text: His legs {are as} pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance {is} as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
verses.nlt_text: His legs are like marble pillars set in sockets of finest gold. His posture is stately, like the noble cedars of Lebanon.

verses.kjv_text: His mouth {is} most sweet: yea, he {is} altogether lovely. This {is} my beloved, and this {is} my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem. {mouth: Heb. palate}
verses.nlt_text: His mouth is sweetness itself; he is desirable in every way. Such, O women of Jerusalem, is my lover, my friend. Young Women of Jerusalem

verses.kjv_text: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.
verses.nlt_text: Where has your lover gone, O woman of rare beauty? Which way did he turn so we can help you find him? Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
verses.nlt_text: My lover has gone down to his garden, to his spice beds, to browse in the gardens and gather the lilies.

verses.kjv_text: I {am} my beloved's, and my beloved {is} mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
verses.nlt_text: I am my lover's, and my lover is mine. He browses among the lilies. Young Man

verses.kjv_text: Thou {art} beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as {an army} with banners.
verses.nlt_text: You are beautiful, my darling, like the lovely city of Tirzah. Yes, as beautiful as Jerusalem, as majestic as an army with billowing banners.

verses.kjv_text: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair {is} as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead. {overcome...: or, puffed me up}
verses.nlt_text: Turn your eyes away, for they overpower me. Your hair falls in waves, like a flock of goats winding down the slopes of Gilead.

verses.kjv_text: Thy teeth {are} as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and {there is} not one barren among them.
verses.nlt_text: Your teeth are as white as sheep that are freshly washed. Your smile is flawless, each tooth matched with its twin.

verses.kjv_text: As a piece of a pomegranate {are} thy temples within thy locks.
verses.nlt_text: Your cheeks are like rosy pomegranates behind your veil.

verses.kjv_text: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.
verses.nlt_text: Even among sixty queens and eighty concubines and countless young women,

verses.kjv_text: My dove, my undefiled is {but} one; she {is} the {only} one of her mother, she {is} the choice {one} of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; {yea}, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
verses.nlt_text: I would still choose my dove, my perfect one-- the favorite of her mother, dearly loved by the one who bore her. The young women see her and praise her; even queens and royal concubines sing her praises:

verses.kjv_text: Who {is} she {that} looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, {and} terrible as {an army} with banners?
verses.nlt_text: "Who is this, arising like the dawn, as fair as the moon, as bright as the sun, as majestic as an army with billowing banners?"

verses.kjv_text: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, {and} to see whether the vine flourished, {and} the pomegranates budded.
verses.nlt_text: I went down to the grove of walnut trees and out to the valley to see the new spring growth, to see whether the grapevines had budded or the pomegranates were in bloom.

verses.kjv_text: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me {like} the chariots of Amminadib. {Or ever...: Heb. I knew not} {made...: or, set me on the chariots of my willing people}
verses.nlt_text: Before I realized it, I found myself in the royal chariot with my beloved. Young Women of Jerusalem

verses.kjv_text: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies. {of...: or, of Mahanaim}
verses.nlt_text: Return, return to us, O maid of Shulam. Come back, come back, that we may see you again. Young Man Why do you stare at this young woman of Shulam, as she moves so gracefully between two lines of dancers?

verses.kjv_text: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs {are} like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
verses.nlt_text: How beautiful are your sandaled feet, O queenly maiden. Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of a skilled craftsman.

verses.kjv_text: Thy navel {is like} a round goblet, {which} wanteth not liquor: thy belly {is like} an heap of wheat set about with lilies. {liquor: Heb. mixture}
verses.nlt_text: Your navel is perfectly formed like a goblet filled with mixed wine. Between your thighs lies a mound of wheat bordered with lilies.

verses.kjv_text: Thy two breasts {are} like two young roes {that are} twins.
verses.nlt_text: Your breasts are like two fawns, twin fawns of a gazelle.

verses.kjv_text: Thy neck {is} as a tower of ivory; thine eyes {like} the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: thy nose {is} as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.
verses.nlt_text: Your neck is as beautiful as an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the sparkling pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is as fine as the tower of Lebanon overlooking Damascus.

verses.kjv_text: Thine head upon thee {is} like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king {is} held in the galleries. {Carmel: or, crimson} {held: Heb. bound}
verses.nlt_text: Your head is as majestic as Mount Carmel, and the sheen of your hair radiates royalty. The king is held captive by its tresses.

verses.kjv_text: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
verses.nlt_text: Oh, how beautiful you are! How pleasing, my love, how full of delights!

verses.kjv_text: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters {of grapes}.
verses.nlt_text: You are slender like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters of fruit.

verses.kjv_text: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;
verses.nlt_text: I said, "I will climb the palm tree and take hold of its fruit." May your breasts be like grape clusters, and the fragrance of your breath like apples.

verses.kjv_text: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth {down} sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak. {sweetly: Heb. straightly} {of those...: or, of the ancient}
verses.nlt_text: May your kisses be as exciting as the best wine, flowing gently over lips and teeth. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: I {am} my beloved's, and his desire {is} toward me.
verses.nlt_text: I am my lover's, and he claims me as his own.

verses.kjv_text: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
verses.nlt_text: Come, my love, let us go out to the fields and spend the night among the wildflowers.

verses.kjv_text: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, {whether} the tender grape appear, {and} the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves. {appear: Heb. open}
verses.nlt_text: Let us get up early and go to the vineyards to see if the grapevines have budded, if the blossoms have opened, and if the pomegranates have bloomed. There I will give you my love.

verses.kjv_text: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates {are} all manner of pleasant {fruits}, new and old, {which} I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
verses.nlt_text: There the mandrakes give off their fragrance, and the finest fruits are at our door, new delights as well as old, which I have saved for you, my lover. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: O that thou {wert} as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! {when} I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised. {I should not...: Heb. they should not despise me}
verses.nlt_text: Oh, I wish you were my brother, who nursed at my mother's breasts. Then I could kiss you no matter who was watching, and no one would criticize me.

verses.kjv_text: I would lead thee, {and} bring thee into my mother's house, {who} would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
verses.nlt_text: I would bring you to my childhood home, and there you would teach me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, my sweet pomegranate wine.

verses.kjv_text: His left hand {should be} under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.
verses.nlt_text: Your left arm would be under my head, and your right arm would embrace me.

verses.kjv_text: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake {my} love, until he please. {that...: Heb. why should ye stir up, or, why, etc}
verses.nlt_text: Promise me, O women of Jerusalem, not to awaken love until the time is right. Young Women of Jerusalem

verses.kjv_text: Who {is} this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth {that} bare thee.
verses.nlt_text: Who is this sweeping in from the desert, leaning on her lover? Young Woman I aroused you under the apple tree, where your mother gave you birth, where in great pain she delivered you.

verses.kjv_text: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love {is} strong as death; jealousy {is} cruel as the grave: the coals thereof {are} coals of fire, {which hath a} most vehement flame. {cruel: Heb. hard}
verses.nlt_text: Place me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as enduring as the grave. Love flashes like fire, the brightest kind of flame.

verses.kjv_text: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if {a} man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
verses.nlt_text: Many waters cannot quench love, nor can rivers drown it. If a man tried to buy love with all his wealth, his offer would be utterly scorned. The Young Woman's Brothers

verses.kjv_text: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
verses.nlt_text: We have a little sister too young to have breasts. What will we do for our sister if someone asks to marry her?

verses.kjv_text: If she {be} a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she {be} a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.
verses.nlt_text: If she is a virgin, like a wall, we will protect her with a silver tower. But if she is promiscuous, like a swinging door, we will block her door with a cedar bar. Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: I {am} a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour. {favour: Heb. peace}
verses.nlt_text: I was a virgin, like a wall; now my breasts are like towers. When my lover looks at me, he is delighted with what he sees.

verses.kjv_text: Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand {pieces} of silver.
verses.nlt_text: Solomon has a vineyard at Baal-hamon, which he leases out to tenant farmers. Each of them pays a thousand pieces of silver for harvesting its fruit.

verses.kjv_text: My vineyard, which {is} mine, {is} before me: thou, O Solomon, {must have} a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.
verses.nlt_text: But my vineyard is mine to give, and Solomon need not pay a thousand pieces of silver. But I will give two hundred pieces to those who care for its vines. Young Man

verses.kjv_text: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear {it}.
verses.nlt_text: O my darling, lingering in the gardens, your companions are fortunate to hear your voice. Let me hear it, too! Young Woman

verses.kjv_text: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices. {Make...: Heb. Flee away}
verses.nlt_text: Come away, my love! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.

verses.kjv_text: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, {and} Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
verses.nlt_text: These are the visions that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem. He saw these visions during the years when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.

verses.kjv_text: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the LORD hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.
verses.nlt_text: Listen, O heavens! Pay attention, earth! This is what the LORD says: "The children I raised and cared for have rebelled against me.

verses.kjv_text: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: {but} Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.
verses.nlt_text: Even an ox knows its owner, and a donkey recognizes its master's care-- but Israel doesn't know its master. My people don't recognize my care for them."

verses.kjv_text: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the LORD, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward. {laden: Heb. of heaviness} {gone...: Heb. alienated, or, separated}
verses.nlt_text: Oh, what a sinful nation they are-- loaded down with a burden of guilt. They are evil people, corrupt children who have rejected the LORD. They have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on him.

verses.kjv_text: Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. {revolt...: Heb. increase revolt}
verses.nlt_text: Why do you continue to invite punishment? Must you rebel forever? Your head is injured, and your heart is sick.

verses.kjv_text: From the sole of the foot even unto the head {there is} no soundness in it; {but} wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment. {ointment: or, oil}
verses.nlt_text: You are battered from head to foot-- covered with bruises, welts, and infected wounds-- without any soothing ointments or bandages.

verses.kjv_text: Your country {is} desolate, your cities {are} burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and {it is} desolate, as overthrown by strangers. {overthrown...: Heb. the overthrow of}
verses.nlt_text: Your country lies in ruins, and your towns are burned. Foreigners plunder your fields before your eyes and destroy everything they see.

verses.kjv_text: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.
verses.nlt_text: Beautiful Jerusalem stands abandoned like a watchman's shelter in a vineyard, like a lean-to in a cucumber field after the harvest, like a helpless city under siege.

verses.kjv_text: Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, {and} we should have been like unto Gomorrah.
verses.nlt_text: If the LORD of Heaven's Armies had not spared a few of us, we would have been wiped out like Sodom, destroyed like Gomorrah.

verses.kjv_text: Hear the word of the LORD, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.
verses.nlt_text: Listen to the LORD, you leaders of "Sodom." Listen to the law of our God, people of "Gomorrah."

verses.kjv_text: To what purpose {is} the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the LORD: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats. {he goats: Heb. great he goats}
verses.nlt_text: "What makes you think I want all your sacrifices?" says the LORD. "I am sick of your burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened cattle. I get no pleasure from the blood of bulls and lambs and goats.

verses.kjv_text: When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts? {to appear: Heb. to be seen}
verses.nlt_text: When you come to worship me, who asked you to parade through my courts with all your ceremony?
