verses.nlt_text: Instead, we should write and tell them to abstain from eating food offered to idols, from sexual immorality, from eating the meat of strangled animals, and from consuming blood.

verses.kjv_text: For Moses of old time hath in every city them that preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath day.
verses.nlt_text: For these laws of Moses have been preached in Jewish synagogues in every city on every Sabbath for many generations."

verses.kjv_text: Then pleased it the apostles and elders, with the whole church, to send chosen men of their own company to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas; {namely}, Judas surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, chief men among the brethren:
verses.nlt_text: Then the apostles and elders together with the whole church in Jerusalem chose delegates, and they sent them to Antioch of Syria with Paul and Barnabas to report on this decision. The men chosen were two of the church leaders-- Judas (also called Barsabbas) and Silas.

verses.kjv_text: And they wrote {letters} by them after this manner; The apostles and elders and brethren {send} greeting unto the brethren which are of the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia:
verses.nlt_text: This is the letter they took with them: "This letter is from the apostles and elders, your brothers in Jerusalem. It is written to the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia. Greetings!

verses.kjv_text: Forasmuch as we have heard, that certain which went out from us have troubled you with words, subverting your souls, saying, {Ye must} be circumcised, and keep the law: to whom we gave no {such} commandment:
verses.nlt_text: "We understand that some men from here have troubled you and upset you with their teaching, but we did not send them!

verses.kjv_text: It seemed good unto us, being assembled with one accord, to send chosen men unto you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
verses.nlt_text: So we decided, having come to complete agreement, to send you official representatives, along with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

verses.kjv_text: Men that have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.nlt_text: who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.kjv_text: We have sent therefore Judas and Silas, who shall also tell {you} the same things by mouth. {mouth: Gr. word}
verses.nlt_text: We are sending Judas and Silas to confirm what we have decided concerning your question.

verses.kjv_text: For it seemed good to the Holy Ghost, and to us, to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things;
verses.nlt_text: "For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay no greater burden on you than these few requirements:

verses.kjv_text: That ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication: from which if ye keep yourselves, ye shall do well. Fare ye well.
verses.nlt_text: You must abstain from eating food offered to idols, from consuming blood or the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. If you do this, you will do well. Farewell."

verses.kjv_text: So when they were dismissed, they came to Antioch: and when they had gathered the multitude together, they delivered the epistle:
verses.nlt_text: The messengers went at once to Antioch, where they called a general meeting of the believers and delivered the letter.

verses.kjv_text: {Which} when they had read, they rejoiced for the consolation. {consolation: or, exhortation}
verses.nlt_text: And there was great joy throughout the church that day as they read this encouraging message.

verses.kjv_text: And Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed {them}.
verses.nlt_text: Then Judas and Silas, both being prophets, spoke at length to the believers, encouraging and strengthening their faith.

verses.kjv_text: And after they had tarried {there} a space, they were let go in peace from the brethren unto the apostles.
verses.nlt_text: They stayed for a while, and then the believers sent them back to the church in Jerusalem with a blessing of peace.

verses.kjv_text: Notwithstanding it pleased Silas to abide there still.
Paul also and Barnabas continued in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.
verses.nlt_text: Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. They and many others taught and preached the word of the Lord there.

verses.kjv_text: And some days after Paul said unto Barnabas, Let us go again and visit our brethren in every city where we have preached the word of the Lord, {and see} how they do.
verses.nlt_text: After some time Paul said to Barnabas, "Let's go back and visit each city where we previously preached the word of the Lord, to see how the new believers are doing."

verses.kjv_text: And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark.
verses.nlt_text: Barnabas agreed and wanted to take along John Mark.

verses.kjv_text: But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul disagreed strongly, since John Mark had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not continued with them in their work.

verses.kjv_text: And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus;
verses.nlt_text: Their disagreement was so sharp that they separated. Barnabas took John Mark with him and sailed for Cyprus.

verses.kjv_text: And Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.
verses.nlt_text: Paul chose Silas, and as he left, the believers entrusted him to the Lord's gracious care.

verses.kjv_text: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, confirming the churches.
verses.nlt_text: Then he traveled throughout Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches there.

verses.kjv_text: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father {was} a Greek:
verses.nlt_text: Paul went first to Derbe and then to Lystra, where there was a young disciple named Timothy. His mother was a Jewish believer, but his father was a Greek.

verses.kjv_text: Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.
verses.nlt_text: Timothy was well thought of by the believers in Lystra and Iconium,

verses.kjv_text: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.
verses.nlt_text: so Paul wanted him to join them on their journey. In deference to the Jews of the area, he arranged for Timothy to be circumcised before they left, for everyone knew that his father was a Greek.

verses.kjv_text: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: Then they went from town to town, instructing the believers to follow the decisions made by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.
verses.nlt_text: So the churches were strengthened in their faith and grew larger every day.

verses.kjv_text: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,
verses.nlt_text: Next Paul and Silas traveled through the area of Phrygia and Galatia, because the Holy Spirit had prevented them from preaching the word in the province of Asia at that time.

verses.kjv_text: After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.
verses.nlt_text: Then coming to the borders of Mysia, they headed north for the province of Bithynia, but again the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them to go there.

verses.kjv_text: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.
verses.nlt_text: So instead, they went on through Mysia to the seaport of Troas.

verses.kjv_text: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
verses.nlt_text: That night Paul had a vision: A man from Macedonia in northern Greece was standing there, pleading with him, "Come over to Macedonia and help us!"

verses.kjv_text: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.
verses.nlt_text: So we decided to leave for Macedonia at once, having concluded that God was calling us to preach the Good News there.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next {day} to Neapolis;
verses.nlt_text: We boarded a boat at Troas and sailed straight across to the island of Samothrace, and the next day we landed at Neapolis.

verses.kjv_text: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, {and} a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days. {the chief: or, the first}
verses.nlt_text: From there we reached Philippi, a major city of that district of Macedonia and a Roman colony. And we stayed there several days.

verses.kjv_text: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted {thither}. {sabbath: Gr. sabbath day}
verses.nlt_text: On the Sabbath we went a little way outside the city to a riverbank, where we thought people would be meeting for prayer, and we sat down to speak with some women who had gathered there.

verses.kjv_text: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard {us}: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.
verses.nlt_text: One of them was Lydia from Thyatira, a merchant of expensive purple cloth, who worshiped God. As she listened to us, the Lord opened her heart, and she accepted what Paul was saying.

verses.kjv_text: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought {us}, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide {there}. And she constrained us.
verses.nlt_text: She was baptized along with other members of her household, and she asked us to be her guests. "If you agree that I am a true believer in the Lord," she said, "come and stay at my home." And she urged us until we agreed.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying: {of divination: or, of Python}
verses.nlt_text: One day as we were going down to the place of prayer, we met a demon-possessed slave girl. She was a fortune-teller who earned a lot of money for her masters.

verses.kjv_text: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.
verses.nlt_text: She followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, "These men are servants of the Most High God, and they have come to tell you how to be saved."

verses.kjv_text: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.
verses.nlt_text: This went on day after day until Paul got so exasperated that he turned and said to the demon within her, "I command you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her." And instantly it left her.

verses.kjv_text: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew {them} into the marketplace unto the rulers, {marketplace: or, court}
verses.nlt_text: Her masters' hopes of wealth were now shattered, so they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities at the marketplace.

verses.kjv_text: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,
verses.nlt_text: "The whole city is in an uproar because of these Jews!" they shouted to the city officials.

verses.kjv_text: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.
verses.nlt_text: "They are teaching customs that are illegal for us Romans to practice."

verses.kjv_text: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat {them}.
verses.nlt_text: A mob quickly formed against Paul and Silas, and the city officials ordered them stripped and beaten with wooden rods.

verses.kjv_text: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast {them} into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:
verses.nlt_text: They were severely beaten, and then they were thrown into prison. The jailer was ordered to make sure they didn't escape.

verses.kjv_text: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.
verses.nlt_text: So the jailer put them into the inner dungeon and clamped their feet in the stocks.

verses.kjv_text: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.
verses.nlt_text: Around midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening.

verses.kjv_text: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed.
verses.nlt_text: Suddenly, there was a massive earthquake, and the prison was shaken to its foundations. All the doors immediately flew open, and the chains of every prisoner fell off!

verses.kjv_text: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.
verses.nlt_text: The jailer woke up to see the prison doors wide open. He assumed the prisoners had escaped, so he drew his sword to kill himself.

verses.kjv_text: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul shouted to him, "Stop! Don't kill yourself! We are all here!"

verses.kjv_text: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,
verses.nlt_text: The jailer called for lights and ran to the dungeon and fell down trembling before Paul and Silas.

verses.kjv_text: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
verses.nlt_text: Then he brought them out and asked, "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"

verses.kjv_text: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
verses.nlt_text: They replied, "Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved, along with everyone in your household."

verses.kjv_text: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
verses.nlt_text: And they shared the word of the Lord with him and with all who lived in his household.

verses.kjv_text: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed {their} stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
verses.nlt_text: Even at that hour of the night, the jailer cared for them and washed their wounds. Then he and everyone in his household were immediately baptized.

verses.kjv_text: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
verses.nlt_text: He brought them into his house and set a meal before them, and he and his entire household rejoiced because they all believed in God.

verses.kjv_text: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.
verses.nlt_text: The next morning the city officials sent the police to tell the jailer, "Let those men go!"

verses.kjv_text: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.
verses.nlt_text: So the jailer told Paul, "The city officials have said you and Silas are free to leave. Go in peace."

verses.kjv_text: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast {us} into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul replied, "They have publicly beaten us without a trial and put us in prison-- and we are Roman citizens. So now they want us to leave secretly? Certainly not! Let them come themselves to release us!"

verses.kjv_text: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.
verses.nlt_text: When the police reported this, the city officials were alarmed to learn that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.

verses.kjv_text: And they came and besought them, and brought {them} out, and desired {them} to depart out of the city.
verses.nlt_text: So they came to the jail and apologized to them. Then they brought them out and begged them to leave the city.

verses.kjv_text: And they went out of the prison, and entered into {the house of} Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
verses.nlt_text: When Paul and Silas left the prison, they returned to the home of Lydia. There they met with the believers and encouraged them once more. Then they left town.

verses.kjv_text: Now when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where was a synagogue of the Jews:
verses.nlt_text: Paul and Silas then traveled through the towns of Amphipolis and Apollonia and came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

verses.kjv_text: And Paul, as his manner was, went in unto them, and three sabbath days reasoned with them out of the scriptures,
verses.nlt_text: As was Paul's custom, he went to the synagogue service, and for three Sabbaths in a row he used the Scriptures to reason with the people.

verses.kjv_text: Opening and alleging, that Christ must needs have suffered, and risen again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom I preach unto you, is Christ. {whom...: or, whom, said he, I preach}
verses.nlt_text: He explained the prophecies and proved that the Messiah must suffer and rise from the dead. He said, "This Jesus I'm telling you about is the Messiah."

verses.kjv_text: And some of them believed, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.
verses.nlt_text: Some of the Jews who listened were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with many God-fearing Greek men and quite a few prominent women.

verses.kjv_text: But the Jews which believed not, moved with envy, took unto them certain lewd fellows of the baser sort, and gathered a company, and set all the city on an uproar, and assaulted the house of Jason, and sought to bring them out to the people.
verses.nlt_text: But some of the Jews were jealous, so they gathered some troublemakers from the marketplace to form a mob and start a riot. They attacked the home of Jason, searching for Paul and Silas so they could drag them out to the crowd.

verses.kjv_text: And when they found them not, they drew Jason and certain brethren unto the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;
verses.nlt_text: Not finding them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the other believers instead and took them before the city council. "Paul and Silas have caused trouble all over the world," they shouted, "and now they are here disturbing our city, too.

verses.kjv_text: Whom Jason hath received: and these all do contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, {one} Jesus.
verses.nlt_text: And Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all guilty of treason against Caesar, for they profess allegiance to another king, named Jesus."

verses.kjv_text: And they troubled the people and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.
verses.nlt_text: The people of the city, as well as the city council, were thrown into turmoil by these reports.

verses.kjv_text: And when they had taken security of Jason, and of the other, they let them go.
verses.nlt_text: So the officials forced Jason and the other believers to post bond, and then they released them.

verses.kjv_text: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Berea: who coming {thither} went into the synagogue of the Jews.
verses.nlt_text: That very night the believers sent Paul and Silas to Berea. When they arrived there, they went to the Jewish synagogue.

verses.kjv_text: These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
verses.nlt_text: And the people of Berea were more open-minded than those in Thessalonica, and they listened eagerly to Paul's message. They searched the Scriptures day after day to see if Paul and Silas were teaching the truth.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore many of them believed; also of honourable women which were Greeks, and of men, not a few.
verses.nlt_text: As a result, many Jews believed, as did many of the prominent Greek women and men.

verses.kjv_text: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was preached of Paul at Berea, they came thither also, and stirred up the people.
verses.nlt_text: But when some Jews in Thessalonica learned that Paul was preaching the word of God in Berea, they went there and stirred up trouble.

verses.kjv_text: And then immediately the brethren sent away Paul to go as it were to the sea: but Silas and Timotheus abode there still.
verses.nlt_text: The believers acted at once, sending Paul on to the coast, while Silas and Timothy remained behind.

verses.kjv_text: And they that conducted Paul brought him unto Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timotheus for to come to him with all speed, they departed.
verses.nlt_text: Those escorting Paul went with him all the way to Athens; then they returned to Berea with instructions for Silas and Timothy to hurry and join him.

verses.kjv_text: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry. {wholly...: or, full of idols}
verses.nlt_text: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply troubled by all the idols he saw everywhere in the city.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore disputed he in the synagogue with the Jews, and with the devout persons, and in the market daily with them that met with him.
verses.nlt_text: He went to the synagogue to reason with the Jews and the God-fearing Gentiles, and he spoke daily in the public square to all who happened to be there.

verses.kjv_text: Then certain philosophers of the Epicureans, and of the Stoicks, encountered him. And some said, What will this babbler say? other some, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached unto them Jesus, and the resurrection. {babbler: or, base fellow}
verses.nlt_text: He also had a debate with some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers. When he told them about Jesus and his resurrection, they said, "What's this babbler trying to say with these strange ideas he's picked up?" Others said, "He seems to be preaching about some foreign gods."

verses.kjv_text: And they took him, and brought him unto Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine, whereof thou speakest, {is}? {Areopagus: or, Mars' hill: it was the highest court in Athens}
verses.nlt_text: Then they took him to the high council of the city. "Come and tell us about this new teaching," they said.

verses.kjv_text: For thou bringest certain strange things to our ears: we would know therefore what these things mean.
verses.nlt_text: "You are saying some rather strange things, and we want to know what it's all about."

verses.kjv_text: (For all the Athenians and strangers which were there spent their time in nothing else, but either to tell, or to hear some new thing.)
verses.nlt_text: (It should be explained that all the Athenians as well as the foreigners in Athens seemed to spend all their time discussing the latest ideas.)

verses.kjv_text: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, {Ye} men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. {Mars' hill: or, the court of the Areopagites}
verses.nlt_text: So Paul, standing before the council, addressed them as follows: "Men of Athens, I notice that you are very religious in every way,

verses.kjv_text: For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. {devotions: or, gods that ye worship}
verses.nlt_text: for as I was walking along I saw your many shrines. And one of your altars had this inscription on it: 'To an Unknown God.' This God, whom you worship without knowing, is the one I'm telling you about.

verses.kjv_text: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
verses.nlt_text: "He is the God who made the world and everything in it. Since he is Lord of heaven and earth, he doesn't live in man-made temples,

verses.kjv_text: Neither is worshipped with men's hands, as though he needed any thing, seeing he giveth to all life, and breath, and all things;
verses.nlt_text: and human hands can't serve his needs-- for he has no needs. He himself gives life and breath to everything, and he satisfies every need.

verses.kjv_text: And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;
verses.nlt_text: From one man he created all the nations throughout the whole earth. He decided beforehand when they should rise and fall, and he determined their boundaries.

verses.kjv_text: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:
verses.nlt_text: "His purpose was for the nations to seek after God and perhaps feel their way toward him and find him-- though he is not far from any one of us.

verses.kjv_text: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
verses.nlt_text: For in him we live and move and exist. As some of your own poets have said, 'We are his offspring.'

verses.kjv_text: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man's device.
verses.nlt_text: And since this is true, we shouldn't think of God as an idol designed by craftsmen from gold or silver or stone.

verses.kjv_text: And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
verses.nlt_text: "God overlooked people's ignorance about these things in earlier times, but now he commands everyone everywhere to repent of their sins and turn to him.

verses.kjv_text: Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by {that} man whom he hath ordained; {whereof} he hath given assurance unto all {men}, in that he hath raised him from the dead. {hath given...: or, offered faith}
verses.nlt_text: For he has set a day for judging the world with justice by the man he has appointed, and he proved to everyone who this is by raising him from the dead."

verses.kjv_text: And when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked: and others said, We will hear thee again of this {matter}.
verses.nlt_text: When they heard Paul speak about the resurrection of the dead, some laughed in contempt, but others said, "We want to hear more about this later."

verses.kjv_text: So Paul departed from among them.
verses.nlt_text: That ended Paul's discussion with them,

verses.kjv_text: Howbeit certain men clave unto him, and believed: among the which {was} Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
verses.nlt_text: but some joined him and became believers. Among them were Dionysius, a member of the council, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.

verses.kjv_text: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;
verses.nlt_text: Then Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

verses.kjv_text: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.
verses.nlt_text: There he became acquainted with a Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, who had recently arrived from Italy with his wife, Priscilla. They had left Italy when Claudius Caesar deported all Jews from Rome.

verses.kjv_text: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.
verses.nlt_text: Paul lived and worked with them, for they were tentmakers just as he was.

verses.kjv_text: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.
verses.nlt_text: Each Sabbath found Paul at the synagogue, trying to convince the Jews and Greeks alike.

verses.kjv_text: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews {that} Jesus {was} Christ. {was Christ: or, is the Christ}
verses.nlt_text: And after Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul spent all his time preaching the word. He testified to the Jews that Jesus was the Messiah.

verses.kjv_text: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook {his} raiment, and said unto them, Your blood {be} upon your own heads; I {am} clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.
verses.nlt_text: But when they opposed and insulted him, Paul shook the dust from his clothes and said, "Your blood is upon your own heads-- I am innocent. From now on I will go preach to the Gentiles."

verses.kjv_text: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain {man's} house, named Justus, {one} that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.
verses.nlt_text: Then he left and went to the home of Titius Justus, a Gentile who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.

verses.kjv_text: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.
verses.nlt_text: Crispus, the leader of the synagogue, and everyone in his household believed in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard Paul, became believers, and were baptized.

verses.kjv_text: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:
verses.nlt_text: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision and told him, "Don't be afraid! Speak out! Don't be silent!

verses.kjv_text: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
verses.nlt_text: For I am with you, and no one will attack and harm you, for many people in this city belong to me."

verses.kjv_text: And he continued {there} a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them. {continued there: Gr. sat there}
verses.nlt_text: So Paul stayed there for the next year and a half, teaching the word of God.

verses.kjv_text: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,
verses.nlt_text: But when Gallio became governor of Achaia, some Jews rose up together against Paul and brought him before the governor for judgment.

verses.kjv_text: Saying, This {fellow} persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.
verses.nlt_text: They accused Paul of "persuading people to worship God in ways that are contrary to our law."

verses.kjv_text: And when Paul was now about to open {his} mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O {ye} Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:
verses.nlt_text: But just as Paul started to make his defense, Gallio turned to Paul's accusers and said, "Listen, you Jews, if this were a case involving some wrongdoing or a serious crime, I would have a reason to accept your case.

verses.kjv_text: But if it be a question of words and names, and {of} your law, look ye {to it}; for I will be no judge of such {matters}.
verses.nlt_text: But since it is merely a question of words and names and your Jewish law, take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters."

verses.kjv_text: And he drave them from the judgment seat.
verses.nlt_text: And he threw them out of the courtroom.

verses.kjv_text: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat {him} before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.
verses.nlt_text: The crowd then grabbed Sosthenes, the leader of the synagogue, and beat him right there in the courtroom. But Gallio paid no attention.

verses.kjv_text: And Paul {after this} tarried {there} yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn {his} head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.
verses.nlt_text: Paul stayed in Corinth for some time after that, then said good-bye to the brothers and sisters and went to nearby Cenchrea. There he shaved his head according to Jewish custom, marking the end of a vow. Then he set sail for Syria, taking Priscilla and Aquila with him.

verses.kjv_text: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.
verses.nlt_text: They stopped first at the port of Ephesus, where Paul left the others behind. While he was there, he went to the synagogue to reason with the Jews.

verses.kjv_text: When they desired {him} to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;
verses.nlt_text: They asked him to stay longer, but he declined.

verses.kjv_text: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.
verses.nlt_text: As he left, however, he said, "I will come back later, God willing." Then he set sail from Ephesus.

verses.kjv_text: And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.
verses.nlt_text: The next stop was at the port of Caesarea. From there he went up and visited the church at Jerusalem and then went back to Antioch.

verses.kjv_text: And after he had spent some time {there}, he departed, and went over {all} the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
verses.nlt_text: After spending some time in Antioch, Paul went back through Galatia and Phrygia, visiting and strengthening all the believers.

verses.kjv_text: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, {and} mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, a Jew named Apollos, an eloquent speaker who knew the Scriptures well, had arrived in Ephesus from Alexandria in Egypt.

verses.kjv_text: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.
verses.nlt_text: He had been taught the way of the Lord, and he taught others about Jesus with an enthusiastic spirit and with accuracy. However, he knew only about John's baptism.

verses.kjv_text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto {them}, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.
verses.nlt_text: When Priscilla and Aquila heard him preaching boldly in the synagogue, they took him aside and explained the way of God even more accurately.

verses.kjv_text: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:
verses.nlt_text: Apollos had been thinking about going to Achaia, and the brothers and sisters in Ephesus encouraged him to go. They wrote to the believers in Achaia, asking them to welcome him. When he arrived there, he proved to be of great benefit to those who, by God's grace, had believed.

verses.kjv_text: For he mightily convinced the Jews, {and that} publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ. {Christ: or, is the Christ}
verses.nlt_text: He refuted the Jews with powerful arguments in public debate. Using the Scriptures, he explained to them that Jesus was the Messiah.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus: and finding certain disciples,
verses.nlt_text: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled through the interior regions until he reached Ephesus, on the coast, where he found several believers.

verses.kjv_text: He said unto them, Have ye received the Holy Ghost since ye believed? And they said unto him, We have not so much as heard whether there be any Holy Ghost.
verses.nlt_text: "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" he asked them."No," they replied, "we haven't even heard that there is a Holy Spirit."

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto them, Unto what then were ye baptized? And they said, Unto John's baptism.
verses.nlt_text: "Then what baptism did you experience?" he asked.And they replied, "The baptism of John."

verses.kjv_text: Then said Paul, John verily baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people, that they should believe on him which should come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.
verses.nlt_text: Paul said, "John's baptism called for repentance from sin. But John himself told the people to believe in the one who would come later, meaning Jesus."

verses.kjv_text: When they heard {this}, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.nlt_text: As soon as they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

verses.kjv_text: And when Paul had laid {his} hands upon them, the Holy Ghost came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.
verses.nlt_text: Then when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke in other tongues and prophesied.

verses.kjv_text: And all the men were about twelve.
verses.nlt_text: There were about twelve men in all.

verses.kjv_text: And he went into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, disputing and persuading the things concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.nlt_text: Then Paul went to the synagogue and preached boldly for the next three months, arguing persuasively about the Kingdom of God.

verses.kjv_text: But when divers were hardened, and believed not, but spake evil of that way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, disputing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
verses.nlt_text: But some became stubborn, rejecting his message and publicly speaking against the Way. So Paul left the synagogue and took the believers with him. Then he held daily discussions at the lecture hall of Tyrannus.

verses.kjv_text: And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.
verses.nlt_text: This went on for the next two years, so that people throughout the province of Asia-- both Jews and Greeks-- heard the word of the Lord.

verses.kjv_text: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:
verses.nlt_text: God gave Paul the power to perform unusual miracles.

verses.kjv_text: So that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.
verses.nlt_text: When handkerchiefs or aprons that had merely touched his skin were placed on sick people, they were healed of their diseases, and evil spirits were expelled.

verses.kjv_text: Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.
verses.nlt_text: A group of Jews was traveling from town to town casting out evil spirits. They tried to use the name of the Lord Jesus in their incantation, saying, "I command you in the name of Jesus, whom Paul preaches, to come out!"

verses.kjv_text: And there were seven sons of {one} Sceva, a Jew, {and} chief of the priests, which did so.
verses.nlt_text: Seven sons of Sceva, a leading priest, were doing this.

verses.kjv_text: And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?
verses.nlt_text: But one time when they tried it, the evil spirit replied, "I know Jesus, and I know Paul, but who are you?"

verses.kjv_text: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and overcame them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.
verses.nlt_text: Then the man with the evil spirit leaped on them, overpowered them, and attacked them with such violence that they fled from the house, naked and battered.

verses.kjv_text: And this was known to all the Jews and Greeks also dwelling at Ephesus; and fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
verses.nlt_text: The story of what happened spread quickly all through Ephesus, to Jews and Greeks alike. A solemn fear descended on the city, and the name of the Lord Jesus was greatly honored.

verses.kjv_text: And many that believed came, and confessed, and shewed their deeds.
verses.nlt_text: Many who became believers confessed their sinful practices.

verses.kjv_text: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all {men}: and they counted the price of them, and found {it} fifty thousand {pieces} of silver.
verses.nlt_text: A number of them who had been practicing sorcery brought their incantation books and burned them at a public bonfire. The value of the books was several million dollars.

verses.kjv_text: So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed.
verses.nlt_text: So the message about the Lord spread widely and had a powerful effect.

verses.kjv_text: After these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
verses.nlt_text: Afterward Paul felt compelled by the Spirit to go over to Macedonia and Achaia before going to Jerusalem. "And after that," he said, "I must go on to Rome!"

verses.kjv_text: So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus; but he himself stayed in Asia for a season.
verses.nlt_text: He sent his two assistants, Timothy and Erastus, ahead to Macedonia while he stayed awhile longer in the province of Asia.

verses.kjv_text: And the same time there arose no small stir about that way.
verses.nlt_text: About that time, serious trouble developed in Ephesus concerning the Way.

verses.kjv_text: For a certain {man} named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
verses.nlt_text: It began with Demetrius, a silversmith who had a large business manufacturing silver shrines of the Greek goddess Artemis. He kept many craftsmen busy.

verses.kjv_text: Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
verses.nlt_text: He called them together, along with others employed in similar trades, and addressed them as follows:"Gentlemen, you know that our wealth comes from this business.

verses.kjv_text: Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:
verses.nlt_text: But as you have seen and heard, this man Paul has persuaded many people that handmade gods aren't really gods at all. And he's done this not only here in Ephesus but throughout the entire province!

verses.kjv_text: So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth. {set at nought: or, brought into disrepute, or, contempt}
verses.nlt_text: Of course, I'm not just talking about the loss of public respect for our business. I'm also concerned that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will lose its influence and that Artemis-- this magnificent goddess worshiped throughout the province of Asia and all around the world-- will be robbed of her great prestige!"

verses.kjv_text: And when they heard {these sayings}, they were full of wrath, and cried out, saying, Great {is} Diana of the Ephesians.
verses.nlt_text: At this their anger boiled, and they began shouting, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

verses.kjv_text: And the whole city was filled with confusion: and having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel, they rushed with one accord into the theatre.
verses.nlt_text: Soon the whole city was filled with confusion. Everyone rushed to the amphitheater, dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, who were Paul's traveling companions from Macedonia.

verses.kjv_text: And when Paul would have entered in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.
verses.nlt_text: Paul wanted to go in, too, but the believers wouldn't let him.

verses.kjv_text: And certain of the chief of Asia, which were his friends, sent unto him, desiring {him} that he would not adventure himself into the theatre.
verses.nlt_text: Some of the officials of the province, friends of Paul, also sent a message to him, begging him not to risk his life by entering the amphitheater.

verses.kjv_text: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was confused; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.
verses.nlt_text: Inside, the people were all shouting, some one thing and some another. Everything was in confusion. In fact, most of them didn't even know why they were there.

verses.kjv_text: And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
verses.nlt_text: The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander forward and told him to explain the situation. He motioned for silence and tried to speak.

verses.kjv_text: But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great {is} Diana of the Ephesians.
verses.nlt_text: But when the crowd realized he was a Jew, they started shouting again and kept it up for two hours: "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians! Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"

verses.kjv_text: And when the townclerk had appeased the people, he said, {Ye} men of Ephesus, what man is there that knoweth not how that the city of the Ephesians is a worshipper of the great goddess Diana, and of the {image} which fell down from Jupiter? {a worshipper: Gr. the temple keeper}
verses.nlt_text: At last the mayor was able to quiet them down enough to speak. "Citizens of Ephesus," he said. "Everyone knows that Ephesus is the official guardian of the temple of the great Artemis, whose image fell down to us from heaven.

verses.kjv_text: Seeing then that these things cannot be spoken against, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
verses.nlt_text: Since this is an undeniable fact, you should stay calm and not do anything rash.

verses.kjv_text: For ye have brought hither these men, which are neither robbers of churches, nor yet blasphemers of your goddess.
verses.nlt_text: You have brought these men here, but they have stolen nothing from the temple and have not spoken against our goddess.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another. {the law...: or, the court days are kept}
verses.nlt_text: "If Demetrius and the craftsmen have a case against them, the courts are in session and the officials can hear the case at once. Let them make formal charges.

verses.kjv_text: But if ye enquire any thing concerning other matters, it shall be determined in a lawful assembly. {lawful: or, ordinary}
verses.nlt_text: And if there are complaints about other matters, they can be settled in a legal assembly.

verses.kjv_text: For we are in danger to be called in question for this day's uproar, there being no cause whereby we may give an account of this concourse.
verses.nlt_text: I am afraid we are in danger of being charged with rioting by the Roman government, since there is no cause for all this commotion. And if Rome demands an explanation, we won't know what to say."

verses.kjv_text: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.
verses.nlt_text: Then he dismissed them, and they dispersed.

verses.kjv_text: And after the uproar was ceased, Paul called unto {him} the disciples, and embraced {them}, and departed for to go into Macedonia.
verses.nlt_text: When the uproar was over, Paul sent for the believers and encouraged them. Then he said good-bye and left for Macedonia.

verses.kjv_text: And when he had gone over those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece,
verses.nlt_text: While there, he encouraged the believers in all the towns he passed through. Then he traveled down to Greece,

verses.kjv_text: And {there} abode three months. And when the Jews laid wait for him, as he was about to sail into Syria, he purposed to return through Macedonia.
verses.nlt_text: where he stayed for three months. He was preparing to sail back to Syria when he discovered a plot by some Jews against his life, so he decided to return through Macedonia.

verses.kjv_text: And there accompanied him into Asia Sopater of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timotheus; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
verses.nlt_text: Several men were traveling with him. They were Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea; Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica; Gaius from Derbe; Timothy; and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.

verses.kjv_text: These going before tarried for us at Troas.
verses.nlt_text: They went on ahead and waited for us at Troas.

verses.kjv_text: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we abode seven days.
verses.nlt_text: After the Passover ended, we boarded a ship at Philippi in Macedonia and five days later joined them in Troas, where we stayed a week.

verses.kjv_text: And upon the first {day} of the week, when the disciples came together to break bread, Paul preached unto them, ready to depart on the morrow; and continued his speech until midnight.
verses.nlt_text: On the first day of the week, we gathered with the local believers to share in the Lord's Supper. Paul was preaching to them, and since he was leaving the next day, he kept talking until midnight.

verses.kjv_text: And there were many lights in the upper chamber, where they were gathered together.
verses.nlt_text: The upstairs room where we met was lighted with many flickering lamps.

verses.kjv_text: And there sat in a window a certain young man named Eutychus, being fallen into a deep sleep: and as Paul was long preaching, he sunk down with sleep, and fell down from the third loft, and was taken up dead.
verses.nlt_text: As Paul spoke on and on, a young man named Eutychus, sitting on the windowsill, became very drowsy. Finally, he fell sound asleep and dropped three stories to his death below.

verses.kjv_text: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing {him} said, Trouble not yourselves; for his life is in him.
verses.nlt_text: Paul went down, bent over him, and took him into his arms. "Don't worry," he said, "he's alive!"

verses.kjv_text: When he therefore was come up again, and had broken bread, and eaten, and talked a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.
verses.nlt_text: Then they all went back upstairs, shared in the Lord's Supper, and ate together. Paul continued talking to them until dawn, and then he left.

verses.kjv_text: And they brought the young man alive, and were not a little comforted.
verses.nlt_text: Meanwhile, the young man was taken home unhurt, and everyone was greatly relieved.

verses.kjv_text: And we went before to ship, and sailed unto Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, minding himself to go afoot.
verses.nlt_text: Paul went by land to Assos, where he had arranged for us to join him, while we traveled by ship.

verses.kjv_text: And when he met with us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.
verses.nlt_text: He joined us there, and we sailed together to Mitylene.

verses.kjv_text: And we sailed thence, and came the next {day} over against Chios; and the next {day} we arrived at Samos, and tarried at Trogyllium; and the next {day} we came to Miletus.
verses.nlt_text: The next day we sailed past the island of Kios. The following day we crossed to the island of Samos, and a day later we arrived at Miletus.

verses.kjv_text: For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, because he would not spend the time in Asia: for he hasted, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
verses.nlt_text: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, for he didn't want to spend any more time in the province of Asia. He was hurrying to get to Jerusalem, if possible, in time for the Festival of Pentecost.

verses.kjv_text: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called the elders of the church.
verses.nlt_text: But when we landed at Miletus, he sent a message to the elders of the church at Ephesus, asking them to come and meet him.

verses.kjv_text: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye know, from the first day that I came into Asia, after what manner I have been with you at all seasons,
verses.nlt_text: When they arrived he declared, "You know that from the day I set foot in the province of Asia until now

verses.kjv_text: Serving the Lord with all humility of mind, and with many tears, and temptations, which befell me by the lying in wait of the Jews:
verses.nlt_text: I have done the Lord's work humbly and with many tears. I have endured the trials that came to me from the plots of the Jews.

verses.kjv_text: {And} how I kept back nothing that was profitable {unto you}, but have shewed you, and have taught you publickly, and from house to house,
verses.nlt_text: I never shrank back from telling you what you needed to hear, either publicly or in your homes.

verses.kjv_text: Testifying both to the Jews, and also to the Greeks, repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.nlt_text: I have had one message for Jews and Greeks alike-- the necessity of repenting from sin and turning to God, and of having faith in our Lord Jesus.

verses.kjv_text: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
verses.nlt_text: "And now I am bound by the Spirit to go to Jerusalem. I don't know what awaits me,

verses.kjv_text: Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me. {abide me: or, wait for me}
verses.nlt_text: except that the Holy Spirit tells me in city after city that jail and suffering lie ahead.

verses.kjv_text: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
verses.nlt_text: But my life is worth nothing to me unless I use it for finishing the work assigned me by the Lord Jesus-- the work of telling others the Good News about the wonderful grace of God.

verses.kjv_text: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I have gone preaching the kingdom of God, shall see my face no more.
verses.nlt_text: "And now I know that none of you to whom I have preached the Kingdom will ever see me again.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore I take you to record this day, that I {am} pure from the blood of all {men}.
verses.nlt_text: I declare today that I have been faithful. If anyone suffers eternal death, it's not my fault,

verses.kjv_text: For I have not shunned to declare unto you all the counsel of God.
verses.nlt_text: for I didn't shrink from declaring all that God wants you to know.

verses.kjv_text: Take heed therefore unto yourselves, and to all the flock, over the which the Holy Ghost hath made you overseers, to feed the church of God, which he hath purchased with his own blood.
verses.nlt_text: "So guard yourselves and God's people. Feed and shepherd God's flock-- his church, purchased with his own blood-- over which the Holy Spirit has appointed you as elders.

verses.kjv_text: For I know this, that after my departing shall grievous wolves enter in among you, not sparing the flock.
verses.nlt_text: I know that false teachers, like vicious wolves, will come in among you after I leave, not sparing the flock.

verses.kjv_text: Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them.
verses.nlt_text: Even some men from your own group will rise up and distort the truth in order to draw a following.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears.
verses.nlt_text: Watch out! Remember the three years I was with you-- my constant watch and care over you night and day, and my many tears for you.

verses.kjv_text: And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.
verses.nlt_text: "And now I entrust you to God and the message of his grace that is able to build you up and give you an inheritance with all those he has set apart for himself.

verses.kjv_text: I have coveted no man's silver, or gold, or apparel.
verses.nlt_text: "I have never coveted anyone's silver or gold or fine clothes.

verses.kjv_text: Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
verses.nlt_text: You know that these hands of mine have worked to supply my own needs and even the needs of those who were with me.

verses.kjv_text: I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.
verses.nlt_text: And I have been a constant example of how you can help those in need by working hard. You should remember the words of the Lord Jesus: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"

verses.kjv_text: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down, and prayed with them all.
verses.nlt_text: When he had finished speaking, he knelt and prayed with them.

verses.kjv_text: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul's neck, and kissed him,
verses.nlt_text: They all cried as they embraced and kissed him good-bye.

verses.kjv_text: Sorrowing most of all for the words which he spake, that they should see his face no more. And they accompanied him unto the ship.
verses.nlt_text: They were sad most of all because he had said that they would never see him again. Then they escorted him down to the ship.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the {day} following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:
verses.nlt_text: After saying farewell to the Ephesian elders, we sailed straight to the island of Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and then went to Patara.

verses.kjv_text: And finding a ship sailing over unto Phenicia, we went aboard, and set forth.
verses.nlt_text: There we boarded a ship sailing for Phoenicia.

verses.kjv_text: Now when we had discovered Cyprus, we left it on the left hand, and sailed into Syria, and landed at Tyre: for there the ship was to unlade her burden.
verses.nlt_text: We sighted the island of Cyprus, passed it on our left, and landed at the harbor of Tyre, in Syria, where the ship was to unload its cargo.

verses.kjv_text: And finding disciples, we tarried there seven days: who said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not go up to Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: We went ashore, found the local believers, and stayed with them a week. These believers prophesied through the Holy Spirit that Paul should not go on to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till {we were} out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed.
verses.nlt_text: When we returned to the ship at the end of the week, the entire congregation, including wives and children, left the city and came down to the shore with us. There we knelt, prayed,

verses.kjv_text: And when we had taken our leave one of another, we took ship; and they returned home again.
verses.nlt_text: and said our farewells. Then we went aboard, and they returned home.

verses.kjv_text: And when we had finished {our} course from Tyre, we came to Ptolemais, and saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.
verses.nlt_text: The next stop after leaving Tyre was Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and sisters and stayed for one day.

verses.kjv_text: And the next {day} we that were of Paul's company departed, and came unto Caesarea: and we entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was {one} of the seven; and abode with him.
verses.nlt_text: The next day we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the Evangelist, one of the seven men who had been chosen to distribute food.

verses.kjv_text: And the same man had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy.
verses.nlt_text: He had four unmarried daughters who had the gift of prophecy.

verses.kjv_text: And as we tarried {there} many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus.
verses.nlt_text: Several days later a man named Agabus, who also had the gift of prophecy, arrived from Judea.

verses.kjv_text: And when he was come unto us, he took Paul's girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver {him} into the hands of the Gentiles.
verses.nlt_text: He came over, took Paul's belt, and bound his own feet and hands with it. Then he said, "The Holy Spirit declares, 'So shall the owner of this belt be bound by the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem and turned over to the Gentiles.'"

verses.kjv_text: And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: When we heard this, we and the local believers all begged Paul not to go on to Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.nlt_text: But he said, "Why all this weeping? You are breaking my heart! I am ready not only to be jailed at Jerusalem but even to die for the sake of the Lord Jesus."

verses.kjv_text: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.
verses.nlt_text: When it was clear that we couldn't persuade him, we gave up and said, "The Lord's will be done."

verses.kjv_text: And after those days we took up our carriages, and went up to Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: After this we packed our things and left for Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: There went with us also {certain} of the disciples of Caesarea, and brought with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an old disciple, with whom we should lodge.
verses.nlt_text: Some believers from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to the home of Mnason, a man originally from Cyprus and one of the early believers.

verses.kjv_text: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
verses.nlt_text: When we arrived, the brothers and sisters in Jerusalem welcomed us warmly.

verses.kjv_text: And the {day} following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.
verses.nlt_text: The next day Paul went with us to meet with James, and all the elders of the Jerusalem church were present.

verses.kjv_text: And when he had saluted them, he declared particularly what things God had wrought among the Gentiles by his ministry.
verses.nlt_text: After greeting them, Paul gave a detailed account of the things God had accomplished among the Gentiles through his ministry.

verses.kjv_text: And when they heard {it}, they glorified the Lord, and said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands of Jews there are which believe; and they are all zealous of the law:
verses.nlt_text: After hearing this, they praised God. And then they said, "You know, dear brother, how many thousands of Jews have also believed, and they all follow the law of Moses very seriously.

verses.kjv_text: And they are informed of thee, that thou teachest all the Jews which are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, saying that they ought not to circumcise {their} children, neither to walk after the customs.
verses.nlt_text: But the Jewish believers here in Jerusalem have been told that you are teaching all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to turn their backs on the laws of Moses. They've heard that you teach them not to circumcise their children or follow other Jewish customs.

verses.kjv_text: What is it therefore? the multitude must needs come together: for they will hear that thou art come.
verses.nlt_text: What should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.

verses.kjv_text: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men which have a vow on them;
verses.nlt_text: "Here's what we want you to do. We have four men here who have completed their vow.

verses.kjv_text: Them take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges with them, that they may shave {their} heads: and all may know that those things, whereof they were informed concerning thee, are nothing; but {that} thou thyself also walkest orderly, and keepest the law.
verses.nlt_text: Go with them to the Temple and join them in the purification ceremony, paying for them to have their heads ritually shaved. Then everyone will know that the rumors are all false and that you yourself observe the Jewish laws.

verses.kjv_text: As touching the Gentiles which believe, we have written {and} concluded that they observe no such thing, save only that they keep themselves from {things} offered to idols, and from blood, and from strangled, and from fornication.
verses.nlt_text: "As for the Gentile believers, they should do what we already told them in a letter: They should abstain from eating food offered to idols, from consuming blood or the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality."

verses.kjv_text: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them entered into the temple, to signify the accomplishment of the days of purification, until that an offering should be offered for every one of them.
verses.nlt_text: So Paul went to the Temple the next day with the other men. They had already started the purification ritual, so he publicly announced the date when their vows would end and sacrifices would be offered for each of them.

verses.kjv_text: And when the seven days were almost ended, the Jews which were of Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the people, and laid hands on him,
verses.nlt_text: The seven days were almost ended when some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul in the Temple and roused a mob against him. They grabbed him,

verses.kjv_text: Crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man, that teacheth all {men} every where against the people, and the law, and this place: and further brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath polluted this holy place.
verses.nlt_text: yelling, "Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who preaches against our people everywhere and tells everybody to disobey the Jewish laws. He speaks against the Temple-- and even defiles this holy place by bringing in Gentiles. "

verses.kjv_text: (For they had seen before with him in the city Trophimus an Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.)
verses.nlt_text: (For earlier that day they had seen him in the city with Trophimus, a Gentile from Ephesus, and they assumed Paul had taken him into the Temple.)

verses.kjv_text: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together: and they took Paul, and drew him out of the temple: and forthwith the doors were shut.
verses.nlt_text: The whole city was rocked by these accusations, and a great riot followed. Paul was grabbed and dragged out of the Temple, and immediately the gates were closed behind him.

verses.kjv_text: And as they went about to kill him, tidings came unto the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
verses.nlt_text: As they were trying to kill him, word reached the commander of the Roman regiment that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.

verses.kjv_text: Who immediately took soldiers and centurions, and ran down unto them: and when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, they left beating of Paul.
verses.nlt_text: He immediately called out his soldiers and officers and ran down among the crowd. When the mob saw the commander and the troops coming, they stopped beating Paul.

verses.kjv_text: Then the chief captain came near, and took him, and commanded {him} to be bound with two chains; and demanded who he was, and what he had done.
verses.nlt_text: Then the commander arrested him and ordered him bound with two chains. He asked the crowd who he was and what he had done.

verses.kjv_text: And some cried one thing, some another, among the multitude: and when he could not know the certainty for the tumult, he commanded him to be carried into the castle.
verses.nlt_text: Some shouted one thing and some another. Since he couldn't find out the truth in all the uproar and confusion, he ordered that Paul be taken to the fortress.

verses.kjv_text: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was, that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the people.
verses.nlt_text: As Paul reached the stairs, the mob grew so violent the soldiers had to lift him to their shoulders to protect him.

verses.kjv_text: For the multitude of the people followed after, crying, Away with him.
verses.nlt_text: And the crowd followed behind, shouting, "Kill him, kill him!"

verses.kjv_text: And as Paul was to be led into the castle, he said unto the chief captain, May I speak unto thee? Who said, Canst thou speak Greek?
verses.nlt_text: As Paul was about to be taken inside, he said to the commander, "May I have a word with you?" "Do you know Greek?" the commander asked, surprised.

verses.kjv_text: Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?
verses.nlt_text: "Aren't you the Egyptian who led a rebellion some time ago and took 4,000 members of the Assassins out into the desert?"

verses.kjv_text: But Paul said, I am a man {which am} a Jew of Tarsus, {a city} in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and, I beseech thee, suffer me to speak unto the people.
verses.nlt_text: "No," Paul replied, "I am a Jew and a citizen of Tarsus in Cilicia, which is an important city. Please, let me talk to these people."

verses.kjv_text: And when he had given him licence, Paul stood on the stairs, and beckoned with the hand unto the people. And when there was made a great silence, he spake unto {them} in the Hebrew tongue, saying,
verses.nlt_text: The commander agreed, so Paul stood on the stairs and motioned to the people to be quiet. Soon a deep silence enveloped the crowd, and he addressed them in their own language, Aramaic.

verses.kjv_text: Men, brethren, and fathers, hear ye my defence {which I make} now unto you.
verses.nlt_text: "Brothers and esteemed fathers," Paul said, "listen to me as I offer my defense."

verses.kjv_text: (And when they heard that he spake in the Hebrew tongue to them, they kept the more silence: and he saith,)
verses.nlt_text: When they heard him speaking in their own language, the silence was even greater.

verses.kjv_text: I am verily a man {which am} a Jew, born in Tarsus, {a city} in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, {and} taught according to the perfect manner of the law of the fathers, and was zealous toward God, as ye all are this day.
verses.nlt_text: Then Paul said, "I am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, and I was brought up and educated here in Jerusalem under Gamaliel. As his student, I was carefully trained in our Jewish laws and customs. I became very zealous to honor God in everything I did, just like all of you today.

verses.kjv_text: And I persecuted this way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.
verses.nlt_text: And I persecuted the followers of the Way, hounding some to death, arresting both men and women and throwing them in prison.

verses.kjv_text: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and went to Damascus, to bring them which were there bound unto Jerusalem, for to be punished.
verses.nlt_text: The high priest and the whole council of elders can testify that this is so. For I received letters from them to our Jewish brothers in Damascus, authorizing me to bring the Christians from there to Jerusalem, in chains, to be punished.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and was come nigh unto Damascus about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.
verses.nlt_text: "As I was on the road, approaching Damascus about noon, a very bright light from heaven suddenly shone down around me.

verses.kjv_text: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
verses.nlt_text: I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?'

verses.kjv_text: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.
verses.nlt_text: " 'Who are you, lord?' I asked."And the voice replied, 'I am Jesus the Nazarene, the one you are persecuting.'

verses.kjv_text: And they that were with me saw indeed the light, and were afraid; but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.
verses.nlt_text: The people with me saw the light but didn't understand the voice speaking to me.

verses.kjv_text: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.
verses.nlt_text: "I asked, 'What should I do, Lord?'"And the Lord told me, 'Get up and go into Damascus, and there you will be told everything you are to do.'

verses.kjv_text: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me, I came into Damascus.
verses.nlt_text: "I was blinded by the intense light and had to be led by the hand to Damascus by my companions.

verses.kjv_text: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, having a good report of all the Jews which dwelt {there},
verses.nlt_text: A man named Ananias lived there. He was a godly man, deeply devoted to the law, and well regarded by all the Jews of Damascus.

verses.kjv_text: Came unto me, and stood, and said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And the same hour I looked up upon him.
verses.nlt_text: He came and stood beside me and said, 'Brother Saul, regain your sight.' And that very moment I could see him!

verses.kjv_text: And he said, The God of our fathers hath chosen thee, that thou shouldest know his will, and see that Just One, and shouldest hear the voice of his mouth.
verses.nlt_text: "Then he told me, 'The God of our ancestors has chosen you to know his will and to see the Righteous One and hear him speak.

verses.kjv_text: For thou shalt be his witness unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
verses.nlt_text: For you are to be his witness, telling everyone what you have seen and heard.

verses.kjv_text: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on the name of the Lord.
verses.nlt_text: What are you waiting for? Get up and be baptized. Have your sins washed away by calling on the name of the Lord.'

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that, when I was come again to Jerusalem, even while I prayed in the temple, I was in a trance;
verses.nlt_text: "After I returned to Jerusalem, I was praying in the Temple and fell into a trance.

verses.kjv_text: And saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
verses.nlt_text: I saw a vision of Jesus saying to me, 'Hurry! Leave Jerusalem, for the people here won't accept your testimony about me.'

verses.kjv_text: And I said, Lord, they know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:
verses.nlt_text: " 'But Lord,' I argued, 'they certainly know that in every synagogue I imprisoned and beat those who believed in you.

verses.kjv_text: And when the blood of thy martyr Stephen was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting unto his death, and kept the raiment of them that slew him.
verses.nlt_text: And I was in complete agreement when your witness Stephen was killed. I stood by and kept the coats they took off when they stoned him.'

verses.kjv_text: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
verses.nlt_text: "But the Lord said to me, 'Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles!'"

verses.kjv_text: And they gave him audience unto this word, and {then} lifted up their voices, and said, Away with such a {fellow} from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.
verses.nlt_text: The crowd listened until Paul said that word. Then they all began to shout, "Away with such a fellow! He isn't fit to live!"

verses.kjv_text: And as they cried out, and cast off {their} clothes, and threw dust into the air,
verses.nlt_text: They yelled, threw off their coats, and tossed handfuls of dust into the air.

verses.kjv_text: The chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, and bade that he should be examined by scourging; that he might know wherefore they cried so against him.
verses.nlt_text: The commander brought Paul inside and ordered him lashed with whips to make him confess his crime. He wanted to find out why the crowd had become so furious.

verses.kjv_text: And as they bound him with thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?
