verses.nlt_text: When they tied Paul down to lash him, Paul said to the officer standing there, "Is it legal for you to whip a Roman citizen who hasn't even been tried?"

verses.kjv_text: When the centurion heard {that}, he went and told the chief captain, saying, Take heed what thou doest: for this man is a Roman.
verses.nlt_text: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and asked, "What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!"

verses.kjv_text: Then the chief captain came, and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? He said, Yea.
verses.nlt_text: So the commander went over and asked Paul, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" "Yes, I certainly am," Paul replied.

verses.kjv_text: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this freedom. And Paul said, But I was {free} born.
verses.nlt_text: "I am, too," the commander muttered, "and it cost me plenty!" Paul answered, "But I am a citizen by birth!"

verses.kjv_text: Then straightway they departed from him which should have examined him: and the chief captain also was afraid, after he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him. {examined him: or, tortured him}
verses.nlt_text: The soldiers who were about to interrogate Paul quickly withdrew when they heard he was a Roman citizen, and the commander was frightened because he had ordered him bound and whipped.

verses.kjv_text: On the morrow, because he would have known the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him from {his} bands, and commanded the chief priests and all their council to appear, and brought Paul down, and set him before them.
verses.nlt_text: The next day the commander ordered the leading priests into session with the Jewish high council. He wanted to find out what the trouble was all about, so he released Paul to have him stand before them.

verses.kjv_text: And Paul, earnestly beholding the council, said, Men {and} brethren, I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day.
verses.nlt_text: Gazing intently at the high council, Paul began: "Brothers, I have always lived before God with a clear conscience!"

verses.kjv_text: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
verses.nlt_text: Instantly Ananias the high priest commanded those close to Paul to slap him on the mouth.

verses.kjv_text: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, {thou} whited wall: for sittest thou to judge me after the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?
verses.nlt_text: But Paul said to him, "God will slap you, you corrupt hypocrite! What kind of judge are you to break the law yourself by ordering me struck like that?"

verses.kjv_text: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest?
verses.nlt_text: Those standing near Paul said to him, "Do you dare to insult God's high priest?"

verses.kjv_text: Then said Paul, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
verses.nlt_text: "I'm sorry, brothers. I didn't realize he was the high priest," Paul replied, "for the Scriptures say, 'You must not speak evil of any of your rulers.' "

verses.kjv_text: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Men {and} brethren, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee: of the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.
verses.nlt_text: Paul realized that some members of the high council were Sadducees and some were Pharisees, so he shouted, "Brothers, I am a Pharisee, as were my ancestors! And I am on trial because my hope is in the resurrection of the dead!"

verses.kjv_text: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and the Sadducees: and the multitude was divided.
verses.nlt_text: This divided the council-- the Pharisees against the Sadducees--

verses.kjv_text: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit: but the Pharisees confess both.
verses.nlt_text: for the Sadducees say there is no resurrection or angels or spirits, but the Pharisees believe in all of these.

verses.kjv_text: And there arose a great cry: and the scribes {that were} of the Pharisees' part arose, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: but if a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
verses.nlt_text: So there was a great uproar. Some of the teachers of religious law who were Pharisees jumped up and began to argue forcefully. "We see nothing wrong with him," they shouted. "Perhaps a spirit or an angel spoke to him."

verses.kjv_text: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should have been pulled in pieces of them, commanded the soldiers to go down, and to take him by force from among them, and to bring {him} into the castle.
verses.nlt_text: As the conflict grew more violent, the commander was afraid they would tear Paul apart. So he ordered his soldiers to go and rescue him by force and take him back to the fortress.

verses.kjv_text: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
verses.nlt_text: That night the Lord appeared to Paul and said, "Be encouraged, Paul. Just as you have been a witness to me here in Jerusalem, you must preach the Good News in Rome as well."

verses.kjv_text: And when it was day, certain of the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul. {under a curse: or, with an oath of execration}
verses.nlt_text: The next morning a group of Jews got together and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.

verses.kjv_text: And they were more than forty which had made this conspiracy.
verses.nlt_text: There were more than forty of them in the conspiracy.

verses.kjv_text: And they came to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, that we will eat nothing until we have slain Paul.
verses.nlt_text: They went to the leading priests and elders and told them, "We have bound ourselves with an oath to eat nothing until we have killed Paul.

verses.kjv_text: Now therefore ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you to morrow, as though ye would enquire something more perfectly concerning him: and we, or ever he come near, are ready to kill him.
verses.nlt_text: So you and the high council should ask the commander to bring Paul back to the council again. Pretend you want to examine his case more fully. We will kill him on the way."

verses.kjv_text: And when Paul's sister's son heard of their lying in wait, he went and entered into the castle, and told Paul.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul's nephew-- his sister's son-- heard of their plan and went to the fortress and told Paul.

verses.kjv_text: Then Paul called one of the centurions unto {him}, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain: for he hath a certain thing to tell him.
verses.nlt_text: Paul called for one of the Roman officers and said, "Take this young man to the commander. He has something important to tell him."

verses.kjv_text: So he took him, and brought {him} to the chief captain, and said, Paul the prisoner called me unto {him}, and prayed me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say unto thee.
verses.nlt_text: So the officer did, explaining, "Paul, the prisoner, called me over and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you."

verses.kjv_text: Then the chief captain took him by the hand, and went {with him} aside privately, and asked {him}, What is that thou hast to tell me?
verses.nlt_text: The commander took his hand, led him aside, and asked, "What is it you want to tell me?"

verses.kjv_text: And he said, The Jews have agreed to desire thee that thou wouldest bring down Paul to morrow into the council, as though they would enquire somewhat of him more perfectly.
verses.nlt_text: Paul's nephew told him, "Some Jews are going to ask you to bring Paul before the high council tomorrow, pretending they want to get some more information.

verses.kjv_text: But do not thou yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, which have bound themselves with an oath, that they will neither eat nor drink till they have killed him: and now are they ready, looking for a promise from thee.
verses.nlt_text: But don't do it! There are more than forty men hiding along the way ready to ambush him. They have vowed not to eat or drink anything until they have killed him. They are ready now, just waiting for your consent."

verses.kjv_text: So the chief captain {then} let the young man depart, and charged {him, See thou} tell no man that thou hast shewed these things to me.
verses.nlt_text: "Don't let anyone know you told me this," the commander warned the young man.

verses.kjv_text: And he called unto {him} two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
verses.nlt_text: Then the commander called two of his officers and ordered, "Get 200 soldiers ready to leave for Caesarea at nine o'clock tonight. Also take 200 spearmen and 70 mounted troops.

verses.kjv_text: And provide {them} beasts, that they may set Paul on, and bring {him} safe unto Felix the governor.
verses.nlt_text: Provide horses for Paul to ride, and get him safely to Governor Felix."

verses.kjv_text: And he wrote a letter after this manner:
verses.nlt_text: Then he wrote this letter to the governor:

verses.kjv_text: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix {sendeth} greeting.
verses.nlt_text: "From Claudius Lysias, to his Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings!

verses.kjv_text: This man was taken of the Jews, and should have been killed of them: then came I with an army, and rescued him, having understood that he was a Roman.
verses.nlt_text: "This man was seized by some Jews, and they were about to kill him when I arrived with the troops. When I learned that he was a Roman citizen, I removed him to safety.

verses.kjv_text: And when I would have known the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him forth into their council:
verses.nlt_text: Then I took him to their high council to try to learn the basis of the accusations against him.

verses.kjv_text: Whom I perceived to be accused of questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.nlt_text: I soon discovered the charge was something regarding their religious law-- certainly nothing worthy of imprisonment or death.

verses.kjv_text: And when it was told me how that the Jews laid wait for the man, I sent straightway to thee, and gave commandment to his accusers also to say before thee what {they had} against him. Farewell.
verses.nlt_text: But when I was informed of a plot to kill him, I immediately sent him on to you. I have told his accusers to bring their charges before you."

verses.kjv_text: Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought {him} by night to Antipatris.
verses.nlt_text: So that night, as ordered, the soldiers took Paul as far as Antipatris.

verses.kjv_text: On the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:
verses.nlt_text: They returned to the fortress the next morning, while the mounted troops took him on to Caesarea.

verses.kjv_text: Who, when they came to Caesarea, and delivered the epistle to the governor, presented Paul also before him.
verses.nlt_text: When they arrived in Caesarea, they presented Paul and the letter to Governor Felix.

verses.kjv_text: And when the governor had read {the letter}, he asked of what province he was. And when he understood that {he was} of Cilicia;
verses.nlt_text: He read it and then asked Paul what province he was from. "Cilicia," Paul answered.

verses.kjv_text: I will hear thee, said he, when thine accusers are also come. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's judgment hall.
verses.nlt_text: "I will hear your case myself when your accusers arrive," the governor told him. Then the governor ordered him kept in the prison at Herod's headquarters.

verses.kjv_text: And after five days Ananias the high priest descended with the elders, and {with} a certain orator {named} Tertullus, who informed the governor against Paul.
verses.nlt_text: Five days later Ananias, the high priest, arrived with some of the Jewish elders and the lawyer Tertullus, to present their case against Paul to the governor.

verses.kjv_text: And when he was called forth, Tertullus began to accuse {him}, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy great quietness, and that very worthy deeds are done unto this nation by thy providence,
verses.nlt_text: When Paul was called in, Tertullus presented the charges against Paul in the following address to the governor:"Your Excellency, you have provided a long period of peace for us Jews and with foresight have enacted reforms for us.

verses.kjv_text: We accept {it} always, and in all places, most noble Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.nlt_text: For all of this we are very grateful to you.

verses.kjv_text: Notwithstanding, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I pray thee that thou wouldest hear us of thy clemency a few words.
verses.nlt_text: But I don't want to bore you, so please give me your attention for only a moment.

verses.kjv_text: For we have found this man {a} pestilent {fellow}, and a mover of sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:
verses.nlt_text: We have found this man to be a troublemaker who is constantly stirring up riots among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the cult known as the Nazarenes.

verses.kjv_text: Who also hath gone about to profane the temple: whom we took, and would have judged according to our law.
verses.nlt_text: Furthermore, he was trying to desecrate the Temple when we arrested him.

verses.kjv_text: But the chief captain Lysias came {upon us}, and with great violence took {him} away out of our hands,
Commanding his accusers to come unto thee: by examining of whom thyself mayest take knowledge of all these things, whereof we accuse him.
verses.nlt_text: You can find out the truth of our accusations by examining him yourself."

verses.kjv_text: And the Jews also assented, saying that these things were so.
verses.nlt_text: Then the other Jews chimed in, declaring that everything Tertullus said was true.

verses.kjv_text: Then Paul, after that the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I do the more cheerfully answer for myself:
verses.nlt_text: The governor then motioned for Paul to speak. Paul said, "I know, sir, that you have been a judge of Jewish affairs for many years, so I gladly present my defense before you.

verses.kjv_text: Because that thou mayest understand, that there are yet but twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem for to worship.
verses.nlt_text: You can quickly discover that I arrived in Jerusalem no more than twelve days ago to worship at the Temple.

verses.kjv_text: And they neither found me in the temple disputing with any man, neither raising up the people, neither in the synagogues, nor in the city:
verses.nlt_text: My accusers never found me arguing with anyone in the Temple, nor stirring up a riot in any synagogue or on the streets of the city.

verses.kjv_text: Neither can they prove the things whereof they now accuse me.
verses.nlt_text: These men cannot prove the things they accuse me of doing.

verses.kjv_text: But this I confess unto thee, that after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets:
verses.nlt_text: "But I admit that I follow the Way, which they call a cult. I worship the God of our ancestors, and I firmly believe the Jewish law and everything written in the prophets.

verses.kjv_text: And have hope toward God, which they themselves also allow, that there shall be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
verses.nlt_text: I have the same hope in God that these men have, that he will raise both the righteous and the unrighteous.

verses.kjv_text: And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and {toward} men.
verses.nlt_text: Because of this, I always try to maintain a clear conscience before God and all people.

verses.kjv_text: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings.
verses.nlt_text: "After several years away, I returned to Jerusalem with money to aid my people and to offer sacrifices to God.

verses.kjv_text: Whereupon certain Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, neither with multitude, nor with tumult.
verses.nlt_text: My accusers saw me in the Temple as I was completing a purification ceremony. There was no crowd around me and no rioting.

verses.kjv_text: Who ought to have been here before thee, and object, if they had ought against me.
verses.nlt_text: But some Jews from the province of Asia were there-- and they ought to be here to bring charges if they have anything against me!

verses.kjv_text: Or else let these same {here} say, if they have found any evil doing in me, while I stood before the council,
verses.nlt_text: Ask these men here what crime the Jewish high council found me guilty of,

verses.kjv_text: Except it be for this one voice, that I cried standing among them, Touching the resurrection of the dead I am called in question by you this day.
verses.nlt_text: except for the one time I shouted out, 'I am on trial before you today because I believe in the resurrection of the dead!'"

verses.kjv_text: And when Felix heard these things, having more perfect knowledge of {that} way, he deferred them, and said, When Lysias the chief captain shall come down, I will know the uttermost of your matter.
verses.nlt_text: At that point Felix, who was quite familiar with the Way, adjourned the hearing and said, "Wait until Lysias, the garrison commander, arrives. Then I will decide the case."

verses.kjv_text: And he commanded a centurion to keep Paul, and to let {him} have liberty, and that he should forbid none of his acquaintance to minister or come unto him.
verses.nlt_text: He ordered an officer to keep Paul in custody but to give him some freedom and allow his friends to visit him and take care of his needs.

verses.kjv_text: And after certain days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, which was a Jewess, he sent for Paul, and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
verses.nlt_text: A few days later Felix came back with his wife, Drusilla, who was Jewish. Sending for Paul, they listened as he told them about faith in Christ Jesus.

verses.kjv_text: And as he reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee.
verses.nlt_text: As he reasoned with them about righteousness and self-control and the coming day of judgment, Felix became frightened. "Go away for now," he replied. "When it is more convenient, I'll call for you again."

verses.kjv_text: He hoped also that money should have been given him of Paul, that he might loose him: wherefore he sent for him the oftener, and communed with him.
verses.nlt_text: He also hoped that Paul would bribe him, so he sent for him quite often and talked with him.

verses.kjv_text: But after two years Porcius Festus came into Felix' room: and Felix, willing to shew the Jews a pleasure, left Paul bound.
verses.nlt_text: After two years went by in this way, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And because Felix wanted to gain favor with the Jewish people, he left Paul in prison.

verses.kjv_text: Now when Festus was come into the province, after three days he ascended from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
verses.nlt_text: Three days after Festus arrived in Caesarea to take over his new responsibilities, he left for Jerusalem,

verses.kjv_text: Then the high priest and the chief of the Jews informed him against Paul, and besought him,
verses.nlt_text: where the leading priests and other Jewish leaders met with him and made their accusations against Paul.

verses.kjv_text: And desired favour against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him.
verses.nlt_text: They asked Festus as a favor to transfer Paul to Jerusalem (planning to ambush and kill him on the way).

verses.kjv_text: But Festus answered, that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself would depart shortly {thither}.
verses.nlt_text: But Festus replied that Paul was at Caesarea and he himself would be returning there soon.

verses.kjv_text: Let them therefore, said he, which among you are able, go down with {me}, and accuse this man, if there be any wickedness in him.
verses.nlt_text: So he said, "Those of you in authority can return with me. If Paul has done anything wrong, you can make your accusations."

verses.kjv_text: And when he had tarried among them more than ten days, he went down unto Caesarea; and the next day sitting on the judgment seat commanded Paul to be brought. {more...: or, as some copies read, no more than eight or ten days}
verses.nlt_text: About eight or ten days later Festus returned to Caesarea, and on the following day he took his seat in court and ordered that Paul be brought in.

verses.kjv_text: And when he was come, the Jews which came down from Jerusalem stood round about, and laid many and grievous complaints against Paul, which they could not prove.
verses.nlt_text: When Paul arrived, the Jewish leaders from Jerusalem gathered around and made many serious accusations they couldn't prove.

verses.kjv_text: While he answered for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, neither against the temple, nor yet against Caesar, have I offended any thing at all.
verses.nlt_text: Paul denied the charges. "I am not guilty of any crime against the Jewish laws or the Temple or the Roman government," he said.

verses.kjv_text: But Festus, willing to do the Jews a pleasure, answered Paul, and said, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these things before me?
verses.nlt_text: Then Festus, wanting to please the Jews, asked him, "Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial before me there?"

verses.kjv_text: Then said Paul, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged: to the Jews have I done no wrong, as thou very well knowest.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul replied, "No! This is the official Roman court, so I ought to be tried right here. You know very well I am not guilty of harming the Jews.

verses.kjv_text: For if I be an offender, or have committed any thing worthy of death, I refuse not to die: but if there be none of these things whereof these accuse me, no man may deliver me unto them. I appeal unto Caesar.
verses.nlt_text: If I have done something worthy of death, I don't refuse to die. But if I am innocent, no one has a right to turn me over to these men to kill me. I appeal to Caesar!"

verses.kjv_text: Then Festus, when he had conferred with the council, answered, Hast thou appealed unto Caesar? unto Caesar shalt thou go.
verses.nlt_text: Festus conferred with his advisers and then replied, "Very well! You have appealed to Caesar, and to Caesar you will go!"

verses.kjv_text: And after certain days king Agrippa and Bernice came unto Caesarea to salute Festus.
verses.nlt_text: A few days later King Agrippa arrived with his sister, Bernice, to pay their respects to Festus.

verses.kjv_text: And when they had been there many days, Festus declared Paul's cause unto the king, saying, There is a certain man left in bonds by Felix:
verses.nlt_text: During their stay of several days, Festus discussed Paul's case with the king. "There is a prisoner here," he told him, "whose case was left for me by Felix.

verses.kjv_text: About whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed {me}, desiring {to have} judgment against him.
verses.nlt_text: When I was in Jerusalem, the leading priests and Jewish elders pressed charges against him and asked me to condemn him.

verses.kjv_text: To whom I answered, It is not the manner of the Romans to deliver any man to die, before that he which is accused have the accusers face to face, and have licence to answer for himself concerning the crime laid against him.
verses.nlt_text: I pointed out to them that Roman law does not convict people without a trial. They must be given an opportunity to confront their accusers and defend themselves.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore, when they were come hither, without any delay on the morrow I sat on the judgment seat, and commanded the man to be brought forth.
verses.nlt_text: "When his accusers came here for the trial, I didn't delay. I called the case the very next day and ordered Paul brought in.

verses.kjv_text: Against whom when the accusers stood up, they brought none accusation of such things as I supposed:
verses.nlt_text: But the accusations made against him weren't any of the crimes I expected.

verses.kjv_text: But had certain questions against him of their own superstition, and of one Jesus, which was dead, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
verses.nlt_text: Instead, it was something about their religion and a dead man named Jesus, who Paul insists is alive.

verses.kjv_text: And because I doubted of such manner of questions, I asked {him} whether he would go to Jerusalem, and there be judged of these matters. {I doubted...: or, I was doubtful how to enquire hereof}
verses.nlt_text: I was at a loss to know how to investigate these things, so I asked him whether he would be willing to stand trial on these charges in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: But when Paul had appealed to be reserved unto the hearing of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I might send him to Caesar. {hearing: or, judgment}
verses.nlt_text: But Paul appealed to have his case decided by the emperor. So I ordered that he be held in custody until I could arrange to send him to Caesar."

verses.kjv_text: Then Agrippa said unto Festus, I would also hear the man myself. To morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.
verses.nlt_text: "I'd like to hear the man myself," Agrippa said.And Festus replied, "You will-- tomorrow!"

verses.kjv_text: And on the morrow, when Agrippa was come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and was entered into the place of hearing, with the chief captains, and principal men of the city, at Festus' commandment Paul was brought forth.
verses.nlt_text: So the next day Agrippa and Bernice arrived at the auditorium with great pomp, accompanied by military officers and prominent men of the city. Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.

verses.kjv_text: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men which are here present with us, ye see this man, about whom all the multitude of the Jews have dealt with me, both at Jerusalem, and {also} here, crying that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.nlt_text: Then Festus said, "King Agrippa and all who are here, this is the man whose death is demanded by all the Jews, both here and in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: But when I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and that he himself hath appealed to Augustus, I have determined to send him.
verses.nlt_text: But in my opinion he has done nothing deserving death. However, since he appealed his case to the emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.

verses.kjv_text: Of whom I have no certain thing to write unto my lord. Wherefore I have brought him forth before you, and specially before thee, O king Agrippa, that, after examination had, I might have somewhat to write.
verses.nlt_text: "But what shall I write the emperor? For there is no clear charge against him. So I have brought him before all of you, and especially you, King Agrippa, so that after we examine him, I might have something to write.

verses.kjv_text: For it seemeth to me unreasonable to send a prisoner, and not withal to signify the crimes {laid} against him.
verses.nlt_text: For it makes no sense to send a prisoner to the emperor without specifying the charges against him!"

verses.kjv_text: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
verses.nlt_text: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You may speak in your defense." So Paul, gesturing with his hand, started his defense:

verses.kjv_text: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
verses.nlt_text: "I am fortunate, King Agrippa, that you are the one hearing my defense today against all these accusations made by the Jewish leaders,

verses.kjv_text: Especially {because I know} thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
verses.nlt_text: for I know you are an expert on all Jewish customs and controversies. Now please listen to me patiently!

verses.kjv_text: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
verses.nlt_text: "As the Jewish leaders are well aware, I was given a thorough Jewish training from my earliest childhood among my own people and in Jerusalem.

verses.kjv_text: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.nlt_text: If they would admit it, they know that I have been a member of the Pharisees, the strictest sect of our religion.

verses.kjv_text: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
verses.nlt_text: Now I am on trial because of my hope in the fulfillment of God's promise made to our ancestors.

verses.kjv_text: Unto which {promise} our twelve tribes, instantly serving {God} day and night, hope to come. For which hope's sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews. {day and night: Gr. night and day}
verses.nlt_text: In fact, that is why the twelve tribes of Israel zealously worship God night and day, and they share the same hope I have. Yet, Your Majesty, they accuse me for having this hope!

verses.kjv_text: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
verses.nlt_text: Why does it seem incredible to any of you that God can raise the dead?

verses.kjv_text: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.nlt_text: "I used to believe that I ought to do everything I could to oppose the very name of Jesus the Nazarene.

verses.kjv_text: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against {them}.
verses.nlt_text: Indeed, I did just that in Jerusalem. Authorized by the leading priests, I caused many believers there to be sent to prison. And I cast my vote against them when they were condemned to death.

verses.kjv_text: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled {them} to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted {them} even unto strange cities.
verses.nlt_text: Many times I had them punished in the synagogues to get them to curse Jesus. I was so violently opposed to them that I even chased them down in foreign cities.

verses.kjv_text: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.nlt_text: "One day I was on such a mission to Damascus, armed with the authority and commission of the leading priests.

verses.kjv_text: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
verses.nlt_text: About noon, Your Majesty, as I was on the road, a light from heaven brighter than the sun shone down on me and my companions.

verses.kjv_text: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? {it is} hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
verses.nlt_text: We all fell down, and I heard a voice saying to me in Aramaic, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is useless for you to fight against my will. '

verses.kjv_text: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
verses.nlt_text: " 'Who are you, lord?' I asked."And the Lord replied, 'I am Jesus, the one you are persecuting.

verses.kjv_text: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
verses.nlt_text: Now get to your feet! For I have appeared to you to appoint you as my servant and witness. You are to tell the world what you have seen and what I will show you in the future.

verses.kjv_text: Delivering thee from the people, and {from} the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
verses.nlt_text: And I will rescue you from both your own people and the Gentiles. Yes, I am sending you to the Gentiles

verses.kjv_text: To open their eyes, {and} to turn {them} from darkness to light, and {from} the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
verses.nlt_text: to open their eyes, so they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then they will receive forgiveness for their sins and be given a place among God's people, who are set apart by faith in me.'

verses.kjv_text: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
verses.nlt_text: "And so, King Agrippa, I obeyed that vision from heaven.

verses.kjv_text: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and {then} to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
verses.nlt_text: I preached first to those in Damascus, then in Jerusalem and throughout all Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that all must repent of their sins and turn to God-- and prove they have changed by the good things they do.

verses.kjv_text: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill {me}.
verses.nlt_text: Some Jews arrested me in the Temple for preaching this, and they tried to kill me.

verses.kjv_text: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
verses.nlt_text: But God has protected me right up to this present time so I can testify to everyone, from the least to the greatest. I teach nothing except what the prophets and Moses said would happen--

verses.kjv_text: That Christ should suffer, {and} that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
verses.nlt_text: that the Messiah would suffer and be the first to rise from the dead, and in this way announce God's light to Jews and Gentiles alike."

verses.kjv_text: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
verses.nlt_text: Suddenly, Festus shouted, "Paul, you are insane. Too much study has made you crazy!"

verses.kjv_text: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul replied, "I am not insane, Most Excellent Festus. What I am saying is the sober truth.

verses.kjv_text: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
verses.nlt_text: And King Agrippa knows about these things. I speak boldly, for I am sure these events are all familiar to him, for they were not done in a corner!

verses.kjv_text: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
verses.nlt_text: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know you do--"

verses.kjv_text: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
verses.nlt_text: Agrippa interrupted him. "Do you think you can persuade me to become a Christian so quickly?"

verses.kjv_text: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
verses.nlt_text: Paul replied, "Whether quickly or not, I pray to God that both you and everyone here in this audience might become the same as I am, except for these chains."

verses.kjv_text: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
verses.nlt_text: Then the king, the governor, Bernice, and all the others stood and left.

verses.kjv_text: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.nlt_text: As they went out, they talked it over and agreed, "This man hasn't done anything to deserve death or imprisonment."

verses.kjv_text: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
verses.nlt_text: And Agrippa said to Festus, "He could have been set free if he hadn't appealed to Caesar."

verses.kjv_text: And when it was determined that we should sail into Italy, they delivered Paul and certain other prisoners unto {one} named Julius, a centurion of Augustus' band.
verses.nlt_text: When the time came, we set sail for Italy. Paul and several other prisoners were placed in the custody of a Roman officer named Julius, a captain of the Imperial Regiment.

verses.kjv_text: And entering into a ship of Adramyttium, we launched, meaning to sail by the coasts of Asia; {one} Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.nlt_text: Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was also with us. We left on a ship whose home port was Adramyttium on the northwest coast of the province of Asia; it was scheduled to make several stops at ports along the coast of the province.

verses.kjv_text: And the next {day} we touched at Sidon. And Julius courteously entreated Paul, and gave {him} liberty to go unto his friends to refresh himself.
verses.nlt_text: The next day when we docked at Sidon, Julius was very kind to Paul and let him go ashore to visit with friends so they could provide for his needs.

verses.kjv_text: And when we had launched from thence, we sailed under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.nlt_text: Putting out to sea from there, we encountered strong headwinds that made it difficult to keep the ship on course, so we sailed north of Cyprus between the island and the mainland.

verses.kjv_text: And when we had sailed over the sea of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra, {a city} of Lycia.
verses.nlt_text: Keeping to the open sea, we passed along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, landing at Myra, in the province of Lycia.

verses.kjv_text: And there the centurion found a ship of Alexandria sailing into Italy; and he put us therein.
verses.nlt_text: There the commanding officer found an Egyptian ship from Alexandria that was bound for Italy, and he put us on board.

verses.kjv_text: And when we had sailed slowly many days, and scarce were come over against Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under Crete, over against Salmone; {Crete: or, Candy}
verses.nlt_text: We had several days of slow sailing, and after great difficulty we finally neared Cnidus. But the wind was against us, so we sailed across to Crete and along the sheltered coast of the island, past the cape of Salmone.

verses.kjv_text: And, hardly passing it, came unto a place which is called The fair havens; nigh whereunto was the city {of} Lasea.
verses.nlt_text: We struggled along the coast with great difficulty and finally arrived at Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

verses.kjv_text: Now when much time was spent, and when sailing was now dangerous, because the fast was now already past, Paul admonished {them}, {the fast: the fast was on the tenth day of the seventh month}
verses.nlt_text: We had lost a lot of time. The weather was becoming dangerous for sea travel because it was so late in the fall, and Paul spoke to the ship's officers about it.

verses.kjv_text: And said unto them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be with hurt and much damage, not only of the lading and ship, but also of our lives. {hurt: or, injury}
verses.nlt_text: "Men," he said, "I believe there is trouble ahead if we go on-- shipwreck, loss of cargo, and danger to our lives as well."

verses.kjv_text: Nevertheless the centurion believed the master and the owner of the ship, more than those things which were spoken by Paul.
verses.nlt_text: But the officer in charge of the prisoners listened more to the ship's captain and the owner than to Paul.

verses.kjv_text: And because the haven was not commodious to winter in, the more part advised to depart thence also, if by any means they might attain to Phenice, {and there} to winter; {which is} an haven of Crete, and lieth toward the south west and north west.
verses.nlt_text: And since Fair Havens was an exposed harbor-- a poor place to spend the winter-- most of the crew wanted to go on to Phoenix, farther up the coast of Crete, and spend the winter there. Phoenix was a good harbor with only a southwest and northwest exposure.

verses.kjv_text: And when the south wind blew softly, supposing that they had obtained {their} purpose, loosing {thence}, they sailed close by Crete.
verses.nlt_text: When a light wind began blowing from the south, the sailors thought they could make it. So they pulled up anchor and sailed close to the shore of Crete.

verses.kjv_text: But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, called Euroclydon. {arose: or, beat}
verses.nlt_text: But the weather changed abruptly, and a wind of typhoon strength (called a "northeaster") caught the ship and blew it out to sea.

verses.kjv_text: And when the ship was caught, and could not bear up into the wind, we let {her} drive.
verses.nlt_text: They couldn't turn the ship into the wind, so they gave up and let it run before the gale.

verses.kjv_text: And running under a certain island which is called Clauda, we had much work to come by the boat:
verses.nlt_text: We sailed along the sheltered side of a small island named Cauda, where with great difficulty we hoisted aboard the lifeboat being towed behind us.

verses.kjv_text: Which when they had taken up, they used helps, undergirding the ship; and, fearing lest they should fall into the quicksands, strake sail, and so were driven.
verses.nlt_text: Then the sailors bound ropes around the hull of the ship to strengthen it. They were afraid of being driven across to the sandbars of Syrtis off the African coast, so they lowered the sea anchor to slow the ship and were driven before the wind.

verses.kjv_text: And we being exceedingly tossed with a tempest, the next {day} they lightened the ship;
verses.nlt_text: The next day, as gale-force winds continued to batter the ship, the crew began throwing the cargo overboard.

verses.kjv_text: And the third {day} we cast out with our own hands the tackling of the ship.
verses.nlt_text: The following day they even took some of the ship's gear and threw it overboard.

verses.kjv_text: And when neither sun nor stars in many days appeared, and no small tempest lay on {us}, all hope that we should be saved was then taken away.
verses.nlt_text: The terrible storm raged for many days, blotting out the sun and the stars, until at last all hope was gone.

verses.kjv_text: But after long abstinence Paul stood forth in the midst of them, and said, Sirs, ye should have hearkened unto me, and not have loosed from Crete, and to have gained this harm and loss.
verses.nlt_text: No one had eaten for a long time. Finally, Paul called the crew together and said, "Men, you should have listened to me in the first place and not left Crete. You would have avoided all this damage and loss.

verses.kjv_text: And now I exhort you to be of good cheer: for there shall be no loss of {any man's} life among you, but of the ship.
verses.nlt_text: But take courage! None of you will lose your lives, even though the ship will go down.

verses.kjv_text: For there stood by me this night the angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve,
verses.nlt_text: For last night an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me,

verses.kjv_text: Saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must be brought before Caesar: and, lo, God hath given thee all them that sail with thee.
verses.nlt_text: and he said, 'Don't be afraid, Paul, for you will surely stand trial before Caesar! What's more, God in his goodness has granted safety to everyone sailing with you.'

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.
verses.nlt_text: So take courage! For I believe God. It will be just as he said.

verses.kjv_text: Howbeit we must be cast upon a certain island.
verses.nlt_text: But we will be shipwrecked on an island."

verses.kjv_text: But when the fourteenth night was come, as we were driven up and down in Adria, about midnight the shipmen deemed that they drew near to some country;
verses.nlt_text: About midnight on the fourteenth night of the storm, as we were being driven across the Sea of Adria, the sailors sensed land was near.

verses.kjv_text: And sounded, and found {it} twenty fathoms: and when they had gone a little further, they sounded again, and found {it} fifteen fathoms.
verses.nlt_text: They dropped a weighted line and found that the water was 120 feet deep. But a little later they measured again and found it was only 90 feet deep.

verses.kjv_text: Then fearing lest we should have fallen upon rocks, they cast four anchors out of the stern, and wished for the day.
verses.nlt_text: At this rate they were afraid we would soon be driven against the rocks along the shore, so they threw out four anchors from the back of the ship and prayed for daylight.

verses.kjv_text: And as the shipmen were about to flee out of the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under colour as though they would have cast anchors out of the foreship,
verses.nlt_text: Then the sailors tried to abandon the ship; they lowered the lifeboat as though they were going to put out anchors from the front of the ship.

verses.kjv_text: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, Except these abide in the ship, ye cannot be saved.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul said to the commanding officer and the soldiers, "You will all die unless the sailors stay aboard."

verses.kjv_text: Then the soldiers cut off the ropes of the boat, and let her fall off.
verses.nlt_text: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and let it drift away.

verses.kjv_text: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought {them} all to take meat, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye have tarried and continued fasting, having taken nothing.
verses.nlt_text: Just as day was dawning, Paul urged everyone to eat. "You have been so worried that you haven't touched food for two weeks," he said.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore I pray you to take {some} meat: for this is for your health: for there shall not an hair fall from the head of any of you.
verses.nlt_text: "Please eat something now for your own good. For not a hair of your heads will perish."

verses.kjv_text: And when he had thus spoken, he took bread, and gave thanks to God in presence of them all: and when he had broken {it}, he began to eat.
verses.nlt_text: Then he took some bread, gave thanks to God before them all, and broke off a piece and ate it.

verses.kjv_text: Then were they all of good cheer, and they also took {some} meat.
verses.nlt_text: Then everyone was encouraged and began to eat--

verses.kjv_text: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.
verses.nlt_text: all 276 of us who were on board.

verses.kjv_text: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, and cast out the wheat into the sea.
verses.nlt_text: After eating, the crew lightened the ship further by throwing the cargo of wheat overboard.

verses.kjv_text: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they discovered a certain creek with a shore, into the which they were minded, if it were possible, to thrust in the ship.
verses.nlt_text: When morning dawned, they didn't recognize the coastline, but they saw a bay with a beach and wondered if they could get to shore by running the ship aground.

verses.kjv_text: And when they had taken up the anchors, they committed {themselves} unto the sea, and loosed the rudder bands, and hoised up the mainsail to the wind, and made toward shore. {taken...: or, cut the anchors, they left them in the sea}
verses.nlt_text: So they cut off the anchors and left them in the sea. Then they lowered the rudders, raised the foresail, and headed toward shore.

verses.kjv_text: And falling into a place where two seas met, they ran the ship aground; and the forepart stuck fast, and remained unmoveable, but the hinder part was broken with the violence of the waves.
verses.nlt_text: But they hit a shoal and ran the ship aground too soon. The bow of the ship stuck fast, while the stern was repeatedly smashed by the force of the waves and began to break apart.

verses.kjv_text: And the soldiers' counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.
verses.nlt_text: The soldiers wanted to kill the prisoners to make sure they didn't swim ashore and escape.

verses.kjv_text: But the centurion, willing to save Paul, kept them from {their} purpose; and commanded that they which could swim should cast {themselves} first {into the sea}, and get to land:
verses.nlt_text: But the commanding officer wanted to spare Paul, so he didn't let them carry out their plan. Then he ordered all who could swim to jump overboard first and make for land.

verses.kjv_text: And the rest, some on boards, and some on {broken pieces} of the ship. And so it came to pass, that they escaped all safe to land.
verses.nlt_text: The others held onto planks or debris from the broken ship. So everyone escaped safely to shore.

verses.kjv_text: And when they were escaped, then they knew that the island was called Melita.
verses.nlt_text: Once we were safe on shore, we learned that we were on the island of Malta.

verses.kjv_text: And the barbarous people shewed us no little kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us every one, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.
verses.nlt_text: The people of the island were very kind to us. It was cold and rainy, so they built a fire on the shore to welcome us.

verses.kjv_text: And when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks, and laid {them} on the fire, there came a viper out of the heat, and fastened on his hand.
verses.nlt_text: As Paul gathered an armful of sticks and was laying them on the fire, a poisonous snake, driven out by the heat, bit him on the hand.

verses.kjv_text: And when the barbarians saw the {venomous} beast hang on his hand, they said among themselves, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped the sea, yet vengeance suffereth not to live.
verses.nlt_text: The people of the island saw it hanging from his hand and said to each other, "A murderer, no doubt! Though he escaped the sea, justice will not permit him to live."

verses.kjv_text: And he shook off the beast into the fire, and felt no harm.
verses.nlt_text: But Paul shook off the snake into the fire and was unharmed.

verses.kjv_text: Howbeit they looked when he should have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but after they had looked a great while, and saw no harm come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.
verses.nlt_text: The people waited for him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But when they had waited a long time and saw that he wasn't harmed, they changed their minds and decided he was a god.

verses.kjv_text: In the same quarters were possessions of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius; who received us, and lodged us three days courteously.
verses.nlt_text: Near the shore where we landed was an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and treated us kindly for three days.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that the father of Publius lay sick of a fever and of a bloody flux: to whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laid his hands on him, and healed him.
verses.nlt_text: As it happened, Publius's father was ill with fever and dysentery. Paul went in and prayed for him, and laying his hands on him, he healed him.

verses.kjv_text: So when this was done, others also, which had diseases in the island, came, and were healed:
verses.nlt_text: Then all the other sick people on the island came and were healed.

verses.kjv_text: Who also honoured us with many honours; and when we departed, they laded {us} with such things as were necessary.
verses.nlt_text: As a result we were showered with honors, and when the time came to sail, people supplied us with everything we would need for the trip.

verses.kjv_text: And after three months we departed in a ship of Alexandria, which had wintered in the isle, whose sign was Castor and Pollux.
verses.nlt_text: It was three months after the shipwreck that we set sail on another ship that had wintered at the island-- an Alexandrian ship with the twin gods as its figurehead.

verses.kjv_text: And landing at Syracuse, we tarried {there} three days.
verses.nlt_text: Our first stop was Syracuse, where we stayed three days.

verses.kjv_text: And from thence we fetched a compass, and came to Rhegium: and after one day the south wind blew, and we came the next day to Puteoli:
verses.nlt_text: From there we sailed across to Rhegium. A day later a south wind began blowing, so the following day we sailed up the coast to Puteoli.

verses.kjv_text: Where we found brethren, and were desired to tarry with them seven days: and so we went toward Rome.
verses.nlt_text: There we found some believers, who invited us to spend a week with them. And so we came to Rome.

verses.kjv_text: And from thence, when the brethren heard of us, they came to meet us as far as Appii forum, and The three taverns: whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
verses.nlt_text: The brothers and sisters in Rome had heard we were coming, and they came to meet us at the Forum on the Appian Way. Others joined us at The Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and thanked God.

verses.kjv_text: And when we came to Rome, the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard: but Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier that kept him.
verses.nlt_text: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to have his own private lodging, though he was guarded by a soldier.

verses.kjv_text: And it came to pass, that after three days Paul called the chief of the Jews together: and when they were come together, he said unto them, Men {and} brethren, though I have committed nothing against the people, or customs of our fathers, yet was I delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
verses.nlt_text: Three days after Paul's arrival, he called together the local Jewish leaders. He said to them, "Brothers, I was arrested in Jerusalem and handed over to the Roman government, even though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our ancestors.

verses.kjv_text: Who, when they had examined me, would have let {me} go, because there was no cause of death in me.
verses.nlt_text: The Romans tried me and wanted to release me, because they found no cause for the death sentence.

verses.kjv_text: But when the Jews spake against {it}, I was constrained to appeal unto Caesar; not that I had ought to accuse my nation of.
verses.nlt_text: But when the Jewish leaders protested the decision, I felt it necessary to appeal to Caesar, even though I had no desire to press charges against my own people.

verses.kjv_text: For this cause therefore have I called for you, to see {you}, and to speak with {you}: because that for the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.
verses.nlt_text: I asked you to come here today so we could get acquainted and so I could explain to you that I am bound with this chain because I believe that the hope of Israel-- the Messiah-- has already come."

verses.kjv_text: And they said unto him, We neither received letters out of Judaea concerning thee, neither any of the brethren that came shewed or spake any harm of thee.
verses.nlt_text: They replied, "We have had no letters from Judea or reports against you from anyone who has come here.

verses.kjv_text: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.
verses.nlt_text: But we want to hear what you believe, for the only thing we know about this movement is that it is denounced everywhere."

verses.kjv_text: And when they had appointed him a day, there came many to him into {his} lodging; to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and {out of} the prophets, from morning till evening.
verses.nlt_text: So a time was set, and on that day a large number of people came to Paul's lodging. He explained and testified about the Kingdom of God and tried to persuade them about Jesus from the Scriptures. Using the law of Moses and the books of the prophets, he spoke to them from morning until evening.

verses.kjv_text: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.
verses.nlt_text: Some were persuaded by the things he said, but others did not believe.

verses.kjv_text: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed, after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers,
verses.nlt_text: And after they had argued back and forth among themselves, they left with this final word from Paul: "The Holy Spirit was right when he said to your ancestors through Isaiah the prophet,

verses.kjv_text: Saying, Go unto this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive:
verses.nlt_text: 'Go and say to this people: When you hear what I say, you will not understand. When you see what I do, you will not comprehend.

verses.kjv_text: For the heart of this people is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with {their} eyes, and hear with {their} ears, and understand with {their} heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
verses.nlt_text: For the hearts of these people are hardened, and their ears cannot hear, and they have closed their eyes-- so their eyes cannot see, and their ears cannot hear, and their hearts cannot understand, and they cannot turn to me and let me heal them.'

verses.kjv_text: Be it known therefore unto you, that the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and {that} they will hear it.
verses.nlt_text: So I want you to know that this salvation from God has also been offered to the Gentiles, and they will accept it."

verses.kjv_text: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, and had great reasoning among themselves.
And Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came in unto him,
verses.nlt_text: For the next two years, Paul lived in Rome at his own expense. He welcomed all who visited him,

verses.kjv_text: Preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching those things which concern the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
verses.nlt_text: boldly proclaiming the Kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ. And no one tried to stop him.

verses.kjv_text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called {to be} an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,
verses.nlt_text: This letter is from Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, chosen by God to be an apostle and sent out to preach his Good News.

verses.kjv_text: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)
verses.nlt_text: God promised this Good News long ago through his prophets in the holy Scriptures.

verses.kjv_text: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;
verses.nlt_text: The Good News is about his Son, Jesus. In his earthly life he was born into King David's family line,

verses.kjv_text: And declared {to be} the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: {declared: Gr. determined}
verses.nlt_text: and he was shown to be the Son of God when he was raised from the dead by the power of the Holy Spirit. He is Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.kjv_text: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name: {for obedience...: or, to the obedience of faith}
verses.nlt_text: Through Christ, God has given us the privilege and authority as apostles to tell Gentiles everywhere what God has done for them, so that they will believe and obey him, bringing glory to his name.

verses.kjv_text: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:
verses.nlt_text: And you are included among those Gentiles who have been called to belong to Jesus Christ.

verses.kjv_text: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called {to be} saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.nlt_text: I am writing to all of you in Rome who are loved by God and are called to be his own holy people.May God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ give you grace and peace.

verses.kjv_text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
verses.nlt_text: Let me say first that I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith in him is being talked about all over the world.

verses.kjv_text: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers; {with: or, in}
verses.nlt_text: God knows how often I pray for you. Day and night I bring you and your needs in prayer to God, whom I serve with all my heart by spreading the Good News about his Son.

verses.kjv_text: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.
verses.nlt_text: One of the things I always pray for is the opportunity, God willing, to come at last to see you.

verses.kjv_text: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;
verses.nlt_text: For I long to visit you so I can bring you some spiritual gift that will help you grow strong in the Lord.

verses.kjv_text: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me. {with: or, in}
verses.nlt_text: When we get together, I want to encourage you in your faith, but I also want to be encouraged by yours.

verses.kjv_text: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles. {among: or, in}
verses.nlt_text: I want you to know, dear brothers and sisters, that I planned many times to visit you, but I was prevented until now. I want to work among you and see spiritual fruit, just as I have seen among other Gentiles.

verses.kjv_text: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.
verses.nlt_text: For I have a great sense of obligation to people in both the civilized world and the rest of the world, to the educated and uneducated alike.

verses.kjv_text: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.
verses.nlt_text: So I am eager to come to you in Rome, too, to preach the Good News.

verses.kjv_text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.
verses.nlt_text: For I am not ashamed of this Good News about Christ. It is the power of God at work, saving everyone who believes-- the Jew first and also the Gentile.

verses.kjv_text: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.
verses.nlt_text: This Good News tells us how God makes us right in his sight. This is accomplished from start to finish by faith. As the Scriptures say, "It is through faith that a righteous person has life."

verses.kjv_text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;
verses.nlt_text: But God shows his anger from heaven against all sinful, wicked people who suppress the truth by their wickedness.

verses.kjv_text: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed {it} unto them. {in them: or, to them}
verses.nlt_text: They know the truth about God because he has made it obvious to them.

verses.kjv_text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, {even} his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: {so...: or, that they may be}
verses.nlt_text: For ever since the world was created, people have seen the earth and sky. Through everything God made, they can clearly see his invisible qualities-- his eternal power and divine nature. So they have no excuse for not knowing God.

verses.kjv_text: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified {him} not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, they knew God, but they wouldn't worship him as God or even give him thanks. And they began to think up foolish ideas of what God was like. As a result, their minds became dark and confused.

verses.kjv_text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,
verses.nlt_text: Claiming to be wise, they instead became utter fools.

verses.kjv_text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.
verses.nlt_text: And instead of worshiping the glorious, ever-living God, they worshiped idols made to look like mere people and birds and animals and reptiles.

verses.kjv_text: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:
verses.nlt_text: So God abandoned them to do whatever shameful things their hearts desired. As a result, they did vile and degrading things with each other's bodies.

verses.kjv_text: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen. {more: or, rather}
verses.nlt_text: They traded the truth about God for a lie. So they worshiped and served the things God created instead of the Creator himself, who is worthy of eternal praise! Amen.

verses.kjv_text: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:
verses.nlt_text: That is why God abandoned them to their shameful desires. Even the women turned against the natural way to have sex and instead indulged in sex with each other.

verses.kjv_text: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.
verses.nlt_text: And the men, instead of having normal sexual relations with women, burned with lust for each other. Men did shameful things with other men, and as a result of this sin, they suffered within themselves the penalty they deserved.

verses.kjv_text: And even as they did not like to retain God in {their} knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient; {to retain: or, to acknowledge} {a reprobate...: or, a mind void of judgment or, an unapproving mind}
verses.nlt_text: Since they thought it foolish to acknowledge God, he abandoned them to their foolish thinking and let them do things that should never be done.

verses.kjv_text: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,
verses.nlt_text: Their lives became full of every kind of wickedness, sin, greed, hate, envy, murder, quarreling, deception, malicious behavior, and gossip.

verses.kjv_text: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
verses.nlt_text: They are backstabbers, haters of God, insolent, proud, and boastful. They invent new ways of sinning, and they disobey their parents.

verses.kjv_text: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: {without natural...: or unsociable}
verses.nlt_text: They refuse to understand, break their promises, are heartless, and have no mercy.

verses.kjv_text: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them. {have...: or, consent with}
verses.nlt_text: They know God's justice requires that those who do these things deserve to die, yet they do them anyway. Worse yet, they encourage others to do them, too.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art that judgest: for wherein thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.
verses.nlt_text: You may think you can condemn such people, but you are just as bad, and you have no excuse! When you say they are wicked and should be punished, you are condemning yourself, for you who judge others do these very same things.

verses.kjv_text: But we are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such things.
verses.nlt_text: And we know that God, in his justice, will punish anyone who does such things.

verses.kjv_text: And thinkest thou this, O man, that judgest them which do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God?
verses.nlt_text: Since you judge others for doing these things, why do you think you can avoid God's judgment when you do the same things?

verses.kjv_text: Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?
verses.nlt_text: Don't you see how wonderfully kind, tolerant, and patient God is with you? Does this mean nothing to you? Can't you see that his kindness is intended to turn you from your sin?

verses.kjv_text: But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God;
verses.nlt_text: But because you are stubborn and refuse to turn from your sin, you are storing up terrible punishment for yourself. For a day of anger is coming, when God's righteous judgment will be revealed.

verses.kjv_text: Who will render to every man according to his deeds:
verses.nlt_text: He will judge everyone according to what they have done.

verses.kjv_text: To them who by patient continuance in well doing seek for glory and honour and immortality, eternal life:
verses.nlt_text: He will give eternal life to those who keep on doing good, seeking after the glory and honor and immortality that God offers.

verses.kjv_text: But unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath,
verses.nlt_text: But he will pour out his anger and wrath on those who live for themselves, who refuse to obey the truth and instead live lives of wickedness.

verses.kjv_text: Tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Gentile; {Gentile: Gr. Greek}
verses.nlt_text: There will be trouble and calamity for everyone who keeps on doing what is evil-- for the Jew first and also for the Gentile.

verses.kjv_text: But glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good, to the Jew first, and also to the Gentile: {Gentile: Gr. Greek}
verses.nlt_text: But there will be glory and honor and peace from God for all who do good-- for the Jew first and also for the Gentile.

verses.kjv_text: For there is no respect of persons with God.
verses.nlt_text: For God does not show favoritism.

verses.kjv_text: For as many as have sinned without law shall also perish without law: and as many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law;
verses.nlt_text: When the Gentiles sin, they will be destroyed, even though they never had God's written law. And the Jews, who do have God's law, will be judged by that law when they fail to obey it.

verses.kjv_text: (For not the hearers of the law {are} just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.
verses.nlt_text: For merely listening to the law doesn't make us right with God. It is obeying the law that makes us right in his sight.

verses.kjv_text: For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves:
verses.nlt_text: Even Gentiles, who do not have God's written law, show that they know his law when they instinctively obey it, even without having heard it.

verses.kjv_text: Which shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and {their} thoughts the mean while accusing or else excusing one another;) {their conscience...: or, the conscience witnessing with them} {the mean...: or, between themselves}
verses.nlt_text: They demonstrate that God's law is written in their hearts, for their own conscience and thoughts either accuse them or tell them they are doing right.

verses.kjv_text: In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ according to my gospel.
verses.nlt_text: And this is the message I proclaim-- that the day is coming when God, through Christ Jesus, will judge everyone's secret life.

verses.kjv_text: Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God,
verses.nlt_text: You who call yourselves Jews are relying on God's law, and you boast about your special relationship with him.

verses.kjv_text: And knowest {his} will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law; {approvest...: or, triest the things that differ}
verses.nlt_text: You know what he wants; you know what is right because you have been taught his law.

verses.kjv_text: And art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness,
verses.nlt_text: You are convinced that you are a guide for the blind and a light for people who are lost in darkness.

verses.kjv_text: An instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law.
verses.nlt_text: You think you can instruct the ignorant and teach children the ways of God. For you are certain that God's law gives you complete knowledge and truth.

verses.kjv_text: Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal?
verses.nlt_text: Well then, if you teach others, why don't you teach yourself? You tell others not to steal, but do you steal?

verses.kjv_text: Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?
verses.nlt_text: You say it is wrong to commit adultery, but do you commit adultery? You condemn idolatry, but do you use items stolen from pagan temples?

verses.kjv_text: Thou that makest thy boast of the law, through breaking the law dishonourest thou God?
verses.nlt_text: You are so proud of knowing the law, but you dishonor God by breaking it.

verses.kjv_text: For the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you, as it is written.
verses.nlt_text: No wonder the Scriptures say, "The Gentiles blaspheme the name of God because of you."

verses.kjv_text: For circumcision verily profiteth, if thou keep the law: but if thou be a breaker of the law, thy circumcision is made uncircumcision.
verses.nlt_text: The Jewish ceremony of circumcision has value only if you obey God's law. But if you don't obey God's law, you are no better off than an uncircumcised Gentile.

verses.kjv_text: Therefore if the uncircumcision keep the righteousness of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be counted for circumcision?
verses.nlt_text: And if the Gentiles obey God's law, won't God declare them to be his own people?

verses.kjv_text: And shall not uncircumcision which is by nature, if it fulfil the law, judge thee, who by the letter and circumcision dost transgress the law?
verses.nlt_text: In fact, uncircumcised Gentiles who keep God's law will condemn you Jews who are circumcised and possess God's law but don't obey it.

verses.kjv_text: For he is not a Jew, which is one outwardly; neither {is that} circumcision, which is outward in the flesh:
verses.nlt_text: For you are not a true Jew just because you were born of Jewish parents or because you have gone through the ceremony of circumcision.

verses.kjv_text: But he {is} a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision {is that} of the heart, in the spirit, {and} not in the letter; whose praise {is} not of men, but of God.
verses.nlt_text: No, a true Jew is one whose heart is right with God. And true circumcision is not merely obeying the letter of the law; rather, it is a change of heart produced by God's Spirit. And a person with a changed heart seeks praise from God, not from people.

verses.kjv_text: What advantage then hath the Jew? or what profit {is there} of circumcision?
verses.nlt_text: Then what's the advantage of being a Jew? Is there any value in the ceremony of circumcision?

verses.kjv_text: Much every way: chiefly, because that unto them were committed the oracles of God.
verses.nlt_text: Yes, there are great benefits! First of all, the Jews were entrusted with the whole revelation of God.

verses.kjv_text: For what if some did not believe? shall their unbelief make the faith of God without effect?
verses.nlt_text: True, some of them were unfaithful; but just because they were unfaithful, does that mean God will be unfaithful?

verses.kjv_text: God forbid: yea, let God be true, but every man a liar; as it is written, That thou mightest be justified in thy sayings, and mightest overcome when thou art judged.
